Zann rubbed his hands together and pointed at the huge metal lock on Boz's cell door. "Open," he said.
Nothing happened. "Don't bother, Zann," Boz said. "Morb has put a Dousing spell over the entire dungeon."
"That's right," Teplo added wryly. "Do you think we would have stuck around if we'd had a choice?"
Zann's shoulders slumped. He'd just regained his magic, and now it was useless again.
"Without magic, how am I supposed to . . ." His words trailed off. He could almost hear Darb's voice in his head: It is possible to get into a house without magic, you know!

Zann grinned. Any door that could be opened with magic could also be opened without it. He stepped away from the cells and scanned the walls near the steps. The item he needed should be here somewhere . . .
"Aha!" said Zann. He reached over and grabbed a key off a hook on the wall. It was inside the stairwell, just out of sight of the prisoners.
Boz's eyes widened when he saw it. "Good thinking, my boy! Now hurry and get us out of here!"

Morb rubbed his fingers together and touched the talisman in his hand. Energy emanated from it and flowed through the air and into the talismans of the trolls standing in front of him. Morb hated to give up that magical energy, especially when he had so little left. But he couldn't risk leaving the palace without strong trolls to guard him—especially not now, when he was so close to victory.
"Come with me," Morb ordered the trolls.
They marched behind him as he walked through the palace. The blob Wyssa had brought last week was still guarding the entrance, but it shrank back respectfully as Morb passed.
Morb strode across the square, ignoring the few citizens that were scurrying about. Soon he reached the riverbank.
"I should find what I need here," he muttered.
Rubbing his hands together, Morb focused on the river before him.
"Levitate!" he intoned.
Energy sizzled from Morb's hands. With a groan the entire riverbank rose, dripping water and dirt. Morb waved a hand, and the mass moved until it was directly over him.
The trolls stepped back, staring fearfully up at the huge chunk of earth hanging overhead. Morb smiled as his sharp amber eyes spotted a small, gray shape wriggling out of the dirt above him.
Just as he'd expected, the leeches had burrowed into the riverbank as soon as they'd felt his spell. Now they had burrowed straight through and were falling from the bottom.
Morb reached out and caught the first leech as it fell. Then he turned away, ignoring the dozens of others that were raining down around him.
"That's all," he told the trolls. "Let's go."
"Hurry!" Zann urged the prisoners. "We need to get out of here fast!"

He had opened all the cells, and now Boz and Teplo were helping him guide the released prisoners up the narrow stairway. When everyone was at the top of the stairs and out of the Dousing spell's range, some of the stronger Reds began zapping the weaker Reds to safety.
The king approached Zann.
"Well done, young man," said the king. "You're a hero. I'm going to recommend that you . . ."

Just then Zann heard a faint sound—it sounded like a heartbeat. He tried to ignore it, but it was impossible. It was as if the sound wouldn't let him think about anything else—it was forcing him to listen.
"Your Majesty," said Zann, interrupting the king. "I'm sorry, but do you hear that sound?"
The king gave Zann a funny look. "What sound are you talking about?"
"It sounds like a heartbeat," said Zann.
The king listened but didn't seem to hear it.
Boz and Teplo hurried over to them.
"Did you say you hear a heartbeat?" Teplo asked, looking anxious. "It's probably a Guiding spell! You said Fala is here in the palace, yes?"
Zann had no idea what Teplo was talking about. "What's a Guiding spell?" he asked.

"It's a very old-fashioned spell," Teplo explained. "I taught Fala how to do it. Hardly anybody uses a Guiding spell these days—ever since message moths were discovered. But you never know when you might find yourself in a precarious situation without one of those moths."
"You and your strange old tricks!" Boz laughed.
"Focus on the sound, Zann," Teplo said. "Fala is directing it to you, so you're the only one who can hear it. The closer you get to Fala, the louder the sound will get."
Zann focused on the heartbeat. He noticed that he could hear it slightly better if he turned toward the long hallway. He took a step in that direction and the sound became much more distinct.
"I think we're supposed to go this way," said Zann, pointing down the hallway.
"That leads to the ballroom," said the king.
"To the ballroom!" Teplo commanded.

Zann headed along the hallway, followed by all the freed Reds. With each step he took, he could hear the sound become louder and clearer. Soon they rounded a corner and arrived in the ballroom. Fala was there, along with Perda, Gliss, Darb, and all the rebels. As soon as Zann saw Fala, the sound stopped.
The rebels gasped when they saw the freed Reds come into the room.
"Mom! Dad!" Gliss cried, flinging herself into her parents' arms.
"Gliss! You're safe!" Her mother hugged her tightly.
"We were terribly worried about you," her father added. "And so was your uncle Gar."
"I'm glad you're okay, Gliss," said Uncle Gar, who had just walked over.

Meanwhile Perda and Darb rushed over to Zann, along with Zing. "You did it! You found the dungeon!" Perda exclaimed. Darb grinned and clapped Zann on the back while Zing flew in circles overhead, whistling.
Zann was happy to see his friends, but he also felt nervous. Morb could show up at any moment.
Nearby Fala was speaking with the king.
"Your Majesty, Morb left the palace a short time ago," Fala told him. "But I'm not sure why, and I don't know when he'll return."
The king nodded. Still weakened from the leech treatments, he spoke quietly to the crowd.

"Citizens of Magica, I hereby declare Morb to be an enemy of our world," said the king. "Not since the Dark Times has Magica faced such a serious threat. Morb is to be arrested immediately when he returns."
"Your Majesty, that might not be as easy as it sounds," said Boz. "Morb has become quite powerful in the last few days."
"Even with all the Reds, we still might not be able to apprehend him," Vig added.
"Then what are we going to do?" asked the queen.
"We need a plan to ambush Morb," someone said.
Growing impatient, Zann looked for his friends. Darb and Perda had gone over to join Gliss and her parents. Zing was nearby, nosing at a beetle on the floor.

The far end of the ballroom opened out to the courtyard where Zann had seen Morb's magic-sucking machine. Zann wandered over, and he could see the machine crouched out there like a dark, terrible monster. Something new had been added to it since Zann had seen it yesterday. Perched at the very top was a strange-looking object.
"What is that?" he murmured to himself.

Zann stepped outside for a better look. When he got closer, he could see the new item more clearly. It was the jawbone from some kind of animal, perhaps a dragon. It was lined with large, razor-sharp teeth.

Zann stood in front of the machine, staring at the pythons writhing in a tube filled with silvery liquid. Below that was a basin of dark water. Floating in the water was a multicolored, spongelike creature. Zann leaned in for a closer look. He'd never seen anything like it. Suddenly he heard a soft thump. Zann looked up to see that one of the pythons was looking right at him. Startled, Zann leaped backward with a gasp.

Walking around to the other side of the machine, Zann examined the complicated network of bones and wire. How had Morb ever built such a thing? Just then Zann heard footsteps entering the courtyard. He quickly ducked behind a large plant and held his breath. His heart pounding, Zann peeked between the leaves and saw Morb, flanked by several ugly trolls.

Zann crouched unseen behind the large plant as Morb and the trolls walked toward the machine. Morb stopped in front of the enormous contraption and studied it. He had a strange and frightening look on his face. He barely noticed when Slib came scurrying into the courtyard.
"Thank you for saving me from that terrifying creature, Your Majesty," said Slib. "And for lifting the Dousing spell."
"I almost didn't bother to save you," he told Slib, still looking at the machine. "You really aren't worth the energy it took. But I wanted you to witness my moment of triumph."
"It will be my honor, Your Majesty," said Slib, simpering.

Zann crouched lower, taking care to stay hidden. He wished he knew how to do that Guiding spell that Fala had used. Boz and all those other powerful Reds were right inside. They could stop Morb. If only Zann could somehow let them know that Morb was back!
But it was too risky. If Zann made a move, Morb would hear him. The trolls would hear him. Zann decided to stay put and wait.
He watched as Morb held up a hand. Dangling from it was something small. Zann squinted and saw that it was a leech.
"Do you see this, you incompetent fool?" Morb said, thrusting the wriggling gray creature toward Slib. "This was all I needed to complete my machine and put the final step of my plan into action."

"B-but how, Your Majesty?" Slib stammered. "I thought you needed the blue leeches to make the machine work. It would take thousands of ordinary Magica leeches to equal just a handful of the blue ones!"
Morb sneered. "If it's thousands I need, then it's thousands I'll have."
He tossed the leech onto the ground. Then he rubbed his hands together, causing sparks to fly. There was a flash of energy, and another identical leech appeared beside the first.
Slib stared in awe. "How is that possible?"
Zann was awed too. Morb had just used a Duplication spell on the leech. "I didn't know that spell could work on a living creature!" Zann thought.
He watched as Morb used the spell again and again. Soon there were dozens of leeches writhing on the ground—and then hundreds.
Zann glanced at Morb, wondering when he was going to stop. Morb was red-faced and breathless. It was obvious that the Duplication spell was using up a lot of his energy.
Finally Morb lowered his hand and stepped back. "Put them in the machine," he ordered the trolls.
The trolls scooped up handfuls of leeches and started shoving them into a hole directly beneath the jawbone.
"Careful!" Morb said as a troll's hand bumped the machine. "That's a one-of-a-kind relic, you clumsy fool!"
Regardless of the danger to himself, Zann knew he had to do something. He stood up and quickly created some friction.
"Boz! Morb is in the courtyard!" he shouted, using a Swelling spell to make his voice carry into the ballroom.
Morb spun around. His eyes widened when he saw Zann.
"You again!" he snarled.

Morb sent a Blast spell flying at Zann. Zann barely managed to dodge it, and it demolished a stone bench instead. Zann gulped. Morb might have been weakened by the Duplication spell, but he was still incredibly strong.
"Protect!" Zann blurted out, rubbing his hands together. A glowing purple bubble appeared, surrounding him on all sides.
"Nice try, boy," Morb said sarcastically, rubbing his fingers together until sparks flew. "But your pathetic Shield spell is no match for my power!"
Zann gulped, amazed at the energy sparking out of Morb's hands. Morb was right. Zann's Shield spell could never stop one of Morb's blasts. And it was too late to run.
But Zann wasn't going to let Morb see him cower. Squaring his shoulders, he stared at the ball of energy hurtling toward him, waiting for the Blast spell to blow him apart.
Just as Morb's blast was about to reach him, Zann saw his Shield spell change colors and expand. His eyes widened as the Blast spell bounced off it, shattering part of a nearby fountain.
"What just happened?" wondered Zann.
"Zann!" Boz shouted.
Turning his head, Zann saw that his grandfather was running into the courtyard, along with a few other Reds. Boz had seen what was happening just in time to add his power to Zann's shield.
Morb raised his hand. "Freeze!"
Boz and the other Reds were instantly frozen in place. Without Boz's magic, Zann's shield lost its power.
Morb turned back to Zann and smiled. "Now, if I remember correctly, I was about to blast you into oblivion."

But before Zann could react, he heard a long, wheezing groan—it was the machine. The trolls were forcing the last of the leeches into the hole. Now the pythons in the glass tube were writhing furiously.
"Uh-oh," Zann muttered.
Morb lifted his arms in triumph. "Yes! Now Magica will witness my true power!"
A thick, dark circle of smoke rose from the jawbone and slowly spread out in every direction.

A troll standing next to the machine blinked as the smoke enveloped its body. Within seconds the troll slumped to the ground with a grunt. Zann could see the magical energy leave its body and flow into the spongelike creature. From there the energy appeared to mix with the water and then drip down into a glass tank beneath.
Morb eyed the tank and smiled. "It's working! The ancient texts were right! Soon I will control every last bit of magic in Magica, and everyone will be forced to bow before me!"

Zann kept watching in horror as the smoke sucked the last bit of energy out of the troll. The creature grunted weakly, and the other trolls stared at it, not understanding what had happened. One by one, they grunted and fell over as the smoke surrounded them.
"Excellent!" Morb cackled as the last of the trolls crumpled to the ground.
The smoke was still expanding. Slib backed away, keeping out of range. "Er, how do you turn it off, Your Majesty?" he asked nervously.
Morb laughed. "I don't." With one hard shove, he sent Slib stumbling into the smoke.
"No!" Slib struggled to escape as the smoke wrapped its tendrils around him. Moments later he lay on the ground, panting.
"I've lost my magic!" he cried.
Zann could see Boz and the others still frozen in place. And the smoke was slowly drifting toward them. If it reached them, they would all lose their magic!
"Getting nervous, boy?" Morb cackled again.
Zann quickly pointed at Morb. "Blast!" he shouted.
Morb lifted a hand and deflected Zann's Blast spell.
"You can't stop me." Morb laughed.
The smoke was coming toward Zann. He looked at the jawbone perched atop the magic-sucking machine.
"Hmm," he thought. "I stopped the other machine by removing that skull."
Zann held out a hand toward the jawbone.
"Come to me," he murmured.
The jawbone shifted slightly.
Morb scowled. "Haven't you learned that you're no match for me?"
Morb held up a hand. A shaft of energy shot out, blocking Zann's Transport spell and burning his hand.
"Ouch!" Zann cried. But, holding out his hand again, he commanded, "Come to me."
"You just won't give up, will you?" said Morb, sending several bolts of energy toward Zann. Zann jumped out of the way, and the wall behind him exploded.

Morb strode over to the magic-sucking machine. "Now I'll show you why there's no point in fighting me." Morb dipped his hand into the tank and scooped out some of the magic-infused water. But before he could take a sip, his talisman began to glow, and his hand froze in place.
Glancing over, Zann could see Fala entering the courtyard. In her hand was the troll talisman.
"How did you . . . ?" Morb cried, unable to move his hand.

Although Morb was immobilized, he apparently still had enough magic to maintain the Flash Freeze he'd placed on Boz and the others. And the smoke was now just inches from them. Fala was frantically trying to free them with the talisman, but it wasn't working. Zann turned his gaze back to the jawbone and focused all his energy.
"Come to me," he murmured again, holding out his hand.

The jawbone leaped off the machine, and the smoke disappeared instantly. As soon as Zann caught the bone, its magic energized him. He could feel sparks flying; his eyes felt strange. Pointing at Boz and the others, he shouted, "Free!"

Energy shot out everywhere. Within a moment all the frozen people were able to move again. But the chaotic magic had also freed Morb, who still had the magic-infused water in his hand. He raised his hand to his lips.
Using a Blast spell, Zann quickly knocked Morb down, causing him to spill the water. Then he blasted the tank on the machine.
"No!" Morb howled as the last of the liquid was absorbed into the ground.
Zann lifted the jawbone over his head to smash it.
Morb's eyes filled with panic. "Wait!" he blurted out. "I have a proposition for you!"
"I'm not interested," Zann said.
"Oh, you'll be interested in this ," Morb said quickly, standing up. "How would you like to know what happened to your parents?"
"I already know about the accident," said Zann.
Morb was silent for a moment and then spoke. "Let me tell you something, young man. Your parents' disappearance was no accident."
Zann was confused. "Wyssa said—"
Morb chuckled. "Yes, Wyssa thinks it was an accident. She also thinks it was her fault—that's how I've been able to blackmail her all this time."
Boz called out, "Don't listen to him, Zann!"
But Zann barely heard his grandfather. Could Morb tell him what really happened to his parents?
Morb's lips curled into an evil grin. "Just hand me the Mouth of the Undead, Zann, and I'll tell you where your parents are."
"You know where they are?" said Zann.
"Of course I know where they are," Morb retorted. "Would you like to see them?"
"What?" Zann thought. His parents were alive, and he could see them again . . .? The arms holding the bone dropped slightly.
Morb saw that his words were working—he was getting to the boy. "I'll even let your grandfather go with you," he added.
Zann looked at Boz. The old man had a faint smile that seemed to say, "I know you'll make the right choice." Zann breathed deeply. He knew what that choice was. He looked back at Morb.
"Can I bring Darb too?" Zann asked.
"Who?" asked Morb.
"What about Perda?" Zann added. "And Gliss? Fala? Teplo? Can they all come with me? What about everyone else over there? What about the rest of Magica?"
"Wh-what are you talking about?" Morb stammered.
Zann stared deep into Morb's eyes. "You have nothing to offer me, Morb. Maybe you can't understand this, but I would never turn my back on my friends—or Magica."
Zann raised the jawbone over his head and threw it down as hard as he could.
Morb's eyes widened with horror. "No—!"
There was a deafening crack, and the two splintered halves of the bone skidded across the cold floor.
"No!" Morb howled, lunging toward the pieces of the broken jawbone.
"Get him!" Vig shouted, raising his sword. A blast of energy shot out of it, but Morb dodged the blast.
Morb snarled, looking around for somewhere to run. But he was surrounded. He rubbed his hands together, using his last bit of magic to levitate to a second-story balcony.
"Stop him!" the king shouted.
"Quick—get a Shield spell up around the palace!" another Red added.
Perda, Darb, and Gliss sprinted over to Zann. "Wow, you were great!" Perda exclaimed.
Zann stared at the balcony where Morb had disappeared, and then at the enormous glowing bubble that had just engulfed the entire palace.
"Morb will never get through that shield," said Boz.
"Morb has no intention of getting through the shield," said Zann, still looking at the balcony. "We need to go after him—now!"
Zann rubbed his hands together. "Levitate!"
As Zann rose into the air, Fala, Boz, Teplo, and all of his friends followed him. In a moment the whole group was on the balcony.
"What do you think Morb is up to, Zann?" Boz asked.
"Just come with me." Zann sprinted down the hall and burst into the storage room.
"Stop!" he shouted.
Morb was there, standing in front of the open wormhole. He glanced over his shoulder at Zann and the others.
Boz rubbed his fingers together. "Freeze!'
The spell flew directly at Morb, but before it hit him, it spun out of control and disappeared into the vortex.
Morb laughed.
"Immobilize!" said Fala. Her spell veered into the wormhole too, and Morb laughed again.
"Where do you think you'll go, Morb?" said Boz. "You can't run forever."
Morb glared at Boz for a moment and then looked at the others. His eyes rested on Zann.
"I don't plan to run forever, Boz," warned Morb. "Magica hasn't seen the last of me!"
With those words Morb stepped into the wormhole and disappeared.
"I've never been so terrified in my entire life!" Gliss exclaimed, peeking through a heavy velvet curtain.
"Really?" said Zann. "After everything we've been through, you're scared of a little crowd?"
"A big crowd," Perda corrected. "I think at least half of Magica is out there!"

It was a few days after Morb had disappeared, and Magica was slowly returning to normal. Zann and his friends were waiting in a small room beside the ballroom. They were about to be officially named "Heroes of Magica" by the king and queen.

Darb was sitting on an overstuffed chair patting Zing, who wore a jaunty ribbon around his scaly neck. The little dragon was so excited that there were singe marks all over the room. Zann stepped over and repaired a burnt spot on Darb's shirt.
"Thanks." Darb sounded distracted.
"Are you okay?" Zann asked.
"I guess." Darb shrugged. "Do you think Morb will ever come back?"
Zann sighed. "It's better not to worry about it. If Morb does return, Magica will be ready for him."
Just then they heard a shout of greeting from the doorway. Several of the kids' friends from Swamp Bottom rushed into the room.
"You came!" Perda exclaimed, racing over to hug some of them.
"Of course we came!" another kid exclaimed. "Everyone wants to see you guys get your reward!"
Jev was there too. He walked over to Gliss, smiling sheepishly.
"Hi, Gliss," he said. "I wanted to say I'm sorry. You know . . . about what I said to you before."
"It's okay, Jev." Gliss smiled back at him. "You did a lot to help us."
Jev looked relieved. "Cool." He grinned and reached for Gliss' hand.
But Darb got there first. He slid his hand into Gliss', and she squeezed it.
"Yes, we really appreciate what you did to help us," Darb said.
Jev's face went red as he realized what was happening. "Whatever," he muttered.
Zann grinned. He couldn't blame Jev for being surprised. Zann hadn't noticed how close Gliss and Darb were getting either. But he was happy for them.
He was still smiling when Perda rushed over. "Are you ready?" she asked breathlessly, looking prettier than ever in her formal gown. "It's time for us to go in!"

Moments later Zann, Perda, Gliss, and Darb were marching up a long aisle, with Zing flying joyfully alongside. The enormous ballroom was filled with a cheering crowd, and even more people spilled into the courtyard. Colorful puffs of energy popped and sparkled overhead. The king and queen stood on a dais at the far end of the room. To their right stood the entire Red Council, and to their left were Boz, Teplo, and Fala.

Zann felt self-conscious but proud as he walked up the long aisle with his friends. Still, looking at all the faces in the crowd, Zann couldn't help thinking that there were two very important people missing from the celebration. Were his parents still alive somewhere, trapped between worlds? What if Morb really was the sole person who knew where they were? Had Zann given up his one and only chance of finding them?
He dismissed these thoughts. Morb's offer had tempted him, but Zann had made the only choice he could make—his parents would never have wanted him to sacrifice Magica just to save them.

Reaching into his pocket, Zann touched the stone Wyssa had given him. His gaze wandered upward, toward the storage room with the wormhole. He didn't need Morb to find his parents. He just needed the courage to take a step into that vortex on his own. The wormhole was still up there—it would always be up there—waiting for him.
"Zann! Is that really you?"
Zann turned. A teenage girl he'd never seen before was rushing toward him, grinning widely.
"Uh-oh," Perda whispered. "It's another fan!"
"Perda!" the girl exclaimed. She noticed Zann's pet dragon sniffing at a beetle nearby. "And Zing! Oh wow—it's an honor to meet you all!"
The girl rubbed her hands together. Flowers rained down on the street all around them.
"They're beautiful," Perda said politely, catching one of the blossoms. "Thank you."
The girl beamed. "No, thank you ! You guys saved Magica!"
A few passing pedestrians stopped to see what was going on. "Look, son," a man told a little boy. "It's Zann and Perda. They're heroes!"

Zann forced a smile as the little boy stared up at him. It had been less than two days since the grand ceremony celebrating Morb's defeat. But Zann and his friends were already getting used to attracting attention everywhere they went. Still, Zann felt a little uncomfortable whenever someone called him a hero.
"We just did what we had to do," he mumbled.
Several people chuckled or clapped their hands to create puffs of colorful magic energy or pretty sparkles.

Zann wondered what his fans would think if they knew he sometimes still thought about Morb's offer. Zann knew he'd done the right thing by refusing the offer—if he hadn't, Morb would now control Magica. But Zann still couldn't help wondering . . . Did Morb really know where Zann's parents were?
By now a small crowd had gathered around Zann and Perda. Thinking about Morb's offer had reminded Zann of today's errand. "Excuse us," he said. "We have to get going."
"Of course, of course." An older woman beamed at him. "I'm sure heroes like you have lots of important things to do."
Zann smiled weakly and then hurried off. Perda and Zing followed.
"Slow down!" Perda complained as they raced around a corner. "Otherwise I'll have to use an Acceleration spell to keep up!"
"Sorry." Zann slowed his pace slightly. "But there's no time to waste. Who knows how much longer we'll get to stay in First City?"

Perda made a face at the mention of leaving. "We're lucky the king and queen asked Boz and Gliss' parents to stay for a few days. Otherwise we'd already be back to our regular lives in boring old Swamp Bottom."

"Yeah." Zann was a little surprised by Perda's words. Before their adventures had started, Perda seemed content to live in Swamp Bottom. Zann was the one who had always complained about how boring the town was.
They passed a wall on which someone had scribbled "Voids are Magicians too!" in large letters.
Perda glanced at the graffiti. "Looks like the Void Rights group has been here," she commented. "At least their messages are polite. Some of the ones from the new anti-Red groups are pretty rude."
Zann nodded, but he wasn't really listening. They'd just reached the university.
"My parents' old lab is this way," he told Perda.
A young woman looked up when they entered the building. A nameplate on her desk said "Elbi."
"Oh! It's two of the young heroes!" she exclaimed.
Zing spurted out a small blast of flame. Elbi yanked a potted melody plant out of the way just in time to keep it from getting singed.
"And the dragon." Elbi narrowed her eyes at Zing and frowned.
"Hi," Zann said. "My parents used to run this lab. Their names are Nax and Asta. Did you know them?"
"Sorry, no." Elbi shrugged. "I've heard of them, of course, but I only started working here two years ago."
"Oh. Well, is Olpa around?"
"No. Olpa and the other senior researchers are all at some big meeting at the palace. I'm not sure when they'll be back. Should I tell Olpa you were here?"
Zann was disappointed. "Are you sure there's nobody here who knew my parents?"
Elbi looked sympathetic. "Sorry. But listen, I have an idea. Would you like to see their storage shelf?" She stood up. "When your parents disappeared, someone put their things there for safekeeping."
"That would be great!" Zann felt a surge of hope. Could there be clues to his parents' whereabouts on that shelf?

Elbi led the way through the lab. Being back there after so long felt strange to Zann. Many things looked the same, but others looked very different. Only a few people were in the main room. A couple of university students were reading near the bookshelves. A Void was cleaning a nibbler's cage. A young researcher was studying a bubbling beaker and scribbling notes.
"Wow, this place is cool!" Perda whispered to Zann, looking around with wide eyes. "It must be amazing to work here!"
"Yeah, I guess," said Zann, distracted. He followed Elbi as she opened a closet door.
"It's the middle shelf in the back," Elbi said, rubbing her fingers together to create a light.

As soon as Zann saw the shelf, he was flooded with memories. There was his mother's favorite hair clip. His father's lab coat. Even a dragon-shaped paperweight that Zann had given his parents as a gift.
"What's this?" Perda picked up a large metal sculpture. It was so blackened by fire that the edges were crumbling away.
"I don't know," Zann said. "I've never seen it before."
"It looks kind of like Teplo's pet sniffer goose, doesn't it?" Perda said.
Before Zann could answer, there was an enormous explosion from somewhere in the city. The building shook, causing some books to fall from the bookshelf. Everyone shouted in surprise.
Zann froze, immediately thinking of Morb and the evil Void's final words: Magica hasn't seen the last of me!
Zann and Perda rushed back to the main room. Elbi was staring out the window, along with the students and the Void. The young researcher had disappeared. A second later he zapped back into the lab.

"Everything's okay," he announced. "I went to the palace square to see what's going on; it's just another protest. The anti-Reds set off a banner cloud that said 'Letting Reds rule is inside out! Brains matter more than hair.'"
"Ugh." Elbi rolled her eyes. "There’ve been so many protests lately. I'm getting really tired of them."
The Void glanced over. "The protests only started yesterday," she reminded Elbi. "And some people think the anti-Reds' concerns are valid."
Just then one of the students shouted. "My notes!"
Zann turned and saw Zing standing near some burning papers. "Oops, sorry about that," said Zann. "He shoots flames when he's startled."
The student glared at Zing. Rubbing his hands together, he touched his papers. "Restore!"
"We should probably go before Zing burns the whole place down," Perda whispered to Zann. "We can come back tomorrow and talk to Olpa."
Zann nodded. Nothing in the closet had looked like a clue, except maybe that weird bird sculpture. But still, he wished he didn't have to wait until tomorrow to find out more.
Zann and Perda thanked Elbi and then hurried outside with Zing. "Let's go see how Darb and Gliss are doing at the zoo," Perda suggested.
Zann sighed and glanced back at the lab. "Okay," he said. He rubbed his fingers together. "Zap!"
Splash !
"Drat," Zann grumbled.
He climbed out of the zoo's fishpond and rubbed his hands together. "Dry," said Zann, placing his hands on his pants. He felt a small lump in his pocket.
"Double drat!" Zann mumbled.
Perda appeared just in time to hear him. "What's wrong?" she asked.

"I meant to ask someone at the lab about this." Zann pulled out the stone Wyssa had given him. "I thought they might know if it came from a different magical world. I think it's a clue to where my parents are."
"You still have that?" Perda looked surprised. "I thought Wyssa told you to give it to Boz."
Zann shrugged. "I haven't had a chance yet. He's been really busy, in case you haven't noticed."
Perda frowned. "We've been running around looking for clues, but that stone might be the only clue you need! You really should ask Boz about it."
"I will." Zann put the stone back in his pocket. "Look, Darb and Gliss are over there."
Darb had volunteered to help restore the wild dragon pen at the zoo. He knew a lot about dragons. Gliss was helping him by providing the magic to make repairs.

They looked up when Zann and Perda approached. "Good, you're here," Gliss said with a weary sigh. "We've been working hard since lunchtime, and I'm exhausted. I could use your help creating friction."
"Did you learn anything useful at the lab?" Darb asked Zann.
"Not really." Zann filled him in on what had happened.

"I wonder what the burnt bird sculpture is," Darb said. He was interested in anything related to animals. He even seemed to get along with Teplo's ill-tempered sniffer goose. Zann and Darb, as well as Boz, had been staying at Teplo's house since Morb had disappeared, and the goose still honked suspiciously every time she saw Zann.
"I don't know," Zann told Darb. "I'm not even sure the sculpture belonged to my parents. I never saw it before. Maybe someone put it on their shelf by mistake."
Perda held out her hands to join friction with Gliss. "You can ask about it when we go back to the lab tomorrow."

Zann sighed. "I hope Boz doesn't zap us back to Swamp Bottom before tomorrow." He clenched his fists with frustration. "I can't go back! There aren't any wormholes within a day's walk of Swamp Bottom."
"Wormholes?" Gliss said. "Why do you need to be near a wormhole?"
Zann shrugged. "My parents disappeared in one."
Gliss gave Zann a funny look. "Yeah, but it's not as if you can just jump into a wormhole to look for them."
"Why not?" Zann shrugged again. "Maybe I should do exactly that!"
"Really?" Perda sounded excited. "Hey, that reminds me—you promised to tell us what it was like when Wyssa took you through the wormhole!"
Gliss ignored her. "You can't be serious, Zann!" she cried. "Wormholes are way too dangerous to mess around with."
"She's right," Darb said. "Jumping into a wormhole isn't exactly a smart plan for finding your parents."
"Well, it's the only plan I've got," said Zann.
"Not really," Perda said. "You haven't shown Boz that stone, remember? Maybe that would—"
"You haven't shown Boz what stone?" a familiar voice interrupted.
Zann spun around. "Boz!" he exclaimed. His grandfather had just zapped into view. Teplo was with him.
"Hello, kids." Teplo greeted them with a smile. "We came to let you know that we're all invited to dinner at Saffa's house tonight. We're meeting there in an hour."
Boz wasn't paying attention to Teplo. He was still looking at Zann.
"What stone?" he said again. "Zann?"
Zann pulled out the stone. He explained how Wyssa had told him to pass it on to Boz. "Could it be a clue to where my parents are?" Zann asked.
Teplo leaned in for a look. One bushy eyebrow shot up in surprise. "Why, that's a—"
Zip ! A flash of energy shot from Boz's fingertips, sealing Teplo's lips shut. Teplo's eyes widened in surprise.
Boz turned to Zann. "Wyssa can't be trusted," he said grimly, plucking the stone from Zann's hand. "This stone means nothing."
"Hey! What are you doing?" Zann cried.
Zing glanced at his master and then at Boz. With a burst of smoke, the dragon leaped into the air.
"Oh!" Boz exclaimed as the little dragon flew at him, snatched the stone out of his hand, and swallowed it. "Give that back or you'll be sorry, you scaly scoundrel!"
Teplo put a hand on Boz's arm. He had already undone Boz's Lip-Zip spell.
"Settle down, old friend," Teplo said soothingly. "It won't do any harm to let the boy keep his souvenir, eh?"
Boz glared at Zing and sighed. "I suppose you're right," he said, straightening his clothes. "Come, Teplo. I promised the king I'd fetch those texts from the archives right away."
Teplo nodded and then glanced at the kids. "See you at Saffa's in an hour."
"We'll be there," Gliss promised.
"What was that all about?" Perda wondered after the two old men zapped away.
"I have no idea." Zann whistled for Zing.
The little dragon flew over and landed in front of him. Zing shot out a burst of flame. The stone tumbled out with it.

Zann grabbed the stone. "Ow!" he blurted out, juggling it from one hand to the other to keep it from burning his skin. "Extinguish!" he said, rubbing one leg against the other to create enough friction for the spell.
Instantly the stone felt cool in Zann's hand. Gliss leaned over to peer at it. "Hey, it doesn't look burned at all," she said.
"It must be fireproof," Darb said. "I wonder where it came from."
"Me too." Zann turned the stone over in his hand. "Teplo seemed to recognize it."
"So did Boz," Gliss said. "I can't believe he did a Lip-Zip spell on Teplo! He's lucky Teplo didn't get mad."
"Yeah," Perda said. "If they won't tell us about the stone, maybe we can try to research it on our own."

Zann sighed. "We can try. But we're running out of time. Once we're back in Swamp Bottom, it will be much harder to do anything." He leaned over and scratched Zing. "Anyway, thanks for getting the stone back for me, little buddy."
Honk ! Honk !
Zann jumped back as Teplo's sniffer goose leaped out the front door at him. "Quit it!" said Zann, dodging the goose's beak.
"Down, girl," Teplo added with a chuckle. "It's just us."

The goose backed down, but her beady little eyes were still trained on Zann. Zann ignored her as he followed Teplo, Boz, and Darb into the house. The four of them had just returned from that evening's dinner party, though Zann had been too distracted to enjoy himself much.
"Anyone care for a game of exploding dominoes?" Teplo rubbed his hands together to trade his party clothes for his usual robe and sandals.
"No thanks," Zann said. "I'm pretty tired. I think I'll go to bed."
"Me too," Darb said.
Zann and Darb headed upstairs to the guest room they were sharing. When the door shut behind them, Zann spun to face his friend.
"I can't stand this anymore," he blurted out. "I need to know what happened to my parents!"
"I understand," Darb said. "Maybe Boz—"
"Forget Boz!" Zann interrupted. "I need to come up with a plan to find my parents on my own." He paced back and forth. "Maybe I should just try jumping into a wormhole like I said before."
Bang ! A small explosion came from downstairs. Boz and Teplo were apparently playing dominoes.
"What?" Darb sounded alarmed. "Zann, that's crazy! It's no plan at all. You'll end up lost just like your parents!"
"Well, it would be better than doing nothing!" Zann stopped pacing and glared at his friend. "Morb and Wyssa both seem to think my parents are still out there somewhere in the vortex!"
Another domino exploded.
"I know," Darb said. "But you need help from someone who knows more about these things. Why don't you try talking to your grandfather again?"
Zann rolled his eyes. "Are you kidding? You saw how Boz reacted when he saw the stone."
Darb shrugged. "I think you just took him by surprise. Boz is a reasonable person, and he cares about you. Maybe if you ask nicely, he'll talk to you about what's going on."
"Do you really think so?" Zann was dubious. Boz hadn't seemed very reasonable when he'd snatched the stone earlier.
"It's worth a try," said Darb. "What have you got to lose?"
Zann hesitated. But finally he nodded. He trusted Darb's judgment.
"Okay," he said. "I'll talk to him."

Zann opened the door and headed for the stairs. At the top he took a deep breath to calm himself. The dominoes had stopped exploding, and he could hear Boz and Teplo talking quietly. Feeling curious, Zann leaned forward to listen.
". . . and that doesn't leave much time," Teplo was saying.
"Perhaps not," Boz replied. "But the plan is set. We leave First City tomorrow afternoon."
Zann gasped and backed away from the staircase. Tomorrow afternoon? It was too late to try to talk to Boz about the stone. Zann had to act now!
He hurried back to the guest room.
Darb looked surprised. "What happened?"
"Nothing. I, uh, decided I'm too tired to argue with Boz right now." Zann zapped himself into his pajamas and climbed into bed. "I'll talk to him tomorrow."
"Oh. Okay, good-night." Darb got into bed too.

Zann rubbed his fingers to extinguish the light. Then he lay in the dark, staring at the moonlit ceiling. He felt guilty about lying to his best friend. But Zann's plans had changed, and Darb definitely wouldn't approve of what Zann was going to do next.
Zann froze as Zing snorted and spurted out a puff of smoke. But the little dragon was only turning over in his sleep. Soon he was snoring in harmony with Darb once again.

Rubbing his fingers, Zann touched the note he'd just written. It disappeared, though he could still feel the paper under his fingers. He hoped he'd performed the Vanishing spell correctly. If he had, the note would reappear in exactly three hours.
He glanced at Darb's sleeping form, feeling guilty. The note explained where Zann was going and why—just in case he never made it back.

Zann tiptoed out of the room. Then he zapped himself to the palace. When he saw the hulking guard standing outside the main entrance, he realized he hadn't thought his plan through very well. Powerful Shield spells stopped people from zapping into the palace uninvited. How was he going to get inside?
Just then the guard looked up and spotted him. "Zann!" he exclaimed. "Is that really you? What an honor!"
"Oh," Zann said in surprise. "Um, thanks."
"Are the king and queen expecting you, or do you need me to wake them?" the guard asked. "Shall I show you to the throne room?"
Zann was amazed. At last his new celebrity status was coming in handy!
"Thanks, but I remember the way," he told the guard, trying to sound casual. "And you don't need to wake anybody."

Zann hurried inside. Only a few flickering candles lit the palace halls, but Zann had no trouble finding his way to the main courtyard. He shuddered as he glanced at the spot where Morb's monstrous magic-sucking machine had stood.
Then he headed toward a balcony jutting from the second floor. He levitated to it and stepped into the hallway beyond. Spotting the door he wanted, he opened it and stepped inside.
"Oops," he whispered as he looked around. He was in a bedroom he'd never seen before. A stout older man was snoring. Luckily the man didn't wake up as Zann quickly backed out of the room.
Zann glanced up and down the hall. Okay, if that wasn't the right door, then surely it was the next one down . . .
But the second door he opened revealed only a linen closet. And the third opened onto a deserted dining room.

Zann stood in the hallway, trying to figure out why he couldn't find the room he wanted. "This is stupid," he muttered. Rubbing his hands together, he took a moment to focus his mind. "Zap," he whispered.

He landed in a storage room. He smiled, sure he'd finally found the right room. But Zann's smile faded as he realized the room's window overlooked the aviary in the palace menagerie. This wasn't the right storage room. It wasn't even in the same part of the palace.
"Drat," he muttered. Zann carefully pictured the right storage room in his mind. "Zap!"
This time he landed in the palace library. He zapped again and ended up in the banquet hall.
"Zann?" a familiar voice said. "What are you doing here?"
Zann spun around. Yog sat at the table in his pajamas, feasting on wiggle root pie.
"Yog!" Zann exclaimed. "Um, hi. I just came to, uh . . ." He thought fast. "To get something Boz left here earlier. But Boz said it was near the wormhole, and I can't seem to find the right room."

Yog looked surprised. "Didn't Boz warn you that you wouldn't be able to get to it? The Red Council didn't like having a wormhole inside the palace. Anyone or anything could wander through from another world."
Zann was confused. "Then why didn't they do something about it sooner?" he asked.
"You know how wormholes work," said Yog. "They can appear or disappear at random. We didn't know that one was in the palace until Morb used it."
"Are the king and queen afraid that Morb might try to come back?" Zann asked.

"I doubt it," Yog said. "Once you destroyed Morb's magic-sucking machine, he went back to being a Void, remember? It takes powerful magic to navigate the vortex connecting the wormholes. Morb will probably be lost forever."
Zann thought anxiously of his parents. Were they still lost in the vortex, just like Morb?
Thinking of them brought Zann's mind back to his quest. "So what happened?" he asked. "Did the Red Council close up the wormhole, or blow it up or something?"

Yog shook his head. "Even the strongest magic can't destroy a wormhole," he explained. "All the Magic Masters joined together to block it off with a special Repel spell paired with an extra-strong Containment spell."
"So that's what Boz and Teplo were doing here at the palace all day," Zann said.
"Right," Yog said, taking another bite of his pie.
"Okay. I should get home," Zann said. "See you later."
He zapped himself out of the palace and stood in the moonlit courtyard outside, feeling frustrated. Now what?
With the palace wormhole blocked, there was only one other option. Before he had time to get nervous, Zann muttered, "Zap!"

Wormwood was a scary place at night. Moonlight shone through the branches of the gnarled old tree, casting spooky shadows over the ramshackle huts. Strange smells and stranger sounds drifted on the night breeze. Doing his best to ignore the creepy atmosphere, Zann stepped toward the tree's massive trunk.
The wormhole opened, and Zann stared into its spinning, pulsating depths, feeling terrified and dizzy. Could he do this?
Zann thought of his parents and knew he had to try. Holding his breath, he stuck one leg into the wormhole. A second later he felt the vortex's powerful energy pulling him in.
"Zann! Stop!"
A sudden blast of energy grabbed Zann's body, flinging him back. He landed hard on the ground, several yards from the wormhole. When he looked up, the wormhole was spinning shut.
A moment later Boz was hauling him up by the arm. The old man's face was livid.
"What were you thinking?" Boz shouted, his long nose quivering with rage. "Have you gone mad, boy?"
"How did you—" Zann didn't get a chance to finish the question. Boz snapped his fingers and zapped them both away.
They landed in Teplo's living room. "You got him in time!" Gliss cried. "Thank goodness!"
Zann ducked as Zing flew at him, blasting him with angry flames. "Quit it," Zann muttered. Glancing around, he saw Perda, Darb, and Teplo staring at him. "What's going on?"
"Zing woke up and realized you were gone," Darb said. "He freaked out and rushed to find me."
Zann scowled at the dragon. Then he realized what Darb had said. "Wait," said Zann. "What do you mean, he rushed to find you? You were in the same room."
"Not exactly." Darb's face went red. "Um, I promised Gliss I'd meet her after midnight. I guess I didn't notice you were gone when I woke up and sneaked out."
Zann looked at Gliss. She was blushing too. "I had something important to tell him," she said. "I'm leaving First City tomorrow."

Zann just shrugged, thinking of what he'd overheard earlier. He wasn't surprised that Gliss was leaving for Swamp Bottom tomorrow too. Her parents and her uncle had been involved in the same meetings as Boz.
"Whatever you say," he said with a smirk. "I think Darb would have figured out you'd left First City when he saw you in Swamp Bottom tomorrow with the rest of us."
"Huh?" Darb looked confused. "No, you don't understand. Gliss isn't going back to Swamp Bottom. She's going on an expedition to the Cave of the Unknown."
"What?" Zann whirled toward Gliss. "The Cave of the Unknown," he repeated. "Are you serious? Why are you going there?"

The Cave of the Unknown was a remote and dangerous place. Few people had seen it, and even fewer had survived to describe it. Zann's parents were among those few. They had visited the Cave a couple of times, returning with many frightening stories about it.
Staring at the floor, Gliss shrugged. "My parents are making me go."
Zann hardly heard her. He was still thinking about all the stories he'd heard during his childhood.

"My parents said the Cave of the Unknown is huge and really spooky, with countless tunnels and chambers," he said. "The whole place is littered with ancient relics and manuscripts from the Old Times and stuff."
"Yeah. Like the relics and texts Morb used to try to take over Magica," Perda said with a shudder.

"Exactly. That's why the Red Council decided it's time to seal the place off," Teplo put in. "Until now they've relied on the Cave's reputation to keep people away. But after Morb's recent adventures, they don't want anyone else coming along and trying the same thing. The Council is sending an expedition to seal it off so the relics can't be removed."

Boz didn't seem to be paying much attention to the conversation. His nose quivering wildly, he was still glaring at Zann. Zann recognized that look. It meant his grandfather was thinking hard. He was probably trying to come up with the perfect way to punish Zann for sneaking out tonight.
Boz spoke out at last. "Enough about the expedition. We were discussing Zann's outrageous behavior."
Zann cringed. Then he looked over at Darb. "So you saw I was missing and ran to tell Boz?" he asked. "I never thought you were the type to tell on your friends."

"That's not what happened," Gliss said. "When Darb and I realized you were missing, we checked with Perda. She didn't know where you were, but she tried all your passwords and was eventually able to make your note appear."

"I can't believe you didn't tell me you were going, Zann," Perda added. Her eyes flashed with anger, and her voice was cool and unfriendly. Zann hated having her look at him that way. He wished he could make her understand why he’d tried to go through the wormhole without telling his friends. But he wasn't sure how to communicate that.
"Gliss came to us right away, thank goodness," Teplo said. "Since we knew you wouldn't be able to reach the palace wormhole, Boz guessed you might try the one in Wormwood."
Zann glared at Gliss. " You ratted me out? I thought we were friends!"
"We are," Gliss said, looking hurt. "I was trying to help you."
" Help me?" Zann gritted his teeth, furious. "I helped you to reunite with your parents, remember? All you did tonight was stop me from doing the same thing!"
"No," Darb said. "She stopped you from disappearing forever."
"That's right, Zann." Boz sounded disapproving. He glanced at Teplo. "I'm starting to think it's a mistake to let Zann come along when we leave tomorrow."
"You mean you might not take me back to Swamp Bottom?" Zann rolled his eyes. That didn't sound like much of a punishment to him.
"Swamp Bottom? Who's going to Swamp Bottom?" Boz asked.
"We are," Zann said. "I heard you two talking about it earlier. You said we leave tomorrow afternoon."
"Yes, we do," Teplo said. "But not for Swamp Bottom. Your grandfather and I are part of the expedition Gliss mentioned. That means you're part of it too."
Boz nodded. "That's right, Zann. You're going to the Cave of the Unknown."
"Gliss doesn't seem very excited about the expedition," Zann said to Boz the next day. They were at Teplo's house, preparing to depart. "Why are her parents making her go?"
"Her uncle Gar is an important member of the expedition," Boz said. "Gliss' parents thought this would be a good educational opportunity for her."
Zann didn't believe it. He wondered if Gliss' parents were trying to push her and Zann together again. They probably weren't happy that she had become so close to Darb, a Void.
Teplo rushed in, his goose snapping irritably at his heels. "Ready to go?" Teplo asked.
"Ready." Boz grabbed Zann by the elbow and snapped his fingers. Zann barely had time to grab Zing before his grandfather zapped them away.
They landed on a grassy lawn, in front of an ancient stone mansion. Beyond was deep forest.
"Where are we?" Zann spotted a large ship. A heap of colorful fabric was attached to it by a number of heavy ropes. "And what's that ?"
"This place is called Moonstone Manor," Teplo said, appearing beside them. "And that's the airship that will transport us to the Cave."
Zann was surprised. "I know people can't just zap to the Cave of the Unknown because of its weird energy—"
"Correct," Teplo interrupted. "The Cave, as well as the relics inside, constantly sends out destabilizing surges. It makes performing any magic near the Cave very dangerous."
"But I didn't know there was a special airship," Zann continued. "I assumed we'd fly there on dragons or something."
"The Cave's unstable energy frightens most creatures," someone said. It was Venna. "Even the best-trained riding dragons usually refuse to fly anywhere near it."
Venna was representing the Red Council on the expedition. Beside her was a tall, handsome man. Venna introduced him as Tok, the airship's pilot. She turned to Zann.
"This vehicle is the traditional way of traveling to the Cave of the Unknown," she said. "Come inside and have a look."
The airship's main room looked like someone's living room. Tok led the way down a hallway and into another room.

Three large, vicious-looking creatures with fiery red scales were writhing in a tank of thick glass. When Zann and the others entered, the creatures spit balls of flame at them. Zann jumped back, and Zing cowered behind him. But the flames didn't penetrate the glass wall.
"Are those dragons?" Zann asked. "I've never seen any like that!"
"They're known as flame furies," Teplo explained. "They originally came from another world."

"And many years ago," said Boz, "several young furies were smuggled into Magica. They've been breeding in the darkest reaches of the forest beyond Mount Mystery ever since. Few people know they exist."

Venna nodded. "The original owner of this manor caught these three furies and found a way to harness their fiery power to travel to the Cave." She swept a hand at the vehicle. "He called it the Dragon Wagon."
Zann stared at the fierce creatures. He wished Darb could be there to see them. Darb loved learning about new magical creatures!

"When we're ready to go," Tok explained, "we'll release an image of the snuffer, which is the furies' natural enemy from their home world. The furies will blast it with their flaming breath until the image is removed."
"Or until the image is so singed that the furies realize it's not real," Teplo said.
"Indeed." Tok chuckled. "We have to replace the fake snuffer for each journey."

Zann wondered what kind of terrifying creature could scare the furies. Before he could ask, several other people entered, including Gliss and her uncle. Uncle Gar greeted everyone cheerfully, but Gliss looked glum. Zann could tell she wasn't thrilled to be there.
"Let's get started," said Venna. "We have a long journey ahead."
Tok nodded. "Snuffer up."
A metal sculpture popped into view at the back of the furies' tank. " That's a snuffer?" Zann exclaimed. "There's one of those on my parents' storage shelf at the lab!"
"That makes sense," Teplo said. "Their last journey was to the Cave. Well, second-to-last."
The airship shuddered and lifted. "You should go sit down," Tok said to the group. "It can be tricky keeping your balance when the airship takes off."
The furies' fiery breath quickly filled the Dragon Wagon's cloth balloon. Soon the airship was flying over the treetops. Zann spent the first hour of the journey peering out the window.
Then Gliss' uncle called Zann's name. "You kids don't have to sit here with us boring old people," he said with a wink. "Why don't you two explore the rest of the ship together?"
Zann forced a smile. He didn't want the adults to know that he and Gliss weren't on good terms. "Sure. Let's go, Gliss."
They headed into the hallway leading to the furies' tank. "Are you still mad at me?" Gliss asked tentatively.
"You know how important finding my parents is to me." He glared at her. "At least you should know."
"Zann—" Gliss began.
Zing interrupted her with an excited squawk. The little dragon rushed forward.
"Zing, leave the furies alone," Zann said. "They'll roast you alive!"

But Zing wasn't heading for the tank. He was scratching at a large feed bin. The expedition leaders had packed plenty of food for humans and dragons alike, since it was risky to conjure anything near the Cave.
"Is he hungry?" Gliss wondered.
Zann hurried over to the bin. "I guess Tok wouldn't mind if Zing had a snack." He swung open the top and gasped in shock. Perda and Darb were crouched inside!
"Surprise!" Perda stood up. "We didn't want to miss all the fun!"
A few minutes later, the kids were in the main room facing the adults. Venna glared at the stowaways. "This is outrageous! The expedition is supposed to be top secret."
"Does that mean we have to turn back?" Gliss sounded almost hopeful.
"If so, the furies will have to rest for a few days before departing again," Tok warned.

"Impossible." Venna frowned. "The king and queen won't appreciate any delay. Besides, there's no need to turn back. These kids can zap themselves home. We aren't close enough to the Cave yet to interfere with their magic."
"No zapping," Tok said. "The furies will sense that level of magic. They'll get distracted and crash."
Zann gulped. Tok had warned them earlier about not using any major magic during the journey. Now he understood why.
"Perda and Darb will have to come with us then." Teplo glanced at Tok. "Is it safe to summon a message moth? We should let their parents know they're with us."
"Yes, that minor sort of magic should be okay," Tok said.
"We can't use magic?" Perda whispered to Zann. "It's like Morb is back again!"
"Don't say that." Zann shuddered. "Let's explore the rest of the ship."
"Prepare for landing!" Tok called out.

Zann peered out the window. It was the next morning, and the sky was streaked with the remnants of sunrise. Below lay a vast desert littered with rocks and blowing red sand. Swirls of energy spurted out of a jagged opening, which looked like a mouth full of teeth.
"The Cave of the Unknown," Zann whispered. After hearing his parents talk about the place all his life, he was really here!
As the group exited the aircraft, Tok warned everyone not to use magic in or around the Cave. "We've got something to help you. I'll fetch it now."

"This place is amazing!" Perda said, staring at the cave opening in front of them. "Maybe we'll see some of the famous relics we learned about in school. Like the Mask of Zanta, or even the Horn of the Otherworld."
Gliss shivered. "I'm not going in there. What if we get lost? We won't be able to use magic to find our way out."
Teplo heard her. "Don't worry, that's what cave crawlers are for."
"Cave crawlers?" Perda echoed.
"Yes. Here they are." Tok had just returned, carrying a wire cage. Inside were a dozen large rodents with pale fur, long tails, and huge, glowing eyes.
"Yuck!" Gliss said. "They look like swamp rats!"

"You'll each get one," Tok said. "They're native to this area, so they know how to avoid the Cave's energy bursts. The glowworms they eat give their bodies a natural glow you can use as a light. And no matter how lost you get, your crawler can find the way out of the Cave."
He set down the cage. Zing lunged toward it, shooting flames.
"Zing, no!" said Zann, grabbing the dragon. He looked at Tok. "Sorry, I guess he thinks they're food. I hope he didn't scare them."
"Once your crawler bonds to you, nothing will scare it off," Tok said. "Be careful not to let Zing actually catch one though."
Tok placed a crawler on Zann's shoulder and muttered a quick spell. Even that little bit of magic made the energy storms intensify.
"There," said Tok. "This crawler is bonded to you now."
The crawler dug its claws into Zann's shoulder and chirped nervously at Zing, who was watching it intently. Meanwhile Tok bonded crawlers to each of the other members of the group.
"All right, everyone," Venna called out. "We'll begin by locating and cataloging each relic. I've drawn a diagram of the Cave based on the ancient texts and divided it into several sections."
Venna continued to talk, but Zann stopped listening. "How can she make something as exciting as exploring the Cave of the Unknown sound so boring?" he whispered to his friends.
He wondered what his parents' last journey to the Cave had been like. He stuck his hand into his pocket and touched the stone. To his surprise, it felt warm.
"Weird," he muttered.
"What?" Perda asked.
"Nothing." Zann shivered as he took a step toward the gaping cave mouth. "Let's go in."
The kids spent the next hour exploring the Cave. Sounds echoed off the cold rock walls. Tiny, strange creatures scurried through the shadows.
"Oops!" Perda blurted out as they crossed a large, shadowy chamber.
"What's wrong?" Zann asked.
"I tripped over a rock or something." Perda leaned down. "Actually, it looks like another relic."
Gliss gasped. "Not just any relic. I think it's the Horn of the Otherworld!"
"Careful!" Darb said. "Don't touch—whoa!" He skidded on some loose stones and fell.
"Darb! Are you okay?" Gliss cried.
"Sure. I just skinned my knee."
Gliss hurried over. "Let me see." She rubbed her fingers to do a Healing spell.
"No magic!" Zann shouted.
It was too late. Energy crackled from Gliss' fingertips, and the Horn lit up. Zann felt the air sizzle.
Zap !
"Ow!" he exclaimed, landing hard in a different tunnel. A second later his friends landed beside him.
"What happened?" Gliss cried.
"You used magic," Perda said. "The Horn must have zapped us away!"
"Where are we?" Gliss sounded panicky.
"Don't worry," Darb said. "Our crawlers can find the way out."
Zann cocked his head. "Maybe they won't have to. I hear someone talking. We must have landed near the entrance."
He hurried in the direction of the voice. It was coming from the next chamber.
"Hello," Zann called as he entered the chamber. "We—"
Zann took one look at the speaker and gasped.
It was Morb!
Zann's heart pounded with terror. What was Morb doing here? He was supposed to be lost in the vortex!
Zann listened as Morb continued to speak. ". . . and I require a few key ingredients before my new masterpiece is complete." His face twisted into an evil grin.
"Zann?" Perda's voice sounded very loud as she came up behind him. "Did you find the—?"
"Shh," said Zann. He braced himself, waiting for Morb to turn and spot them. But Morb kept facing the same direction.
Perda had spotted Morb by now too. "Whoa!" she whispered. Then she frowned. "Wait—he's glowing."
Zann stared at the figure. He realized Perda was right. Morb was glowing from within, just like their cave crawlers.
Gliss, Darb, and Zing appeared. "What's going on?" Darb asked.
"It's a hologram, I think." Zann picked up a pebble and tossed it at Morb. It passed right through the villain.
The Morb hologram was still talking. ". . . and then Magica shall be mine!" he cried. "See that you don't fail me."
The image blinked out of sight. A second later it blinked back on. "Good day," Morb began. "I have need of your services once again . . ."
"It must be a message for someone," Perda guessed. "Maybe Wyssa?"
Zann nodded. "An old message. It's probably been playing over and over again for months."
Gliss shuddered. "Creepy."
"Yeah." Zann took a step closer. Even though he knew the image wasn't real, it made him nervous.
His foot hit something that skittered across the stone floor. "What was that?" Darb asked.
Zann bent to see. "A stone. It looks just like mine!"
"Look." Gliss pointed. "There are lots more!"
The glow of the crawlers showed dozens of identical stones scattered across the chamber floor. Then Zann noticed something glowing and vibrating in the wall nearby.
"Hey, there's one stuck in the wall." He touched the stone, which felt warm. When he tugged on it, it popped out. The hologram instantly vanished.
"Oh!" Perda said. "The stone must contain the message!"
Gliss' eyes widened. "Maybe that's why we landed here," she said. "Zann's stone might have led us to this spot when the relic zapped us away."
Zann couldn't speak for a second. What if the stone Wyssa had given him held a message from his parents? He stuck his hand in his pocket and gasped. His stone was so hot it almost burned his hand.
"Let's try plugging mine into that hole," he said, his voice shaking.
He stepped toward the hole in the wall. But he hesitated when he heard the clatter of footsteps. A second later Tok burst into the chamber.
"There you are!" the pilot said breathlessly. "We felt a huge disruption in energy a few minutes ago, and we were worried about you. What happened?"
"Nothing," Darb said quickly. "We just, uh, tripped over a relic."
Zann shot a look at Gliss, who looked guilty. But Tok didn't seem to notice.
"You must be careful," Tok said with a frown. "The Cave is a dangerous place. Anyway, you kids need to come back with me. We're planning to seal off this section of the Cave shortly."
"What?" Zann blurted out. "But I need to—"
Tok didn't let him finish. "No arguments," he said briskly. "Everyone needs to get out of the Cave before the Magic Masters get to work."
"What do we do now?" Perda wondered, staring at the cave entrance.
Zann didn't answer. He was still angry that Tok had dragged the kids outside. It wasn't fair! What if that stone held a message from Zann's parents?
"We have to get back in there," he muttered.
Darb glanced over. "How? Tok's guarding the entrance."
Zann spotted Teplo nearby. "I'll be right back."
He hurried over to the Magic Master, checking to be sure that Boz wasn't around. When Zann described what had happened, Teplo looked guilty.
"You're right, Zann," Teplo said. "It's a message stone. I recognized it right away."
"Why didn't Boz let you tell me that?" Zann asked.
Teplo hesitated and then said, "He's trying to protect you. Besides, I doubt that stone has anything to do with you or your parents."
"But Wyssa said—"
"You can't trust anything that otherworldly old woman says," Teplo said.
Before Zann could respond, Boz let out a shout and appeared near the cave entrance.
"Oh dear, he doesn't look happy," Teplo muttered, hurrying off.
Zann saw little choice but to follow. "What's going on?" he asked his friends, who were at the edge of the group gathering around Boz.
"I'm not sure," Gliss whispered. "It sounds like some of the relics are missing."
"Are you sure about this, Boz?" someone called out. "It's possible that Morb stole some relics that we don't know about."
Boz's nose quivered with dismay. "Yes, that's possible. But I saw the Mask of Zanta myself an hour ago. When I went back a few minutes ago, it was gone!"
"The Dragontamer's Charm is missing too," said Uncle Gar. "I cataloged it earlier. Some minor relics from the same cavern have disappeared as well."
"We'll have to postpone the Sealing spell," Teplo said with a frown. "We need to get everyone else back here and make sure the relics weren't moved by one of us."
"I'll get Venna," Tok said. "I think she's in the airship."
Zann backed away. Zing followed, though Zann's friends were watching the adults and didn't notice his and Zing's departure.
"Good," thought Zann. He didn't want to get his friends in trouble for what he was about to do. This could be his only chance to play the message on his stone.
"Quiet, Zing," he whispered. "We're going back in."
Zann tiptoed through a small cavern and into another tunnel. "I think the intersection is just ahead," he whispered to Zing.
Zing breathed out a small flame, allowing Zann to see a little farther than the crawler's feeble glow permitted. There was no intersection—just a blank stone wall.
"Drat," Zann muttered.
He retraced his steps and tried a different tunnel. Why hadn't he paid more attention when Tok was leading them out earlier?
"Never mind," Zann whispered. At least he'd managed to sneak away undetected.
Or had he? Zann froze as he heard a soft scraping sound behind him. It echoed down the tunnel, barely louder than a heartbeat.
"Did you hear that?" he whispered to Zing.

But apparently Zing hadn't heard the sound. The dragon was staring at Zann's crawler hungrily. Zann sighed. Being in the creepy cave was making him jumpy. The sound had probably been nothing more than a cave creature or a stray burst of magic energy. Zann kept moving, watching for anything that looked familiar.
Clink!
Zann froze. Was that a footstep?
"Quiet!" he hissed, dragging Zing into a crevasse in the wall.

He pressed both hands over his crawler, trying to block its light. Zing's breath felt hot on Zann's leg, but Zann didn't dare move. The footsteps came closer. Soon Zann could hear the sound of breathing.
He pressed himself back against the stone and watched. A figure passed, lit only by the soft glow of the crawler perched on its shoulder.
"Perda!" Zann blurted out.
Perda jumped in surprise and spun to face him. "Zann! I was afraid I'd lost you."
Zann frowned. "You were following me?"
"Of course." Perda laughed. "You didn't think you could sneak off and have another adventure without me, did you?"
"But I was sure nobody saw me leave," said Zann.

"You're right. I didn't notice you were gone for a few minutes. I used my crawler to track you." Perda pointed to her crawler, which was keeping a wary eye on Zing. "I'd already noticed it gets more and more nervous the closer we are to Zing. All I had to do was pay attention to how deeply its claws were digging into my shoulder to guess how close you were."
Zann rolled his eyes. At the same time, he had to admire Perda's cleverness.
"You have to go back," he told her. "It's too risky. Besides, maybe you can figure out a way to delay the Sealing spell until I'm finished."
"Don't worry about that," Perda said. "The adults will be arguing for a while yet. Venna showed up right after you disappeared. She admitted to taking the relics. Most of them anyway."
Zann was stunned. "Venna took the relics? Why?"

"She doesn't think it's right to seal off the Cave and all the powerful magic in the relics. She thinks we should take some of the relics back to First City. That way the Red Council can use them in case a threat like Morb ever comes along again."
"Wow." Zann knew how persuasive Venna could be. "Does anyone agree with her?"
"A few people." Perda shrugged. "Not Boz and Teplo, though. They'll all be arguing about it for a long time."
"Good," Zann said. "That will give me enough time to find the message chamber."

"You mean it'll give us enough time," Perda said. "If you don't let me come, you'll never get there. You've been going the wrong way for the past ten minutes. Fortunately I remember how to get there. It's back this way." Perda quickly headed down the tunnel.
Zann hurried to keep up with her. He was still annoyed that she'd followed him. But another part of him was glad to have her help.
Half an hour later, they stepped into the message chamber.
"Hurry," Perda urged. "Who knows how long we have until they start the Sealing spell. Then we'll be trapped in here forever."
Zann’s stone was still burning hot. He took a deep breath and plugged it into the wall.
"Oh!" he gasped as two figures appeared before him.
"Is that your parents?" Perda whispered.
Zann just nodded, taking in the sight.
"Greetings, Wyssa," his father's familiar voice said. "We received your last message."
"We accept your terms," Zann's mother added. "We're very eager to locate World X. If you're sure you can lead us there, we'll pay your fee."
Zann's father nodded. "We've just returned from the Cave of the Unknown and have one more short trip to make. We'll contact you when we return."
Zann was so overwhelmed he could barely move. His parents' holograms flickered out and then reappeared.
"Greetings, Wyssa . . . " the message began again.
"Wow," Perda said. "I—ouch!" She poked her crawler. It was trembling.
Zann realized his own crawler was digging its claws into his shoulder. "What's the matter with the crawlers?" he mumbled, still watching his parents.
"They seem nervous," said Perda. "And Zing isn't even trying to eat them right now."
The entire chamber shuddered. The message stone popped out of the wall, cutting off the hologram.
"Uh-oh," Perda said. "Did you feel that? The Magic Masters must be starting the Sealing spell. We have to get out of here!"
Zann didn't want to leave. He wanted to plug the stone back in and watch his parents' message again and again.
There was another rumble. Zing let out a squeak. Zann's crawler moaned with fear.
"Okay, let's go," Zann said.
With Zing flying ahead of her, Perda ran for the exit. Zann started to follow. Suddenly he paused.
Turning, he raced over and grabbed the message stone off the floor. Then he sprinted after Zing and Perda.
"I still can't believe nobody saw you guys sneaking out of the Cave earlier," Darb said.
Zann and his friends were sitting at the campsite, a little apart from the adults. Dinner had ended an hour ago, and people were beginning to crawl into their tents for the night.
Gliss nodded. "You're lucky you escaped in time. Why'd you pull such a risky stunt, anyway?"
Zann shot her a look. "I wanted to see my parents any way I could, since somebody stopped me from searching for them through the wormhole."
Gliss turned away, stung by Zann's remark.
"Zann, that was mean!" Perda whispered. Darb just frowned.

Zann felt a twinge of guilt, though he didn't say anything. He knew Gliss was right. He, Perda, and Zing had barely made it out of range before the Sealing spell had blocked off that section of the Cave.
"I didn't expect Venna to give in so quickly," Perda said. "I thought we'd have more time in the Cave."
Darb shrugged. "What could she do? She got outvoted."

Zann didn't pay much attention as the others continued to discuss the matter. Venna had turned over the relics she'd collected to Tok. He was supposed to take them deep into an unsealed section of the Cave tonight. Then that section would be sealed off in the morning.

Seeing his parents' message had left Zann feeling restless. Could the reference to World X, whatever that was, be a clue? His parents had sounded eager to find the place. Would they have tried to find their way there, knowing they might not make it back to Magica?
Zann was still surprised that his parents had known Wyssa. Why hadn't Wyssa told him that? Maybe Teplo was right—maybe Zann couldn't trust anything she said.
"It doesn't matter," he thought. "I can't search for my parents way out here in the middle of nowhere. And we'll probably head right back to Swamp Bottom once the Cave is sealed."
He sighed with frustration and then stood up. "I'm tired," he told his friends. "I'm going to sleep."
Zann woke abruptly from a confusing dream about his parents. All he could remember was swirling magic and a strong sense of danger.
He sat up and looked around. The camp was dark and still. He'd been asleep for hours.
At first Zann assumed the dream had awakened him. Then he heard a rustle in the scrubby trees at the edge of the camp.
"Zing?" he whispered. "Leave the crawlers alone!"
He heard a soft snore from his other side. Glancing that way, he saw Zing sound asleep, cuddled against Darb's side. The crawlers were also asleep, perched on the highest branches of the trees.
The rustle came again, and was followed by the sound of voices. Curious, Zann got up and tiptoed toward the sound.
Parting the tree branches, he saw Venna and Tok walking away from the campsite together. Their voices were low and urgent. Zann strained his ears to hear.
". . . so I've come up with a new plan," Venna was saying. "I know how to get those relics back to First City after all."
Tok stopped and turned to face Venna. Zann crouched lower behind the trees, hoping the adults wouldn't spot him.
"You do?" Tok said. "How? If you try to smuggle them aboard the Dragon Wagon, the furies will go crazy."
Zann could barely believe his ears. Venna hadn't given in after all. And apparently Tok was working with her.
"That's not my plan," Venna told Tok. "You'll be taking the relics into the Cave, as everyone expects. But you won't be leaving them there."
"What?" Tok sounded confused.

"You'll be taking those relics straight back to the capital—through the wormhole I discovered today!" Venna explained quickly. "It's deep within the western arm of the Cave. It must be a new one—I don't think anyone else in Magica knows about it."
Zann was stunned. There was a wormhole in the Cave?
"You're crazy!" Tok exclaimed. "Take some of the most powerful relics in Magica through a wormhole? That's much more dangerous than what I signed up for!"
"I never expected you to lose your nerve," Venna snapped. "After all, this isn't your first time through a wormhole!"
"True," Tok said. "But the other wormholes weren't inside the Cave of the Unknown! Wormholes, especially new ones, are unstable enough without adding the Cave's unpredictable energy."

"We have to do this, Tok," said Venna. "The very future of Magica might depend on it!" She clenched her fists. "Those old fools think they're doing the right thing here. But what if another villain like Morb appears one day? What if a wormhole opens up right in the middle of the palace square and lets something even worse through? Magica would be helpless!"

Tok didn't seem convinced. "We have plenty of magic at our disposal even without those relics. Boz and the others don't think it's worth the risk of having such unpredictable energy around. Let alone the risk of trying to take relics through a wormhole." He shook his head. "I'm sorry, Venna. I know you believe you're doing the right thing for Magica. But you'll have to do it without me. I'm out."
He turned and strode back toward camp. Zann ducked aside just in time to avoid being seen.
"Aargh!" Venna cried. She stormed off into the darkness in the opposite direction.

Still in shock, Zann sat where he was for a moment. After seeing his parents' message—and the clue about World X—he was more eager than ever to go looking for them. And now he knew there was a wormhole somewhere in the Cave!
Zann's mind whirled as he finally got up to follow Venna. For a moment he thought he'd lost her—he couldn't hear or see her anywhere. Then he heard the soft clang of the airship door opening.
As he neared the airship, Zann saw that the door was standing open. He crept closer and peered in. Venna was inside with her back to him. She was pulling things out of a box. The relics!

Zann watched as Venna gathered them into a large sack. He recognized a few of the relics—the Horn of the Otherworld, a scary-looking skull mask he guessed was the Mask of Zanta, and several others he'd studied in school.
"Wow," he whispered. His teachers said the Horn alone held enough power to control all of Magica!
Venna slung the sack over her shoulder and then hurried toward the Cave.

Zann wasn't sure what to do. It seemed Venna was planning to take the relics through the wormhole herself. If Zann followed her, she'd lead him to the wormhole. He could hide until she went through it and then jump through. He'd be on his way to search for his parents within minutes.

But if he did that, he wouldn't have time to leave a message for Boz or his friends about Venna's plan. And what if Tok was right? What if the wormhole was too unstable to handle all those powerful relics passing through it? What if Venna accidentally blew up the entire cave and everyone nearby?
"Oh, man," Zann muttered.
He had to warn Boz and the others. It was the only responsible thing to do.
Zann turned and sprinted toward camp.
"Are we there yet?" Perda wondered breathlessly.

Zann and his friends were racing through a narrow tunnel behind Boz, Teplo, and several others. Magic energy was bouncing off the walls all around them. Despite the risks, the Magic Masters were using magic to lead them to Venna. Otherwise they were afraid they'd be too late to stop her.
"Venna!" Uncle Gar shouted. "Where are you?"
There was no answer. "This way," Boz said grimly, taking off down another tunnel.
Zann's crawler squeaked a warning, and Zann ducked just in time to avoid a burst of energy.
"Close one," Gliss exclaimed behind him.
Zann nodded and kept going.
They ran through one tunnel after another. Finally they all burst into a huge chamber dripping with stalactites. In the center stood Venna.
"Stop!" Boz cried. "Venna, this is madness!"
Venna glanced over her shoulder, looking surprised. "I don't care how risky it is," she cried. "I'm doing this for Magica!"
