Zann watched as Venna stepped forward and the wormhole swirled open. The edges flashed with silvery bursts of energy.
"Douse!" Boz cried, rubbing his hands.
"No!" Venna froze as the spell hit her. Without magic she couldn't go into the wormhole. She needed magic to navigate through the vortex.
"This is an outrage!" Venna ranted. "You can't douse me!"
"We'll remove the spell after you've listened to us," Teplo said. "I swear it. The final decision on what to do is yours."
Venna scowled. "Fine. Say your piece. My mind is made up."

"I don't think you comprehend the true risks," Boz said. "Those relics contain a stupendous amount of energy. Trying to take even one of them through this particular wormhole is a dangerous proposition. Taking them all—"
"You could blow us to bits!" Uncle Gar finished.
Venna blinked. "I . . . I never thought about that. But I can't let you seal off these relics forever. Magica must be able to defend itself. I'm doing this for all of us."
Teplo held out a hand to her. "If you feel that strongly, perhaps we can reopen the discussion. I won't speak for the others, but I'll listen to your arguments."
"Me too," Boz said. The others nodded.
Venna peered at them all suspiciously. Finally her expression softened.
"All right. You have a deal." She handed the sack to Teplo.
"Thank you." Teplo smiled at her and then pulled out the Horn of the Otherworld. "Magnificent," he murmured. He glanced at Boz. "Don't forget to remove the Dousing spell. Carefully."
"Oh, yes." Boz rubbed his fingers together.
At that moment all the crawlers let out a loud chirp.
"Careful!" Perda blurted out.
Friction sparked around Boz's fingers. A bolt of energy shot straight at the Horn of the Otherworld. The relic glowed and shuddered in Teplo's hand.
"Duck!" Teplo shouted.

Zann pressed himself against the wall as sparks shot from the horn. The wormhole glowed more brightly, and a tentacle of energy shot out. Venna screamed as the energy surrounded her. A second later the wormhole pulled her in, her scream still echoing off the chamber's walls.
"Venna!" Boz cried, but it was too late.
"Oh no!" Perda's face was white. "She was still under the Dousing spell!"
There was an ominous rumble. Chunks of stone rained down, and the entire chamber shook.
Tok gulped. "I think we just destabilized the Cave. Everybody run!"
"Too late!" Teplo dropped the sack of relics and grabbed Perda's hand. "Join hands—quickly!"
A small stalactite dropped and shattered at Zann's feet. "Hurry!" he shouted, grabbing Darb and Zing. Soon the entire group was holding hands.
" Zap !" shouted all the Magic Masters in unison.
Zann landed near the camp with the others just in time to see the entire cave collapse into a heap of rubble. He ducked as a stray bolt of energy shot over them. At first all he felt was relief.
Then his heart sank as he realized what this meant. He'd just lost another chance to search for his parents.

Zann's breath came in ragged gasps as he ran through the darkness. He could feel powerful magic swirling around him. He did his best to avoid the magic energy, but it wasn't easy. It was so dark he could barely see his hand in front of his face.

Where was he? What sort of place could be so dark and frightening? Could it be the Cave of the Unknown? Was he deep within its endless, winding tunnels? He touched his shoulder, but there was no crawler there to lead him out. He could be lost forever . . .
"No!" he shouted as panic overtook him.
He stumbled and almost fell, but he caught himself and kept running. He couldn't stop running. He had to find . . . to find . . .
"Zann?" a voice called. It sounded distant and faint.
Zann's heart jumped with hope. He knew that voice!
"Dad?" he shouted. "Where are you? Dad!"
Zann leaped forward to follow the voice. But someone grabbed his shoulder from behind. Zann felt the person's sharp, strong fingers tightening. Or were they claws?
"Ow!" he cried, struggling to free himself. "Let me go! I have to save my parents—they're in danger!"
But the hand only gripped more tightly.
"Zann!" the voice came again, sounding even fainter. "Zann!"
"Zann?"
Zann opened his eyes and saw his grandfather peering down at him.
"Boz?" he mumbled, squinting in the bright morning light.
Boz let go of Zann's shoulder. "Are you okay? You were shouting in your sleep."

Zann sat up and looked around. He was in his familiar bedroom in Swamp Bottom. Well, mostly familiar. Boz had rebuilt the house as soon as they'd returned from the capital the previous day. It looked almost the same as it had before Morb destroyed it. But a few things were different now. The kitchen was a little bigger. Some of the furniture was a new color or shape. The hole that Zing had once blasted in Zann's window was gone.
"Zann?" Boz sounded concerned. "Did you have a nightmare?"
"Yes," Zann mumbled. "I mean no, not really. Sort of."
Boz sighed, rubbing his long nose. "I'm afraid it was a mistake to take you to the Cave of the Unknown. Obviously it affected you. I'm sorry."
"I'm not sorry." Zann shrugged and swung his legs over the edge of the bed. "I'm glad I went."
He shot a look at the bedside table. The message stone was there, tucked behind a framed blink image of his parents.
Boz didn't notice the look. He seemed distracted. "I'll go and conjure some breakfast," he said. "Hurry and get dressed."
As Boz left the room, Zing scurried in. "Morning, little buddy," Zann said.
He stood up and glanced out the window. The grass had a purplish sheen, indicating that it had rained overnight. But the sun was bright and the aurora birds were singing.
"Nice day. Too bad I have to spend it here in Swamp Bottom," Zann muttered.

For a moment his dream came back to him. It reminded him of the dream he'd had outside the Cave of the Unknown. This latest dream had been scary and confusing, just like the previous one. But he'd felt so close to reaching his parents this time!
Those were just dreams though. How was he ever going to find his parents for real?
"It's hopeless as long as I'm stuck here," he told Zing. "I need to figure out how to get to one of those wormholes."
Zann rubbed his hands together and pictured his favorite outfit. A second later his pajamas disappeared, and he was fully dressed.

He stepped over to his dresser and picked up a comb. "I have to come up with a plan," he said. "I could probably make it to First City in five or six zaps if I really tried. Once I got there, I could rest for a while and then hop through that Wormwood wormhole."
Zing responded by shooting a small flame at Zann's leg. Zann glanced at the dragon and sighed.
"I know it's a crazy plan," he admitted. "But school starts again in a few days, and then I won't have time to do anything!"
He seemed no closer to finding his parents than he'd been before his adventures. It was almost as if none of them had ever happened.
When Zann reached the breakfast table, his grandfather was waiting for him. "Sit down, boy," Boz said, nodding toward a bowl of rice with glowberry sauce. "I want to talk to you about something."
Zann sat down and grabbed his food. "Um, okay," he said.

"Recent events have made me think about a few things," Boz said, rubbing his nose and staring at Zann solemnly. "You're growing up so fast, Zann. You remind me of your mother when she was your age. She always wanted excitement and adventure too . . ."
Zann kept his eyes on his food. His grandfather often lectured him about being too adventurous. But no matter what Boz said, Zann was never going to give up on finding his parents.
"I have to remember that you're not a child anymore," Boz went on. "It might be time to—"
Just then a message moth flapped in. It landed on Zann's arm.
"It's from Perda," said Zann, scanning the insect's wings. "She wants me to meet her in the swamp right away." He gulped down the last bite of rice and stood up.
"Wait a minute, Zann," Boz said. "I really think we need to talk."
"Can it wait until later?" Zann said. "I should find out what Perda wants."
As Boz sighed and nodded, Zann grabbed Zing and zapped out of the house.
"Ow—drat!" Zann said as he landed in a clawthorn bush.
"That's what you get for zapping in a hurry," Perda said with a laugh.
Zann pushed the prickly branches aside. He frowned when he saw that Perda wasn't alone. Darb and Gliss were with her.
"Hi, Zann," Gliss said as Zann climbed out of the bush. "Need help healing those scratches?"
"No, thanks." Zann wasn't ready to forgive Gliss yet. If she hadn't ratted him out to Boz, he might be searching for his parents right now instead of being stuck in Swamp Bottom!
"Um, okay." Gliss sounded tentative. "Listen, Zann. Can we talk for a second? I really want to—"
"Not now," Zann interrupted. "Perda's note sounded urgent." He turned toward Perda. "What's up?"
"I ran into Professor Huli this morning," Perda said. "I asked her about World X."
Professor Huli was the kids' Advanced Magic teacher. If anyone might know about World X, it was she.
"Really?" Zann said eagerly. "What did she say?"
Perda shrugged. "She's never heard of it."
Zann's heart sank. "Oh well. My parents' message made it sound like World X might be a newly discovered world. So it's no surprise if most people—even an Advanced Magic teacher—haven't heard of it."
"I don't understand," Darb said. "How is it possible World X was just discovered? I thought people have been everywhere through the vortex."

"No, definitely not," Perda said. "There are probably lots of worlds that haven't been discovered yet. Most worlds are actually really difficult to find. There isn't always a direct route from one place to another, and wormholes open and close all the time, which makes travel through them even more complicated."
Gliss nodded. "We just learned about all that in school."
"So if Zann's parents got knocked off course by that weird otherworld animal—" Darb glanced at Zann.
"A scatter beast," Zann said. "They're from a world called Fardark. My parents mentioned them in one of their books, but nobody knows much about them."
"Zann's parents could be anywhere," Perda continued. "For all we know, they're in World X right now!"
"Or maybe they're asking around about it while they're looking for a way back to Magica," Zann said. "It might be a clue, anyway. If I can get myself back into the vortex—"
"That reminds me," Perda interrupted. "You never told us about your trip with Wyssa. What was it like?"
"Well, I wasn't in the vortex for long . . ." Zann began. It was hard to describe the experience. But he did his best.
"Wow. I bet it was cool!" Perda looked impressed. "But it sounds like Wyssa did all the work. Do you think you could navigate through the vortex on your own?"
Zann shrugged. "I'll figure it out."
"What if you don't have enough magic?" Darb sounded worried. "You're only a kid."
"I'm a Red too." Zann touched his hair, trying to sound confident. "That should give me some extra power."
"It just sounds too dangerous, Zann," Gliss said.
Zann frowned. " Everything sounds too dangerous to you," he snapped. "Especially when it's my parents who are missing instead of yours!"
Gliss gasped, and tears came to her eyes. "I—I have to go," she mumbled. Snapping her fingers, she zapped out of sight.
"Zann!" Perda scowled at him. "That was mean!"
"Gliss was just worried about you," Darb added. He glanced at Perda. "Will you take me to check on her?"
"Sure." Perda grabbed Darb's hand. "Zap!"

They disappeared, leaving Zann alone with Zing. Zann felt guilty for hurting Gliss' feelings. But he did his best to shake off his guilt. In a few days he would be stuck at school. This could be his last chance to come up with a plan to find his parents. If his friends didn't want to help, he would do it on his own.

Two days later Zann was no closer to a plan. He'd researched the locations of all the known wormholes in Magica, but they were all far away from Swamp Bottom. Zapping to any of those wormholes would use up all his energy, leaving little or no energy to navigate through the vortex. He would have to rest for at least a day first. That would give Boz enough time to notice Zann was missing, figure out what was going on, and stop Zann from leaving Magica.

The day before school was due to start, Zann zapped to the swamp to meet Darb. Darb had stopped by earlier to set up a time and place to meet. But when Zann reached their meeting spot, nobody was there. That was surprising. Darb was almost always on time. Zann sat down to wait.
A moment later Gliss zapped into view. "Hi, Zann," she said.
Zann jumped to his feet. "What are you doing here?"
"I asked Darb to arrange to meet you so I could talk to you alone," Gliss said.
"You mean you asked him to help you trick me." Zann frowned.
"I'm sorry!" Gliss exclaimed. "But I've been trying to apologize, and you won't—"
Suddenly Perda zapped into view. "Zann!" she cried, her eyes wide and excited. "I've been looking for you! I need to talk to you—now!"
"No problem," said Zann before Perda had a chance to notice Gliss standing behind her. Grabbing Perda's hand, he said, "Zap!"
They landed in another part of the swamp. Perda looked confused. "Why did you zap us away?"
"Never mind," Zann said. "What did you want to talk about?"
"Oh!" Perda smiled. "Right. Listen to this—I just found a new wormhole. And it's right here in Swamp Bottom!"
"You found a wormhole?" Zann exclaimed. "In Swamp Bottom?"

"Uh-huh." Perda looked pleased with herself. "See, I've been practicing some spells since we got home. Mostly Seeking spells and a few others." She shrugged. "I've been thinking I might want to be an explorer someday, so I want to be ready."
Zann was surprised. Since when did Perda want to be an explorer?
But he didn't have time to think about that right now. "So what happened?" he asked. "How did you find the wormhole?"

"I was using the Seeking spell to find the strongest sources of magic in Swamp Bottom," Perda said. "Mostly the spell pointed me to the spots I expected—City Hall, your house, the spellstone quarry, places like that. But there was one source I couldn't identify. I went and checked it out, and that's when I found the wormhole."
"Wow!" Zann was impressed. Seeking spells were advanced magic—he didn't have any idea how to perform one himself. "And you're sure it's a wormhole?" he added.
"Of course I'm sure! It's small and kind of unstable-looking. It's probably brand-new, which is why nobody else has noticed it yet."
Zann's head spun. This changed everything!
"You have to show me," he said.
"I will." Perda smiled. "But only if you'll let me come with you."
"Come with me? You mean, through the wormhole?"
"Yes." Perda's eyes shone with excitement. "I want to see what the vortex is like. I want to help you search all those other worlds."
Zann shook his head. "I can't let you come. It's too dangerous!"
Perda folded her arms. "I don't care if it's dangerous. That's my deal. Take it or leave it."
Zann bit his lip. For a second he was tempted to agree to her deal. Perda was smart and brave and good at magic. It could be helpful to have her along.

Then Zann remembered all the adventures they'd been through together lately. No, he couldn't put Perda in that kind of danger again. This was his quest, and he should be the only one to take the risks.
Still, he couldn't pass up this chance to find a wormhole close to home.
"It's a deal," he said, trying to sound sincere. "You can come along."
"Cool!" Perda grinned.

Zann forced a smile, though he already felt guilty. He hated lying to Perda. And he knew she was going to be furious when she figured out that he'd tricked her. But what other choice did he have? He just had to hope that she would forgive him someday.
"Let's go check out the wormhole," he said.

"Right now?" She sounded surprised. "Shouldn't we gather some supplies first? Professor Huli says some other worlds don't have the same kind of magic we do. So we can't count on just creating anything we need, like food or extra clothes."
"Oh, we aren't going right now." Zann thought fast. "We should go tomorrow after school. That will give us plenty of time to gather supplies."
"Tomorrow?" Perda frowned. "Why not later today?"
"Um, well, it might take some time to find the supplies we need. We don't want to rush."
Perda didn't say anything for a second. Zann held his breath. He needed her to think they were really going tomorrow. That would give him plenty of time to sneak back to the wormhole later today.
"Okay, I guess that makes sense," she said at last. "We'll go tomorrow."
"Great. Now where is it?"

"It's this way." Perda zapped them both out of the swamp. They landed on the street a few blocks from Zann's house. From there they walked to a wooded area at the edge of town. In the middle of a small clearing was a ripple of magic energy. When Zann and Perda stepped closer, it opened into a wormhole!
"Wow," Zann said, staring at it.
It was small, just as Perda had said—much smaller than the ones in First City. The edges sparked and swirled wildly, and the opening changed size and shape every few seconds.
Zann jumped back as the wormhole let out a small burst of magic energy, sucking in some fallen leaves.
Perda took a step closer. "Are you sure you don't want to go today?"
"I'm sure," Zann said quickly. "Let's each pack a bag to take with us, and then hide the bags in the swamp. We can meet there after school tomorrow."
"Zann! Come here, please!" Boz called.
Zann was in his room stuffing things into a backpack. He shoved it under his bed and hurried out of the room. Boz was standing near the front door.
"What is it?" Zann tried to sound normal even though he was nervous. Could Boz have figured out what was going on?
But Boz looked distracted, as usual lately. "I have a meeting with the mayor," he said. "But I'll be home for dinner."
"Okay," Zann said. "I'll see you then."
"Good." Boz smiled at him. "We've both been so busy since returning from the capital that I feel I've hardly seen you. Perhaps we can finally have that talk this evening."
Boz zapped out of sight, and Zann slumped with relief. This could be his chance to go back to that wormhole. He just had one thing to do first.
"Come on, boy." Zann whistled for Zing. "Let's go see Darb."
Zing stared at him and let out a puff of smoke. But the dragon stayed where he was.
"What's wrong with you?" Zann said impatiently, grabbing Zing. "Let's go!"
Zann snapped his fingers and zapped out of the house. Once Zing was safe with Darb, there would be nothing standing in Zann's way.
When Zann arrived at the swamp, Darb was waiting. So was Gliss.

Zann was still mad at Gliss. But he tried not to let those feelings show. After today he might not see his friends for a long time. In fact, he might never see them again. He didn't want to leave on bad terms.
Gliss smiled uncertainly. "Hi, Zann."
"Hi, Gliss." Zann smiled back briefly. Then he turned toward Darb. "I need a favor. Can you watch Zing for a few hours?"
"Sure," Darb said. "Why? What's up?"
"Right before the trouble with Morb started, I told Professor Nurt I'd do some extra credit work for Food and Drink Creation class," Zann said. "I need to finish it before school starts tomorrow."
Gliss looked surprised. "I doubt Professor Nurt will care about that," she said. "Everyone knows you've been kind of busy."
Zann forced a laugh. "I know. But I still want to do it."
"Wow." Darb grinned. "Saving Magica must have changed you, Zann. You never cared that much about schoolwork before."

"Ha-ha, very funny." Zann was nervous. Were his friends suspicious? Maybe he should have thought of a different cover story. "Anyway, it will be easier to create puffberry soufflés without Zing there trying to eat them."
"No problem." Darb gave Zing a pat. "We'll have fun. Right, buddy?"
Usually Zing loved spending time with Darb. But today he ignored him, staying pressed against Zann's leg.
"What's wrong with him?" Gliss wondered.
"Nothing." Zann gave Zing a nudge. "Go with Darb, boy."
The dragon whined and emitted a puff of smoke. Zing refused to leave Zann's side even when Darb called him.

Finally Zann snapped his fingers and created a dragon harness. He slipped it onto Zing's scaly body and then handed the leash to Darb. "I'm sure he'll be fine once I'm gone. He's just annoyed because he knows he'll be missing all those soufflés."
Darb chuckled. "You're probably right." But he looked concerned as he glanced at Zing.
Zann didn't want to give his friends the chance to ask any more questions. "Thanks," he said. "See you in a few hours." He zapped home.

Soon he was stepping out of his room with his backpack strapped onto his shoulders. He reached into his pocket to make sure the message stone was there. As he touched its cool, hard surface, he shivered. What was he getting himself into?
But he couldn't lose his nerve now. After taking one last look around the house, Zann hurried outside.
He'd already decided to walk to the wormhole instead of zapping there. It wasn't far, and he would need all his energy for navigating the vortex.
Just as he reached the clearing, the wormhole let out a magical burp that rattled the branches of nearby trees and made Zann jump. Could he really do this?
"Yes," he whispered. "I have to do it."
Taking a deep breath, Zann stepped toward the wormhole. Its ragged mouth opened wider, and its chaotic energy reached out and began to suck him in.
"Zann!" someone shouted. It was Perda, and she sounded angry. "You didn't think you really tricked me with that pathetic story, did you?"
Zann tried to pull away from the wormhole. But its pull was too strong. "Perda, no! You have to get back!"
"No way." Perda rubbed her fingers together with one hand while she grabbed Zann's wrist with the other. A second later a glowing band of energy appeared, linking their wrists together.
"A Shackle spell?" Zann blurted out. "Where'd you learn to do that?"
"I'm full of surprises." She smirked, tugging at the magical shackles to test them. "Now you can't leave me behind!"
Zann gritted his teeth, trying again to escape the wormhole's pull. But it was no use. It was all he could do to stay where he was. He had to convince Perda to back off before she got sucked in too!
"Listen," he said. "I didn't want to lie to you, but—"
"Then why did you?" she shot back.
"Perda, I—" Before he could go on, Gliss burst into view.
"Oh no!" she cried as she saw the wormhole. "What are you two doing? Are you crazy?"
Zann glared at Perda. "Did you tell everyone I was here?"
"I didn't tell anyone," Perda said. "I don't know what she's doing here."

"I zapped to your house, Zann." Gliss took a step closer while keeping a wary eye on the wormhole. "I wanted to talk to you. I saw you rushing off down the street, so I followed. Now I'm glad I did. You can't do this—it's way too dangerous!"
"Too late," Perda said. "We're going, and you can't stop us!"
Gliss frowned. "Oh yeah?" She stepped forward and grabbed Perda's free arm, trying to drag her back. "Don't be stupid!"
"Get back!" Zann was still struggling to hold his position. "The wormhole's energy is too strong. You'll get sucked in with us!"
Just then he heard a familiar whistle. Zing! The dragon flew at Zann with a blast of irritated flame. His harness was trailing behind him.
"Zing, no!" Perda exclaimed, ducking her head to avoid the fire.
"Zing! Where are you going?" Darb called, rushing into sight. He gasped when he saw what was happening.
"Hurry!" Gliss called to Darb. "Help me pull Zann and Perda out!"
Darb jumped forward, grabbing onto Gliss. At the same time, Zing latched onto Zann's backpack with his claws. Zann felt the wormhole's hold on him loosen slightly.
"Fine, I give up!" Zann called. "Everyone pull back together, and—"
Whoosh ! Energy suddenly expanded and contracted, sucking the whole group into the wormhole's gaping mouth.

Once again Zann found himself plummeting through a shadowy kaleidoscope of colors and shapes. This time, though, Wyssa wasn't there to steady or guide him. As he felt Perda's hand slipping from his arm, he panicked. Then he realized the magical shackles were still in place, binding him and Perda together.

"Is everyone still here?" he shouted, struggling to look back. The movement sent him flying in a new direction. But he could see his friends strung out behind him. Perda and Gliss were clinging to each other, while Darb hung onto Gliss' legs. Zing was clutching Zann's backpack with his claws. Everyone looked terrified.
Zann tried to gather his thoughts. It wasn't easy. His trip through the vortex with Wyssa had been overwhelming enough. This was much, much worse.
Countless wormholes slid past, offering glimpses into other worlds. How had Wyssa pulled them through one of them? Zann struggled to remember.
"Zann!" Darb's voice sounded faint and frightened. "What do we do now?"
Zann lunged for the next wormhole they passed. His friends were counting on him.
"Oof!" His fingers grasped only empty air. The effort sent the entire group spinning. Gliss let out a shriek.
"Hold on!" Darb shouted.
"Is everyone okay?" Zann yelled. He could feel Perda's arm shackled to his, and Zing's hot breath on his neck. Were the other two still with them?
"We're okay!" Gliss sounded breathless. "I—I don't know how much longer we can hold on though!"

Zann gulped. He had to get them out of here! More worlds slid by, but Zann was unable to reach any of them. It was a struggle merely staying conscious and alert; with every passing moment, he could feel more energy draining from him.

Soon he felt as if even a simple Door-opening spell would be more than he could manage. Would he and his friends end up spinning through the vortex forever? Like Morb, like poor Venna under the Dousing spell, like Zann's parents?
"We have to do something!" Perda cried.
"I know." Even pushing out the words took almost more energy than Zann had left. "I just don't—"
Suddenly Zing whistled eagerly in his ear. Another wormhole was sliding past; this one revealed a large fish leaping out of the water.
Zing lunged, stretching out with his front claws while keeping his hind claws in Zann's backpack.
"Zing!" Darb cried. "This is no time to think about food!"
But somehow Zing was clawing at the edge of the wormhole. Zann felt a strong sucking sensation, as if his entire body were being compressed.
"Wait!" Gliss cried. "I'm losing hold of Perda—"
Splash !

Zann plunged into a gray sea. Its waves grabbed him, flipping him head over heels. It was almost as disorienting as being in the vortex. Zann was so tired that he wasn't sure he could fight the angry water. He was tempted to give up, let himself sink beneath the waves forever . . .
Then he felt a yank on his arm. A moment later his head popped above the surface and he gulped in cool, moist air. Perda was bobbing beside him, panting with exhaustion.
"Where's everyone else?" she asked.

Wind-driven rain made it hard to see. Zann blinked away the moisture. Zing was floating nearby, flapping his wings and looking disgusted. Zann almost smiled. The dragon wasn't a fan of swimming. One of Zann's favorite tricks was to dunk him in the river.
Zann tried to focus; he realized his weary mind was wandering. Treading water, he turned and spotted Gliss and Darb bobbing nearby.
"There you are!" he called.

He struck out toward them but realized his arm was still attached to Perda's. For a moment he was annoyed. Then he realized that the shackles were what had saved him. She must have pulled him to the surface.
By now Darb and Gliss had spotted them and were swimming over. "Everyone okay?" Darb panted.
"I think so." Zann squeezed his eyes shut as a larger wave washed over them. He was relieved to feel his magic energy already coming back.
He glanced at Zing, who had finally shaken off enough water to fly.
"Go higher, boy!" Zann called. "Find land!" He glanced at the others. "Try to rest. Then when Zing shows us which direction to go, we can zap to land."
"Yeah," Gliss said. " If our magic works in this world."
Zann gulped. He hadn't thought of that.
"I'll test my magic." Perda touched the shackles. "Release!"
The shackles disappeared. "Looks like it still works," Zann said.
"It's weird here," Gliss said, her voice shaking. "The rain—it's not any color at all! Just clear!"
"Never mind that," Perda said. "I'm getting tired. Let's make a boat or something."

She linked hands with Zann and Gliss. Even combined, their energy was weak. All they could manage was a small wooden raft. When it was finished, Zann felt drained once again. Still, the raft was big enough to hold them all.
"What's taking him so long?" Gliss squinted up at Zing, who was circling rapidly overhead. The dragon's whistle sounded uneasy.
Suddenly Zing squawked loudly and dived toward them. Zann frowned.
"What's he doing?" he wondered.
At that moment something jolted the raft from below, flipping it up and over. Zann barely had time to gasp before he felt himself falling into the sea.

He fought his way back to the surface just in time to see their raft being swallowed by a creature like none he'd ever seen before. It was a huge, jelly-like beast the size of the largest dragons—like an enormous jellyfish with a gaping, hungry mouth.
And several more were surfacing nearby!
"Look out!" Zann yelled. One of the giant jellyfish was moving straight toward Perda, its huge mouth gaping open.

Rubbing his wet fingers together, Zann tried to send a Blast spell at the monster. But he could barely manage a small sizzle of energy. Still, he distracted the creature long enough for Perda to swim away from it.
Zing dive-bombed the creatures, trying to blast them with his fiery breath. But he was too wet. Nothing but a small puff of steam came out.
"Sing, Zing!" Darb yelled.
Zing started whistling his hypnotic tune. Zann didn't know if it would work. He'd already seen that at least some otherworldly creatures weren't affected by it.
These creatures didn't seem to be hypnotized by Zing's song either. But at least they did appear curious. They turned and swam after Zing, peering up at him with huge, watery eyes.
"Hey!" a voice shouted from the other direction. "Heads up!"
Zann turned and saw a long sailboat shooting toward them. Seconds later the boat arrived, and hands reached out to drag the kids aboard.
"Hurry!" a man shouted in a gruff, urgent voice. "The gulpers are turning back."

Stiff winds lifted the sails and carried the boat swiftly over the waves, leaving the monsters far behind. Moments later Zing caught up and landed beside Zann. The dragon was out of breath, panting out little bursts of steam.
"Gulpers are always hungry, but luckily they're slow," someone said.
Zann turned and saw a boy around his own age smiling at him. "Hi," Zann said. "Thanks for saving us. How did you know we needed help?"
"We were fishing when we saw your strange bird flying around." The boy pointed at Zing. "We came to see what it was."
"His name is Zing," Zann said. "He's a dragon. Oh, and I'm Zann."
"My name's Ello," the other boy said. "Nice to meet you."
Zann introduced Ello to his friends.
"Where are you taking us?" Perda asked Ello.
"Our island." Ello pointed ahead. "We'll be there soon."
Zann squinted into the driving rain. He could barely see a small lump on the horizon. "Is that the island? Where's the mainland?"
Ello shook his head sadly. "There is no mainland anymore. Not since the seas started rising."
"Ello!" someone shouted. "We need your help with the mainsail."

Ello hurried off to help the other fishermen. Zann and his friends tried to stay out of the way, and soon the boat landed on the rough, rocky shore of the tiny island. About a dozen people were waiting to help drag the sailboat onto the beach. Ello and the others quickly explained the situation, and Zann and his friends were surrounded by welcoming faces.
"Come inside—you're soaked," a kind-faced woman said, gesturing toward a handful of humble wooden huts on stilts clustered nearby. "Ello! Find our visitors some dry clothes and stoke the fire."
"Yes, Mother," Ello replied, running ahead up the beach.

Soon Zann and his friends were climbing a rough rope ladder into the largest hut. It felt good to get out of the constant wind and rain, though it was still damp and chilly inside. The fire sputtering in the center of the main room offered little light and even less heat.

Most of the people from the beach crowded into the hut. Ello's mother poured warm drinks from a kettle resting in the embers and passed a mug to each visitor. "Please make yourselves at home," she said.
"Thank you," Zann said. The drink tasted strange, but it made him feel warm.
"And thank you for rescuing us," Perda added. "What were those creatures that attacked us?"
"You mean the gulpers?" One of the men looked surprised. "How can you not know them? They're the most dangerous beasts in all of Skellia."
"Skellia? Is that the name of this land?" asked Gliss. "We're not from here. We came through a wormhole."
Another man gasped. "From the vortex?"
Immediately the Skellians started whispering among themselves. "Are you from a land of magic?" a woman asked, leaning forward.
"Yes," Zann said. "Isn't this a magical land too? Our magic seems to work here."
Perda nodded, rubbed her hands together, and pointed at the fire. "Increase!" she said.
The fire grew bigger and hotter. The Skellians gasped with amazement.
Perda smiled. "See?"
"That explains why the gulpers were after you," one of the fishermen said.
"What do you mean?" Zann was confused. "What is this place?"

Taking turns, their hosts finished explaining what Ello had started to tell them in the boat. Over the past few generations, most of the land in Skellia had been swallowed up by rough, rising seas. The people of Skellia had weak and limited magic. They couldn't do much more than conjure food and fresh water. Even working together, they were unable to stop the seas or create more land.

"That's why everyone is desperate to escape to other worlds before all the land is gone," Ello said. "The trouble is the gulpers. They're attracted to magic energy—they feed on it. And there's no stronger magic in Skellia than a wormhole."
A woman nodded. "Every time one pops into existence, the gulpers quickly gulp it down."
"You mean they eat the wormholes?" Gliss exclaimed.
"They swallow them whole." Ello shrugged. "Unless a wormhole happens to pop up on land, it's nearly impossible to reach one before a gulper finds it."
"For instance," a fisherman said, "those gulpers you saw have probably swallowed the wormhole you came through."
Zann stared at his friends as they all realized what this meant. They were trapped in this world, just like the natives!
"Hello?" someone shouted from outside. "Come and look!"
The Skellians headed for the door of the hut.
"What are we going to do?" Gliss whispered. "We can't get back to Magica without a wormhole!"
"We'll figure something out," Zann said, trying to sound confident.
Zann and his friends joined the Skellians at the doorway. Everyone was staring at the beach.
"What's going on?" Perda asked Ello.
"It's the gulpers." Ello pointed. "They're clustering along the shore! It's weird—they don't usually do that."
Zann squinted through the rain. Several gulpers were splashing around in the shallows.
A few Skellians climbed down the rope ladder for a better look.
"Isn't it dangerous to get too close to those things?" Gliss asked.
"It's okay," Ello replied. "The gulpers can't come onto land. Let's take a look!"
Following Ello, Zann and his friends climbed down to the beach. That seemed to make the gulpers even more excited. They churned up the water so much that part of the beach was flooded.
"It's because of our visitors," a woman said, staring at Zann and the others. "They must give off enough magic energy to attract the gulpers."
"Good thing they can't come on land." Gliss sounded nervous. "Be careful, Darb! Don't get too close!"
Zann smiled. "Darb is always curious about new creatures," he told Ello.
"I think that's the same gulper that bumped our raft." Darb pointed to one of the creatures. "See? I recognize its color and the shape of its eye."
"If you say so," Perda said dubiously. "They all look the same to me."

"I can't see anything in all this rain," Gliss complained. Snapping her fingers, she conjured up an umbrella. That caused the gulpers to go into a frenzy. One even flopped onto the beach, splashing everyone.
"Wow," Zann said. "They definitely noticed that magic you just did, Gliss."
"Yeah." Perda stared at the gulpers with amazement. "It's almost like we're having our magic tracked by Morb again!"
Until that moment the Skellians had been laughing and pointing at the gulpers, seeming to enjoy the unusual spectacle. But at Perda's comment, they all became silent.
"What did you say?" one of the women asked Perda.
Perda looked confused. "What? You mean about Morb? He's just this guy from Magica. It's a long story, but I guess we could tell you . . ."
The Skellians traded serious glances. "I'm sorry," an older man said. "I'm afraid we cannot welcome you into our village after all. You'll have to leave."
"What?" Perda exclaimed. "Where are we supposed to go? You just told us there's hardly any land here!"
The man shrugged. "I'm sorry," he said again, though Zann didn't think he sounded very sorry.
Ello looked dismayed. "Rellu, no! You can't turn them away."
"You don't understand, Ello." The man's voice was stern. "Come, let's get inside."
Most of the Skellians turned to leave. But Ello grabbed his mother. "We can't do this," he said. "I'm sure they're not—"
"Hush, son." His mother shot a nervous look at the visitors.
"What's wrong?" Gliss cried, her chin quivering. "Please! We don't understand."
Ello's mother's expression softened. "Wait here," she said. "Let me talk to Rellu."
She hurried off with Ello at her heels.
"What was that all about?" Darb wondered.
Zann shook his head. "It's like they heard Morb's name and freaked out."
"But how would they know about Morb here?" Perda said.
"Shh," Gliss shushed her. "Here they come."
Ello was hurrying back. "I'm sorry, they're being very stubborn," he said. "They still won't let you stay with us. But they said you can stay in the old village for a few days."
"The old village?" Zann said.

"It's this way." Ello led them over a ridge. Then he pointed down a slope. A single hut stood at the bottom. The lower halves of its stilts were in the water. "That's where the village used to be when I was born," Ello explained. "The waters rose and submerged most of the houses, but that one is still out of reach of the gulpers. You'll be all right there."
"Why did everyone get upset when we mentioned Morb?" Perda asked.
Ello shrugged, looking uncomfortable. "I'd better go," he said. "The others will need my help cleaning and cooking today's catch." He rushed off.
"That was weird," Darb said.
"Never mind." Gliss shivered. "It's cold out here. Let's get inside."
The hut's interior was damp and moldy. But Perda created a fire, and Zann conjured up some food. As they ate, Darb wandered onto a balcony facing the sea.
"The gulpers are swimming near this hut now," he reported. "They must have sensed your magic."
"Let's hope they can't knock the hut off its stilts," Zann joked weakly. "Or they might swallow us right up!"
Perda glanced out the window. "It's getting darker. It must be almost night."
"How can you tell?" Gliss grimaced. "The rain makes everything so gloomy all the time! No wonder these people want to escape to other worlds."
Zann yawned. "It's been a long day. Let's try to get some sleep. Maybe we can figure out a plan tomorrow."
Zann was in the midst of yet another confusing dream about his parents when a shout awakened him. His eyes popped open, and he sat up.
Ello was standing in the doorway. "A storm is coming!" he said breathlessly.
"Huh?" Gliss mumbled, rubbing her eyes. "So what? It never stops raining here."
"You don't understand!" Ello's voice was urgent. "This storm is big. It may cause the water to rise again. If that happens, you'll be cut off from the shore, and at the mercy of the gulpers!"
"What?" Zann cried. "What should we do?"
"I can't stay." Ello was already rushing off. "Just—please—get yourself to safety!" he called out over his shoulder.
"What are you waiting for?" Gliss exclaimed. "Let's get inland!"
"Wait," Perda said. "I might have a better idea."
Zann noticed that Perda looked thoughtful. "What is it?" he asked.
"I couldn't sleep, so I've been lying here thinking about how we can get off this world," Perda said. "I may have come up with a plan."
"This is never going to work." Gliss' voice shook as she glanced over the edge of the balcony at the dark, churning sea below. "It's a crazy plan!"
"She's right." Darb sounded doubtful. "Too many things could go wrong. Maybe we should think about this some more."
Zann glanced down too. The waves were wilder than ever. He wasn't sure if it was because of the growing storm, or because of the gulpers still swimming below their hut. Probably both.
"I think Perda's plan could work," he said. "I know it's risky. But it could be our best chance of ever escaping from Skellia."
Perda nodded. "Let's join friction."
She held out her hands. Zann touched his palm to hers. Then he looked at Gliss and held out his other hand. She still looked scared. But she joined her palms with the others.
"Stand in the middle of the circle," Zann told Darb. "And hang on to Zing."
Darb nodded. Grabbing the dragon, he ducked under his friends' arms.
"Ready?" Perda closed her eyes. "Protect!"
"Protect!" Zann and Gliss chorused.
Instantly they were surrounded by a glowing orange bubble.
"Let's hope this Shield spell is strong enough," Perda said.
"And let's hope Darb really can tell one gulper from another," Zann added.
"I'm pretty sure I can," Darb said.
" Pretty sure?" Gliss echoed. "Or really sure?"
"Just come on." Perda sounded impatient. "Over to the edge, everyone."
They shuffled to the edge of the balcony, still contained within the shield bubble. "Wait," Gliss said. "What happens next?"
Perda rolled her eyes. She'd already explained her plan several times.
But when Zann looked at Gliss, he couldn't help feeling sorry for her. She looked really scared.
"We need to find that first gulper," he explained again. "The one Darb recognized back on the beach."
"Right," Perda continued. "That gulper probably swallowed our wormhole, since it was the first one to arrive after we came through."
"And we already know that even the strongest magic can't destroy a wormhole," Zann went on. "That means the wormhole will probably still be intact inside the gulper."
"At least for a while." Darb sounded nervous. "If gulpers feed on magic energy, won't the wormhole be digested eventually?"
"That's why we shouldn't waste any more time talking about it," Perda said. "Let's go! One, two, three . . . Jump!"
As they all leaped off the balcony, Zann held his breath, hoping the Shield spell would hold.
Splash! The glowing bubble sank under the waves, but the water didn't get inside.
"It's working!" Perda cried. "We can still breathe!"
"Look out!" Darb pointed. "A gulper—and it's not the one we want!"
"Away!" Zann yelled, rubbing his hands together. The bubble bounced away from the gulper.
"More are coming!" Gliss exclaimed.
"We have to find the original gulper," Perda cried. "Darb, do you see it?"
"I'm looking." Darb was peering through the glowing orange wall. "There! I think that's the original gulper coming at us right now."
"It's going to swallow us!" Gliss shrieked.
"That's the whole idea," Perda reminded her. But her voice shook a little as she said it.
Zann didn't blame them for being scared. He felt his own throat go dry with fear as the gulper swam closer, its enormous mouth gaping open, ready to swallow the entire group. Gulp !
"Aah!" Zann cried as they were sucked into the gulper's mouth.
For a moment he couldn't see anything. The inside of the gulper was dark and slimy.
"It looks like they don't only eat magic," Perda said, wrinkling her nose at the smell. "They eat fish and other stuff too."
"Does anyone see the wormhole?" Gliss asked.
"There it is!" Darb pointed.
Zann spun around and saw the wormhole glowing in the darkness. "Hurry!" he cried. "It looks kind of weak already!"
"Quick, everybody join hands," Perda said.
Zann grabbed Perda's hand. She grabbed Gliss' hand, and Gliss grabbed Darb's. Darb picked up Zing.
Then Zann touched the side of the bubble. "Is everybody ready?" When the others nodded, he muttered, "Dissipate." He quickly sucked in a deep breath of air as the Shield spell bubble disappeared.

The kids were plunged into watery coldness. Without the orange glow of the bubble, it was even harder to see. But the wormhole threw off a faint glow of its own. Zann kicked his feet, moving himself through the water with his free hand.
Soon he felt the wormhole tugging at him. Its pull was surprisingly strong—so strong that he felt his hand slipping away from Perda's!
"No!" He screamed, accidentally sucking in a mouthful of the disgusting water.

Perda quickly restored the shackles that had bound their arms together back in Magica, and Zann felt his arm clamped safely to hers. A moment later the wormhole sucked them in, pressing all the breath from their bodies for a second before tossing them into the rushing whirl of the vortex.
As Zann tumbled head over heels, he heard a sharp scream behind him. He glanced back just in time to see Gliss lose her grip on Perda's hand.
"No!" Gliss shrieked.
A second later she, Darb, and Zing were swept away out of sight!
"No!" Zann yelled. But it was too late. Darb, Gliss, and Zing were gone.
"I couldn't hold on!" Perda cried. "I tried to hold on to Gliss, but I couldn't!"
"I know," Zann said. He was glad Perda had restored the Shackle spell. Otherwise, his friends might all be gone. "We have to get out of the vortex. Then we'll figure out what to do."
He glanced around. A wormhole was sliding past, showing a peaceful green meadow. He lunged for it, but his hand came up empty.
"How do we get through one?" Perda asked.
"I don't know." Zann grabbed for another wormhole and missed again. "Wyssa got me out the first time. And Zing brought us out into Skellia."
He felt a pang of despair as he said Zing's name. Would he ever see his fiery little buddy again? Or Darb, his best friend? Or Gliss, whom he'd accidentally dragged into danger yet again?

Zann tried not to think about it. "Zing got us out when he tried to grab that fish he saw. He spotted it through the Skellia wormhole and really jumped at it. Hang on. I'm going to try harder for the next one."
"Okay. But even if that works, how will we know which world we're entering?" Perda wondered.
"We won't. But anywhere has got to be better than here, right?" Zann glanced forward. "Hold on!"
He hurled himself toward the next wormhole. This time he felt his fingers latch onto the edge of the wormhole. Its magic energy burned his hand.
"Ouch!" he cried, letting go. He caught a glimpse of a gleaming city as he tumbled away. "Drat!"
"What happened?" Perda asked.
"Nothing. I'll try again in a second."
This time Zann vowed not to let go, no matter what. He lunged at the next wormhole. His fingers caught the edge, and he ignored the magical burn, pulling himself forward.
"Oof!" he said as he slid through the wormhole and fell flat on his face on the other side.
Perda landed beside him. "You did it!" she said. "Now, where are we?"

"I don't know. But at least it's dry." Zann looked around. They had landed on an open plain surrounded by a dark forest. A flash of lightning lit up the sky. Strange lights flickered on and off, and strange sounds came from every direction. The air crackled with strong magical energy.
"Where are we?" Perda asked again. This time she sounded a little nervous.
Zann climbed to his feet and then helped Perda up. She undid the Shackle spell to release his arm.
"Come on," said Zann. "Let's—"
"Look out!" Perda shouted, yanking him back as the ground opened up at their feet.
They jumped backward as the opening grew bigger, emitting a blast of energy that sizzled several nearby trees into burnt stumps. A second later the ground closed again.
"Let's get away from here," Perda said, backing away toward a cluster of trees.
"Stop!" Zann cried. One of the trees was reaching toward Perda, its branches snaking out like tentacles.
Zann grabbed her and dragged her out of range just in time. He didn't stop until they were in the open, well away from any of the trees.
"What's wrong with this world?" Perda said, looking worried and confused.

Zann didn't answer for a second. He was staring at something passing by on the far side of the plain. Something huge and hairy. It looked like a giant spider, but with ten legs and three long, curved teeth sticking out from its mouth.

"I think I just figured it out." He pointed at the creature, which was too far away to notice them. "See that? I think it's a deca-stinger. I recognize it from one of my parents' books— Creatures of the Known Magical Worlds ."
"S—so this is a known magical world?" Perda asked. "Which one?"
Zann gulped. "I think it's . . . Fardark."
"Fardark?" Perda echoed. "Oh boy."
Zann knew exactly how she felt. Fardark was known for its dark magic and dangerous creatures. Zann tried to remember what else he'd read about Fardark, but he was soon interrupted.
"Look out!" Perda cried, pointing up.

Zann glanced up. A huge dragon was flying down toward them, its claws bared. Boiling droplets fell from its mouth like hail, leaving burned spots sizzling all around Zann and Perda. Zann raised his hand to throw up a Shield spell, but realized it was no use. Once again the vortex had drained most of their energy. Their magic might not be strong enough to protect them.
"Run!" Zann yelled.
He grabbed Perda's hand and sprinted across the plain. The dragon turned and came at them again. This time Zann heard Perda cry out as one of the droplets burned her arm, leaving a red mark.
"This way!" Zann pulled her toward the trees. They would just have to hope they weren't the same kind of trees that had tried to grab them.
As lightning flashed again, he spotted a hollow tree trunk just ahead. Pulling Perda with him, he ducked into it. A rain of sizzling droplets burned the earth around them.
"Did that dragon see us hide in here?" Perda whispered, peering out.
"I don't know." Zann looked out too. The dragon landed with a thud, its red eyes searching the darkness and its nostrils sniffing the air.
Suddenly there was a wail. A second later the deca-stinger appeared and flung itself onto the dragon! The two huge beasts rolled in the dirt, clawing each other and howling.
"This could be our chance!" Zann whispered. "Let's get out of here while they're both distracted."
Zann and Perda scurried out of the tree trunk. The forest was dark and spooky, and Zann didn't want to go any deeper into it. Besides, he didn't want to get too far from the wormhole.
"Look, a cave!" Perda pointed. "Let's hide in there."

At the cave's entrance, Zann used the small amount of energy he had left to do a quick Life Force Locator spell. The cave was empty, so he and Perda huddled inside. As the two monsters continued to fight outside, Zann and Perda caught their breath and talked about what had happened.
"Did you see whether Darb, Gliss, and Zing stayed together?" Zann asked.
"I couldn't tell." Perda looked worried. "If Darb gets separated from Gliss . . ."
"I know. Without magic, he'd be helpless in the vortex." Zann's mind flashed again to Venna. What had become of her? And what about Morb? Without his stolen magic, he was a Void, just like Darb.
"We need to figure out how to find them," Perda said. "Fast!"

"How?" Zann glanced out of the cave. "Even if we can make it past those two monsters and back to the wormhole, we can't even navigate our way through the vortex. Let alone find our friends." He looked at Perda. "I can't believe I dragged you all into this," he mumbled.
Perda shrugged. "You didn't drag me—I wanted to come."
Zann gave a small chuckle. "Well, we've both said we want to be explorers. Now here we are—exploring."
Perda peered out from the cave and then smiled. "Look! They're running off!"
Zann looked out. The battling monsters had stopped fighting and were now racing away in opposite directions.
"That's weird," he said. "I wonder why they're leaving."
"Who cares?" said Perda. "This could be our chance to get back to the wormhole." She crawled out of the cave. "Come on!"

They raced out of the forest and across the dark plain, dodging random bursts of energy. Zann could see the wormhole winking at them just ahead. Being in the vortex was pretty scary. But they'd just discovered that certain worlds were even scarier.
"Hurry!" he called to Perda. "We have to—argh!"
Zann suddenly felt a stinging sensation, as if he were being stuck with burning needles all over his body. He fell to the ground, twitching and groaning.
"What's happening?" Perda cried in a shaky voice. Out of the corner of his eye, Zann saw her fall, twitching, beside him.

Then a new creature stepped into view. It was much smaller than the dragon or the deca-stinger—in fact, it wasn't much bigger than Zing. It didn't look very scary either. It resembled a hairy walking mop.
Even so, Zann shivered when he saw it. "Oh no," he said. "It's a scatter beast!"
" That's a scatter beast?" Perda said. "The thing that knocked your parents off course?"

Zann couldn't answer. As the scatter beast crept closer, the stinging sensations grew worse. Besides, Zann didn't know much more about scatter beasts than Perda did. All he knew was that they threw off chaotic energy that confused the magic of others.

He struggled to regain control of his body, but it was no use. The scatter beast was still approaching. A skinny tentacle appeared from amid the dirty, grayish hair and stretched toward the kids. Zann could only stare at it, mesmerized by the spiral-shaped claw at the end.
"We have to get away!" Perda cried. She rubbed her hands together. "Blast!"
A small sizzle of energy spit out of her hand. It made it halfway to the scatter beast before suddenly doubling back toward the kids. At the same time, it swelled into a fireball.
"Look out!" Zann yelled, throwing himself aside.
Perda rolled away just in time too. The fireball blasted a large hole in the rocky ground between them.

Zann tried to turn to make sure Perda was okay. But he couldn't move anymore. He realized he'd thrown himself even closer to the scatter beast. All Zann could do now was stare helplessly as the creature moved toward him, its claw aimed at his forehead.
Zann knew he should be scared. After all, he was about to die.

But instead the only thing he felt was regret. He regretted that he would never find his parents, that Boz would never know what had happened to him, and that he'd never have the chance to make up with Gliss—or even find out if she and the others had survived . . .

Then, out of the corner of his eye, he noticed something strange. A sparkling rain of colorful glitter was falling gently from the sky, seemingly out of nowhere. At first Zann assumed it was an illusion, that the scatter beast's energy was affecting his vision.

Then the first bits of glitter touched the scatter beast. They sizzled and burned some of its fur, causing the beast to jump back and howl with pain. Its wild energy went even wilder, sparking fires here and there and making the ground shudder.
"Huh?" Zann mumbled through numb lips.
Then he felt someone grab him by the arm and drag him across the hard, rocky ground. A moment later he felt the increasingly familiar sensation of passing through a wormhole.
The vortex felt almost welcoming after Fardark. When he felt Perda bump against him, Zann was relieved. They'd both made it out. But who had rescued them?
"That was close," an irritated voice snapped. "I thought I warned you about the wormholes, boy."
Zann blinked, his vision swimming back into focus. He gasped as he finally got a good look at the person who had grabbed him.
It was Wyssa!
"W—Wyssa?" Zann stammered. His lips were still numb from the scatter beast's attack. "How did you—?"
"Save your energy, boy." Wyssa sounded irritated. "The more you talk, the more you slow us down. Now, where are the others?"
Perda gasped. "This is the old woman we spoke with in Wormwood! She's Wyssa?"

"Yes," Zann said. The effects of the scatter beast's magic were wearing off. But being in the vortex still made it hard to think clearly. "How did you find us?" he asked Wyssa. "How did you even know to look for us?"
"I have my ways," Wyssa said. "Now we need to get you kids back to Magica. Where are your friends?"
"Back to Magica?" Zann immediately thought about his parents. He couldn't go home until he'd found them!
"You can do that?" Perda sounded relieved. "You can get us home?"
"Of course," Wyssa snapped. "But where are the others? There should be another Red with you. A girl, yes? And the young Void?"
Zann felt his heart sink as he thought about Gliss, Darb, and Zing. "They're gone," he said. "We got separated in the vortex earlier. I don't know where they are now."
"What?" Wyssa snapped. She yanked at Zann's arm so hard that he cried out in surprise.

He felt his body being sucked through another wormhole. A moment later he, Wyssa, and Perda were standing on a cliff overlooking a rough sea. Cold wind whipped around them, and strange gray birds circled overhead, letting out shrill cries. But Wyssa didn't seem to notice any of that. She was glaring at Zann.
"Let me make sure I understand this," Wyssa said. "You brought your friends into the vortex. Then you lost track of two of them?"
"Three, actually," Zann admitted. "Zing, my pet dragon, was with them too."
"You found us," Perda said. "Can't you find them too?"
Wyssa glanced at her. "It's not that easy, girl."
"Perda," Perda said. "My name is Perda. Not 'girl.'"
Wyssa gnashed her teeth, and Zann cringed. He didn't want Wyssa and Perda to start arguing. Not when his friends were still missing.
"How did you find us?" he asked Wyssa. "Maybe you can find Darb and Gliss the same way."

"As I said, it's not that easy." Wyssa paced back and forth along the cliff's edge. "The Interworld Tracking spell I used to find you is complicated. To do it, you need an object that has some of the lost person's magic energy."
Perda folded her arms. "I've never heard of a spell like that."
"There are whole worlds out there you've never heard of, girl," Wyssa told her. "That doesn't mean they don't exist."
"So you tracked our magic energy?" Zann asked. "Mine and Perda's? How?"
"Not hers—just yours." Wyssa stopped pacing. "I used this." She reached into the folds of her cloak and pulled out a small object. Zann recognized it right away.
"That's a chew toy I created for Zing yesterday," he said. "How did you get that?"

Wyssa tucked the chew toy away. "Since you created it so recently, it still contains traces of your magic energy," she said, without answering Zann's question. "I was able to use it to track you through the vortex and into Fardark."

Zann shivered, but only partly because of the cold wind. Hearing the name "Fardark" reminded Zann of his visit with Perda to that dark and dreadful world. "Thanks for saving us," he said. "But can't you use that chew toy to track Zing? He drooled all over it."
"The spell doesn't work that way." Wyssa frowned. "It requires magic energy, not dragon drool."
"You said you can get us back to Magica, right?" Perda said. "I'm sure we could find something Gliss created there."
"That would take much too long." Wyssa started pacing again. "Your friends could be in grave danger, alone in the vortex."
"Then what are we going to do?" Perda cried. "We have to find our friends!"
Zann could only nod. His throat was too dry to speak. He couldn't believe he'd accidentally led his friends into danger again. If they were lost in the vortex forever, it was his fault!
Wyssa stopped pacing and looked down at the ground. She appeared to be deep in thought. A minute later she looked up. "I have an idea. Come."
She grabbed Zann and Perda and yanked them through the wormhole. Soon all three of them were rushing through the vortex again.
"What's your plan?" Zann asked.

"I know how to make a potion that will show me which wormholes have been used recently," Wyssa replied. "If your friends managed to get through one and into another world, I might be able to track them."
"Great," Perda said. "But what if they haven't gone through a wormhole?"
"Yeah, what if they're still in the vortex?" Zann added. "It's not easy to grab one of those wormholes, you know."
Wyssa shrugged. "Let's just hope they have gotten out by now," she said.

Zann gulped, afraid to ask what she meant. Still, he was glad that she had a plan. First they needed to find Darb, Gliss, and Zing. Then Zann needed to figure out a way to keep searching for his parents—without dragging his friends into more danger.
"Hold on," Wyssa said. "I need to find a world that contains the ingredients for my—"

Zann gasped, not hearing any more of what she was saying. As he slid past another wormhole, an image of his parents' terrified faces flashed through his mind. The vision was just like the horrible nightmares he'd been having about his mother and father. Only this time Zann was wide awake!
Zann couldn't see what was scaring his parents. All he could see was their terrified faces and the powerful magic swirling around them.
"No!" Zann cried as his mother screamed and his father let out a yell of fear.
Then he felt a sharp pain on one side of his head, and the vision faded away. He was still in the vortex. Wyssa had let go of his arm, but now she was pinching his ear—hard.
"Ow!" Zann exclaimed. "Stop that!"
"I'll let go of your ear when you let go of that wormhole," Wyssa said.
Zann realized he was clinging to the edge of a wormhole. He had grabbed it without even knowing he was doing so. Was that because of the dream? Could this wormhole be a clue?
"Wait," he said, peering into the wormhole. He caught a glimpse of purple-leaved trees waving in a soft breeze. "I want to see if—"
Wyssa gave one last yank on Zann's ear, and he lost his grip. A second later the wormhole was out of sight behind him.
"What was that all about?" Perda asked.
Zann couldn't respond. He was too breathless and confused by what had just happened.
"Hold on tight," Wyssa said. "A useful world is coming up shortly. You two can rest there and regain your energy while I put my potion together."
She pulled them through a new wormhole. They landed in a beautiful little park in the middle of a town.
However, Zann barely had a second to take in the scenery before he gasped and grabbed his nose.
"Ew!" Perda cried beside him. She was pinching her nose shut. "What is that stink ?"
"Where are we?" Zann's voice sounded funny now that he was holding his nose. "Why does it smell so bad?"

Wyssa sniffed the air. "We're in Niffia. It may not smell nice to us. But it's a peaceful place with friendly, intelligent, and welcoming people. You'll be safe here while I work. Oh, and your magic should function normally in this world. So you two might want to create some food to fortify yourselves for the rest of our journey."
Zann couldn't imagine wanting to eat anything in this place. Before he or Perda could say anything else, though, Wyssa zapped out of sight.
"Ugh," Perda said. "I can't believe this stench!"
"Yeah. I can't stand it any longer." Zann let go of his nose and rubbed his hands together. "Protect!" he said.
He frowned as a puff of smoke wafted up from his hands. Nothing else happened.
"What are you trying to do?" Perda asked.
"Create a Shield spell around my head." Zann grabbed his nose again. "I thought Wyssa said our magic would work here."
Perda shrugged. "Magic requires focusing our minds. It's pretty hard to focus on anything except this awful smell."
Zann saw several figures hurrying toward them across the park. They looked like regular humans except for one thing: they had no noses!
"Welcome!" a man said. "Are you visitors to Niffia?"
"Yes," Zann said. "We, um, won't be here long. Sorry to bother you."
"No bother at all!" The Niffian beamed. "We love visitors, and yet we have so few. May we show you around town?"

For the next half hour, the Niffians gave Zann and Perda a tour. The rest of the town was just as charming as the park. Everywhere Zann and Perda went, friendly Niffians stopped to say hello. Even the songs of the birds were beautiful.
"Too bad we don't know any spells to shut off our sense of smell," Perda whispered to Zann.
"Yeah," Zann muttered back. He wasn't paying much attention to the tour. He wished Wyssa would hurry, and not only because of the smell. He was worried about Gliss, Darb, and Zing.
Finally Wyssa zapped into sight.
"Wyssa?" One of the Niffians greeted her with a smile. "It's been far too long since we've enjoyed a visit from you!"

Wyssa bowed. "Thank you for your hospitality, my friend. I'm grateful that you're always so generous with your natural resources. Once again I've found exactly what I need for one of my potions." Wyssa held up her hands, which were now covered with strange purple symbols.
"Ah," another Niffian said with a smile. "Yes, our native oogberry is useful for many spells, isn't it?"
"Indeed," Wyssa said. "Now I'm afraid my young friends and I must be going. We have urgent business in the vortex."
"Travel safely," a Niffian said. "I hope we'll see you all again soon."
"Thanks," Zann said. He had enjoyed meeting the Niffians. But secretly he hoped he'd never have to smell anything like Niffia ever again!
Soon Wyssa, Zann, and Perda were passing through the wormhole.
"Whew!" Perda exclaimed. "I've never been so glad to be back in the vortex!"
"What happens now?" Zann asked Wyssa.
Wyssa stared at her hands. "These markings will let us know which wormholes have been used recently."
The group drifted through the vortex. After a few minutes, the purple symbols began to glow.
"There's a wormhole just ahead," said Wyssa. "Someone has passed through it recently." She reached out as an opening spun into view.
A moment later Zann felt himself leave the vortex.
"Oof!" he grunted as he landed on cold, hard ground.
This new world was so dark, Zann could barely see his hand in front of his face. A strange buzzing sound filled the air. It seemed to be coming from all around them.
Feeling nervous, Zann snapped his fingers. "Light," he whispered, holding out his hand.
A glowing orb of light appeared in his hand. A second later it exploded into a huge fireball!
Zann screamed as the fire consumed his arm. Hoping to create more friction, he started to rub his other hand against his side.
"Stop!" Wyssa's harsh voice rang out.
A moment later the fire was gone. Zann felt Wyssa touch his hand and arm, and the pain disappeared.
"What happened?" Perda asked. "Why is it so dark here?"
A cool white flame appeared in Wyssa's hands. Wyssa dropped it on the ground, and it spread to surround her, Zann, and Perda so they could see one another clearly.
"You'll need to be careful here," Wyssa said. Her voice was calm now. "Galvan is a land of extra-strong magic energy. Any magic you perform will be greatly intensified, often in unpredictable ways."
Zann could still hear a buzzing sound. Now he realized it was the steady hum of magic energy.
"Let me try some magic." Perda sounded intrigued. She snapped her fingers. A cup of airberry juice appeared in her hand. "There," she said. "That didn't—"
She gasped as the airberry juice expanded and flowed over the edge of the cup like a fountain. Soon all three of them were drenched.
"No more magic!" Wyssa snapped. She waved her hand, and the airberry juice disappeared.
"Wow," Perda said. "Just imagine what someone with Morb's powers could do in a place like this!"
Wyssa glared at her. Zann wasn't sure if that was because of the airberry juice stunt, or because Perda had mentioned Morb's name.
"Don't do any magic, either of you," Wyssa said sternly. "Leave it to me."
"Okay," Zann said. "Now, how are we supposed to figure out whether our friends are here?"
"I'm going to do a Seeking spell," Wyssa said. "Join hands."

Zann took Perda's hand and then reached for Wyssa's. Wyssa grabbed his wrist with one hand and snapped her fingers. A second later all three of them were yanked off their feet and flying through the air.
"Whoa!" Perda yelled. "What's happening?"

"It's the Seeking spell," Zann called back. They were moving so fast he couldn't see a thing. "The intense magic here must be affecting the spell, like Wyssa said. It's pulling us toward the others! That means they're definitely here, right?"
"Not necessarily," Wyssa replied. "A Seeking spell can't be used to find one particular person. Don't they teach you anything in those Magica schools?"
"We haven't really done Seeking spells yet," Perda said. "At least not in school."
"Well, we're Seeking anything from Magica," Wyssa explained. "The spell could be leading us to your friends, or—oh!"
They flew through the doorway of a small cottage and came to a sudden stop. A short man with large ears and feet was staring at them with a look of total surprise.
"Zann!" Perda pointed toward a table. "It's your parents' book— Creatures of the Known Magical Worlds !"
Zann gasped. "What's that doing here?"
Wyssa smiled at the strange little man. "Greetings, Fud," she said. "I should have realized where my Seeking spell was leading us."
Fud smiled and clasped her hand. "Wyssa! What a wonderful surprise!"

Zann was pretty surprised too. First the Niffians had greeted Wyssa like an old friend, and now Fud was doing the same. Until now Zann hadn't thought of Wyssa as the type of person who had many friends. Or any friends, really.
"Where did you get this?" Zann asked Fud, picking up the book.
"Wyssa brought it to me," Fud replied. "She knows of my interest in other worlds."
"Have you visited many of the worlds in the book?" asked Perda.
"Sadly, I've visited none of them," Fud said with a wry smile. "We Galvanites can barely manage to feed ourselves with our weak magic. I'd have little chance of surviving the vortex."
"Really?" Zann said. "But this world has such strong magic energy!"
"That's true," Wyssa said. "And as you saw "—she glared at Perda—"it can be dangerous to perform magic in such a place. The Galvanites have evolved to avoid that danger."
She went on to tell Fud about their search for Darb, Gliss, and Zing.
"Oh, dear," Fud said. "I'll send out a message to see if they've been spotted."
With the others following, he hurried outside.
"If these people don't have much magic, how can he send a message?" Perda wondered.
"Just watch," Wyssa said.
Fud began stomping his large bare feet on the ground. The sound echoed like a drumbeat as the constant magic energy caught it. Soon the rhythm was vibrating all around Zann and the others.
Before long they heard another rhythm.
"Is that someone answering?" Zann asked.
"Yes." Fud frowned with concentration as he listened. "And here comes another response."
For the next few minutes, more and more drumbeats came from all directions. Finally, though, Fud shook his head.
"I'm sorry," he said, "but it seems nobody has seen your friends."
"That means they're likely not in Galvan," Wyssa said with a sigh. "Especially since my Seeking spell didn't find them either. Thank you, Fud. We'd better get back to the wormhole."
"Please visit again soon," Fud urged her.
"I will, my friend." Wyssa grabbed Zann and Perda. "Zap!"
Splash!
"Drat!" Zann had landed in a muddy stream, and his legs were soaked.
"This doesn't look like the right spot," Perda said. She and Wyssa had landed on the stream bank. "Where's the wormhole?"
Wyssa shrugged. "As I said, magic can be unpredictable here."
Zann climbed out of the stream and rubbed his hands, automatically conjuring dry pants and shoes.
A second later he was wrapped in reams of heavy fabric from head to toe. "Help!" he gasped. "I can't breathe!"
Zann struggled for breath as the fabric completely enveloped everyone.
"Don't you ever listen, boy?" Wyssa's muffled voice came from nearby. "I'd better get us out of Galvan before you kill us all."
Zann felt a hand grab him. Zap ! He landed in front of the Galvan wormhole.
"Nice work, Zann," Perda said breathlessly, as Wyssa dragged them into the wormhole. "You almost smothered us!"
"Sorry," Zann mumbled.
Once again they were speeding through the vortex.
"How many magical worlds are there, anyway?" asked Perda.
"Nobody knows," Wyssa replied. "The nature of wormholes makes it impossible to know for sure."
"My parents said that hundreds of worlds have been cataloged already," Zann said. "But more are being discovered all the time."
He thought about World X. His parents had contacted Wyssa for help in finding it. Did she know where it was?
He opened his mouth to ask. But a flash of purple light distracted him. The symbols on Wyssa's hands were glowing again.
"Oh no," Wyssa muttered when she saw the next wormhole.
Whatever world the wormhole led to, Zann could tell she wasn't happy about going through it.

He soon landed on something soft and squishy. Looking around, Zann could see that they were standing on a puffy white cloud floating peacefully in a clear golden sky. Dozens of similar clouds surrounded them.
"I feel as light as a dragon's scale!" Perda exclaimed.
Zann felt the same way. He jumped and found himself floating up surprisingly high before floating gently back down to the cloud.
Perda did a somersault in the air. "Look at me! I'm flying!" she cried.
"Settle down, both of you." Wyssa's voice was stern. "We need to figure out whether your friends are here. Quickly ."
"Okay, okay." Perda sat down on a fluffy patch of cloud. "How do we do that?"
"I'm thinking," Wyssa said sharply. "Just be quiet for a moment."

Zann bounced gently, still looking around. "Hey, look at that," he said, pointing at a cloud far overhead. It was dark and stormy, with lightning flickering through it every few seconds. It definitely stood out in the otherwise pale and peaceful sky.
"I said, be quiet, boy!" Wyssa barked.
Her face looked pinched and anxious. Before Zann could ask what was wrong, he noticed a new cloud zooming toward them. This one looked oddly glittery. When it came closer, he gasped.
"It's a whole flock of those little stinging dragons that Morb brought to Magica!" he cried.
"They're called flizzes," Wyssa said. "They're very useful as long as you know how to control them."
Zann recalled the painful stings he and Darb had received from the flizzes. He conjured a sturdy stick to use as a weapon if the creatures came any closer.
"You won't need that," Wyssa said with a faint smile. "I know exactly how to control flizzes. I'm the one who brought them to Morb."

Zann wanted to ask how many other dangerous creatures Wyssa had brought to Morb. But before he could speak, his mouth widened into a sudden yawn. Lowering the stick, he sank onto the soft, welcoming cloud. He watched the flizzes gather around Wyssa, who began speaking softly to them in a language Zann didn't understand.
Beside him Perda yawned as well. "It's been a long day, hasn't it?" she mumbled. "I think I'll just close my eyes for a second."
Zann was drifting off to sleep too when he heard a soft snore. Opening his eyes, he was surprised to see Perda floating. Above them both was the dark cloud. It appeared much closer than before.
"Weird," he mumbled.
Wyssa heard him and looked over. "Oh dear," she muttered. "They're succumbing even faster than I'd feared." Glancing at the flizzes, she waved her hand. "Go! And hurry!"
Zann watched the flizzes speed off. "Where . . . Where are they . . . ?" Zann paused. What had he been planning to ask? He couldn't remember. "Oh well," he mumbled. "Doesn't matter."
He felt himself floating upward, as Perda was doing. It seemed like too much trouble to resist, so he didn't. Besides, floating felt kind of nice.
The stick felt heavy in his hand. He let it go, watching through half-closed eyes as it drifted slowly upward.
Suddenly Zann felt a yank. Wyssa was pulling him back down. "Wake up!" she ordered loudly. "You too, girl!" The old woman bounced away and grabbed Perda, pulling her over to Zann's cloud.
Perda opened her eyes. "What's going on?"
Now Zann was falling back to sleep. Breathing desperately, Wyssa gave him a good kick to the shin.
"Ow," Zann mumbled, scooting away from her foot. "I just want a quick nap, that's all."
"You must fight it!" cried Wyssa. "Do not fall asleep!"
Zann looked at her with half-closed eyes. "Did you say something?"
He heard a snore and saw Wyssa turn her head quickly. Perda was floating upward again. The dark cloud was very close now.
"Wake . . . up," said Wyssa, pinching Perda. The old woman was beginning to sound sleepy herself.
"Stop," Perda protested weakly.
Zann noticed his stick was getting closer and closer to the dark cloud, which was now directly above him. He closed his eyes and felt his body move up off his cloud once more.
Nearby he heard Wyssa mumbling. "If the flizzes don't return soon, we'll have to . . ." She slowly closed her eyes and drifted into sleep.
Zann smiled. "This is so relaxing. I could stay . . . here . . . forever."
Suddenly a bolt of magic energy shot from the dark cloud, obliterating Zann's stick.
Zann opened his eyes for a moment. "What was . . . ?" Before he could finish, Zann fell back to sleep, unaware of the danger right above him.
"I hope Darb and Gliss came here," Zann mumbled in his sleep. "It's so relaxing."
Zann's mind drifted in and out of a dreamlike state. Empty of all energy, all he wanted to do was float, float, float.
He was roused slightly by the buzz of the flizzes as they returned and zipped around Wyssa. Her eyes popped open, and she dropped back down to the cloud.
"Thank goodness," she said faintly.
Zann heard Wyssa call his name, but he didn't respond. Then he felt a hard pinch. "Ouch!" he yelped. He heard Perda cry out as well.
"We need to get to the wormhole!" Wyssa said. "The flizzes said your friends aren't here."
Something seemed to be holding Zann back. He heard a crackle overhead. The dark cloud was so close he could almost touch it.
He reached out but suddenly felt himself pulled backward.
"Let's go, you two!" Wyssa cried in frustration.
Just as another bolt of energy shot out from the dark cloud, Wyssa dragged Zann and Perda into the wormhole.
"Whoa!" Perda cried as the three of them tumbled wildly through the vortex. "What's happening?"
"That place drained almost all our energy," Zann said, beginning to wake up a bit. "Even Wyssa's!"
Wyssa lunged at the next wormhole they passed, scrabbling for a hold. It was nothing like her usual, effortless navigation.
"Come," she croaked weakly. With a grunt she pulled herself through.
"Ouch!" someone said when Zann landed on the other side.
"Sorry!" Zann scooted aside quickly, fearing he'd just crushed some tiny native of this world.
But he didn't see anyone. All he saw was a small rock.
"That's better," the voice said.
"Who said that?" Zann demanded.
"I did," the voice came again. "Right in front of you."
Wyssa smiled weakly. "Ah, we're in Gabble. Sorry about this young man's clumsiness, friend."
"Who are you talking to?" Perda asked. "Are the people here invisible?"
"Not at all." Wyssa bent and patted the rock. "In Gabble, everything has a voice. Not just people, but plants, animals, and other objects as well."
Zann's jaw dropped. "You mean we're talking to . . . a rock ?"
"You can call me Gray," the rock said cheerfully.
Zann and Perda stared in amazement.
"Don't stand there staring like idiots," Wyssa said. "Introduce yourselves!"
"Um, hello," Zann stammered. He and Perda introduced themselves to the friendly rock.
"Welcome to Gabble," the rock said.
