"Thank you," Wyssa replied. "This will be a safe place to rest," she told Zann and Perda.
Zann felt a flash of anxiety. How much time had they wasted in that cloud world? "Rest? But our friends—" he began.
"Are still out there somewhere, yes," Wyssa said. "But we're no use to them until we've regained our energy. That requires time."

Zann realized she was right. So he and Perda wandered around, chatting with various plants, animals, and other objects. As Perda got involved in a discussion with an opinionated squirrel, Zann talked with a tree.
"What brings you to Gabble?" the tree asked.
"It's kind of a long story . . ." Zann described their escape from the cloud world. That led to more questions. Before he knew it, Zann was telling the tree the whole story.
"Oh my," the tree said sympathetically. "I hope you find your friends soon. Then you can return to searching for your parents."
"I hope so." Zann sighed. "I'm afraid Wyssa will make me go back to Magica once we find the others."
"Can she do that?" the tree asked.
"She can try." Zann squared his shoulders. "But she won't succeed. I'll sneak away if I have to!"
Just then Perda called him over to settle an argument between her and the squirrel. After that Zann had a long conversation with a pretty flowering vine.

"Zann!" Wyssa snapped, stomping over and interrupting. "A tree just told me you're planning to sneak off and look for your parents. Forget about that crazy plan right now. It's far too dangerous." She stomped off again.
"I can't believe that tree told Wyssa my plans!" Zann complained.
The vine chuckled. "We residents of Gabble love to talk."
Zann saw Perda hurrying toward him. "Keep quiet about this, okay?" he whispered. "Please!"
"I'll try." The vine sounded doubtful. So Zann intercepted Perda, dragging her off to talk to a boulder instead.
Ten minutes later Wyssa approached. "It's time to go," she said. "We should be recovered well enough by now."
"She's right, I feel better. Come on!" Perda hurried toward the wormhole.
Zann started to follow, but then he heard his name. A bird landed on a branch beside him.
"Don't fret," the bird chirped. "Wyssa wants to find your parents as much as you do."
"No, she doesn't." Zann kicked at the dirt.

"I heard her muttering to herself just now," the bird said. "When I asked why she was upset, she said that she feels responsible for your parents' disappearance. She wants to find them and help get them back to your home world."
Zann frowned. "Really? How's she going to do that?"
"I don't know," the bird admitted. "She stopped talking after that."
"Zann! Now!" Wyssa shouted.
Back in the vortex, Zann thought about what the bird had said. Could it be true? He was distracted by a bright purple glow.
"Someone has passed this way very recently," Wyssa said. "Hold on!"
She pulled them through another wormhole and into a bustling city. Zann landed hard, scraping his knee.
"Ow." He snapped his fingers. "Heal!"
Nothing happened. "Let me try," Perda said. "You've always done sloppy Healing spells."
"Don't bother," Wyssa said. "Your Healing spells won't work here. We've just landed in a world with no magic at all."
"We're in a world with no magic?" Perda exclaimed. "You must be kidding!"
"Not at all." said Wyssa. "Such places do exist."

Feeling worried, Zann gulped. He and Perda had been unable to use their magic on other occasions. Like when Morb was tracking them, or when they were in the Cave of the Unknown. But this situation was much worse. Zann felt completely helpless knowing that he couldn't use magic, even in an emergency.
"This must be what it feels like to be a Void," Perda said, her voice shaking.
"Or under a Dousing spell," Zann added, thinking briefly of Venna.
"Don't get distracted," Wyssa ordered. "The signal that brought us here was strong and recent. If your friends are here, we need to find them quickly. And it won't be easy, since we can't use magic."
Zann took a deep breath. "Okay. If they came through the same wormhole, they should still be nearby, right? After all, they wouldn't be able to zap anywhere else."
"Good thinking, boy." Wyssa sounded almost impressed.
"Speaking of the wormhole, I guess we can't use magic to find it again," Perda pointed out. "We'd better make sure we remember where it is."
Zann nodded. The wormhole had closed as soon as they stepped away. But he remembered where it was. He stepped toward the spot, waiting for the wormhole to open again.
But nothing happened. "Are you sure it was there?" Perda asked. "Maybe it was a little more to the left."
Zann took a step to the left. The wormhole still didn't appear.
"Use your heads, you two," Wyssa said harshly. "You need magic to open a wormhole. Everyone knows that!"
She turned and hurried off, leaving Zann and Perda staring at each other.
"But . . . if there's no magic here—" Zann began.
". . . we have no way of opening the wormhole!" Perda swallowed hard. "So how are we ever supposed to leave this world?"
Wyssa had almost disappeared into the crowds. "We'll have to worry about that later, I guess," Zann said. "First, let's find the others."
He and Perda followed Wyssa, which wasn't easy. This world was much more crowded than anywhere in Magica, even First City.
"How are we going to find our friends among all these people?" Perda wondered as she and Zann finally caught up with Wyssa.
Wyssa stared around uncertainly. "I'm not sure," she admitted. "I suppose we'll just have to start looking."
A toddler passed by, clinging to her mother's hand. The little girl babbled curiously, pointing at Zann's head.

"I think she was staring at my hair," Zann said as the mother pulled the toddler away. Glancing around, he noticed something. "Look, almost everyone here has dark hair. That should make it easier to spot Darb and Gliss."
"You're right!" Perda exclaimed. "Gliss has bright red hair like yours. And Darb's is light. Both of them should stand out in this crowd."
Wyssa looked relieved. "Yes, that's true. Come, let's ask the natives if they've seen them."
Zann stopped a man who was passing by. "Pardon me," Zann said. "Have you seen a girl around here with hair like mine?"
The man paused and stared at Zann. "No, I'm sorry," he said. "Is she lost? Perhaps you should notify the police."
"The police?" Perda said as the man moved on. "What's that?"
"I have no idea," said Wyssa. "Let's check in here."
She led the way into a marketplace. It was even more crowded than the street outside.
"Look at all this stuff," Zann said. "Do you think it's food?"
"Yes—look!" Perda pointed. "Here's a whole bin full of turnips. Teplo was right. They do come from another world!"
"If turnips originally came from this world, that means somebody traveled from here to Magica," Zann said. "So there must be a way to open the wormhole without magic!"
"True." Perda picked up a turnip. "How do you think the people here create their food without magic?"
Just then a woman came over. "May I help you?" she asked.
"We're looking for our friends," Zann said. "A red-haired girl, a light-haired boy, and a small dragon."

"A dragon, huh?" The woman laughed, even though Zann hadn't said anything funny. "The only dragon I've seen lately is right over there." She pointed at a banner with a picture of a fierce golden dragon on it.
"No, Zing is much smaller, and—" Zann began. But the woman was already talking to another customer.
After that Zann, Perda, and Wyssa asked more people if they'd seen Darb, Gliss, or Zing. However, as soon as Zann described Zing, people either laughed at him or got angry and hurried off.
"I'm serious!" Zann insisted as yet another woman chuckled and shook her head. "He's about this big, with reddish-colored scales . . ."
"Very funny, young man." The woman smiled. "Excuse me, I'm late for work."
As the woman hurried off, Perda sighed with frustration. "This place is weird. It's like nobody here has ever seen a real dragon before!" she exclaimed.
Zann felt a tap on his shoulder. Turning, he saw a young man.
"Excuse me," the man said. "You're looking for a dragon? A real one?"
"Yes!" Zann suddenly felt hopeful. "His name is Zing. Have you seen him?"

The man indicated for them to follow. He led the way out of the market, across the street, and into a shop. The shop was crammed with knick-knacks, including a whole shelf full of fake dragons. For a moment Zann was afraid that the man had misunderstood him.
"This way," the young man said, stepping into a dimly lit back room.
Zann entered and gasped. "Zing!" he cried, spotting his dragon cowering behind the bars of a small metal cage.
"Zing!" Zann cried again, relieved. "Hey, little buddy. Let's get you out of there."
He reached for the latch on the cage. The young man stopped him.
"Not so fast," the man said. "This creature is one of a kind—that makes him quite valuable. I can't just let you take him."
"What do you mean?" Perda said. "He belongs to Zann. Zing is his pet."
The man smiled slyly. "He was wandering loose when I found him. That means he belongs to me now."
Zann could hardly believe his ears. "But he wants to be with me! See?" He pointed to Zing, who was jumping excitedly.
"I'm not saying you can't have him," the man said. "I'm saying you must pay."
"Pay?" Zann wasn't sure what the man meant.
Wyssa stepped forward. "We have no money," she said. "Perhaps you'll accept this in trade?" She pulled a shiny stone out of her clothes.

Zann finally realized what the man wanted. In Magica most people could acquire whatever they needed through magic. But Voids sometimes traded for goods and services. And this was a whole world of Voids!
The man examined the stone, and then tossed it back. "Not good enough. I'm sure I can find a buyer who's willing to meet my price for a real, live dragon!"
Zann was furious. First he'd lost his parents, and then his friends. Now this man was trying to steal his dragon!
"You can't do this!" Zann yelled. "You have no right to keep him!"
"Yeah!" Perda added. "He's Zann's!"
An old woman peered into the room. She'd been sitting behind a tall counter when Zann and the others had entered, though she'd paid them no attention.
"Is everything all right?" she asked. "I heard yelling."
"It's nothing, Grandmother," the young man said quickly. "We're just talking."
"Why don't you tell her the truth?" Perda snapped. "You're stealing Zann's pet!"
The old woman peered at the cage. "What an odd-looking dog," she commented. Then she turned to the young man. "What's the problem, Hyun? Give the kids back their pet."
"But Grandmother!" the young man began.
"No back talk!" the old woman scolded.
Slowly she walked to the back of the shop and opened the cage. "There you go, young ones!"
Zing flew out and dive-bombed the young man. "Ah!" the man cried. "It's trying to bite me!"
"No," Zann said. "He's trying to flame you." He guessed that without magic energy, Zing couldn't create fire. "Come on, boy. Let's get out of here!"
"Thank you, ma'am," Perda said to the old woman.
"Stop, thieves!" the young man yelled.
Zann, Perda, and Wyssa ran out of the shop with Zing flying overhead. They didn't slow down until they were several blocks away.
"Whew!" Perda said when they finally stopped to catch their breath. "I've never been so glad to see you, Zing."
"Me too," said Zann, scratching the dragon's knobby head. Zing panted with delight. "But where are Darb and Gliss? They must be in this world too!"
"Zing probably doesn't know; they obviously got separated," Perda pointed out.
"Perhaps he can lead us to where he last saw them," Wyssa suggested.
Zing seemed to understand. With a whistle he took off and flew down the street. The others followed.
They ended up in front of an interesting-looking building. The area was just as busy as the rest of the city.
"Look!" Perda exclaimed. "There's someone with red hair!"
They all rushed over. But when they got closer, Zann saw that the redhead was a short, stout man—not Gliss.

Looking around, he saw more people with light hair. Zann clenched his fists in frustration. How would they ever find Gliss and Darb without magic? Why did they have to end up here of all places? If none of them ever made it home to Magica, it would be all Zann's fault. And he couldn't stand that thought! How could he have been so angry with Gliss before? She was the one who should be mad at him for dragging her into danger. Darb too.
The others were still searching for their friends. But Zann stopped, completely overwhelmed by guilt and despair.
"Zann!" a familiar voice cried.
Zann gasped. "Gliss?"
Spinning around, he saw Gliss racing toward him. Darb was right behind her.
"Oh!" Perda cried, running to meet them. Zing flew after her. Zann, Perda, Darb, Gliss, and Zing all met in an excited tangle of hugs, laughter, and relief.
"I was afraid we'd never see you guys again!" Gliss exclaimed.
"Us too," Perda said.
Darb gave Zing a scratch on the head. "I'm so glad you found Zing. We were looking for some food and when I turned around, he was gone!"
"That guy must have grabbed him," Zann said.
"What guy?" Gliss asked.
Zann and Perda told their friends about the young man named Hyun. That led to more questions, especially when Wyssa joined in. Both sides ended up sharing the stories of what had happened to them.
"And then Zing led us here," Zann finished.
"Yes," Perda said. "But there were so many people here I was ready to give up! How did you find us?"
"It was Zann." Gliss glanced at Zann shyly. "We had a . . . Red Share."
Zann was amazed. "A Red Share? But I thought that required magic."
Wyssa looked thoughtful. "I thought so too. Perhaps this land is not completely devoid of magic after all."
"Does that mean there's enough magic to open the wormhole?" Perda asked hopefully.
"No, I'm afraid not," Wyssa said.
Everyone stared at the old woman.
Finally Gliss said what they were all thinking. "How are we going to get back to Magica?"
"Don't fret," Wyssa said. "I learned magic in a world nearly as devoid of natural magic as this one."
"Really?" Gliss said. "You can get us home?"
"I know some tricks," Wyssa said. "First we need to find a spice market."

She led them in and out of several shops, gathering mysterious ingredients—a strong-smelling powder, some dried leaves, a ceramic bowl, and more. After a while Zann noticed that they were attracting more and more attention.
Perda noticed too. "People are staring at us," she whispered.
"I think they're staring at Zing," Darb said, sounding worried. "What if someone else tries to grab him?"
"Or what if the man who took Zing finds us?" Zann said. "He seemed really angry."
He felt nervous as Wyssa led the way back to the wormhole. They were pretty close to the young man's shop. What if he spotted them?
"Do you think this will work?" Gliss whispered as Wyssa started mixing ingredients and muttering spells under her breath.
Zann shrugged. He knew that Wyssa was powerful. After all, she'd rescued him and Perda from that scatter beast.
Then again, Zann couldn't help thinking about another time when Wyssa had lost control of a scatter beast. Maybe she wasn't quite as powerful as she let on.
A little boy came toward them, kicking a ball. "Hi," he said, staring at Zing. "What's that?"
Zann and his friends exchanged a cautious look. "Um, what does he look like?" Perda asked the boy.
"He looks like a dragon," the boy said. "But dragons aren't real. My daddy said so."
Zann glanced at Wyssa. She'd finished mixing and was stepping toward the spot where the wormhole should be.
"Excuse us," Zann told the little boy. "We're kind of busy."
The boy ignored him, stepping closer to Zing. "There's no such thing as dragons," he insisted. "So what is he?"

Zann was so anxious that he lost his patience. "There might not be dragons in your world, but there are in ours," he snapped. "We're trying to get home, and we're worried that a bad man might try to stop us. So we don't have time for questions, okay?"
The boy took a step back. He didn't say anything.
"That wasn't very nice," Darb whispered.
Zann shrugged. He felt bad, but he tried not to worry about it. All he cared about was getting out of this no-magic world.
Just then a shout came from across the street. "Oh no!" Perda hissed. "It's the guy who took Zing!"
The young man raced toward them clutching a large net. Behind him were two other men. They didn't look friendly.
Zann glanced at Wyssa. She was sprinkling her potion over the wormhole, which was starting to glow. But the men had almost reached them!
"Hurry!" Gliss screamed. "They're coming!" She grabbed Darb and crowded toward the wormhole. Zann grabbed Zing and did the same. But it was opening so slowly.
"Stop, thief!" the young man shouted. "That dragon is mine! I—whoa!"
The little boy had kicked his ball. The man tripped over it and slammed facedown into the pavement.
"Oh no!" the other men cried, but they were running too fast to stop. They fell on top of their friend.
"The wormhole's open!" Perda cried.
"Let's go," said Wyssa.
Everyone held hands as Wyssa pulled the group into the wormhole. Zann barely had time to glance back at the little boy, who was grinning at the fallen men.
"Thank you!" Zann shouted to the boy.
The boy waved. "You're welcome!"
Then Zann found himself back in the vortex.
"Whew!" Perda exclaimed. "I've never been so glad to be in this crazy place."
Gliss laughed. "Yeah. At least there's magic here!"
"We'd better stop and rest," Wyssa said. "Being in a world without magic might have weakened our energy. And we'll need plenty to get safely back to Magica."
She pulled them through another wormhole. This time there were no people or buildings in sight. A babbling brook weaved its way through a grove of purple-leaved trees waving in a soft breeze.
"The magic here isn't particularly strong," Wyssa said. "But there's enough to conjure food and fresh clothes. Then you'd better sleep for a while."
"Good idea." Gliss stifled a yawn. "I feel as if I haven't slept in days!"

Soon they were all clothed and fed. Zann lay down beside his friends, his mind racing with questions and plans. Wyssa knew he wanted to search for his parents. How could he get away without her noticing?
Before he could figure it out, his weariness overcame him and he drifted off to sleep.

He woke some time later, his heart pounding. He'd just had a dream about his parents again. This one had been especially intense, though Zann couldn't remember much about it. Just that his father was trying to tell him something about Morb.
"Weird," Zann muttered. He reached into his pocket and touched the message stone. It was warm. That was weird too.
"Are you awake, boy?" Wyssa stepped into view. "Good. We shouldn't stay here much longer."
"Why not?" Zann asked. "What world is this, anyway?"
"It's my home world," Wyssa admitted. "I'm, er, not exactly welcome here anymore. Besides, I promised your grandfather I'd get you kids home as quickly as possible."
"Boz?" Zann was startled. "What does he have to do with this?"
Wyssa turned away without answering, nudging the others with her foot to wake them. "Time to go," she said. "Next stop, Magica."
Zann's friends cheered. But Zann felt his heart sink. He should have sneaked away while the others were sleeping. How was he ever going to escape from Wyssa now?
"I can't go back to Magica!" Zann blurted out. "Not without finding my parents."
"Don't be a fool, boy," Wyssa snapped.
"I know I can find them," Zann retorted. "I even have a clue—World X. I know my parents wanted to find it. Maybe that's where they are—they could be trapped there!"

Wyssa looked startled. "How do you know about—never mind," she said, interrupting herself. "Yes, it's true they wanted to find World X. But I have no idea where it is. I promise I'll try to find out—after you and your friends are safely back in Magica."
"That sounds like a good offer, Zann," Gliss said.
Ignoring her, Zann glared at Wyssa. "They're my parents," he said. "Nobody cares about finding them as much as I do!"
"I'm not so sure about that, boy," Wyssa muttered. "Morb is—" Once again she stopped herself.
"Morb?" Perda spoke up. "What does he have to do with this?"
"Forget it. I shouldn't have said anything." Wyssa stalked off toward the wormhole. "Let's go."
"Not until you tell me what's going on," Zann said. "Why did you mention Morb? Is he looking for my parents too?"
Wyssa scowled and then sighed. "I suppose you deserve to know. Maybe it will convince you not to rush off by yourself. Yes, I've heard rumors that Morb is looking for your parents. Nobody knows why."
Zann froze. What could Morb possibly want with Zann's parents?
"Hold on," Perda said. "How can Morb be searching for anyone? I thought he went back to being a Void when Zann defeated him."
"I don't know how he's able to use the wormholes," Wyssa said. "But he's not keeping his search a secret." She grimaced. "He's left a trail of terrified worlds behind him."
Perda's eyes widened. "That must be why the Skellians freaked out when we mentioned Morb's name!"
"Whatever," Zann said to Wyssa. "I'm still not going back to Magica." He rubbed both hands on his legs, hoping this spell would work. Touching the trunk of a sturdy tree, he cried, "Shackle!"
It worked! Magical shackles appeared, binding Zann to the tree.
Wyssa gnashed her teeth. "Stop this foolishness! Remove those shackles at once, or I'll do it for you."
"You can't," Perda said. "Nobody can remove another person's Shackle spell."
"She's right. And you won't change my mind," Zann said. "Take my friends home, and then we can search together. Otherwise I'll search on my own."
"You don't know what you're doing, boy." Wyssa narrowed her eyes at Zann. "If even half the rumors about Morb's new powers are true, you won't have a chance against him."
Zann stared at her. "You can't make me do anything," he said defiantly. "You didn't even know when Morb was tricking you!"
"What are you talking about?" Wyssa demanded.
"When you sent my parents off course with that scatter beast, it wasn't an accident," said Zann. "It was part of Morb's plan. He told me so himself."
Wyssa's eyes went wide. "What?" Her yell echoed through the quiet forest. She leaped forward and touched Zann's forehead. "Truth!" she intoned.
"Ow!" Zann yelped as he felt a sizzling sensation in his head. A second later Wyssa backed away, her eyes burning with rage.
"So it is true," she said through gritted teeth. "I've been torturing myself all these years, thinking I was to blame for your parents' disappearance. Morb will pay for this!"
Alarmed, Zann glanced at his friends. They were all staring at Wyssa in silence. Zing cowered behind Darb.
Wyssa swept toward Zann again. "Release!" she said.
The shackles exploded. Zann gasped. "How did you—"
Before he could finish, Wyssa grabbed Gliss. "You're in charge now, Red," Wyssa said. "Take Zann and these others straight back to Magica."
"I . . . I . . . ," Gliss stammered. She seemed too scared to speak.
"This will ensure that you follow my orders, girl."
Wyssa put her hands over Gliss' face. When the old woman pulled them away, glowing purple goggles covered Gliss' eyes.

"Those goggles will show you the way," Wyssa said. "They'll also provide extra magic for navigating the vortex. But don't try to remove them until all of you are safely back in Magica, or you'll suffer intense pain."
"I . . . I understand," Gliss said.
"Good." Wyssa leaped for the wormhole. "Revenge will be mine!" she cried as she disappeared.
"Wow," Perda said, her voice shaking. "That was scary!"
Zann nodded, no longer doubting Wyssa's power. For a moment they all stayed quiet. "Maybe Wyssa is right," Zann thought. Maybe it was better to let her handle the search . . .
Finally Gliss spoke up. "Zann, what do you want me to do?"
Zann turned to her and sighed. "It's not like we have much choice."
"There's always a choice." Gliss took a deep breath and reached for the goggles.
"No!" Darb cried.
"Gliss!" said Zann. "You don't have to—"
"Aah!" cried Gliss, ripping the goggles from her face. She collapsed on the ground, writhing and crying out in pain.
Darb rushed over to her. A minute later she was able to climb back to her feet.
"Th—there," Gliss said. "If you want to continue your search, I won't stop you. In fact I'll come along."
Perda looked at Zann. "We all will."
Zann gulped. Putting himself in danger was one thing. But could he also risk his friends' lives again?
"Are you sure?" he asked.
Gliss, Perda, and Darb nodded. Zing let out an excited whistle.
Zann suddenly felt braver. He and his friends had defeated Morb once before. They made a powerful team, the kind of team that could do anything.
"Okay," he told them. "Let's go!"
Zann's friends headed toward the wormhole. Zann noticed that Gliss' arms and legs were shaking. He winced, remembering how painful it had looked when she'd ripped off the magical goggles.
"Wait," he said to his friends. "Are you sure you want to come with me? I mean, really sure? It could be dangerous. Especially if Morb is involved."
"Of course we're sure," Perda said. "Right, guys?"
Gliss was still trembling, but she smiled. "You'd better not quit now, Zann. I don't want to think I defied Wyssa's command for nothing!"
"Yeah." Darb took Gliss' hand. "Besides, we make a good team. And we want to help.""Okay. Thanks." Zann glanced at the wormhole. "But we don't have Wyssa to guide us anymore. We need a plan."
"Good point." Perda paced back and forth in front of the wormhole. "Does anyone have any good ideas?"
"Wyssa said Morb left a bunch of terrified worlds behind him," Darb said. "Maybe we could start visiting worlds and asking people about Morb. That might give us some clues."
Zann shook his head. "I'm not sure we should visit worlds randomly. We might end up back in that no-magic world again."
Perda shuddered. "Or Fardark, or stinky Niffia, or that crazy cloud world."
She was still pacing. Just then her foot hit a stone, which tumbled toward Zann.
"Hey, check it out," said Zann, bending down to pick up the stone. "This looks just like my message stone!"
Perda shrugged. "So what? It looks like a stone."
"No, I mean I think they're the same type of stone." Zann fished out his message stone. It still felt warm. He held the two stones side by side. "See?"
"Weird," Darb said. "They do look alike."
Gliss glanced around. "Look, there are more stones like that!"
She was right. Dozens of similar stones lay near the wormhole.
"I assumed my stone came from the Cave of the Unknown because I'd never seen one like it anywhere else in Magica," said Zann. "But maybe it actually came from this world."
"That makes sense," Darb said. "This is Wyssa's home world, right? That's probably why she used that stone to communicate with your parents."
"And with Morb," Perda added. "It also explains why none of us had ever heard of message stones before."
"Teplo and Boz knew about them," Gliss pointed out.
Perda shrugged. "They're Magic Masters. It's their job to know lots of obscure stuff."
Zann squeezed the stone in his hand. If his stone came from this world, that might explain why he'd had that extra-vivid dream here earlier.
"I think we should look for a place to play my parents' message again," he said. "There might be more clues."
"Clues? Like what?" Perda sounded dubious.
"I don't see any place to plug in the stone," said Gliss, looking around.

"She’s right," Perda said. "Anyway, I just thought of another plan. We should try to follow Wyssa. She's looking for Morb, right? And Morb is looking for Zann's parents. So if we can catch up to Wyssa, we might find Zann's parents too."
"Wyssa left a while ago, though," Darb said. "We'll never find her in the vortex now."
"Besides, how do we know we can trust her?" Zann asked. "Wyssa was the one who brought those flizzes to Morb. She also tried to bring him a scatter beast."
"That was earlier," Perda said. "She's not working with Morb anymore."
Darb shrugged. "Still, she may not be on our side. She broke Zann's Shackle spell and put that nasty spell on Gliss, remember?"
Gliss nodded. "Plus, she used a Truth spell on Zann without his consent, and—oh! That's it!"
"That's what?" Perda asked.
Gliss pointed at Zann's forehead. "Look! When Wyssa touched Zann's face to do the Truth spell, she left purple fingerprints on his skin!"
"She did?" Zann said, reaching up to wipe away the marks.

"Stop!" Perda leaped forward, grabbing Zann's hands before he could touch his forehead. "Don't wipe them off. Maybe we can use that purple stuff to track Wyssa the same way she used it to track Gliss and Darb!"
"I was thinking the same thing," said Gliss with a smile.
"You mean we can figure out which wormholes have been used recently, and see if she's in those worlds?" Zann said.
Perda looked excited. "It's the only good plan we have. What do you say, Zann?"
Zann turned his message stone over in his hand. "You're right," he said. "Let's not waste any more time."
"Okay." Gliss glanced at the wormhole. "We'd better make sure we're all shackled together this time. We don't want to get separated again."
"Good idea." Perda held out her hands. "Join friction, everyone. We'll make this one a Mutual Shackle spell so any of us can break it if we need to."
"Just don't do that in the vortex," Zann warned.
Soon the four of them were shackled together. Zann even conjured a harness for Zing.
"Everyone ready?" Darb asked.
"Let's go!" Perda said, leading the way toward the wormhole.
Zann held his breath as they all dived into the vortex. It felt much scarier being there without Wyssa. But he tried not to think about that.
"It's working!" Gliss cried, staring at Zann's forehead. "The fingerprints are glowing!"
Zann's left hand was shackled to Perda. He used his right hand to grab the nearest wormhole. "Hang on, everyone!" he cried as he yanked his friends through.
He felt the familiar sensation of passing through the wormhole. It felt weird but not unpleasant.
Splash!
"Drat! Aah!" Zann screamed in horror. They had just landed in a pool of boiling water!
I'm burning!" Zann screamed.
Only his head and shoulders were above the hot, bubbling water. His friends were screaming too. But Zann could only think about his own searing pain.
A sharp whistle came from overhead. Zing was flying back and forth between the kids and the rocky shore. Being a fire dragon, Zing was immune to heat and had already shaken off the hot water.
Seeing Zing cleared Zann's mind a little. The wormhole was over their heads—too high to reach. The shore was pretty far away. There was only one way he and his friends would survive this.
"Focus, everyone!" Zann yelled. "We have to zap out of the water!"
He hoped their magic would work in this world. If not . . . He tried not to think about it.
"Everyone join hands!" Gliss cried.
Zann felt someone grab his hand. He almost yanked it away because the touch hurt his injured skin. He forced himself to squeeze back though.
"Zap!" he cried.

He landed on the rocky shore with a grunt. The heat was gone. Well, some of it was gone. Looking around, Zann could see that they were in a world of flame and scorching heat. A fiery red sky hung overhead. Steam rose from the bubbling lake. Zann could already feel sweat beading on his burned skin. But at least he no longer felt as if his whole body were melting.
Gliss rubbed her hands together, wincing at the pain. Then she touched Darb. "Heal!"
Instantly Darb's skin went from fiery red to its normal color. "Thanks," he said, slumping with relief.
Gliss quickly healed herself next. Zann and Perda did the same.
"That was close." Perda looked around. "What world is this?"
"I don't know," said Zann. Zing landed, and Zann scratched the dragon's head. "Thanks for the help, little buddy."
Zing chirped, sounding nervous. A large shadow passed over the group. Glancing up, Zann saw an enormous dragon flying overhead. Luckily it didn't seem to notice them.
"We need to figure out whether Wyssa is here," Perda said. "Quickly."
Zann and his friends picked their way carefully up the rocky slope.
"There goes another dragon." Darb shaded his eyes to watch a shadowy creature fly by in the distance.
"Look out!" Gliss grabbed Darb and yanked him back. "You almost stepped in that puddle!"
Zann wasn't sure why she sounded so anxious until he looked down. Right near his feet was a puddle of burning hot lava!
"Everyone be careful," Perda warned.
They continued walking. Several more dragons flew by in the distance. The only other signs of life were a few scrubby trees and shrubs.
"This is crazy," Perda said after a few minutes. "How are we supposed to figure out if Wyssa or Morb is here?"
Gliss mopped her brow. "It seems like the kind of place Morb would like—dangerous and scary."
A scraping sound came from behind a house-sized boulder nearby.
"Shh," Zann whispered. "That could be an unfriendly dragon." He tiptoed around the boulder. A teenage boy was scraping at the dirt.
"Hey!" Zann blurted out. "It's a person!"
The boy spun around. "Oh! You startled me!" he exclaimed.
"Sorry. My name is Zann."
"I'm Arrano," the boy replied with a smile.
By then Zann's friends had appeared, and Zann quickly introduced them.
"What's the name of this world?" Perda asked Arrano.
Arrano looked surprised. "Don't you know where you are?"
"We just arrived through a wormhole," Gliss explained.

"Really? You came here, to Drac, from another world?" Arrano's friendly expression changed to a worried one. "We don't get many visitors here. It would probably be best for you to leave before they see you."
"Before who sees us?" Perda asked.
Arrano didn't answer. He was staring past the visitors.
Zann turned. A pair of dragons had just waddled into sight. They were a little smaller than Zing but much plumper, with shiny blue scales.
"Shoo!" Gliss said, waving her hands at the little dragons. "Get out of here!"
The dragons ignored her. Darb watched them with interest. "They look a little like river hoppers, don't they?" he remarked.
Zann nodded. "One of Boz's friends has a hopper as a pet. It's bigger than these though." He frowned as the dragons came closer. "And much less bold."
He turned, planning to ask Arrano how to get rid of the pests. To Zann's surprise, Arrano was nowhere in sight.
"Hey, where'd he go?" Darb wondered.
Perda shrugged. "He seemed kind of nervous or something."
"No wonder, living in a crazy world like this." Gliss shuddered.
Zing was glaring at the approaching dragons. He sent out a warning blast of flame. The smaller dragons jumped back.
Then one of them let out a sharp cry. The second one opened its mouth and shot out a stream of lava.
"Whoa!" Zann jumped aside. The lava hit a shrub, which was instantly burned to a stump.
"Okay, maybe they're not much like river hoppers after all," Darb said. "Let's get out of here!"
"Good idea." Zann whistled for Zing. "Come on, boy!"
Before Zing could get to Zann, one of the other dragons leaped up and batted him out of the air. Zing landed on the hard ground with a grunt and lay there stunned.
"Zing!" Zann cried. He tried to rush over, but one of the blue dragons blocked him with another lava blast.
"I've got him!" Darb dodged around the second dragon and grabbed Zing.
"Darb! Look out!" Gliss screamed.
Both dragons had turned toward Darb and Zing, who were now backed up against the huge boulder. The dragons moved closer.
"Uh-oh!" cried Darb. "I can't get past them—we're trapped!"
"Darb, run!" Zann yelled. "We'll meet you on the other side of the boulder. Then we can all zap away!"
Darb nodded and darted out of sight. The blue dragons waddled after him.
Zann and the others ran in the opposite direction, with Perda in the lead. Suddenly she stopped, and Zann almost crashed into her.
He quickly saw why. Arrano was nearby, talking to several adults.
"Arrano!" Zann exclaimed. "Where did you go before?"
Arrano turned to face him. "I had to summon the others before you got yourselves in trouble."
Just then Darb and Zing came around the other side of the boulder, running fast. "They're right behind me!" Darb cried.
"Oh dear." One of the adults bit her lip. "You must have angered them."
"Quick! Get behind us," a man said as Darb reached the group.

Zann grabbed Zing and huddled with his friends behind the Dracians, expecting them to fend off the dragons. But instead of fighting, the Dracians threw themselves onto their knees in front of the small creatures.
"What are they doing?" Gliss whispered.
Zann shrugged. The Dracians were talking now, but Zann couldn't understand their words.
"Weird," Perda murmured. "It sounds like they're begging or something."
Darb nodded. "And they must be speaking in the dragons' language."
The dragons looked irritated as they listened to the humans. One dragon spit a small glob of lava near the Dracians. Finally both dragons turned and waddled away. The Dracians climbed to their feet.
Arrano hurried over to Zann. "Let's go before the dragons change their minds."
The Dracians rushed away, and Zann and his friends followed. Finally everyone stopped in the shelter of a rock overhang.
"Whew!" one of the adults said. "You kids are lucky the first dragons you encountered were lava leapers instead of something bigger and less reasonable."
Arrano nodded. "Most dragons would have roasted you just for looking directly at them."
"What are you talking about?" Zann said. "Dragons don't usually attack people without a good reason."
Darb shrugged. "Maybe things are different here."
One of the adults eyed Zing. "Why does this dragon travel with you?" he asked. "Is he training you?"
"Zing? Training us?" Perda chuckled. "He's Zann's pet."
"Pet?" Arrano said the word as if he'd never heard it before. "What's a pet?"
Zann was confused. "Uh, he lives in my house and I feed him and play with him and stuff."
"Oh." Arrano's expression cleared. "You mean you're his servant."
Zann laughed, but quickly realized Arrano wasn't joking.
"Wait," Darb said. "I get it. In this world the dragons are the dominant species, aren't they?"
"Of course." Arrano sounded surprised. "Isn't it that way everywhere?"
"No," Perda said. "In Magica, humans are in charge."
The Dracians looked skeptical. "Humans rule over dragons?" a woman said. "Impossible. Who would serve the dragons?"
Another adult nodded. "And what would the dragons eat?"
Zann gulped. "Do dragons eat people here?"
"Yes, when necessary," Arrano said, "though most prefer other fare."
Zann wasn't sure what to say. It was weird to think about living in a world where people were dragons' servants—and sometimes their dinner. But he pushed the thought aside.
"We're looking for someone," he said. "Two people, actually. Their names are Wyssa and Morb."
The Dracians exchanged a glance. "They were both here," a man said. "Wyssa left shortly before you kids arrived."
"Yes," another man said. "She only stayed long enough to determine that Morb had moved on."
"When did Morb leave?" Perda asked.
"About ten days ago," Arrano said. "He was here for almost a week, though nobody knew his purpose."
"Did either of them mention World X?" Zann asked.
"World X?" A woman shrugged. "I don't think so. I've never heard of such a place."
Arrano and the others murmured in agreement. One of the women cast a nervous glance upward as several large dragons flapped past high overhead.
"You'd better return to the wormhole," she said. "It won't be long before you're noticed."
"Good idea." Zann glanced at his friends. "Come on, guys. Let's zap back to the boiling lake."
"Wait!" Arrano looked alarmed. "You shouldn't use magic. Some of the dragons can sense it. They might get curious and come to investigate."

All the Dracians were still watching the skies. Their anxious expressions reminded Zann of the people of Skellia. He wished he could have helped the Skellians escape their watery world. Maybe he could help these people now.
"Why don't you guys all come with us?" he blurted out. "We could take you to another world where you won't be ruled over by dangerous dragons."
To Zann's surprise the Dracians shook their heads.
"Leave Drac?" a woman said. "Oh, we couldn't."
"Thank you," Arrano added. "But Drac is our home. We wouldn't want to live anywhere else."

The Dracians offered to guide the visitors on foot to the wormhole. But Zann could tell that they were afraid. And no wonder! He couldn't imagine how it would feel to know that any passing dragon might eat you.
"Thanks, but we remember how to get back to the lake," Zann said. "Come on, guys."
Zann and his friends said good-bye and then set off through the scorched landscape.
"Are you sure we can't zap to the wormhole?" Perda complained after a few minutes, mopping her brow.
"We'd better not," Darb said. "You heard what the Dracians said."
The group walked without talking for a while. Zann frowned when they crested a ridge. A patch of tall trees lay below.
"I don't remember seeing any trees like that before." Zann's heart sank as he realized what this meant. "We're lost!"
"Now what?" Zann said.
He and his friends were huddled beneath some trees, hidden from the dragons flying overhead.
"This is bad," Perda said. "We're lost, and we don't have any way to contact Arrano and the others."
Just then a loud squawk came from directly above them.
"It's the dragons!" Gliss cried. "They found us!"
"No, wait." Darb peered up at the branches. "That didn't sound like a dragon."
Zann looked up too. A large bird was perched on an upper branch.
"That looks a lot like Teplo's sniffer goose," Darb said. "Only smaller and with a shorter neck."
Perda sighed. "This is no time for identifying native species, Darb. Besides, that goose doesn't look very friendly. Let’s get moving." She grabbed Darb's arm and started to drag him away.
"Quiet!" Gliss warned. "Here comes a dragon."
Zann hid behind a tree as a medium-sized dragon walked past. With every step thick orange smoke puffed out of its nostrils.
"This is crazy," Zann said once the dragon was out of sight. "We can't just wander around looking for that wormhole."
"Yeah," Perda agreed. "Besides, we'll have to use magic to levitate over the boiling lake anyway. Let's just save time and zap there."
"We can't," Gliss said. "We're lost, remember?"
"I can try a Seeking spell," Perda offered. "That's how I found the wormhole back in Swamp Bottom."
"Good idea," Zann said. "Join friction."
Perda, Gliss, and Zann rubbed their hands together. "Seek," Perda said.
"It's working!" Zann could feel the magic energy tugging at him.

The Seeking spell led them through the valley below the trees. Zann was climbing over some large rocks when he heard a rustling sound overhead. He looked up and saw a large dragon flying straight at them.
"Everyone get down!" he shouted.Zann threw himself behind a boulder. A blast of fiery air hit the spot where he'd just been standing.
"I think that's a flame fury!" Darb said. "Like the ones that powered the Dragon Wagon. They must come from this world!"
"Great," Gliss said grimly. "All the more reason to get out of here!"
"We'd better zap away," Zann said. "Zap!" He felt a twinge, but nothing happened.
"Oh no!" Perda cried. "That Seeking spell used up our magic energy!"
The fury was circling toward them again. Flames were already curling out of its snout. Darb stood up.
"Darb!" Gliss cried. "Get down!"
Cupping both hands around his mouth, Darb took a deep breath and let out a loud honking sound.
"What are you—" Zann began.
Suddenly an answering honk came from the direction of the trees! A second later the goose flapped into sight and spit a blob of goo directly at the dragon.
The fury howled, falling to the ground with an earth-shaking thump. It pawed frantically at its face, trying to rub away the thick goose spit.
"What are we waiting for?" Perda cried. "Run!"
Zann took off with the girls at his heels and Zing flying overhead. Darb paused just long enough to give a honk of thanks and then followed.
They'd only been running for a few minutes when they almost stumbled over a wormhole.
"The Seeking spell found a different wormhole!" Gliss exclaimed.
"Good," Perda said, panting. "We might not have enough energy left to levitate. And I definitely didn't feel like swimming in that lake again!"
Darb cast a nervous glance over his shoulder. "I think I hear that dragon coming. Hurry!"
Zann grabbed Perda's hand. Perda held out her hand to Gliss, who was holding Darb's hand. They all dived into the wormhole.
Soon the friends were hurtling through the vortex.
"Hold tight, everyone," Gliss said. "It makes me nervous to be here without our Shackle spell."
"Hey, Darb," said Zann. "How did you know that goose would help us?"
"I remembered the fake snuffer goose from the Dragon Wagon," Darb explained. "When I realized we were in the furies' home world, I guessed that goose we saw must have been a snuffer."
"But how did you know how to call it?" Perda asked.

"Because of Teplo’s pet sniffer goose," Darb said. "I picked up a few words of its language while we were staying with Teplo. Since sniffer and snuffer geese look similar, I guessed their languages might be related." He shrugged. "Luckily, I was right."
"Wow." Zann was impressed. He never would have thought of any of that! "You saved us from being roasted, Darb."
"Yeah." Gliss shuddered. "Roasted and eaten ."
"Hey, Zann," Perda said. "Your purple marks are glowing again."
Zann grabbed at the next wormhole and tumbled through it. Jumping to his feet, he was prepared to fight or run, but he quickly relaxed. This world didn't look scary at all.
"Where are we?" Gliss wondered, climbing to her feet.
Perda shrugged. "Wherever it is, it looks boring."

"Yeah." Zann stepped away from the wormhole, which swirled shut and disappeared, leaving almost no color anywhere. Everything—the sky, the ground, the trees and shrubs—was dull shades of beige and gray.
"At least there aren't any scary creatures attacking us," Gliss said.
Darb nodded. "I don't see any signs of people either. How are we going to figure out if Wyssa's here?"
"Zing!" Perda scolded. "Don't eat that. We don't know if it's safe."
The dragon was nibbling on a leaf. "He must be hungry," Zann said. "I am too. Let's conjure some food while we figure out what to do."
"I'll do it." Gliss rubbed her hands together, but nothing happened. She frowned. "It's not working."
"Uh-oh." Zann gulped. "What if we're stuck in another world without magic?"
"We can't open the wormhole again without magic!" Gliss exclaimed. "We could be trapped here forever!"
Crash !
Zann spun around as something landed behind them. It was a large platter of puckerberry pancakes!
"The food!" Darb said. "It's here. I guess the spell worked after all."
"It just took a long time." Perda stuck her finger in the pancake syrup and licked it. "Mmm!"
"It's weird that the spell took so long to work," Zann said. "We should try another spell and see if the same thing happens."
"I'll do it." Perda rubbed her hands together. "Levitate!"
They all waited. Several moments passed before Perda's feet finally lifted off the ground.
"Magic must work really slowly here, that's all." Zann stepped toward the wormhole and waited. Eventually it swirled open again. "Phew! We're not trapped after all."
"Good." Perda reached for a pancake. "Let's eat, and then we can look for Wyssa."
Darb peered into the distance. "Someone's coming."
Several people were moving slowly toward them. They were very slim and tall, with extra-long arms and legs. Their skin, hair, and clothes were the same dull colors as the rest of their world.
"Should we run away or stay and talk to them?" Gliss asked.
"They look pretty friendly," Perda said. "Besides, I'm guessing we can outrun them if we have to."
Several minutes later the natives reached the visitors. "Greetings, strangers," one of them said. His voice was slow but friendly. "Welcome to Chronos."
"Thank you," Zann said. "We just arrived through the wormhole."
"Is everything always so slow here?" Perda asked.
Long-drawn-out chuckles emerged from several of the Chronians.
"That's the first question every visitor asks," said one Chronian. "Yes, time moves more slowly here than it does in most other worlds."
"That's right," another Chronian continued. "For every hour that passes in Chronos, just seconds pass in the vortex or most other worlds."
Zann already felt impatient with the Chronians' slow speech. "Has anyone else visited lately?" he asked. "A woman named Wyssa?"
"Yes," one of the Chronians said. "Wyssa arrived here earlier. But she moved on immediately."
Zann frowned. Their tracking method was working. But they couldn't seem to catch up with Wyssa!
"Do you know where she was going next?" he asked. "Was it a place called World X? A newly discovered world?"
"Wyssa wasn't here long enough to tell us about her plans," a Chronian said.
Another Chronian spoke up. "Wait—Wyssa might not have said anything. But a traveler who passed by a few days ago did mention a new world."
"Really?" Zann spun to face him. "Was the traveler a tall, skinny guy named Morb?"
"No." A look of confusion passed slowly over the Chronian's face. "It was a trader who passes through Chronos frequently. He visits many worlds in his travels."
"What did he say?" Zann's heart pounded. Could this be the clue that would lead to his parents? Maybe they wouldn't need to catch Wyssa after all!
"The trader has heard rumors," the Chronian said. "Supposedly there's a world with wormholes that lead not only into the vortex, but directly into other worlds as well!"
"But that's not how wormholes work," Perda said. "You have to travel through the vortex to go from one world to another."
The Chronian shrugged. "I know. The trader wasn't sure it was true either. He hasn't seen this strange world himself."
"If it's real, it could be World X," Zann said. "It sure sounds like the kind of place that my parents would want to find." He glanced at his friends. "We should go!"
Perda yawned and reached for another pancake. "Why don't we rest here for a little while first? You heard what they said—even if we stay here for hours, only a few seconds will pass everywhere else."
Zann wanted to argue, but he could see that his friends were hungry and tired.
"All right," he said. "But let's make it a short rest, okay?"

The Chronians led them to a gray town nearby. The local innkeeper offered the visitors food and drink, which was nearly tasteless but filling. Then she showed Zann and his friends to comfortable beds.
Zann was sure he'd never be able to sleep. But he drifted off quickly and fell into another vivid dream. His parents were running in terror through a forest with dark magic swirling around them.

Like everything else in Chronos, the dream moved slowly. That gave Zann time to see details he hadn't noticed in his previous dreams. In the forest there were tiny houses with doors no higher than his mother's knee. While the forest seemed dark, the sky overhead was a brilliant shade of blue.

Zann finally awoke, blinking in the pale gray light. Could anything in his dream be a clue to finding his parents? Lots of worlds had blue skies. But not many worlds had such tiny houses. Even Fud from Galvan was too big to fit through those small doors.

Eager to get moving, Zann woke his friends. It seemed to take forever for the Chronians to guide them back to the wormhole. Then Zann had to wait for the mutual shackles to appear, and for the wormhole to open. But finally he and his friends were back in the vortex.
"Wow," Gliss said as wormholes rushed past. "It feels weird to be living at full speed again."
"Yeah." Darb looked at Zann. "Hey, the purple mark is glowing!"
"Good." Zann grabbed the next wormhole and pulled his friends through.
The world they landed in was dark, with jagged lightning splitting the sky. Zann recognized it and gasped.
Apparently Perda recognized it too. "Oh no! We're back in Fardark!"
"Let's get out of here!" Zann exclaimed. "Hurry!"
He and Perda yanked the others back through the wormhole before it could swirl shut behind them. Zann was relieved when they were back in the vortex.
"That was close," Perda said.
"Yeah," Zann agreed. "But what if Wyssa is in Fardark? Or Morb?"
"That definitely looked like the kind of place where they would hang out," Gliss said with a shudder.
"It doesn't matter," Darb said. "It was too risky to stay."
"Right," Perda agreed. "And if Morb and Wyssa had gone there, they probably would have moved on by now anyway. Nobody would stay in Fardark for long."
Zann thought of something. "Actually, we know my parents aren't there. The skies in Fardark are dark, not blue. Plus, Perda and I didn't see any creatures small enough to live in those tiny houses."
"Are you sure your dreams are showing you where your parents are?" Darb sounded dubious. Zann had told his friends about his latest dream while they all walked back to the wormhole in Chronos.

"The more dreams I have, the more sure I am," Zann replied. "I think the images are coming from my message stone. The most realistic dream I had was when we were resting in Wyssa's home world." He remembered something else. "Also, I bet that was Wyssa's world we passed the time I had the waking dream! Remember? All I saw through that wormhole were some trees with purple leaves—just like the ones in Wyssa's world!"
Gliss looked confused. "So we passed Wyssa's world twice?"
"Yeah. Perda and I ended up in Fardark twice too." Zann shrugged. "That does seem weird, now that I think about it."
"Not really," Perda said. "I did some research on the vortex back in Swamp Bottom, and—"
"You did?" Zann broke in.
Perda shot him a look. "I told you I was thinking about becoming an explorer. I started preparing by reading all your parents' books, including the one called Voyages Through the Vortex ."
"Oh." Zann was surprised she had read all of those books. "What did you find out?"
"Haven't you read your parents' books, Zann?" Gliss asked.
"Sure. I mean, some of them." Zann shrugged sheepishly. "Actually, I've mostly just looked at the pictures of the cool monsters and stuff. They wrote the vortex book when I was really young."

"The vortex isn't like a regular road or tunnel or anything like that," Perda explained. "It's just a magical space between worlds that's always shifting in unpredictable ways. Nobody knows exactly how it works. That's why it's important to have an experienced guide like Wyssa if you're not experienced yourself. You also need strong magic to help you navigate. Otherwise you can get yourself in trouble—at least that's what the book said."
"Your parents must have pretty strong magic, huh, Zann?" Gliss said. "Even though they're not Reds?"

"Yeah. Plus they have lots of experience traveling between worlds." But for once Zann wasn't really thinking about his parents. Perda's words had reminded him of Venna. She'd had very strong magic. But she'd been under a Dousing spell when she fell into the wormhole. What had become of her?
He pushed the thought aside, realizing that Perda was still talking.

"So there's no way to predict which wormhole we'll pass next," she was saying. "The next one could lead back into Magica. Or it could take us into Fardark yet again. Or into a brand-new world—maybe even one that's never been discovered before."
"Or World X," Zann murmured.
"Let me get this straight." Gliss sounded worried. "We have no way of finding a wormhole back into Magica?"
Perda shrugged. "Not unless we get lucky."
"Or find Wyssa," Darb said. "Or somebody else who can guide us."
"Like my parents." Zann felt a tingling on his forehead. The marks were glowing again. "Hold on!" he said, reaching for the next wormhole.
As he grabbed the wormhole’s edge, he caught a glimpse of blue sky. He tried not to get too excited though. Lots of worlds, including Magica, had blue skies. Still, he couldn't help hoping.
Splash !
"Drat—glurb!" Zann gurgled as he felt himself sinking under water.
"Oh no," he thought. "Did we land in Skellia again?"
But he quickly realized that this water was much calmer than the rough seas of Skellia. It was also much cooler than the boiling lake in Drac.
When Zann came up for air, his friends were bobbing in the water nearby. "Where are we?" Zann asked, pushing a clump of wet hair out of his eyes.
"I don't know," Gliss said. "But it looks nice."

They were in the middle of a large, tranquil lake. Pretty silver and gold fish darted around, nibbling at the swaying water grasses. On shore a green lawn sloped gently up to a lush forest. A gleaming city of elegant spires and towers stood atop a hill in the distance.
When Zann and his friends swam to shore, they heard birds singing and felt a warm, gentle breeze. The ground was soft and springy beneath Zann's feet.
He snapped his fingers to conjure dry clothes. "Good. Our magic works here," he said. He touched his hair to dry it. "I just have one question. Why are so many of the wormholes located over water?"
Darb started to laugh. Then he stopped, leaning closer to stare at Zann's forehead.
"Uh-oh," he said. "Zann, your face is clean!"
"Gee, thanks," Zann said. "Yours looks pretty clean too."
Perda gasped. "No, Zann. This is a problem!" she cried. "When your head went under water, Wyssa's fingerprints must have washed off. We have no way of tracking her anymore!"
"What?" Zann's hand flew to his forehead. The purple marks were gone!
"Maybe we can get them back with a Restore spell," Perda suggested.
"But we haven't learned those yet," protested Gliss.
"So what? It's worth a try." Perda rubbed her hands together. "Restore!"
Zann stared at her hopefully. "Well?"
"Nothing." Perda's shoulders slumped. "Sorry, guys."
Darb shaded his eyes. "Look, someone's coming."
A woman was walking toward them. She was blue-skinned and bald, with a pretty, smiling face.
"Hello," she greeted them. "My name is Vee. I am the guardian of the wormhole."
"Why does this wormhole need a guardian?" Perda asked.
"We've had some trouble lately," Vee replied.
"What kind of trouble?" said Gliss.
"The details aren't important." Vee was still smiling. "What brings you young people to Pax?"

"Pax? Is that the name of this world?" Zann didn't remember ever hearing his parents mention a world by that name. Perda didn't seem to recognize it either. That meant it probably wasn't in any of his parents' books.
"We're looking for two people," Gliss said. "A woman named Wyssa and a man named Morb."
Vee gasped, her pleasant expression turning fearful. "Why are you looking for Morb? Are you friends of his?"
"No way!" Perda exclaimed. "Morb is evil."
Vee looked relieved. "Yes, we know. He's the reason I was sent to guard the wormhole."
"So he was here recently?" Zann asked.
Vee nodded. "He visited Pax just long enough to steal a mibbit."
"A mibbit?" said Darb. "What's that?"
"One of our most cherished creatures," Vee said.

"Mibbits have very strong and specific magic, and they're prone to panic. When they panic, they send out powerful energy that overwhelms anyone nearby. Victims are unable to think or act or even move."
Zann and the others exchanged concerned glances.
"Uh-oh, that doesn't sound good," Perda said. "I bet Morb wants the mibbit to help him try to take over Magica again."
Vee looked confused. "What are you talking about?"
Zann quickly told her the whole story. "So that's why we're afraid that Morb might be gathering power again," he finished. "Maybe Morb is trying to force my parents to help him."

"Then again, maybe Morb isn't interested in Magica anymore," Darb suggested. "Your parents know a lot about other worlds, right? Maybe Morb is planning to use their knowledge to take over a different world this time."
"Like this one, maybe?" Gliss glanced around at the beautiful scenery. "It's really nice here. And Morb knows the mibbit's magic would definitely work on the people of Pax."
"Or maybe he wants to take over World X," Zann said. "That could be why he's after my parents. He wants them to lead him there!"
"That makes sense," Perda agreed. "If it's true that World X is some kind of gateway to all other worlds, controlling World X could give Morb incredible power."
"Oh dear," Vee said. "I fear the powers of our sweet mibbit could help Morb take over any world."
"How did he capture it, if it's that powerful?" Darb asked.
Vee looked nervous. "We don't know. It would take unimaginable power to immobilize a mibbit without panicking it."
"We really need to catch up to Wyssa now," Perda said. "We have to warn her about this!"
"You're right. I don't think she realizes just how much power Morb must have now," Zann said. "Plus she doesn't know about the mibbit."
"But how will we find Wyssa?" Gliss asked. "We've lost our only way of tracking her."
Zann turned to Vee. "Do you know of any magic that could help us track someone through the vortex?"
"I'm afraid not," Vee said. "Paxian magic is quite different from that of many other worlds. It mostly involves feelings and communications, not physical abilities."
"Really? But you guys must be able to do the basic stuff, right?" Perda asked. "Like conjuring food, performing Blast spells, or building houses by magic?"
"No, we can't do any of that." Vee sighed. "That's why Morb was able to overpower us so easily and steal the mibbit."
"Wow." Zann glanced at the distant city on the hill, awed to think that it had been built entirely without magic.
"That reminds me," Vee went on. "I should let my people know what you've just told me about Morb. Pardon me while I send them a mind message."
"A mind message?" Gliss echoed.
"It's a kind of telepathy," Vee explained. "We can all communicate within our minds anytime we wish."
"Cool," Zann said. "Too bad we can't do that!"
Perda smiled. "Yeah. It would save a lot of time, not having to inscribe message moths."
Vee closed her eyes. "I'll just be a moment . . ."
While Zann waited, he pulled out his message stone and stared at it helplessly. How could he find his parents before Morb did?
"What's that?" Vee asked when she opened her eyes.
Zann explained about message stones. "This one holds a message from my parents," he finished. "Too bad it can't tell us where they are now."
Vee smiled. "Perhaps I can help. All objects hold psychic traces of the people who last held them. I might be able to read your stone—if you want me to."
"Really? That would be great!" Zann handed her the stone.
Vee took it and closed her eyes. "The vision is faint, but I see two people: a man and a woman . . ." She quickly described them.
"That's them!" Zann cried. "My parents! What else can you see?"
"They're in a forest," Vee said. "They're surrounded by tiny people—the people don't even come up to your parents' knees."
Zann gasped. "World X! I knew it—my parents must be in World X!"
"I knew my parents were still out there!" Zann exclaimed. "They must have found World X."
"Yeah. Too bad we still don't know how to get there," Perda said.
Darb looked thoughtful. "We know World X has a blue sky. If we peek through the wormholes and check every world with blue skies, we'll find World X eventually."
Zann smiled hopefully. "That could work!"
"There are lots of worlds with blue skies though." Gliss glanced up at the Paxian sky.
"Yeah. Including that creepy no-magic world we got stuck in," Perda said.
"We'll be careful," Zann said. "We'll hang onto the edge of each wormhole so it can't close behind us. If we recognize that no-magic world, we can duck back into the vortex before we're trapped."
"Like we did the second time in Fardark," Perda said with a nod. "I guess that could work."
Vee was listening carefully. "If you find Morb, will you look for our stolen mibbit?" she asked. "We're very worried about it."
"Sure," Darb said. "What do mibbits look like?"
"I'll show you." Vee closed her eyes. Soon a small, fluffy creature hopped out of the forest.
Zing let out an excited chirp. "Not so fast," Zann said, grabbing the dragon. "That little critter is definitely not lunch."
"It doesn't look very scary," Perda commented as the mibbit nibbled at the grass.
Vee smiled. "I know. But trust me—you don't want to panic one."
"How can we rescue the stolen one without panicking it?" Darb asked.
Vee picked up the mibbit. It snuggled into her arms.
"If the mibbit panics, you can calm it by rubbing its ears." She demonstrated, and the mibbit let out a squeak of pleasure.
Darb was watching intently. "May I try?"
"Certainly." Vee held out the mibbit.
"Easy, little fellow," Darb cooed. He rubbed the mibbit's long ears.
Vee smiled. "The soothing effects usually last a couple of hours."
Perda looked impatient. "Let's get going. The sooner we warn someone about Morb, the better."
"Right." Zann took a step toward the lake. "Guess it's time to get wet again."
"There's no need for that." Vee set down the mibbit, which hopped away into the forest. "I can take you there by boat."
Minutes later Zann and his friends were back in the vortex.
"Pax was nice," Gliss said. "I wouldn't mind visiting again someday."
"Yeah." Perda laughed. "Just watch out for those scary mibbits!"
Zann was barely listening. He watched for glimpses of blue through the wormholes. The first world they passed showed a drab green sky, and the next two skies were gray.
Then he spotted a flash of blue. "There's one!" he cried.
He was so excited that he pulled himself all the way through the wormhole, flopping on his stomach on the other side.
"Oof!" Darb grunted as he landed beside Zann.
"Hey," Perda complained, sitting up. "You were supposed to hold onto the edge, remember?"
Zann's face flushed. "Sorry," he mumbled, glancing back at the wormhole as it swirled shut. "I forgot."
"Um, guys?" Darb said. "We're not alone."
Five girls stood in a semicircle, staring at the visitors. All of them were Zann's age or younger. They looked almost like regular Magicians, except for their green skin and vine-like hair.
"What are they?" one of the girls whispered to the others.
Zann climbed to his feet. "Hey. What world is this?"
The girls all stared at him. "It speaks!" one of them said.
Another girl noticed Zing. "Look, a dragon!" She let out a whistle. Zing chirped with delight and scampered over, snuggling against her leg.
Zann was surprised. Zing didn't usually warm up to strangers so quickly. Zann glanced at Darb, who shrugged.
One of the girls turned to address Gliss and Perda. "What sort of odd creatures are you traveling with?" she asked.
"You mean Zing?" Perda said. "He's a fire whistler."
Hearing his name, Zing let out another chirp.
"Not the dragon, silly," the tallest girl said, laughing. "We mean those creatures." She pointed at the two boys.
"Zann and Darb?" Gliss said uncertainly. "What do you mean?"
"They're so odd!" the girl said. "We've never seen anything like them! Are they dolls, made to look almost human?"
"Or perhaps some magical apparition?" Another girl looked excited. "We've heard tales of such things!"
"We're not dolls or apparitions," Zann said.
All the girls giggled and stared. "It speaks almost as if it understands us!" one exclaimed.
Gliss shook her head. "I don't understand. They're just boys."
"Boys?" The oldest girl echoed. "Is this a species related to humans?"
"Wow, you've really never seen boys before?" Perda sounded amazed. "How can that be?"
"Never mind," Zann said. "We're wasting time." He glanced at the spot where the wormhole had been. "Is there magic in this world?"
The girls stared at him in wonder, not responding. Perda repeated Zann's question.
"Of course there's magic here," one of the girls told her.
Next Zann asked about Wyssa and Morb. Once again the girls merely stared. But when Gliss repeated the question, the girls shook their heads.
"You're the first visitors in many moons," one said.
"Okay." Zann was already tired of the strange girls. "Then let's get going."
"Did you hear what it said?" a girl exclaimed.
"Yes. I'll fix it." The oldest girl let out a puff of air toward Zann and Darb. Suddenly the two boys were completely immobilized!
"Hey!" Zann cried—or tried to anyway. He could barely move his lips.
"What did you do to them?" Perda demanded.
The girls giggled. "They're fine," one said.
"Yes," another said. "We don't want them to run off just yet, that's all. First we must show them to Mother!"
"Who's Mother?" Perda asked.
"Come with us." The oldest girl blew at Zann and Darb.
Zann felt his feet lifting off the ground. He struggled against the spell, but it was no use.
"You can't do this!" Gliss protested. "It's kidnapping!"
The girls giggled. "Come, cute dragon!" a younger girl cooed at Zing, who bounded along happily.
"You'd better stop or else!" Perda warned.
"We must show Mother," the oldest girl said calmly.
"Halt!" Perda cried, rubbing her hands together.
Zann watched magic energy zip toward him and Darb. The tallest girl puffed out a breath.
Bang ! Perda's spell exploded and fizzled out.
"Whoa." Perda sounded impressed. "How'd you do that?"
"Come," the oldest girl said. "Let's find Mother."
The girls walked away, with the boys floating beside them.
"We shouldn't let them out of sight," Gliss told Perda.
Zann felt powerless as he drifted through the forest. Finally the whole group stopped at the base of an enormous tree.
"Here we are," a girl said. "Home."
She blew toward the ground and floated upward. So did her friends. Zann felt himself rise beside them, as Darb rose helplessly too. Zing flew along.
"Wait!" Perda cried. "What about us?"
"We'd better levitate." Gliss sounded nervous. "How high do you think they're going?"
"We'll bring you," the oldest girl said. "With your permission."
Perda looked uncertain. "Um, okay. You have our permission."
Soon Perda and Gliss were floating too. Perda ended up beside Zann.
"Are you okay?" she asked.
He couldn't answer. He couldn't even nod his head.
They floated up to a large, elaborate house built into the treetops. The girls led the way inside.
"Mother!" the youngest cried. "Look what we found!"
A woman looked up. She had green hair and skin like the girls, but her face was wrinkled and wise.
"Ah, visitors," she said. "Have my girls immobilized you? My deepest apologies."
She puffed out a breath, and Zann felt the spell dissipate.
"Be careful, Mother!" a girl said. "They were trying to escape."
Mother smiled. "Sit down, girls, and listen quietly while I talk with our visitors. This will be a learning opportunity for you."
The girls sat down, watching with wide, curious eyes.
"One thing they should do is learn not to immobilize people," Zann grumbled.
Mother chuckled. "Please forgive my girls. They've never left Zon, so they've never seen a male before. There are none here."
"What about you?" Perda asked. "You don't seem surprised to see boys."
"I traveled to many other worlds in my youth," Mother explained.
"Can we keep them?" one of the girls asked. "I've always wanted a pet!"
Mother smiled. "That wouldn't be right," she explained gently. "Boys are people too."
"Oh!" The girl looked disappointed. "If you say so, Mother."
Zann wanted to get away from these strange females. "We refuse to be held prisoner!" he declared, trying to sound tough.
"You're not prisoners," Mother said. "You're free to leave at any time."
"Good." Zann stomped toward the door. "Come on, guys."
"Wait," Gliss said. "Mother seems to—to know things. Maybe she can help us."
Zann hesitated. He still wanted to leave this place, but he realized Gliss was right. Mother seemed wise, and it was obvious that the people in this world had very strong magic.
"Please stay," Mother urged. "At least for a little while. My girls rarely get the opportunity to learn from strangers."
"Yes," a girl said. "We'd love to hear about your world."
"All right." Zann sat down. "We come from Magica, and we're looking for my parents . . ."
With help from his friends, he told the whole story.
". . . So we're checking every world with blue skies that we see," Zann finished. "That's how we landed here."

Mother laughed heartily. "Oh, I'm sorry to laugh!" she exclaimed. "But there are more worlds out there than you can possibly imagine. Many of them—perhaps most—have blue skies. You could get lucky and find World X on your next try. Or you could spend the rest of your lives searching in vain."
Zann frowned. "We have to try!"
Mother smiled sympathetically.
"I admire your spirit. Perhaps I can help. Do you have anything that belongs to the people you're seeking?"
Zann pulled out his message stone. "This came from my parents."
"Good." Mother leaned closer, blowing on the stone. "There. Now it should lead you straight to its rightful owners."
"Really?" Zann said. "It'll take us to my parents?"
"The spell never fails." Mother sounded confident. She turned to the girls. "Say good-bye to our visitors, girls. They must continue their quest."
"Do they have to go?" a girl cried. "We want to hear more stories!"
"Maybe another time," Perda said.
Darb peered out a window. "How do we get down? And how will we find the wormhole?"
"I can help with that too." Mother blew the door open. "Ready?"
Zann and his friends nodded. "Come on, Zing," said Zann.
Zing seemed reluctant to leave his new friends. But after more pats and kisses from the girls, he finally came to Zann.
"Farewell and good luck." Mother blew at them.
This time Zann didn't feel trapped by the spell. Mother's breath carried them gently but swiftly to the ground, through the forest, and finally to the wormhole.
"Wow, that was weird," Perda said as they landed.
"Yeah," Zann said. "But it worked out for the best, didn't it?" He reached into his pocket and touched his message stone. Would Mother's spell really lead him to his parents?
Zann and his friends re-shackled themselves and then jumped through the wormhole. Zann gasped as the message stone suddenly yanked him forward.
"It's working!" he cried.
Zann and his friends careened through the vortex. They were moving so fast that the passing wormholes all blurred together.
Seconds later they crashed into another world. There had been no chance of holding onto the edge of the wormhole this time. Zann felt himself fly at least a dozen yards into the new world.
Splash !
"Drat!" Zann sat up and looked around. The first thing he saw was the bright blue sky overhead. Then he noticed a wormhole winking right beside the stream he was sitting in.
That was weird. How could it still be so close?
"Zann!" Perda cried. "Look!"
She pointed at some houses nearby. They were no taller than Zann's knee.
"Yes!" Zann cried. "We're here—oof!"
He was yanked off his feet. Mother's spell was still working! The message stone pulled Zann and the others through the forest at such speed that Zann felt dizzy.
Thump !
"Ouch!" Zann blurted out as he bumped into something.
"Hey!" a disgruntled voice complained. "Watch where you're going."
Even before the person turned around, Zann knew exactly who it was.
"Wyssa!" He gasped. "Oh no!"
"What are you kids doing here?" Wyssa demanded.
"You?" Perda frowned at Wyssa as she brushed herself off.
Zann felt his heart sink as he realized the mistake. "Mother's magic brought us to the stone's rightful owner—the last person who possessed it."
"Wyssa," Darb said, realization dawning on his face.
Zann nodded, feeling crushed. "I can't believe I got my hopes up," he mumbled. "Stupid spell!" He tossed the message stone away.
Perda grabbed it. "You should keep the stone. It could still be a clue."
Zann frowned. "I never want to see that thing again."
Perda shrugged and tucked the stone into her own pocket.
Wyssa was glaring at all of them. "Well? Why aren't you kids in Magica?"
Gliss took a step backward. "Um . . ."
"Oh, never mind." Wyssa waved a gnarled hand. "I don't care. The important thing is I've found him! I've traced Morb to this world!" Her eyes glittered angrily.
"Really?" Zann still felt disappointed. But maybe all hope wasn't lost. At least they'd found Wyssa. And if Morb was here, maybe Zann's parents were too.
"Is this World X?" Gliss asked.
"I believe so. Look!" Wyssa snapped her fingers. Dozens of wormholes instantly winked into sight all around them!
Zann glanced into the nearest one. "That is so weird. I don't see the vortex at all. Just a bunch of trees."
"I see a dragon through this one!" Gliss said.
"It's true!" Perda looked awed. "The wormholes here lead directly into other worlds."
"Wow." Darb said. "So we could step straight back into Magica if we found the right wormhole?"
"Yes!" Gliss sounded excited. "I wonder how we could find it?"
Zann ignored them. "So where's Morb?" he asked Wyssa. "How do you know he's here?"
"I have my ways." Wyssa looked grim. "When I find him, I'm going to drag him straight through to Fardark, where I'll feed him to the first scatter beast I find!"
Zann gulped, thinking back to his time in Fardark. For a second he almost felt sorry for Morb. Almost .
Just then a tiny man hurried into view. "Wyssa!" he exclaimed. "I have news." He stopped short when he noticed Zann and the others. "Oh, you have company."
"Never mind them," Wyssa said. "Tell me what you know, Whistlefeather. Is he here?"
"Yes," Whistlefeather said fearfully. "Morb is indeed here in Rood. And we've heard that he's brought prisoners from Magica with him!"
"Prisoners from Magica?" Zann blurted out. "That's got to be my parents!" He grabbed Wyssa's sleeve. "We have to find them!"
"Thank you, my friend," Wyssa said to Whistlefeather. She shook off Zann's hand. Then, snapping her fingers, she zapped out of sight.
"No!" Zann cried.
"It's okay, Zann." Perda reached into her pocket. "We still have this, remember?"

Zann and his friends barely had time to grab one another before they were whisked off again by Mother's spell. They flew through the forest and up a steep hill before coming to an abrupt stop at a wall of rocks.
"You again!" Wyssa didn't seem pleased to see them. "Hush, or he'll hear us."
Zann glanced around. The rocks led to a gorge, on the other side of which was a massive waterfall. Over the roar of the water, he could hear voices.
Zann peeked over the rocks and gasped. It was Morb!
"Keep your head down!" Wyssa hissed.
Another person stood between the evil villain and the edge of the cliff.
"Oh!" Gliss whispered, peering out beside Zann. "Is that Venna?"
Venna was staring at Morb, looking terrified. "You can't do this!" she cried. "It's not right!"
Morb lifted a hand and rubbed his fingers together. " I'm the one who decides what's right around here," he sneered. "Now prepare to go for a little swim."
Venna glanced fearfully down at the water behind her. "No—p-please," she stammered.
"Why is she so scared?" Perda whispered.
"She must still not have magic," said Gliss.
"But she doesn't need magic to swim." Perda sidled closer to the cliff's edge. When she looked down, she saw why Venna was so scared. "Oh no!"
"What?" Zann moved over to peer down as well. "Oh, wow—is that a gulper?"
"I guess now we know why Morb went to Skellia," Darb said grimly.
"You have to stop him!" Zann urged Wyssa. "You have to save Venna!"
But it was too late. Just then Morb snapped his fingers. Venna screamed as magic energy shot from Morb's hand, sending her tumbling down into the gulper's waiting jaws!
Zann flinched as he heard the splash of Venna hitting the water. But he didn't dare move, not even to look over the edge of the cliff. Morb was still nearby.
"Good riddance," Morb muttered. He snapped his fingers and zapped out of sight.
"Come on." Perda rushed to the edge. "Maybe there's time to save Venna!"
Zann ran over and looked down at the dark water. Then he noticed Wyssa rubbing her fingers together. He guessed she was about to zap away to find Morb.
"Wait!" He ran to her and grabbed her arm. "Please. You have to help Venna."
"You help her if you like," Wyssa said harshly. "I have more pressing business."
"But she was Morb's prisoner, right?" Darb put in. "Maybe she can tell us more about his plans."
Now Wyssa looked much more interested. "Hmm," she said.
Suddenly everyone heard a splash from below.
Venna had popped to the surface of the water. She was slimy and breathless.
