"Help!" she cried as she desperately treaded water.
"Hold on!" Perda called down to Venna. She turned to Wyssa. "Hurry—before the gulper changes its mind."
Wyssa waved a hand. Venna levitated out of the gorge and landed beside the group, shaking and coughing.
"How did she escape from the gulper?" Gliss asked.
"Venna must still be under the Dousing spell," said Darb. "Maybe the gulper spit her out when it realized she didn't have any magic."
"Are you under a Dousing spell, Venna?" Wyssa waved her hand again. A buzz of magic energy surrounded Venna for a moment.
"Oh!" said Venna. "Did you . . . ?" She rubbed her hands together. Instantly her clothes and hair were dry. "Thank you!" she cried. "It feels so good to have magic again."
"I can't believe you're here!" Perda said. "How did you end up with Morb?"
Venna shuddered. "Morb," she spat, already seeming more like her old self. "Where did he go? We must stop his evil plans!"
Zann stepped forward. "Do you know if he found my parents? We heard he was looking for them."
"Nax and Asta?" Venna looked surprised. "No, as far as I know I was his only Magician prisoner. Besides, I thought your parents disappeared years ago."
Zann's shoulders slumped. Had he reached another dead end in the search for his parents?
Wyssa leaned toward Venna. "You mentioned Morb's plans—did he tell you what he's trying to do?"
Venna nodded. "For the past couple of days, Morb has been searching for the Horn of the Otherworld."
"Huh?" Zann traded a look with his friends. The Horn of the Otherworld was the relic Teplo had been holding right before the Cave of the Unknown collapsed.
"The Horn of the Otherworld?" Gliss frowned. "Why does Morb want that?"
Venna shrugged. "He wouldn't tell me. All I know is that the Horn wasn't where he expected to find it. So he traced its magical essence, which led him to me."
"You?" Wyssa raised an eyebrow. "Why?"
"Because I'd touched it recently." Venna grimaced. "And because I was in a Doused state—that made it much easier for Morb to control me than someone like Tok or Teplo."
"I see," Zann said. "So Morb found you in the vortex?"
"Yes. I suppose I should be grateful." Venna grimaced again. "If Morb hadn't grabbed me, I wouldn't have survived the vortex much longer without magic."
"I bet Morb wants to try to take over Magica again," Perda said. "Maybe with another crazy contraption from the Old Times."
"I'm sure you're right." Venna sounded worried. "I only wish I had access to the ancient texts so I could try to figure out what he has in mind."
"Did Morb feed you to the gulper because you wouldn't tell him where the Horn is?" Darb asked.
"Not exactly. I did resist for some time. But Morb finally got impatient." Venna shuddered. "He forced me to tell by using a Possession spell."
"That spell uses a lot of energy," Wyssa said.
"I know," Venna said. "I suppose that's why he didn't use it as soon as he grabbed me." She rubbed her chin thoughtfully. "If we could find Morb now, he might be in a weakened state."
"It could be our best chance," Wyssa agreed. "Where is the relic? We must reach it before he does."
Venna opened her mouth to answer. But at that moment, Perda let out a sharp cry. Then she crumpled to the ground, unconscious.
"Perda!" Zann exclaimed, kneeling by her side.
"What's wrong with her?" Gliss sounded scared.
"Let me through." Wyssa pushed past the kids. She touched Perda's face and then murmured a few words. "Awaken," she added, snapping her fingers.
Perda blinked and sat up. "Whoa," she mumbled. "That was weird!"
"What happened?" Zann asked.
Perda stared at him. "I saw them," she said. "Your parents. I recognized them from the hologram we saw in the Cave."
"What?" Zann exclaimed. "What do you mean, you saw my parents?"
Perda shrugged. "It was a super strong vision—like a really vivid dream."
"But what caused it?" Gliss wondered. "None of the rest of us saw anything."

"I don't know." Then Perda's eyes widened. "Wait, yes I do! I put my hand in my pocket and touched Zann's message stone. See?" She pointed. "It fell there, on the ground. It must have caused the vision!"
"Let me try!" Zann grabbed the stone and was almost knocked off his feet by a strong vision of his parents.
He could see them more clearly than ever before. They were standing in a dimly lit room. A tiny Roodian woman was with them. All three of them looked terrified!
"Oh no!" Zann exclaimed. He dropped the stone. Instantly the vision of his parents was gone.
"What is it?" Perda asked. "Did you see them too?"
Zann nodded, too overwhelmed to speak. His parents had looked so real—and so scared!
"But why are we seeing them now?" Perda wondered. "I've touched that stone lots of times."
"Message stones are mysterious things," Wyssa said. "They hold on to the magical essence of all who touch them."
"That's how Mother used the stone to help us," Gliss put in.
"Mother? Who's that?" Venna asked.
Gliss, Perda, and Darb quickly told her about their adventure in Zon, the world with no boys.
"Interesting," Wyssa said when they'd finished. "Mother's spell must have made the stone's messages stronger, allowing Perda to see them too."
"Does this mean Zann's parents are nearby?" Gliss asked.
Wyssa nodded. "Such magic works best when it's close to the source of the message."
"The source—you mean Zann's parents?" Darb asked. "Are they here in Rood?"
"It seems likely," said Wyssa.
Zann gasped. "Oh!"
Wyssa continued. "My guess is that Morb has just returned to wherever he's holding Zann's parents captive, and they became frightened."
"And their fear caused the stone to send that vision to whoever was touching it." Venna peered at the stone. "Fascinating!"
"If Morb is back with his prisoners, he probably found the Horn already," Perda pointed out.
"Not necessarily." Wyssa turned to Venna. "Tell me where it is."
"Wait!" Zann blurted out before Venna could respond. "Don't tell her."
"What?" Wyssa glared at Zann. "This is no time for games, boy."
Zann felt nervous, especially when he remembered how easily Wyssa had broken his Shackle spell. But he stood his ground.
"I know you want to punish Morb," he said. "But first we need to find my parents. Morb might be the only one who can lead us to them."
He expected Wyssa to get even angrier. Instead she looked at the ground and sighed.
"You're right," she said. "This is my chance to make things right. Not just by making Morb pay for what he's done, but also by doing what I can to help Nax and Asta."
"Thanks." Zann was relieved. He told Wyssa where they'd seen the Horn.
Her expression darkened again. "The only thing hiding it was some rubble? I'm sure Morb had the Horn within seconds after leaving here."
"We need to find him before he uses it," Venna said. "But how? I don't know if he has a lair here in Rood."
"I have an idea." Wyssa pursed her lips and whistled.
Several tiny people zapped into view. Whistlefeather was among them.
"Have you found him?" Whistlefeather asked eagerly. "Is Morb gone?"
"I'm afraid not," Wyssa said. "We need your help. Does he have a lair in this world?"
Whistlefeather hesitated, trading a look with the other Roodians. "Yes, but . . ." His voice trailed off.
"We'd like to help," a Roodian woman said, her voice trembling. "But we fear Morb's retribution. He's holding our queen prisoner."
"Your queen?" Zann recalled the tiny, frightened woman from his vision.
Whistlefeather nodded. "We're afraid that if we tell you where Morb's lair is, he'll toss the queen through the nearest wormhole."
Perda shrugged. "What's so bad about that?"
"It would kill her," Wyssa said grimly. "The Roodians told me they cannot pass through any wormhole."
The Roodian woman nodded. "Many have tried in the past. All were flung back into Rood—lifeless."
"Wow," Gliss said. "I guess that's why Rood stayed undiscovered for so long."

"Well, it explains why Roodians can't visit other worlds." Perda glanced at a wormhole blinking nearby. "But there are wormholes to so many other worlds here! I'm surprised nobody has ever come through one of them."

"The wormholes here don't work like most wormholes," Whistlefeather said. "One can pass from Rood to any other world. But the wormholes only work in one direction. Rood itself can only be reached via the vortex."

"Yes," Wyssa added. "And there's only one incoming wormhole in Rood. It's very unpredictable." She sighed, rubbing her forehead. "In any case, we can't endanger the queen. We'll have to find another way . . ."
"Wait." A young Roodian stepped forward. "Any other way will take too long. We'll tell you where Morb is."
"Prince Doni, no!" another Roodian exclaimed. "Your mother—"
"My mother would want us to help these people." The prince squared his tiny shoulders. "She's the bravest person I know. She would want to defeat Morb, no matter the risk to her own safety."
He snapped his fingers. A piece of parchment appeared in his hand. "Morb is forcing many of our people to act as his servants, cleaning the lair and preparing food. They drew this map."
"Why would Morb need servants?" Darb wondered. "He should be able to do that stuff with magic."
"He loves bossing people around," said Perda. "That's probably why."
Wyssa was examining the map. "Thank you," she told the Roodians. "We'll try to rescue your queen if we can."
Prince Doni nodded his thanks. "But be careful!" he warned. "The Gray Gorge is a dangerous place."
Zann wasn't worried about danger. He had to find his parents!
"What are we waiting for?" he said. "Let's go!"
Wyssa nodded. "Zap!"

Zann landed with a grunt on hard ground. Looking up he saw a forbidding stone tower shrouded in ghostly gray fog. He looked down and realized everyone was standing near the edge of a huge chasm. It was so deep Zann couldn't see the bottom. A howling wind whipped in and out of it, pulling in anything it could grab.
"Aah!" Zann cried as he felt himself suddenly losing balance.
"Help!" Gliss shrieked. The wind had knocked her down and was whipping her hair over her face. She was now struggling to hang onto the edge of the chasm.
"Hold on!" Darb lunged toward her, but he ended up almost falling over the edge himself. Zing flew overhead, whistling with alarm. A gust of wind grabbed the dragon, tossing him end over end.
"To me!" Wyssa shouted.
Suddenly Zann felt himself being grabbed by magical energy. It yanked him backward, away from the terrifying drop-off. Soon the entire group was safely out of the wind's reach.
"Wow, that was close!" Perda exclaimed.
Venna nodded. "No wonder Prince Doni warned us that the Gray Gorge was very dangerous."
Darb stared up at the stone tower. "That looks like Morb's kind of place."
"Yeah," Zann agreed. "And my parents are in there!"
His heart pounded at the thought that they might be so close. After all this time, was he finally going to be with them again?
"How are we going to get in there?" Gliss wondered.
"Good question," Zann muttered. The tower was perched halfway across a narrow, ancient-looking stone bridge spanning the Gray Gorge.
"Prince Doni said Morb built this place," Perda said. "It must have taken a lot of magic to do that, especially in a spot like this."
"Indeed." Wyssa sounded grim. "It seems he must have figured out a new way to steal magic. Lots of magic."
Zann studied the tower. "The wind will make it hard to cross the bridge without falling into the gorge," he said. "But otherwise, it doesn't look that bad. The gate is small enough to step over."
He pointed to a short gate blocking the entrance to the bridge.
"I suppose it's only meant to keep Roodians out," Venna said.
"Yeah. Or keep them in ," Gliss added. "I doubt they're thrilled to be Morb's servants."
"So what are we waiting for?" Perda took a step toward the bridge.
Wyssa narrowed her eyes. "It seems odd that there's no sentry."
"Yes, it does," Venna said. "I'm sure Morb must have some sort of Shield spell on the place."
"There's only one way to find out. Come on!" Zann hurried toward the bridge. Bracing himself against the gusty wind, he stepped over the gate. Perda was right behind him.
"Wait," Wyssa called from the other side of the gate. She pointed past Zann. "What's that?"
Zann peered through the fog. Something was sitting on the bridge just ahead. It was small and fluffy.
"Oh!" Zann exclaimed. "It must be the missing mibbit!"
"Aw, it's cute." Perda smiled and stepped forward.
"Wait," Zann said. "It looks kind of tense."
"Here, mibbit, mibbit!" Perda cooed. She grabbed for the creature. It squawked and leaped back.
"Careful, don't panic it or—" Zann gasped as a shock wave of magic energy hit him. He saw Perda collapse to her knees. The mibbit was sending out confusing energy waves, just like Vee had described!

Zann had never felt anything like it before. He couldn't move or think clearly. Unlike with the scatter beast attack, though, there was no pain. Still, he felt completely helpless. What if Morb looked out a window and spotted him and Perda on the bridge?

He heard moans from behind him. With great effort he turned his head far enough to see the others. Venna was clinging to a tree, gasping for breath. Gliss was on the ground, helpless—and sliding toward the dizzying drop-off! Zing wasn't far behind her.
Zann wanted to save them. But he still couldn't move. In fact, he realized he and Perda were dangerously close to the edge too.

He looked for Wyssa, hoping she could help them. But she looked just as helpless as the others. She'd stopped herself from rolling over the edge by clutching the gate. But Zann could see that her grip was weakening.
Another wave of magic struck them all. Zann felt himself teetering on the edge of the bridge. Was this the end for him—for all of them?
Then he saw movement near the gate. He couldn't turn his head, but he rolled his eyes far enough to see what was happening.
It was Darb! He was jumping over the small gate. Dodging Zann and Perda, Darb hurried over to the mibbit.
"Easy, little fellow," Darb said soothingly. He gently picked up the mibbit and stroked its ears, just as Vee had taught them.
A moment later the energy waves were gone.
"Whoa!" Perda gasped, sitting up and moving herself away from the drop—off.
Zann did the same. "Thanks, Darb," he said. "But why didn't the mibbit's magic affect you?"
Darb shrugged, cuddling the mibbit. The fluffy creature looked happy and relaxed now.
"Maybe it's because I'm a Void," he said. "I don't have any magic for the mibbit to affect."
Wyssa nodded. "I think you must be right, boy."
Zing flew toward Darb. He circled him, sniffing at the mibbit curiously.
"Down, boy," Zann told his dragon. "That mibbit is not a snack!"
Venna brushed the dirt off her clothes and frowned at the mibbit. "I'm guessing that thing was supposed to be Morb's security guard," she said. "Shall we proceed?"
Zann opened his mouth to say yes. But his words were lost as an eerie howl echoed from the depths of the gorge.
Gliss' eyes widened. "What was that ?"

Before anyone could respond, a huge head on a long, snakelike neck arose from the dark gorge. The orange glow of its eyes cut through the fog like flames. With a loud roar, the creature exposed a mouth full of sharp fangs.
Wyssa went pale. "It's the Beast of the Otherworld!"
"The Beast of the Otherworld?" Zann echoed. "What's that?"
He didn't recognize the creature from his parents' books. And he was sure he'd remember something that looked like that !
"It's the most horrible beast in all the worlds." Wyssa shuddered. "How was Morb able to transport it from its home on Narakan?"
"Narakan?" Venna sounded startled. "I thought that world was only a myth."
"Apparently not," Wyssa said. The creature hissed, and a dark, viscous substance dripped from its jaws and sizzled on the stone bridge.
"How big is that thing, anyway?" Perda cried as the enormous head rose even higher.
"Big!" Zann answered. "And it doesn't seem to be in a good mood either!"
The Beast let out a hoarse, echoing cry. Then its head snaked toward Zann and the others.
"Run!" Venna shouted.
The humans scattered. Zann lunged toward the gate and skidded across the rough stone on his hands and knees.
When he glanced back, the Beast was raising its head again. Zann noticed that the dark goo wasn't coming from its mouth after all. It was oozing out of its head.
"Look out!" Gliss screamed. "It's going to strike again!"
Spurting angry flames, Zing flew toward the Beast.
"Zing, no!" Zann shouted. "It's going to eat you!"
The Beast snapped at the small dragon. Zing barely escaped.
"We have to zap away!" Gliss cried, grabbing Darb's hand.
"No!" Wyssa said. "That's the worst thing we can do. If the legends are true, the Beast can catch hold of Transport spells and pull its victims back—straight into its jaws."
"So we're trapped?" Perda snapped her fingers, and a sword appeared in her hand. "Then we'll have to fight."
Zann stared at her for a second. When had Perda become so brave? He couldn't imagine any other kid his age facing down a monster so calmly.
But this was no time to think about such things. Rubbing his hands together, Zann conjured his own sword.
"Stand back, kids," Venna called. "I'm going to blast it."
"Wait," Wyssa said. "I don't think that will—"
Blast !
A bolt of energy shot out of Venna's hands. It flew straight at the Beast. The Beast opened its giant mouth . . .
Gulp !
"Did the Beast just eat the Blast spell?" Gliss cried.
Zann didn't have time to answer as he dodged another sizzling drop of slime. He found himself beside Darb, who was still cradling the mibbit.
"The mibbit doesn't seem too worried," Zann commented.
Darb nodded. "Vee told us the effects of the ear-rubbing would last a few hours, remember?" he said. "Too bad. I bet the mibbit was the only thing holding the Beast back before."
"You're probably right. No wonder the mibbit was tense with that thing around." Zann glanced up. "Get back!"
He and Darb leaped away in opposite directions. The Beast's head slammed down, shaking the whole bridge.
"Hurry! Run while it's stunned!" Perda shouted. "Maybe it won't be able to climb out of that pit and chase us."
Zann sprinted for the gate. He was only halfway there when a shimmering wall of magic energy shot up in front of him.
"What's that?" Venna cried.
Zann didn't answer. He lowered his head and ran straight toward the magical wall. But he bounced off it and stumbled into Darb.

"Oof," Darb grunted. He fell backward, almost slipping off the edge of the bridge. To catch himself, he had to drop the mibbit. The fuzzy creature landed on its feet and just stood there, flicking its ears lazily.
"Look out!" Perda yelled. "The Beast is coming for you guys!"
Zann grabbed Darb and dragged him away from the Beast. The Beast's orange eyes glowed, and another wall of magic energy sprang up inside the first.
"Why did it make another wall? The first one seemed to be working pretty well." Zann winced, touching his shoulder. He would definitely have a bruise to heal later— if he survived this.
"I think it's herding us back toward itself." Suddenly Perda looked scared. "Look! It's drooling."
"This is hopeless!" Gliss cried, her voice shaking. "The Beast is going to eat us, and there's nothing we can do about it!"
Darb grabbed the mibbit. "Isn't there anything you can do?" he asked Wyssa and Venna.
Wyssa was peering at the magic walls. "Let me think, let me think," she muttered. "There must be a way . . ."

Zann glanced from Wyssa to his friends. Perda and Gliss were clinging to each other, looking terrified. Zing was hiding behind Venna. Darb, cradling the mibbit, was looking nervously at the Beast. The hideous creature was sizing them up, as if deciding whom to eat first.
Suddenly Zann's eyes lit up. "I've got it! Everyone run toward the tower!"
"What?" Venna said. "Are you crazy?"
Zann didn't answer; he raced along the bridge toward the tower.
Perda caught up to him. "Zann, the door is bolted shut! And we won't have time to try to open it with a spell. The Beast will have us cornered!"
"Just go." Zann shoved her forward and then turned to make sure the others were following.
Wyssa was the last to run past. She gave Zann a strange look. "I hope you know what you're doing, boy."

Zann hoped so too. He glanced at the Beast, which was already gathering itself for another attack. As the huge head snaked toward him, Zann sprinted after the others. He could feel the creature's hot breath on the back of his neck. A drop of viscous goo landed on his shoulder, burning right through his shirt.
Zann yelped in pain. He picked up speed, trying not to imagine the Beast's sharp teeth digging into his skin.
As everyone crowded near the door to the tower, Zann glanced back. Mouth wide open, the Beast thrust its giant head toward them.
Crash !
The Beast howled with pain and frustration as it hit an invisible barrier.
"I knew it!" Zann exclaimed. "It's a Shield spell!"
"What?" Perda sounded confused. "But we passed straight through it."
"The shield must have been designed to only keep out the Beast," said Venna.
"Nice thinking, boy," Wyssa added.
"But how did you know the shield was there?" Darb asked Zann.
"I figured Morb wouldn't build his lair here if he didn't have a way to keep the Beast out," Zann explained.
"But the mibbit . . ." Perda gestured toward Darb.
"I know," Zann said. "I figured, or at least I hoped, that Morb had a backup plan, just in case the mibbit couldn't hold back the Beast."
"That makes sense." Darb stroked the mibbit. "If I had a monster like that outside my front door, I'd have a backup plan too!"
The Beast let out another howl of fury. Gliss shot it a nervous look.
"What do we do now?" she asked.
"We go in," said Wyssa. "Carefully." Touching the lock on the door, she muttered a few words. The door opened with a pop.
With Wyssa in the lead, the group stepped quietly into the tower. The entryway inside was long and narrow, lit by a procession of flickering wall torches.
"Weird." Perda peered ahead. "This place looks a lot bigger on the inside than it did from the outside."
"No kidding," Zann said, glancing through an arched doorway. Beyond was a room so enormous that he couldn't see the far wall.
Gliss was staring through another arch. "How are we going to find Morb in this place?"
"Or my parents." Zann looked at Wyssa. "Are there any spells we could use?"
"Hundreds," she replied. "But I'm sure Morb has magic sensors in place. It's better if he doesn't know we're here until we find him."
Suddenly Darb gasped. "Look out!"
Something burst out of a nearby doorway.
"Uh-oh, it's one of those blob monsters," Zann exclaimed. "Like the one Morb had guarding the palace back in First City!"
"A sweller from Ductilan." Wyssa nodded. "They make crude but effective guards. Fortunately they aren't very smart."
She pulled a handful of stones out of her pocket and tossed them down a side hallway. The sweller blobbed after them.
"This way," Wyssa said, heading down a different hall.
Zann peered into each room they passed. No two looked the same.
"This place is strange," Perda commented as she and Zann paused in the doorway of a room that appeared to be made entirely out of fish scales.
"Yeah," Zann said. "Just like the guy who built it."
"Look out!" Venna cried.
Several large trolls lumbered toward them.
"Zing, quick!" Darb urged. "Do your thing!"
Whistling his song, Zing flew forward. The trolls stopped, staring at the dragon.
"Hurry! If we get out of sight, they might forget we were ever here." Venna darted around a corner.
By the time the group rounded the next corner, Zing had caught up. Zann didn't hear any sound of pursuit.
"I think we lost them," he said. "Thanks, little buddy!"
Zing chirped and led the way into a large courtyard filled with trees and shrubs.
"Wow," Perda said. "This place is definitely bigger on the inside than the outside!"
"Perhaps." Wyssa looked worried. "There might be a Bewilderment spell on the whole place. That would explain why we never pass the same room twice."
"A Bewilderment spell?" Gliss said. "I've never heard of—aah!"
Zann spun around. One of the trees had grabbed Gliss!
"It's a tentacle tree!" Perda cried. "Like in Fardark!"
Wyssa stepped forward. A long, curved knife appeared in her hand. With one swift movement, she slashed the tentacle in two.
"Get away from it," she ordered. "Hurry!"
The whole group dashed through another door.
"This is awful!" Venna looked petrified. "It's like Morb brought every scary creature from every world to guard this place!"
There was a sudden flurry of wings. Dozens of large birds burst into the room.
"Snuffer geese!" Gliss exclaimed. "Or sniffer geese? I can't tell the difference."
"Doesn't matter," Wyssa said. "Both breeds are nasty when they're annoyed."
Darb took a deep breath. "Honk! Honk!"
"What's your Void friend doing?" Venna hissed at Zann. "He'll only upset them more!"
"Shh!" Zann watched as Darb honked a few more times. One of the geese honked back. Then the whole flock waddled off!
"Amazing!" Gliss cried.
They all looked at Darb.
He shrugged. "I just told them we didn't mean them any harm. At least I think that's what I said!"
Venna looked impressed.
"Let's move on," said Wyssa. She led the way into the next room. It was large and dimly lit.
As Zann entered the room, he thought he saw a shadowy shape moving along one wall. He paused and peered into the dimness.
"Guys?" said Zann. "I think there's something in here."
Just then the shadowy creature stepped into the light. The creature was orange with black stripes.
Perda gasped. "It's one of those striped monsters. Like the one Morb sent after that sneaky guy, Slib, back at the palace!"
"How do we fight this creature?" Gliss asked.
Venna shrugged. "Run!"
Zann was in the lead as they raced around a corner and straight into a flock of tiny, buzzing creatures.
"Flizzes!" he shouted, steeling himself for the little dragons' painful stings.
But it didn't happen. The flizzes immediately buzzed away.
"Wow," Perda said. "We're lucky they didn't attack us."
"Maybe not." Wyssa sounded grim. "They're probably flying straight to Morb to tell him that we're here."
"Uh-oh." Zann stared after the flizzes. "What now?"
"Should we use magic to find our way?" Venna suggested.
"We might as well," Gliss said. "Wyssa used magic to create that knife just now." She rubbed her neck where the tree had grabbed her.
"That was minor magic," Wyssa said. "Any kind of searching or mapping spell would be—oh, hello."

A Roodian servant was rushing toward them. "The prince sent me to help you," he said in a hushed, urgent tone. "He realized you'd never find the queen and the other prisoners. Morb has put a Bewilderment spell over this whole place."
"I knew it!" Wyssa muttered.
"But we servants need to be able to find our way around to do our jobs." The Roodian cast a nervous look around as he showed them a small object. "That's why Morb gave each of us one of these."
Perda gasped. "A talisman! Just like the one Morb used to control the trolls!"
The Roodian handed the talisman to Wyssa. "It blocks the effects of the Bewilderment spell. Now you'll be able to find the prisoners' cell." He quickly told them the way and then scurried off.
With Wyssa in the lead, Zann and the others followed the Roodian's directions.
Soon they reached a large, dimly lit chamber. A haze of odorless smoke made it impossible to see more than a few steps ahead.
"This should be the cell." Zann peered in. "Do you guys see anything?"
"I can't see a thing through all this misty stuff," Gliss complained.
Zann took a few careful steps forward, waving a hand to clear the haze. "I think I see something . . ."
Zann's voice trailed off; his eyes widened in horror. A scatter beast was stepping out of the mist!
Zann's heart raced. His head filled with memories of his last scatter beast encounter. He tried to speak, to warn his friends. But his voice seemed frozen in his throat.
"Was that Roodian servant working for Morb?" he thought with a shudder. "Did he send us straight into a trap?"
The scatter beast paused, its tentacle waving lazily as it shambled closer.
"No!" Venna shouted. But Zann barely noticed; all he could do was stare at the horrifying creature moving toward him.
Suddenly there was a loud squawk. Zing flew around Zann and the others, spitting fire and whistling urgently.
"Zing, what are you doing?" Zann mumbled, barely feeling the burn of Zing's flames. "Save yourself."
Zing let out a chirp of irritation and flew out of sight. For a moment Zann thought the dragon had taken his advice and escaped the way they'd come in.
Then Zann heard another whistle. A second later something thumped into his back—hard.
"Hey!" Zann blurted out as he stumbled forward. He was about to fall right on top of the scatter beast! "No—oof!"
He landed hard on the stone floor of the chamber.
"Huh?" Zann muttered. He couldn't see the scatter beast anymore.
Zann leaped to his feet and backed up a few steps. Suddenly the scatter beast was there again, in the same spot where Zann had just fallen!
Zing landed beside the scatter beast. The beast didn't seem to notice the dragon at all.
Zann's wild heartbeat slowed. For the first time, he realized he wasn't feeling the pain and other crazy magical effects he'd felt in Fardark. The only thing immobilizing him was his fear.
Taking a cautious step forward, Zann reached for the scatter beast. His hand passed right through it!
"It's an illusion!" Zann shouted with relief. "The scatter beast isn't real!"
He glanced around. Everyone else, except Zing, was staring straight ahead, looking terrified.
"S-scatter beast?" Perda's eyes never left the blank spot right in front of her. "I'd be happy to see a scatter beast right now. Maybe it would scare away that huge swarm of tickle bugs!"

"Tickle bugs?" Zann wrinkled his nose. Tickle bugs had ten legs and whirligig wings and liked to land on people. They were annoying, but they weren't scary. Well, except to Perda. Suddenly Zann remembered that Perda was terrified of the goofy insects. He'd once scared her with one.

"I get it," he muttered. "Guys, none of this is real!" he said loudly. "Whatever you're seeing—tickle bugs, scatter beasts—they're just another one of Morb's spells. Somehow he's making us each see whatever scares us the most."
Venna still didn't move. "Maybe you're right. But that cave hisser sure looks real to me. And everyone knows they don't like sudden movements."
Zann sighed and then glanced at Zing. "Come on, little buddy. Let's show them."
The two of them jumped in front of each person, revealing that whatever each was seeing wasn't real.
"Thank goodness!" Gliss stumbled backward. "I was sure that thunder charger was going to eat me!"
Darb nodded. "I thought I was about to fall into a deep, dark hole."
"What did you see?" Perda asked Wyssa.
Zann waited for Wyssa's answer. What could possibly terrify someone like her?

"It's not important." Wyssa frowned, peering farther into the misty room. "This type of spell is very complex and difficult to cast. With so many real creatures roaming his lair, Morb would only bother to use a spell like this to protect something very important."
She muttered a few words under her breath. Then she waved a hand.
"Reveal!" she intoned.
The chamber seemed to melt away, revealing that it had all been an illusion. Zann and the others found themselves standing in an icy cave.
A tiny woman was frozen in a block of ice. She was motionless, except for her eyes, which darted pleadingly from one person to the next.
Perda stared at the tiny frozen woman. "That must be the Roodian queen!" she exclaimed.
Zann spun around, his eyes searching the icy cave. "But where are my parents?" he cried. "They should be here! The queen was with them in my dream!"
"Let's get the queen free, and maybe she can tell us." Venna turned to Wyssa. "What do you think? Should we try an Extraction spell?"
Wyssa frowned and stroked her chin. "That could injure her if there are any imperfections in the ice. What about a Supplanting spell?"
"Do you think you can manage that?" Venna sounded doubtful. "If we don't get the dimensions exactly right . . ."
Zing bounded over and sniffed at the trapped queen. He whistled curiously, and a wisp of flame escaped his mouth.
"Careful, Zing," Darb said. "Don't burn her."
"No, wait, look." Gliss pointed. "He's melting the ice!"
"Go, Zing," Zann urged. "Keep melting it!"
The little dragon breathed on the block of ice, which quickly melted. Within seconds the queen was free.
Perda grinned. "Good job, Zing. That was much easier than using any of those complicated spells."
"Thank you!" the queen said breathlessly, shaking icy droplets from her clothes. "But please! You have to stop him!"
Venna nodded. "We know. Morb already tried to take over Magica once."
The queen shook her head. "He's not trying to take over your world this time," she said. "He's trying to destroy it!"
"What?" Gliss exclaimed.
"Destroy it?" Zann said. "How?"

Venna shook her head. "Impossible," she said. "Yes, the Horn of the Otherworld is one of the most powerful relics known. But Morb is crazy if he thinks he can use it to destroy an entire world. It doesn't have that much power."
"Not on its own," Wyssa said slowly. "Don't you know where the Horn came from originally?"
Venna shrugged. "A faraway world of powerful magic. That's all the ancient texts say about it."
"Where did it come from?" Perda asked Wyssa.
Wyssa looked grim. "From the head of the Beast of the Otherworld."
"What?" Gliss shuddered. "You mean that horrible thing outside?"
Darb frowned. "But the Beast didn't have any horns."

"Exactly," Wyssa said. "It originally had two horns growing from its head. According to legend, it fought a terrible battle long ago with a Forellian deathshifter. That's how it lost the horn you've seen, the one that later became a relic in Magica."
"And the second horn?" Zann said.
Wyssa shrugged. "That part is a mystery. The legends don't mention anything about the second horn. So as far as I know, the Beast still had it until very recently."
"Yes," said the Roodian queen. "Recently Morb disabled the Beast long enough to cut off the remaining horn."
Zann remembered the dark stuff dripping from the Beast's head and realized it must have been blood.
"But how did Morb disable the Beast?" asked Darb.
The queen pointed to the mibbit, which was peeking out from Darb's arms. "He used that creature."
"Of course, I should have guessed," Wyssa muttered. "The mibbit is probably the only creature in all the known worlds that could overcome the Beast's powerful magic."
"What about a scatter beast?" Venna said.
"Well, yes, that would work too." Wyssa looked thoughtful. "But Morb would have trouble controlling a scatter beast safely. Since he's a Void, a mibbit would be—"
A sudden whooshing sound cut her off.
Gliss screamed. "Something just ripped my sleeve!"

Zann ducked as a tiny shape zipped past his face, missing him by the width of a dragon's scale. Spinning around, he saw a lizard with a sharp blade for a snout, which was embedded in the icy wall. It was already pulling itself free.
"Blade lizards from Redsea," Wyssa said. "Morb has always liked those."
"Run!" Perda cried.
"No, join hands!" Wyssa ordered. "Blade lizards are too fast. We have to zap away."
Zap !
Splash !
"Drat!" said Zann. "I always . . ." His whole body froze before he could finish. Constant shocks were passing through him, making it impossible to move or even think.
"Zann!" Perda cried. "What's wrong?"
"Hold on, boy," Wyssa called. "I've got you."
Zann felt himself being levitated out of the water. By the time he landed, the shocks were wearing off.
Finally he could look around. The whole group was in a small courtyard with an ornate fountain in the middle.
"What happened?" Zann asked.
"Paralyzer pythons," Wyssa said. "It's a good thing you were the only one who landed in the water."
"Yeah," Zann muttered, glancing at the creatures writhing in the fountain. "Good thing."
"This is bad," Wyssa said.
"It sure is!" Gliss exclaimed. "How many creatures does Morb have guarding this place, anyway?"

"I'm not talking about the pythons, girl." Wyssa waved a hand dismissively. "I'm talking about Morb's plan. If he gets his hands on both horns at the same time, his power will be absolutely unimaginable."

"Yes." Venna sounded anxious. "And thanks to that Possession spell he placed on me, the second horn is probably already here in Rood. But I still don't understand. How is he planning to use the horns to destroy Magica?"
The Roodian queen spoke up. "I think I know. The servants here in the fortress have been whispering about a terrible contraption Morb is building. He calls it a Memory Eater."
"That sounds familiar." Venna bit her lip. "I think it's mentioned in the ancient texts. But I'm not sure how it works."
"Do you know any more about this contraption?" Wyssa asked the queen.
"Only that Morb has brought prisoners from his home world to power it," the queen said. "A man and a woman named Nax and Asta."
Zann gasped. "My parents!"
"Can you show us Morb's contraption?" Venna asked the queen.

"I'm not sure exactly where it is," the queen replied. "But now I understand why Morb forced me to tell him where he could find the Magica wormholes. We'll probably find the contraption near one of them."
"You know how to find the wormholes leading to Magica?" Perda asked.

"As the ruler of this world, I'm the only one who knows the location of every wormhole." The tiny queen stretched proudly to her full height. "I'm also the only one with the power to instantly summon every wormhole in Rood to me."
"Really?" Gliss exclaimed. "Can you do that now? Summon all the Magica wormholes? Then Morb can't do whatever horrible thing he's planning to do!"
The queen smiled faintly. "I'm afraid it doesn't work that way. I can't summon individual wormholes. Only all of them at once. We would be overwhelmed by every wormhole to every world there is."
"Oh." Perda sounded disappointed. "Too bad."
Zann felt impatient. "Then how are we going to get to wherever Morb's new contraption is?"
"Follow me," said the queen.
She started down the hallway. Zann and the others followed.
"There are multiple wormholes to Magica," Zann said. "How do you know which one Morb will be near?"
"There's only one Magica wormhole within the walls of this fortress," the queen replied. "I expect that's the one Morb is planning to use."
As he ran, Zann felt something burning him. At first he thought it was Zing flying too close. Then he realized it was the message stone in his pocket. It was fiery hot.
"Hurry," he urged. "We must be almost there!"
"We are. It's just ahead." The queen led the way through an arch.

Zann followed, and then immediately skidded to a stop. They were in a stone room with an enormous contraption in the middle. Like Morb's previous machines, this one was hideous and made up of many different parts. The first thing Zann noticed was two large, glowing horns sticking out of the top.
The second thing he noticed was his parents. Their arms and legs were shackled together, and Morb was shoving them up against the terrible machine!
"Stop!" Zann shouted. "Mom, Dad—it's me!"
"Zann!" his mother cried.
"Zann?" Morb echoed with a scowl. He gestured to several trolls that were hanging around in the corner. "Grab them, you fools!"
Zann tried to duck away, but there was nowhere to run. The trolls grabbed Zann and the others.

"Don't kill them," Morb ordered the trolls. "Not just yet, anyway." He smirked at Wyssa. "I didn't expect to see you again." He widened his gaze to include all of them. "Or any of you, for that matter. But now that you're here, I hope you'll stick around and enjoy the show."
Zann heard Wyssa muttering under her breath. Morb heard it too.

"Let me guess," Morb sneered. "You're planning to try some powerful, little-known spell you've learned during your travels. Don't bother—it's too late. My new pets have already latched onto their victims."

He waved a hand toward the contraption. Tiny creatures, hundreds of them, were swarming out of a tank in the center of the contraption. The creatures looked like small, brightly colored cave crawlers. Zann gasped in horror as the small rodents scampered all over his parents.
"Memory mice!" Wyssa spat. "Of course! I should have guessed you'd use them."
"What are memory mice?" Darb asked.
"They feed on people's memories," Wyssa said. "Their feeding has the side effect of creating very strong magical energy."
"They eat memories?" Gliss frowned. "How awful!"

"Not necessarily," said Wyssa. "In their home world, they're a beloved and valuable species. They help people by deleting painful memories. They also create much useful energy out of useless or unwanted memories."
Zann struggled to free himself from the troll holding him. "Mom, Dad!" he called.
"I'm afraid your parents can't answer you, boy," Morb said. "They're busy right now—having all their memories devoured."

"Like anything," Wyssa went on, "memory mice can be used for evil." She shot Morb a disgusted look. "Normally a person must invite the mice to latch on, and they only feed for a limited amount of time. Morb must have overridden that instinct with some kind of spell."

"Clever, isn't it?" Morb smiled. "My Memory Machine can use any memories to summon the power it needs. I could have used my Roodian servants. Even trolls' feeble brains have enough memories to work." He chuckled. "But I liked the irony of using Magica memories to destroy Magica. Besides, I already had these two as my prisoners. They were very useful in helping me find my way to Rood."
"Your only true talent is holding a grudge," Wyssa retorted. "It's not Nax and Asta's fault you were born a Void."

Morb ignored her. "I'm glad you're here, Zann. Perhaps you can be useful to me at last. I've ordered the mice to drain your parents of all memories of Magica. If that's not enough to fill the machine . . ."
He touched a large clear tube on one side, which was rapidly filling with glowing, sparking magic energy. "Well, then perhaps I'll have to top it off with your memories."
"No!" Zann blurted out.
"Wait," Perda said. "What happens when the tube is full?"

"Why, then all I have to do is open this hatch," said Morb, smiling wickedly. "The energy will get sucked through any wormhole within range. As it happens, the only wormhole in this room leads directly into Wyssa's old home of Wormwood."
Venna looked nervous. "And then what happens?"
"Then the energy will explode," Morb said. "Blowing all of Magica to smithereens!"
"You can't destroy Magica!" Perda cried to Morb. She turned to Wyssa. "You have to stop him!"
Wyssa said nothing. She was staring at the contraption in horror.
"It's too late," Morb sneered. "No one can stop me now!"
Zann stared at his parents. Their bodies twitched as the memory mice scampered over them.
"Are the mice really sucking out my parents' memories?" he asked.
"That's right, boy," Morb said. "But don't worry. Once their memories are emptied, I'll have no further use for your parents. You can have them back."

Zann shuddered. He'd never imagined there could be anything worse than being separated from his parents. Now he wasn't so sure. He couldn't stand the thought of finding them just in time to watch them forget everything. Would they remember their old home in First City? Or that family vacation they'd all taken to the Flower Forest?
Would they even remember him ?
Morb turned to the Roodian queen. "I'm glad you're here to witness this," he taunted. "Without you, it never could have happened."
Still thinking about the past, Zann stared at his parents. Then he noticed a couple of memory mice sniffing curiously in his direction.
He looked over at Wyssa. "How do people invite the mice to eat their memories?" he whispered.
She appeared confused. "Simply by opening their minds to them."
"Good." Zann glanced at his friends and Venna. "Start thinking about Magica," he whispered. "Any memories you can come up with. And invite the mice to come to you."
"What?" Perda looked alarmed. "You mean ask those things to eat our memories?"
Zann nodded. "There are five of us, and only two of my parents," he said. "Maybe we can draw the mice away!"

Morb glanced over. "What are you whispering about over there?" he snapped. "You should be grateful that you're here to see this. Otherwise you'd have only moments to live." He smirked. "Of course, I can't guarantee you have much longer than that. The Beast of the Otherworld is always hungry."
Zann ignored Morb and focused his thoughts on home. As more and more memories flooded his mind, Zann tried to send them toward the mice, inviting them to share.
One mouse wiggled its nose. Then it jumped down from Zann's father and took a step toward Zann. A second mouse followed, and then a third.
Soon all the mice were scampering across the room, headed for Zann and his friends.
"N-now what?" Gliss asked nervously, backing away as far as the troll restraining her would let her.
Once again Morb had turned away to taunt the Roodian queen. When he finally noticed the memory mice moving away from his machine, he let out a howl of fury.
"To me!" Wyssa intoned at the same time.

Zann held his breath as Wyssa's spell grabbed his parents and dragged them over to join the others. A split second later, the trolls were flung against the walls, and a Shield spell appeared around the rest of the group.
"No!" Morb flung a bolt of energy at Wyssa. But it bounced off the glowing shield and ricocheted around the room.
Zann hardly noticed. His parents looked dazed and weak. They stared at him blankly, and for a moment he was afraid it was too late.
Then his mother's eyes brightened. "Zann?" she whispered, reaching out to touch his face. "Is it really you?"
Zann's father smiled feebly. "We've missed you so much, son."
"They remember you!" Perda exclaimed.
"Of course we do," Zann's mother said. "But my head feels so fuzzy . . ."

"You're lucky. The mice probably didn't focus on any particular memory," Wyssa told Zann's parents. "They just nibbled away here and there. You two will be weak for a while, but your memories should come back."
Zann finally looked out through the shield.
Morb was gnashing his teeth and stalking back and forth, occasionally blasting a troll. "It's not enough!" he cried. "I still don't have enough power!"
"He's right. Look!" Perda pointed to the tube. The glowing energy stopped just short of the top.
Morb snarled and then climbed into the machine! "Even a Void has memories," he hissed. "I suppose mine will work just as well as any. I have a few childhood memories I wouldn't mind getting rid of!"
Venna gasped. "We have to do something!"
"Stand back," Wyssa said grimly.
She waved a hand, and the shield disappeared. Wyssa sent a huge Blast spell flying toward the contraption. But it stopped short, fizzling away.
"It's not working!" Gliss cried.
"I can see that, girl," Wyssa snapped. "The power of the Horns is blocking all magic."
"Maybe I can still get through." Darb handed the mibbit to Gliss and then rushed toward the machine. But some unseen force bounced him back. He landed on the stone floor with a grunt.
Venna paled. "There's no way to stop him! Magica is doomed!"
Morb cackled as the mice continued to feed. His body slumped weakly, but his eyes glittered with triumph.

"How do you like that?" he spat. "It took a Void to figure out how to focus enough magic energy to destroy Magica." He grinned nastily. "Then again, who else but a Void could really appreciate the true power of magic energy? Others take it for granted. But I could see how something that's harmless when used for small spells can be devastating when used for large ones!"
"What are we going to do?" Perda cried.

Zann didn't answer. All he could do was watch as the tube filled to the top. Morb brushed the mice off himself and got out of the machine. His mouth curled into an evil smile as he flung the hatch open.

Zann stared in horror as the energy flowed toward a wormhole blinking in the corner. Through the opening he caught a glimpse of the rough bark of the ancient Wormwood tree. It was too late—Magica was about to be destroyed!
Suddenly Zann had an idea. He turned to the queen. "Your Majesty, summon all the wormholes!"
For a second the Roodian queen looked confused. Then her eyes widened. She raised a hand, and the air buzzed with new energy.
"What are you doing?" Morb snarled, still weakened from the mice's feeding.
Suddenly the room was flooded with thousands of wormholes!
Morb looked stunned. "What—how—" he stammered.
Zann held his breath, hoping he was right about what would happen next. If he was wrong, he might have just destroyed not only Magica, but also every other world.
He glanced through a nearby wormhole. In a world he didn't recognize, a funny-looking dragon was nibbling on a tree.
Bzzt ! A tiny spurt of energy snaked in and fizzled out against the dragon's scaly side.
Zann spun around and spotted the rough seas of Skellia through another wormhole.
Bzzt ! A gulper leaped up and swallowed a small blob of energy hovering over the waves.
Everywhere he looked, Zann saw bits of energy fizzling out harmlessly in various worlds.
"It worked!" he cried. "The energy got divided into so many different worlds that it became completely harmless!"
"But how did you know that would happen?" Perda asked.
Zann shrugged. "It was what Morb said about how something that's powerful in large amounts is harmless in small amounts."
Morb gnashed his teeth. "I should have killed you when I had the chance!"
"But you didn't." Wyssa stepped forward and snapped her fingers. Instantly Morb was shackled to her. Then she pointed at the contraption and muttered a few words. Both horns exploded into shrapnel.
Zann and the others ducked, covering their heads until the dust settled. Then Venna stood up.
"Now what are we going to do with Morb?" she asked. "There will have to be a trial."
"Agreed," Zann's mother said. "Nax and I will have plenty of evidence to present."
Zann's father nodded. "I imagine the Red Council will banish him to the Wastelands forever."
Wyssa scowled. "I'll save you all the trouble." She yanked at Morb, who struggled weakly.
"No!" he cried. "Don't let her take me!"

Zann winced, remembering what Wyssa had said about feeding Morb to a scatter beast. Then he looked at his parents. Because of Morb, Zann had almost lost them all over again. Still, did even Morb deserve the fate Wyssa had in mind for him?
"Wait!" Gliss stepped forward. "After you're finished with him"—she glanced at Morb— "will you do something else?"
"What is it, girl?" Wyssa sounded impatient.
"We visited a world called Skellia," Gliss said. "The waters were rising, and the people were scared. Can you help them?"
Wyssa raised an eyebrow in surprise. "I know Skellia," she said. Her voice softened. "And yes, if the Skellians are ready to leave, I can help."
Darb stepped forward too. "Also, can you return this mibbit to Pax?"

"Of course. The Paxians must be worried about him." Wyssa waited while Darb rubbed the creature's ears before handing it over. Then she glanced around. "Any other errands you need me to handle for you?"
Her tone was sharp, but Zann caught a twinkle in her eye. "I think that's it," he said, "but . . ." He hesitated, staring at Morb. "What are you going to do with him?"
"Only what he deserves." Wyssa gave a jerk on the shackles. "I'm sure the queen can help direct you all home. Good-bye."
Dragging Morb, Wyssa stepped into the wormhole.
The evil villain cried, "No!"
"Are we there yet?" Zann joked as he and his parents walked toward their house. Zing was circling overhead, whistling joyfully.
"You tell me, son," his father joked back. "I've never been here before."

After Wyssa had departed with Morb, the Roodian queen sorted through the wormholes. First she located the one leading into Wormwood, which Venna used to return to First City. Then, after a long search, the queen found the one leading into Swamp Bottom.
"I can't wait to see what Boz has done with the interior," Zann's father said when they stopped in front of their house.
His wife chuckled. "Don't expect too much," she warned. "My father was never much of a decorator."
They headed inside. There was no sign of Boz.
"Look!" Zann's mother exclaimed. "Those are the blink images from our trip to the Flower Forest."
She and Zann's father hurried over for a closer look. Meanwhile Zann heard footsteps. A moment later his grandfather burst into the room.

"Zann!" Boz exclaimed. He rushed over and hugged Zann tightly. Then he gently shoved him away and glared. "Where in all the worlds have you been? I've been worried sick! The Directory showed nothing of your whereabouts, and every spell I tried was—"
Zann's mother stepped up behind Boz. "Hello, Dad," she said. "Did you miss me too?"
Boz's jaw dropped. "Asta?" he whispered. Then, his nose quivering wildly and his eyes widening, he spun around. "And Nax too! What—how did you . . .?"
Zann laughed. "We'll tell you all about it!"
That night Zann fell asleep happy. At one point, in the middle of the night, he was awakened by a terrible dream. Morb had escaped! And Zann's parents were in trouble . . .

But as Zann looked around, he remembered where he was. He was back in his own bed. His parents and Boz were nearby. Zing's fiery breath was warming his toes. For the first time in four years, Zann felt content.

It was a beautiful day in First City, and the streets buzzed with energy. At the edge of Treeview Park, the king and queen of Magica were speaking to a large gathering. Angry people held banners and signs. Some signs were magical, with flashing messages that changed words or colors. Others were plain signs written by hand. There had been many protests lately, and now the king and queen were trying to calm down the crowd.
A square-jawed man watched from a balcony overlooking the park. His big hands rested on a railing, and a door behind him was open to an opulent apartment.
"Void rights," he muttered. "What a concept. Seems popular though."
Suddenly he gasped, his knees buckling as his head exploded with pain. Pressing his hands to his head, he staggered through the door and collapsed onto a sofa.
A moment later the pain faded, and his eyes opened wide with surprise.
"Who is this?" he exclaimed. "How are you—?"
He paused, listening to a voice only he could hear. Then he nodded.
"Yes, of course I remember you. Who could forget?" He barked out a short, humorless laugh. "But I thought you were dead! That crazy old woman told the palace that she was going to . . ."
His words trailed off and he cocked his head, listening again.
"Yes, I see," he said. "Well, I'm glad. I've missed your business. But where are you now?"
A loud cheer rose from the gathering below, but the man hardly heard it. The voice in his head was speaking again.
"Who? Oh," the man said. "Yes, I can do that."
This time when he listened, he frowned. He rose to his feet and began pacing.

"I never fail!" he snapped. "Never! Besides, I know the perfect person to help us." Another brief pause followed. "Of course I know who is trustworthy. If you doubt my judgment, perhaps you should find someone else!"
He listened again, his mouth curving into a slight smile. Finally he nodded.

"Yes, I'm glad you see that." He wandered back onto the balcony and glanced at the scene below. "It's a deal. We shall make them all pay!" He laughed along with the voice in his head. "I'll begin immediately."
"See you tomorrow, Zann," someone called.
Zann waved without looking to see who'd spoken, and then stepped outside. After two months at First City Academy, he knew most of the kids' names. But he still didn't feel as if he had true friends.
"Not like back home in Swamp Bottom," he thought.
Zann grimaced, reminding himself that Swamp Bottom wasn't "home" anymore. Rubbing his fingers together, he stepped away from the building and muttered, "Zap!"
Splash!
Zann looked around. He was standing in a neighbor's decorative fountain.
"Drat," Zann said.
The neighbor was picking flutter flowers nearby.
"Sorry," Zann said to her.
She looked irritated for a second before her expression changed.
"Oh, it's young Zann, the hero!" she exclaimed. "How are you? And how are those worlds-traveling parents of yours?"
"Fine, thanks," Zann said politely. "Excuse me, I have to go."
It still felt strange when people treated him like a celebrity. Months had passed, but it still happened all the time.
He hurried over to his house. When he opened the front door, Zing flew out. The dragon chattered and spat flames.
"Sorry I'm late," Zann told Zing. "I had to stay after school for an assembly about Void rights. The headmaster said that we're all supposed to work at getting along—Reds, Voids, dragons . . ."

Zann hadn't been paying much attention to the Void rights protests. But the assembly had made him think about Darb. And that made him homesick for Swamp Bottom again. He hadn't seen Darb for more than two months—nor their friends Perda and Gliss.
Zing started zipping around overhead, sending flames everywhere. Zann conjured some dragon treats.

"It's okay, boy," he called, tossing Zing the treats. "I know you've been stuck in the house all day. But now we can go to Palace Park and play. I just have to stop by the lab first to tell Mom and Dad where we're going."

Zann considered sending his parents a message moth. Luckily, they'd stopped monitoring his every move. But for a month or so after Morb had been banished from Magica, Zann had had to check in with his parents all the time.
Zann tried to grab Zing to zap them both to the lab. But the little dragon wouldn't hold still long enough.
"Okay, I guess we'll walk," Zann said with a shrug.
He headed down the street, whistling for Zing to follow. Zing sped past him, diving to shoot flames at a passing flip fly.
"Hey!" A man cried, jumping aside as the flames missed the fly and almost hit him.
"Oops," Zann called and grabbed Zing by the wing. "Come on, little buddy, let's take the quick way."
Zap!
They landed across the street from the lab where Zann's parents worked. Zing yanked free immediately, diving down to attack a wiggle weed growing out of a crack in the sidewalk.
Zann hardly noticed. He stared at a group of about a dozen people. They were marching around in front of him holding a Void rights banner. Several people stood nearby and watched the marchers.
"Not another protest!" Zann muttered, shaking his head.
He forgot about that when he saw a message moth fluttering toward him. Zing saw it too.
"Zing, stop!" Zann grabbed the moth before the dragon could incinerate it. Zann smiled when he spotted several names scrawled on one wing. The moth had come from his friends in Swamp Bottom!
Before he could read their message, he heard a shout of anger.
"Give that back, you fire-breathing thief!"
Zann stuck the message moth in his pocket and then grabbed Zing. The little dragon had snatched a glowberry muffin away from one of the people watching the protest. The man looked angry.
"Zing!" Zann wrenched the muffin out of Zing's mouth. It had teeth marks and burns on it. Zann looked at the man. "I'll conjure you another one, sir."

"You'd better!" the man grumbled. "There's a reason most people don't keep fire whistlers as pets, you know." Suddenly his expression changed and he peered closely at Zann. "Wait, a fire whistler—hold on. Are you the Red kid who saved Magica from Morb?"
Zann never knew what to say when people asked him questions like that. He couldn't have saved anything without help from his friends and others.
So he said nothing. Instead he rubbed his hands together to create a new glowberry muffin.

But the man brushed it away. "I'm a reporter for the First City Flash. I came here to cover this protest, but nothing much is happening." With a snap of his fingers, he opened a note window in the air beside him.

"I'd love to get your opinion on all the recent protests in First City," the reporter went on. "I'm sure everyone in Magica would love to know what their young Red hero thinks of the Void rights movement!"
Zann shrugged. "I haven't been paying much attention," he answered truthfully. "I'm completely in favor of Void rights, of course. Other than that, I'm not very interested in politics."
Zann's words appeared on the note window as he said them.

"But you must have heard what people are saying." The reporter glanced at Zann's bright red hair. "Some non-Reds think the Red Council is almost as greedy as Morb himself. They say the Reds have too much power, and allowing them to control the relics Morb dug up is dangerous. They say that Magica's ancient relics belong to all citizens, and that the people should have a say in what happens to them. Not the Red Council."

Zann had heard those comments. But he hadn't paid much attention to them. The relics were dangerous—that much he knew. They could have given Morb enough power to take over all of Magica. But Zann trusted his parents and the others to handle the relics wisely now.
"I'm sure my parents are doing what they think is best," he said. "But you’d have to ask them about the details."
The reporter frowned at the note window. He seemed disappointed. Then he shrugged and brightened.
"All right, then," the reporter said. "What's going on with you these days, Zann? I'm sure everyone would enjoy hearing an update on your life since Morb's, er, permanent departure."

Zann winced at the last two words. Nobody ever came right out and said that Morb was dead. But Zann suspected he was. Wyssa had been furious when she'd dragged the villain through the vortex. But she'd never returned to Magica after that, so nobody knew for sure what she'd done with Morb.
"I really need to go," Zann said, glancing toward his parents' lab.
"This will only take a moment." The reporter smiled. "How are those friends of yours doing? I understand they returned to your old hometown."
"Yes." Zann slid a hand into his pocket to check on the message moth. "We moved to First City. But their families are still in Swamp Bottom."

"Yes, yes." The reporter glanced at the note window to make sure it was recording everything Zann said. "Speaking of family, I heard that your grandfather, Boz, came out of retirement to start working with the Red Council again. Is he helping to catalog the relics?"
Zann bit his lip. "Um, I don't pay much attention to that kind of thing."
He hoped the reporter would get bored and end the interview. But the reporter didn't look bored at all.
"What was it like traveling through the vortex?" he asked.

Zann hesitated, thinking back to those travels. Traveling through the vortex had been scary. It had also been exciting. But Zann didn't want to tell this stranger about that. He gulped and tried to think of some way to escape.
"Excuse me!" A girl's voice came from behind Zann. "Are you a reporter for the First City Flash ?"
Turning, Zann saw a girl he recognized from school. She was a year ahead of him, and he didn't know her name.
"Yes, I am," the reporter told her. "But I'm busy right now."
"Okay," the girl said. "But I just heard that Laddno is here. He's speaking soon in the palace square."
"Laddno is here?" someone nearby exclaimed. "Is that true?"
The girl shrugged. "I don't know. It's just what I heard."
The reporter looked excited. "I'd better get over there!" he said. "Thanks, young lady!"
He snapped his fingers and zapped out of sight. Other people zapped away too.
"Who's Laddno?" Zann asked the girl.

She laughed. "I thought everybody had heard of him. He's a super-successful businessman. He's also the new leader of the Void rights movement." She rubbed her fingers together to conjure a dragon treat, which she tossed to Zing. The dragon snapped it up eagerly and then whistled happily at the girl.
"Oh, right." Now Zann remembered hearing his parents mention the name. "Is Laddno a Void?"
"No. He's just interested in equal rights for everyone in Magica. But listen, you should get out of here. That reporter might come back once he finds out Laddno isn't really speaking to the crowd."
"Huh?" Zann was confused. "But you just said—"
The girl giggled. "I could tell that you wanted the reporter to stop bothering you, so I said the one thing I knew would get him to leave."
Zann smiled at the girl from school. "Thanks for getting rid of that reporter," he said. "I'm Zann."
"I know." She smiled. "Everyone at the Academy knows who you are. I'm Mari."
"Nice to meet you. Do you live around here?" Zann asked.
Mari shook her head. "I live in Treeview."
Treeview was a wealthy neighborhood on the southern edge of the city.
"Do you live near here?" Mari asked.
"No. But my parents' lab is right there." Zann pointed across the street.

Mari's eyes widened. "I've heard about them! Are they really working with all the ancient magical relics Morb found in the Cave of the Unknown?" She sounded impressed. "Like the Dragontamer's Charm, and the Mask of Zanta? That must be fascinating!"
"Yeah." Zann shrugged. "Do you want to come in and meet them?"
"Yes!" Mari exclaimed. "I'm super interested in that kind of work. I want to be a researcher someday."
Zann felt another pang of homesickness. Perda was interested in research too. She was always investigating other worlds and new forms of magic.

He led Mari into the lab, with Zing following. His parents were both bent over their work when Zann entered. Zann felt happy every time he saw them. They'd been lost in the vortex for four years, and he still could hardly believe they were really back.
"Zann!" His mother, Asta, spotted him first. "How was school today?"
"Fine." Zann waved toward Mari. "This is Mari. She goes to the Academy too."
"Hello, Mari." Nax, Zann's father, strode over to shake hands. "Any friend of Zann's is a friend of ours."
"It's an honor to meet you both," Mari said. "I've heard a lot about your work."
"It keeps us busy." Zann's mother chuckled. "Would you like a tour of the lab?"
"I'd love it!" Mari eagerly followed Asta into the next room.
Zann stuck his hand in his pocket.
"What do you have there, son?" his father asked.
"A message moth from my friends back home." Zann shot his father a sheepish look. "I mean, from Swamp Bottom."
His father patted his shoulder. "It's okay, Zann. You lived there for over four years. I'm sure you miss it."
"Only a little," Zann said quickly. "It's a pretty boring place. But I do miss my friends."
He pulled out the moth and scanned the message on its wing.
"Are they coming to the party?" his father asked.
Zann's birthday was in a couple of weeks. His parents had suggested a party to celebrate, and Zann had invited the gang from Swamp Bottom.

"They're not sure yet." Zann sighed and released the moth, which flew out the window. "Gliss' parents don't want her to ride a dragon this far. And they're not sure if they'll be able to take time off to zap her and the others here."
"Hmm." Nax scratched his chin. "Well, maybe they'll work something out."
Zann hoped so. First City was far from Swamp Bottom—much too far for his friends to zap here on their own.
Before Zann could say anything else, Mari rushed back in. "I just saw the Mask of Zanta!" she cried, her eyes sparkling. "This is the most incredible day of my life!"
Asta followed her, smiling. "Mari volunteered to help us catalog the relics," she told her husband.
"I'd love to help!" Mari said. "The teachers at school say I'm very precise. I promise I won't make any mistakes."
"That's very nice of you," Nax told her. "We might take you up on that, Mari."
Clunk!
Everyone jumped as a device crashed to the floor. It had a dial and a small hose. Zing quickly snatched the device up in his mouth.
"Zing!" Asta grabbed the device from the dragon. "You naughty beast."
"What is that thing?" Zann asked.
"It's called an infusinator." His mother set the device back on the shelf. "It's a new invention we're working on." She shook a finger at Zing. "And it's not edible!"
"You have so many interesting things here." Mari peered at another item. "What's this?"
"The guidelink? Zann's father invented that one," Asta said. "We think it might allow people to navigate the vortex more easily."
Nax grinned. "Yes, but don't get too excited yet. We're still working out the kinks."
"What does it do?" Zann asked, thinking back to how difficult it had been to travel through the vortex.
"It does several things," Nax said. "So far it seems best at locating and locking onto sources of magic power."
"That way, travelers can recover their magical energy faster," Asta said. "It also helps them avoid worlds with weak or no magic."
Zann shuddered, remembering the time he and his friends had almost been trapped on a world with no magic.
"That's amazing," Mari said. But this time she sounded a little nervous as well as impressed.

Zann wasn't surprised. Most people had never even seen a wormhole up close, let alone traveled through the vortex. "The vortex isn't that scary," he told her. "It's actually pretty cool. We visited this one world where—"
He stopped as another message moth fluttered in and flew over to Mari.
"Oh," she said, scanning the wing. "Sorry, I have to get home to watch my little cousins. Thank you for showing me the lab." She smiled at Zann and his parents. "See you at school, Zann."
As soon as she was gone, Nax grinned. "I'm glad you're making friends, Zann. Especially with such a smart and pretty girl!"
Asta was grinning too.
Zann scowled. "Very funny, Dad," he muttered. "I'm taking Zing to the park for a while." He grabbed the dragon and zapped away before his parents could tease him anymore.

The dinner table at Zann's house was crowded that night. Boz and Teplo were there, along with Teplo's assistant, Fala. Teplo's sniffer goose was there too. The foul-tempered bird lurked under the table, honking at Zing and biting Zann's feet.
Boz had also invited his friend Saffa and her husband, Staz. Like Boz and Teplo, Saffa was a very skilled Magic Master.
"I can't remember the last time I was at a table with so many Reds," Staz commented with a chuckle. "I hope Laddno and his anti-Red followers don't find out."
Teplo looked up from his food. "Is Laddno part of the anti-Red crowd now too? I thought he was only involved with Void rights."

"Maybe so." Boz stirred his puffnut soup, his long nose quivering. "But he's getting people awfully riled up. The mood here in First City feels tense, especially with all those powerful relics at the lab sending out extra magic energy."
"The king and queen are quite concerned about all the unrest," Fala said.
Nax nodded. "Venna keeps muttering about the anger Laddno is churning up between Voids and non-Voids." He looked around the table. "There's also a certain amount of anger between Reds and non-Reds."

Zann was surprised by the worry in his father's voice. Sure, he knew there had been some anti-Red sentiment in First City lately. But that was nothing new. Even back in Swamp Bottom, a few people seemed to resent the fact that Reds had stronger magic than everyone else. He thought about Jev and grimaced.
"Is your soup all right, Zann?" Asta asked.
"Sure." Zann pushed Jev out of his mind. That was one good thing about moving to First City. He would probably never have to see that jerk again!

His mother returned her attention to the conversation. But Zann stopped listening. He had more important things on his mind than politics. He hoped Gliss' parents would change their minds about the dragons. After all, Zann, Perda, Darb, and Gliss had ridden dragons to First City before. And Darb was friendly with a local dragon breeder. Zann was sure the breeder would let the kids borrow a couple of dragons again.

"Oh!" Saffa said suddenly. "There's news." She snapped her fingers, and a large floating image appeared above the table. It showed a crowd of people shaking their fists and yelling. Many of them held signs about Void rights.
"Oh dear," Saffa said. "This image is from the future. It shows a protest that will take place soon."
Boz read the words that appeared on the image. "Laddno says it will be the biggest protest yet."
Zann was reading too. "Ugh! It's going to be on my birthday! I hope Gliss' parents don't hear about it."
"Who's that, boy?" Teplo peered at him. "Gliss . . . You mean your Red friend? Isn't she in favor of Void rights?"
"Yes," Zann said. "And her parents are too, I think. At least they seem to like Darb just fine. But they're kind of overprotective."
"I see," his father chimed in. "You're afraid all the unrest will make them worry about letting Gliss come to the big city."
"Right." Zann yanked his foot away as Teplo's goose bit it again. "And if they won't let her come, the others might not be allowed to come either."
Fala looked sympathetic. "That's tough, Zann. I know you four are awfully close."
Suddenly Zann had an idea. "Hey, if my friends can't come here for my party, why don't we go to them?" He quickly grew excited. "We could celebrate my birthday in Swamp Bottom!"
His parents traded a look with Boz and the others.
"I don't think that will work right now, Zann," Asta said. "I'm sorry."
"Why not?" Zann said. "It would be so much easier for us to just zap out there."
"No, your mother is right," Boz said. "It's not a good time for any of us to leave First City."
"But don't worry," Nax added. "We'll figure out something to get your friends here."
Zann wanted to ask his father how he planned to make that happen. But Nax was already turning to tell Saffa and Staz about something Venna had said the day before.

Zann clenched his fists under the table, ignoring the goose as it yanked on his pant leg. It wasn't fair! All his parents thought about was their work. They were almost as bad as Venna herself, and everyone knew her whole life revolved around her role on the Red Council.
Zann couldn't sit there anymore. He nudged the goose away with his foot and stood up. "May I be excused?" he said. "I want to take Zing out for a walk before it gets dark."
"Good idea, Zann," his father said, barely looking at him.

Soon Zann was wandering along the quiet street near his house. Zing had played for a long time at the park earlier, so he wasn't as hyper as usual. But when a heat hornet buzzed by, Zing shot out a burst of flame and flew after the bug.
"Wait up, Zing," Zann called. "I don't want to—hey, what's that?"

A bright image had appeared in midair when Zing flew past, but now it was gone. Zann stepped closer, assuming the image would appear again. Nothing happened. Zann moved around the sidewalk, but still the image wouldn't reappear.
Zann conjured a dragon treat. "Zing, come back here!" he called.
When Zing came near, the image appeared again. But when Zann stepped closer to it, it disappeared.
"Weird," Zann murmured. "Why does it disappear when I'm nearby?"
"Because you're a Red, that's why," a voice said from behind Zann.
Surprised, Zann spun around. He was even more surprised when he recognized the figure stepping out of the shadows.
"Jev!" Zann blurted out.
"What are you doing in First City?" Zann asked, stunned to see Jev.
Jev ignored the question. "It's a new kind of magic," he said with a smirk. "Your parents aren't the only ones who can invent stuff, you know."
"Huh?" Zann was still confused by his old enemy's unexpected appearance. He glanced at Zing, who was flying overhead, whistling suspiciously at Jev. "What are you talking about? What new magic?"
"The image, dummy." Jev rolled his eyes. "The new magic makes the image visible to any living thing except Reds. See?"
He stepped forward. The image appeared again.
This time Zann was able to get a better look. It was an ad for the mass protest on his birthday.
"What's the big deal?" Zann said with a frown. "Everyone knows about that protest. It's been all over the news."
"Maybe." Jev stepped back, and the ad disappeared again. "But the image is a good way to make it clear that Reds aren't welcome there."
Zann's head was spinning. He'd been wishing all week for visitors from Swamp Bottom. However, Jev definitely wasn't one of the people he'd had in mind!
"I thought the protest was to promote Void rights," Zann said. "Why wouldn't Voids want Reds to support that?"

"You're so naive." Jev was still smirking. "Things are changing in Magica. And Reds like you probably won't like what's coming. That's why my parents decided to come to First City. We want to help Laddno bring about those changes."
"Laddno?" Zann was surprised to hear the man's name again. "You've heard of Laddno?"

"Hasn't everyone?" Jev said. "He's one of the most successful businessmen in Magica. He knows how to get things done. Including the Void rights stuff and, you know, other things. Now that he's involved, everything is going to change. Just you wait and see."
Zann wasn't sure what Jev was talking about. But he didn't want to talk to his old enemy anymore.
"Excuse me," Zann said. "I'm sure you don't want to be seen with a Red like me. So I'm out of here."
He grabbed Zing, snapped his fingers, and zapped away.
Splash!

"Drat," Zann grumbled, realizing he'd barely stopped to think about where he wanted to land. He glanced around and recognized a small local park. Good. At least he hadn't accidentally zapped to Wormwood or some other nasty place.
He stepped out of the small pond where he'd landed. Zing flew off to chase a bird in the treetops. Zann looked around again. The park was deserted.

Zann rubbed his fingers together, preparing to zap back home. Then he paused and decided to wait a moment. Talking to Jev had made Zann curious about Laddno. Everyone seemed to be talking about this guy lately. Yet Zann knew almost nothing about the man.
"I'll check the Directory," he thought.
The Directory listed the names of all the people in Magica, along with basic information about each of them.
Zann rubbed his hands together again, creating more magic friction. A book-like magical image appeared in the air in front of him. Countless tiny photos floated in the image.
"Laddno!" Zann said.

Instantly, the photos scattered as Laddno's picture expanded to fill the screen. Zann scrolled quickly past the photo. Thanks to the ads for the protest, he already knew what Laddno looked like. Now he wanted information about him.

Zann scanned the entry. As Jev had mentioned, Laddno was listed as being a businessman. Some citizens of Magica had no talent or patience for certain types of creative magic. So they hired people like Laddno to help them conjure a nicer house or more comfortable furniture or clothing that fit them properly. And of course, Voids couldn't create their own things at all. They had to rely on family members, friends, or people like Laddno to conjure all their clothes and other necessities.

Zann read that Laddno had been born in First City and was a few years younger than Zann's parents. He was known to have fairly strong magic for a non-Red, and he currently lived in the wealthy neighborhood of Treeview.
"Treeview," Zann muttered. "That's where Mari lives. Maybe she knows him."
Next he read about Laddno's involvement in the Void rights movement. The Directory said he'd joined just a few weeks earlier but had quickly become the leader of the movement.
Before closing the Directory, Zann decided to check for Wyssa. The last time he'd done that, her entry looked the same as it always had. That was shortly after she'd taken Morb away though.
"Wyssa," Zann said. Laddno's page disappeared, replaced immediately with Wyssa's. The page had a new note: Presumed to be off-world.
"Wow. She really is gone," Zann thought. "I wonder what world she's on now."
Zann closed the Directory. "Come on, Zing," he called to the dragon, who was still sniffing around in the treetops. "Let's go home and—aah!"
Zann's head suddenly throbbed with pain. He staggered back, grabbing a tree to steady himself.
