He squeezed his eyes shut and waited for the pain to pass. It felt like a Red Share. But this seemed different from previous Red Shares. For one thing Zann couldn't tell which Red the Share was coming from. He also wasn't sure which emotion had caused it. Was it pain? Fear? Anger? Or some combination of all three?
The feeling started to subside. Zann breathed out with relief.

Then he gasped as the feeling washed over him again. The pain wasn't quite as strong this time, but now a faint voice came with it. Zann couldn't tell who was speaking, but the person was saying just one word: "Help!"
"Wow," Zann blurted out as the faint voice and the pain finally disappeared. "That was the weirdest Share I've ever had."
He was worried about Boz and the other Reds back at his house. What if something had happened after he’d left?
Zann grabbed Zing and zapped back to his family's dining room.
His father smiled brightly at him. "You're back, Zann."
"Yep." Zann glanced around, relieved to see that everyone seemed to be okay. "Is everything all right here?"
"Of course." Teplo reached for the puckerberry pudding. "Except that we're running out of dessert."
Most of the other adults chuckled. But Boz stared at Zann.
"What’s the matter, my boy?" he asked. "You look as agitated as a panic bug."
"Something strange just happened," Zann said. He told the adults about the Red Share.
"That is odd," Saffa said when Zann finished. "If the Share didn't come from any of us, it must have come from another Red whom you know."
Boz stood up and rubbed his fingers together. "We should check around. Just in case."

"Don't worry, though, Zann," Nax said. "The close presence of so many powerful relics could be causing this. Their energy has been interfering with all magic energy, especially for Reds, who are more sensitive to magic."
Zann nodded slowly. He wanted to believe his father was right. But he couldn't help remembering how desperate that faint voice had sounded.

That night Zann had trouble falling asleep. He stared at the ceiling, still thinking about that weird Red Share. Who was trying to contact him? Boz and the others had checked with most of the Reds they knew, and so far everyone was fine.
Tap! Tap!

Zann sat up when he heard a light rapping on his window. A spy fly fluttered outside. Zann was confused. Spy flies usually stayed hidden while spying. But this one was trying to get his attention. After hesitating a moment, Zann opened the window.
He gasped as the spy fly dived straight into his ear.
"What's going on?" Zann thought. "I didn't summon a spy fly."
Suddenly an image filled his mind, and in it he saw his three best friends!
"Hi, Zann!" Perda waved, looking pleased with herself. "If this works, you should be seeing all of us right now."
Gliss grinned. "Yes, Perda is still trying to invent new kinds of magic. Like tinkering with spy flies."
Zann could hardly believe it. Seeing his friends was great!
"Hi, guys," he murmured, even though he knew they couldn't hear him. Suddenly he felt more homesick than ever.
His friends chatted for a while, filling him in on all the news around Swamp Bottom. They even mentioned that Jev had moved away, though none of them knew where he'd gone.
"I know where he is," Zann thought with a sick feeling.
But he didn't think about Jev for long. He was more interested in listening to his friends.
"Okay, we should send the fly off now," Darb said at last.
Gliss nodded. "We haven't figured out how to get there for your birthday yet."
"But we'll definitely be there," Perda added. "Even if we have to take a wormhole to First City!"
"I'm sure that won't be necessary," Gliss said with a shudder. "Although Perda has been studying up on the vortex lately!"
Zann felt alarmed. Perda was bold enough to do something crazy like jump into a wormhole. He'd been the same way once. But he had a healthy respect for the vortex these days.

The spy fly wiggled out of Zann's ear. Zann didn't know how to get it to spy on him and return to the three kids, though he planned to ask Perda. So he summoned a message moth and inscribed a quick note to his friends. Then he fell asleep, thinking about good old Swamp Bottom.
Zap.
Zann landed across the street from the Academy the next morning. Several people raced toward him.
"Red!" one shouted, sounding angry. "We don't want your kind here."
Zann realized he'd landed in the middle of yet another protest.
"Leave me alone!" Zann exclaimed. "I'm leaving."
He snapped his fingers to zap across the street and into the school. But instead he landed on his rear end right in front of the door.

"Drat," he muttered, remembering that the Academy had a special kind of Shield spell over it. The shield was there to prevent kids from zapping in or out during the day. Zann's old school in Swamp Bottom was a lot smaller, so it didn't need that kind of spell.
Grumbling, he opened the door and hurried inside. He almost crashed into Mari.
"Hi, Zann!" She greeted him with a smile. "Did you just get here?"
"Yes," Zann said. "I ran into another protest outside."
"I saw that too." Mari didn't sound very interested. "Hey, did your parents say anything about my offer to volunteer at their lab? I really want to do it."
"They didn't say anything to me," Zann said. "I can remind them if you want. They're so busy these days that they might have forgotten."
"Could you? That would be great!" Mari said. "Thanks, Zann."
Zann didn't answer. He'd just spotted another familiar face.
"What's he doing here?" he said, annoyed.
Mari followed his gaze. "You mean Jev? He just enrolled here."
"Great," Zann said with a sigh. "That's just great."
That afternoon Zann couldn't wait to escape from school. Jev had been in all of Zann's classes. Zann was already tired of his old enemy's sneers and dirty looks.
He hurried outside and took a deep breath. He rubbed his fingers together to create magic friction. But before he could zap away, he noticed a message moth flapping toward him.
The message was from his friends.
Zann smiled. "My friends are coming!"
Several days later Zann rushed for the door as soon as school ended. He heard Mari laugh and call his name.
"Why are you in such a rush?" she exclaimed, catching up with him. "I thought I was the only one so eager to escape today!"
"I think everyone is ready to leave." Zann looked around. The next week was a school holiday, and all the students looked excited. "But why are you so eager? I thought you liked school."
"I do." Mari smiled. "But I like working at your parents' lab even more. Want to walk over there with me?"
"I can't today," Zann said. "My best friends are arriving later for a visit."
Zann had been happy ever since receiving the message moth. Gliss' Uncle Gar was coming to First City for a meeting. He'd offered to zap Zann's friends there for the party.
That reminded Zann—he'd meant to invite Mari to his party the next day. He opened his mouth to tell her about it. But just then Jev walked over.
"Watch out, Mari," Jev said with a smirk. "If you keep hanging out with Reds, people might start to talk."

Zann frowned at him. "Mind your own business, Jev." Then he hurried away, figuring he could send Mari a message moth later. He didn't want Jev to hear about the party, especially since Gliss would be there. Even though Gliss was a Red, Jev had always liked her.
When Zann got home, Zing was the only one there. The dragon looked at him expectantly.
Zann shook his head. "No park today, little buddy. We have guests coming."

Zann ducked as Zing shot an angry flame at him. He felt sorry for the dragon being cooped up in the house all day. But he knew Zing would be happy when Darb arrived later. Darb had a special bond with animals, including dragons.
He conjured up some snacks and puckerberry juice. Then, feeling restless, he wandered around the house. He was still waiting when his parents came in.
"Are your friends here yet?" Asta asked.
"Not yet," Zann said. "You left the lab early?"
Nax nodded. "We wanted to be here when your friends arrive."
"Besides, we're not needed at the lab." Asta chuckled. "Your friend Mari is so enthusiastic, she's doing the work of three people. I'm glad you reminded us to contact her."
Zann noticed that his father was holding something. "Isn't that one of your inventions, Dad?"
"Yes, it's the infusinator." Nax held it up. "I thought Darb might want to use it while he's here."

"It will provide him with magic energy," Asta added. "It uses a magical technique we discovered in a world called Atmo. Atmo's magic source is the energy in its air. Some plants and animals can ingest large quantities of that energy and store it for future use.
"We heard Morb used leeches from Atmo to power one of his contraptions," Asta added grimly.
Zann shuddered. Those blue leeches were horrible!
"Does the infusinator use leeches too?" he asked.
"No, it's made out of wood from lung trees," Asta said. "Lung trees have an amazing ability to store magic."
"Darb just needs to breathe in stored energy from this hose," Nax said. "Then he can use that energy, just like any Magician."
"But we brought back only one piece of wood from the lung tree," Asta said. "And we've already used a lot of its energy while experimenting. So Darb will have to use the infusinator carefully."
"I thought it could suck magic out of the air," Zann said.
His mother shook her head. "Only in Atmo. Magica's energy works differently. We're still trying to figure out how to refill it."

"We've been experimenting with different techniques," Nax added. "For now, Darb won't be able to zap long distances or do anything else that requires lots of energy. But at least he can create food and do other simple tasks."
"Yes, and we hope he'll let us know what he thinks of it," Asta added. "This infusinator is only a prototype, but if it works well, we—"
"Surprise!" Perda cried, appearing in front of them. "We're here!"
Gliss appeared next, holding onto Darb's arm. Zann grinned, so happy to see the three of them that he hardly knew how to respond.
Zing let out a burst of flame and raced toward Darb.
"Hi, Zing." Darb smiled and scratched the dragon's scaly head. "I've missed you."
"I've missed you guys too," Zann blurted out. "I'm so glad you're here!"

For the next few minutes, the four of them couldn't stop talking. There was so much to catch up on! A few times, though, Zann couldn't help feeling a little awkward. His friends mentioned people and events he didn't know anything about. But mostly it was great to be with them again.
After a while his parents showed Darb the infusinator.
"We'd love for you to try it out and let us know how it works for you," said Nax.
"Oh, sure." Darb seemed a little uncomfortable. "Thanks."

Zann had conjured a bed for Darb. But since Zann's house was fairly small, Saffa and Staz had offered to let the girls stay with them. Teplo had offered too, but Zann knew Perda and Gliss wouldn't want to deal with Teplo's cranky goose.
"Let's go to Saffa's so you can settle in," Zann said. "I'll show you my neighborhood on the way."
The kids headed out, with Zing scurrying along at Darb's heels.
"That's the park Zing and I go to," Zann said, pointing. "And over there is—"
Suddenly that weird feeling struck Zann again. This time the pain was so strong, it knocked him to the ground!

Zann writhed on the ground, his head exploding with sounds, feelings, and images. Once again fear, pain, and anger surged through him. A faint voice called for help as waves splashed and rain pounded down. Feeling seasick, Zann pressed both hands to his forehead.
"Zann!" Perda cried. "What's wrong?"
Zann squeezed his eyes shut, trying to block out her voice. The cry in his head was a little louder now, and it sounded vaguely familiar. Who could it be? Zann tried to focus as the cry came again.
"Help me!" the person cried. "Please, someone help me before it's too late!"
Then the feelings disappeared as abruptly as they had come. Zann sat up, sweating and breathing hard.
"Zann!" Darb was squeezing his shoulder. "Are you all right?"
"I—I think so." Zann gulped in a breath and slowly climbed to his feet. His whole body felt shaky. "I mean, yes, I'm okay. This has happened before."
He described the mysterious Shares he'd been receiving. His friends looked confused.
"Are they Red Shares or not?" Gliss asked.
Zann shrugged. "I don't know. I can't tell who they're coming from."
"Are you sure it's not Boz, or some other Red that you know?" Darb asked.
Zann shook his head. "I checked last time. Boz and the others contacted every Red they could think of, and nobody knew anything about the Shares."
"That's weird." Perda chewed her lower lip, looking thoughtful. "I've never read anything about this kind of magic."

"My mom and dad think it could be a result of having all those relics close by," Zann said. "They said the relics possess such strong and ancient magic that they might be affecting our regular magic."
"Speaking of the relics, I hope it's not Morb contacting you," Perda said half-jokingly. "Maybe he's up to more magical tricks."
Gliss frowned at her. "It couldn't be Morb. Wyssa made sure that he will never do magic again."
"Or anything else," Zann put in with a shudder.
"I was only joking," Perda told them. "Do you think it's—"
A shout interrupted her. Two women were hurrying toward them. They both looked excited.
"It's you, isn't it?" one woman exclaimed. "The hero kids?"
The second woman pointed at Zing. "I even recognize the dragon!" she cried. "But I forgot his name!"
For the next few minutes, Zann and his friends had to answer the women's questions. Finally Zann made an excuse to hurry away.
"Maybe we should take a shortcut to Saffa's house," Zann said. "Let's go through the park."
He led the way. Halfway across the park, he heard voices ahead.
"Uh-oh," Gliss said with a smile. "Do you think more of our fans are looking for us?"
Just then a group of people marched into view, waving signs.
Perda's eyes widened. "Is it one of those Void rights protests we keep hearing about?" she whispered to Zann.
Zann nodded. "There are even more protests now," he said. "A guy named Laddno took over the movement."
"Oh, I've heard about him," Gliss said. "My parents were talking about how hard he's working to bring attention to the Void rights cause."
Zann glanced at Darb, who was staring at the ground.
Before Zann could say anything, Perda nudged him.
"Look!" she exclaimed. "Is that Jev? What's he doing in First City?"
Zann sighed. "He's here for the protests."

Jev was marching with the others, waving a colorful sign. He spotted Zann and his friends and came over. Zann expected him to say hi to Gliss, but Jev ignored her. He ignored Zann too and only gave Perda a halfhearted smile.
Instead Jev's eyes were focused on Darb. "Hey, Darb," he said in a friendly voice. "I didn't expect to see you in First City."

Darb looked surprised. Zann knew how he felt. Jev had always been mean to Darb and the other Voids in Swamp Bottom. In fact, that was how Zann and Darb had become friends. Soon after moving to Swamp Bottom, Zann had stood up to Jev when Jev was bullying Darb.

Jev shot the others a dirty look. "You shouldn't be hanging around with Reds," he told Darb. "Why don't you come with me? I can introduce you to some people who are working to get equal magic for all—even Voids like you."
"No thanks," Darb said. "I'd rather stay with my friends."
Jev frowned. "Suit yourself," he said. "But Laddno wants everyone to join in the struggle for equality."
Suddenly cheers came from the group. Most of the protestors were yelling Laddno's name.
Jev brightened. "He's here!" he cried. "I heard he might come today." He smirked at Zann and Gliss. "You might want to hide your hair, you two."
Jev dashed away before anyone could respond.
Gliss looked uneasy. "Let's get out of here," she said.
"Hold on for a second." Perda stepped forward and peered over the heads of the crowd. "I want to get a look at Laddno."

"Me too," Zann said. He and his friends stood on their tiptoes as a man strode onto a dais that someone had just conjured. Zann recognized Laddno right away from the ads. He had a large, square head and broad shoulders. His deep-set eyes swept over the crowd.
"Greetings, citizens of First City!" Laddno shouted, raising both hands. "Thank you for coming today."
"Void rights!" someone in the crowd shouted.
"Banish the greedy Reds!" someone else shrieked. The rest of the onlookers cheered loudly.
Gliss shivered. "Come on, you guys," she said. "We shouldn't be here."
This time Zann agreed. "Let's go." He grabbed Darb and Perda, and Perda grabbed Gliss.
"Zap!" Zann whispered, aiming for Saffa's house.

The next morning Zann took his friends to his parents' lab for a tour. Perda wanted to see where they worked and check out their latest inventions. Saffa decided to go too. When they arrived, they found Boz there with Zann's parents.
"Would you like to see the relics?" Asta asked Zann's friends.
"Sure," Perda said. "Is the Mask of Zanta here?"
"You already saw that," Gliss reminded her.
"That was when it was lying around in the Cave of the Unknown," Perda said. "Seeing it here is different."
Zann followed his mother and his friends into the next room.
"Wow," Gliss said when Asta showed them the Mask of Zanta. It was locked in a glass case. "That's amazing. And kind of scary."
"We keep this relic separate from the others, since it's probably the strongest one we found," Zann's mother said. "Other than the Horn of the Otherworld, maybe. But that was destroyed."
Zann shuddered, remembering how Morb had tried to take over Magica with the Horn.

They moved on to the other relics waiting to be cataloged. Zann's mother even took out a few for the kids to touch. None of the other relics were as powerful as the Mask of Zanta, but still, Zann felt ancient magic crackling around them.
"What are you going to do with them?" Perda asked, examining an old, cracked cup. "Are you still planning to destroy them all?"

"We're not sure yet." Asta sighed. "Most members of the Red Council would prefer that the relics weren't around, in case someone like Morb ever tries to use them for evil purposes. But a few members think we should keep some relics."
"Like Venna?" Zann guessed. The head of the Red Council had been opposed to destroying the relics all along. She wanted to store them away in case the items' strong magic was ever needed.
"I see why she thinks that." Perda carefully set down the relic she was holding. "If someone as strong as Morb does come along, the relics could help us fight him."
Zann's mother nodded. "Yes, that's Venna's argument," she said. "But my father and a few others believe it's not worth the risk. They think—oh, hello, Mari."
Mari had just entered the room. She was holding another relic.
"Hi," she said, looking surprised to see so many people in the lab. "Excuse me. I didn't mean to interrupt."
"No, it's okay." Zann stepped forward. "This is Mari, a friend from my new school," he told the others. "Mari, these are my friends from home—Perda, Darb, and Gliss."
Mari smiled. "Nice to meet you."
"Same here," Gliss said. "Are you coming to the party?"
"Oops!" Zann said. "I've been meaning to invite you. It's this afternoon, but I'd love for you to come." He smiled sheepishly. "Sorry for the late notice."
"That's okay," Mari said. "I think I can come. Thanks for the invitation."
She set down the relic she was holding and followed them back into the main room. Boz and Saffa were leaning over one of Nax's inventions while he explained how it worked.
"What is that?" Perda hurried over. "It looks interesting!"
Nax smiled at her. "I call it the guidelink. It will help people travel through the vortex more easily."
Just then the door flew open. Zann was shocked to see the king and queen of Magica rush in. Right behind them was Venna, followed by a Red, a man whom Zann had never seen before.
Zann's friends also looked shocked by the sight of the king and queen.
"Who's that guy?" Darb whispered. "He looks familiar."
"I don't know," Zann whispered back.
"Good! You're all here," the queen said, staring at Boz, Saffa, and Zann's parents. Then she spotted Zann and the other kids. "Oh! Hello, youngsters."
"We need to talk," Venna told the other adults, ignoring the kids. "It's important."
The king rubbed his fingers together. "I'll zap us all to the palace. It will be private there."
"All right." Zann's mother rubbed her hands together and stepped toward the king. Then she widened her eyes. "Oh! Some of the relics are still out."
"I'll take care of them," Mari said.
"Thanks, Mari," Asta said. "I'm sure we'll be back soon."
The adults zapped away.
"I wonder what's going on," Gliss said.
Perda rubbed her chin. "I'm wondering the same thing," she said. "Do you think they're talking about what to do with the relics?"
"I doubt it," Zann said. "They've been talking about that for months. This seemed urgent."
"Maybe it's about the Void rights protests," Gliss suggested.
"Why would that be urgent?" Perda asked.
"Boz says Laddno is stirring up too much unrest," Zann said. "He thinks the protests are turning people against the Red Council, and Reds in general."
"Wow, really?" Perda looked surprised.
Mari cleared her throat. "Excuse me," she said. "I'd better go take care of those relics." She hurried into the other room.
"She seems nice," Gliss said.
Perda wandered over to pick up the guidelink. "Do you think this really works?" she said. "Maybe we should test it out."
"What do you mean?" Gliss' eyes widened nervously.
Perda laughed. "I'm just kidding. But Zann's dad wants Darb to try out his other invention, right? It would be fun to try this one too. I'd love to see more worlds!"
"Not me," Gliss declared. "I never want to see the inside of the vortex again!"

Zann took the guidelink from Perda and put it on a shelf. "Let's go home and get ready for my party." He glanced at the spot where the adults had zapped away. "I just hope my parents and Boz get back from the palace in time."

Everyone was having fun at Zann's party. His parents had returned from the palace just in time to greet the first guests. Boz, Teplo, and Saffa had arrived a little late, but they all seemed to be enjoying themselves now. The delicious food and fancy decorations that Zann and his parents had conjured made the house look festive.
"This is great, Zann!" Perda said. "Your First City friends are really nice."
"Thanks." Zann had invited several kids from his new school, and most of them had come. Mari hadn't shown up yet though. He hoped she wasn't insulted because he'd invited her at the last minute.
"Over here, Zann!" Gliss called from nearby. "We're going to play Conjure and Vanish."
Zann smiled, forgetting about Mari. Conjure and Vanish was one of his favorite party games. He and Perda hurried over.
"It's your party, so you go first," Gliss told him.

"Okay." Zann rubbed his hands together to create magic friction. He closed his eyes and focused on the object he wanted to conjure—a swamp shiner. That was a type of lamp he'd used when exploring the swamp back home. He then used a Vanishing spell to make the lamp invisible before anyone could see it.
"Are you ready?" a kid asked eagerly.
Zann opened his eyes and nodded. "Gliss, you can go first," he said.
She reached for the invisible item, feeling all around it. "Is it a drinking glass?"
"Nope." Zann grinned and pointed to Perda. "Next?"
Perda smiled as soon as she felt the object. "That's easy! It's a swamp shiner. You made them all the time when we used to sneak out at night to look for flash fish."
"Right!" Zann grinned at her. "Now it's your turn to conjure something."

The sun went down, and everyone was still having fun. Some kids danced while others talked and ate snacks. One group of kids played a game of exploding dominoes. Zann was drinking some airberry punch when his father hurried over.
"Your mother and I just got called back to the palace for an emergency meeting," Nax said.
"Another one?" Zann said. "What's going on?"
His father looked distracted. "We'll tell you later. Right now, just keep having fun with your friends."
He zapped away with Zann's mother. Zann suddenly noticed that Boz was nowhere in sight. Neither were Teplo or Saffa.

Then he spotted Perda standing by the door to the backyard. Seeing her made him feel happy and sad at the same time. He was glad that Perda and his other friends were there. But they would have to go home in a couple of days. How long would it be before they were all together again?
He hurried over to Perda. "Want to get some fresh air?" he asked.
"Sure." She smiled.
They went out onto the patio. The air was cool, with a slight breeze that ruffled Perda's hair.
"Wow, you look—," Zann blurted out, and then stopped himself.
"What?" Perda asked.
Zann gulped. He'd been about to say that she looked pretty. But suddenly he felt awkward about saying that.
"Uh, you look older," he said instead. Then he laughed. "Two months older, I guess."
Perda blinked, seeming confused. Before she could respond, the door burst open.
"There you are, Zann!" a kid from school exclaimed. "There's a huge protest starting outside right now."
"Yeah!" Another schoolmate came up behind him. "Laddno said it's going to be the biggest one yet! Let's go check it out!"
The pair rushed for the front door. Perda started to follow.
"Wait, where are you going?" Zann asked.
"We should see what's going on," she said.
Everyone headed out the front door. Zann sighed, not very interested in another protest. But his best friends were following the crowd, so Zann followed too.
"It's at the palace square," one of the kids called. "Let's zap there so we don't miss anything."
The kids from First City started disappearing. Perda grabbed Zann's hand.
"You'll have to zap us there," she said. "I don't remember how to get to the palace."
Zann nodded, grabbing Gliss with his free hand. She was already holding onto Darb's arm.
"Zap!" Zann cried.
When they landed, Zann saw a massive crowd in the square outside the palace. People waved signs and shouted.
"Wow," Perda said. "This is crazy!"
Zann nodded. "I can't believe the king and queen are allowing a protest like this so close to the palace."
Just then Laddno stepped into view near the palace doors. "This is an important day!" he shouted. "Please welcome my esteemed guests."
The palace doors opened, and the king and queen walked out.
"What's going on?" Gliss said. "They're not joining his movement, are they?"
"We have an important announcement," the king said. His voice sounded shaky.
The queen took her husband's hand. "The king and I are stepping down as your leaders—immediately."
Zann felt stunned. Some people shouted out in dismay, while others cheered.
"Wow," Perda exclaimed. "This is really—"
"Aah!" Another mysterious Share suddenly seized Zann. Images of rolling waves filled his mind. He heard the voice again. Who was it?
Zann squeezed his eyes shut and tried to focus on the voice. A terrified-looking face flashed into view.
Zann gasped, and his eyes popped open. His friends were staring at him.
"Did it happen again?" Perda asked.
"Yes," Zann said. "I know who's trying to contact me."
"Who?" Gliss asked.
Zann gulped. "It's Ello!"
"From Skellia?" Darb exclaimed.
Zann nodded, thinking back to the drowning world they'd visited and the boy who'd helped them escape from it.
"Ello is still stuck in Skellia," he said grimly. "And he needs our help!"
"What are you talking about, Zann?" Perda demanded. "How could Ello send you a Red Share? He's not a Red—he's not even from Magica!"
Zann could hardly hear her over the noise of the rally. "Let's go back to my house!" he shouted. He grabbed his friends. "Zap!"
Zann's house was a mess from the party. When the kids arrived, Zing was standing on a table eating some leftover snacks. He zipped over to Zann, chattering angrily and shooting flames.
"Sorry, boy." Darb patted the dragon. "We didn't mean to leave you behind."

Zann rubbed his fingers together and then pointed at some cups on the table. Poof! They disappeared. Perda and Gliss magically cleaned crumbs off the floor as Zann removed the decorations from the walls. Soon the house was clean.
Remembering Ello's terrified face, Zann looked at his friends. "We have to help Ello."
Gliss sat down. "Tell us what you saw, Zann."
Zann described the mysterious Share as carefully as he could. By the time he was finished, his friends looked worried and confused.
"Why would Ello still be trapped on Skellia?" Gliss said. "Wyssa promised to get the Skellian people to safety on another world."
"But she was going to get rid of Morb first," Perda said. "Maybe he did something to her before she could save the Skellian people."
Zann shook his head. "I doubt it. Wyssa is pretty strong, and Morb had no magic at all when they left."
"Yeah," Gliss said. "But Wyssa was really angry and focused on Morb. Do you think she forgot about Skellia?"
"Maybe we can contact her and ask," Darb suggested. He was sitting with Zing curled on his lap.
Perda wrinkled her nose. "Contact her? How? She could be anywhere in the known worlds."
"Or the unknown ones," Gliss said. "She seemed to know about worlds nobody else knew about."
Zann felt impatient. "I think Ello's in trouble. We don't have time to try to track down Wyssa," he said. "That will take too long—especially if she doesn't want to be found."
"Good point." Perda nodded. "So what should we do?"
Zann paced back and forth across the room. "I'm not sure."
Darb looked thoughtful. "I wonder how Ello got a mental message through to Zann. I thought the Skellians had weak magic. That's why they couldn't escape when the waters started rising, remember?"
"It was because of the gulpers too," Perda said. "But never mind how Ello sent the message. The important thing is that he needs our help."
Zann stopped pacing. "Maybe we can ask my parents to—"
A crackle of magic interrupted him. Boz, Saffa, Teplo, and Zann’s parents appeared in the room. They paid no attention to the kids.
"What are we going to do?" Asta rubbed her head.
"This is a disaster!" Teplo exclaimed.
The other adults started talking too. Zann hurried over and tapped his dad's arm.
"We have to tell you about something," Zann said. "Remember that weird Red Share I had?"
"Not now, son," Nax said before Zann could continue. "We need to figure out how to deal with what the king and queen just did."
Zann had almost forgotten about the king and queen's announcement.
"Their resignation is effective immediately," Boz told the kids, shaking his head so hard that his long nose swayed back and forth. "And they've already gone into hiding."
Saffa nodded. "They refuse to communicate with anyone."
"That's weird," Perda said.
"Yes." Teplo rubbed his chin. "Worse yet, there's been no final decision on how to handle the relics."
"That's what the meeting was about earlier today," Asta told the kids. "The king and queen wanted us to stop cataloging the relics until a new vote takes place."
"They didn't explain why," Saffa said. "Do you think they already knew then that they were going to resign tonight?"
"Listen," Zann said. "You have to hear what I—"
"Laddno isn't giving us much time to figure things out," Nax said to the other adults.
"Laddno?" Perda chimed in. "How is he involved?"
"He's already calling for an election to replace the king and queen," Teplo explained.
"Lots of people seem to agree that it should happen as soon as possible," Asta added. "Many believe that the Red Council shouldn't be in charge of the election this time."
"What?" Gliss blurted out. "But the Red Council always runs elections!"
Zann was surprised. "Venna isn't going to like this," he said.
"Venna has already announced her candidacy," Saffa told him. "She'll win easily, especially if nobody runs against her."
"That's fine," Boz said. "We should start preparing to help her."
Zann traded a look with his friends. This was all big news. But they could worry about it later. Right now they needed to help Ello.
"Okay," he said to the adults. "But I was about to tell you—"
Once again the room crackled with magic. This time Venna appeared, her face nearly as red as her hair.
"You'll never believe who just announced he's running against me," she said. "Laddno!"
All the adults gasped.
"What?" Asta cried. "He's not the least bit qualified to lead Magica. He's never been involved in the government before. The only thing he's done is run a business."
"I know," Venna said grimly. "I've already called an emergency meeting of the Council."
"What are we waiting for?" Boz rubbed his fingers together. "Let's go!"
Zap!
"Now what are we going to do?" Zann said after the adults had all zapped away. "Ello needs our help!"
Perda shrugged. "It's simple. If the adults can't help us rescue him, we'll just have to do it ourselves."
"We're going to help Ello ourselves?" Gliss cried. "But how? He's trapped on Skellia, remember?"
"We went to Skellia before," Perda said. "We can go there again."
"You mean through the vortex?" Zann felt a shiver of fear, but he shook it off. "You're right. It's the only way to help him."

"We've traveled through the vortex before," Perda said. "In fact, we've spent more time in the vortex than anyone we know—except for Wyssa and your parents." She looked at Darb and Gliss. "We can do this."
Zann smiled, impressed by Perda's courage.
"Okay," Zann said. "Should we try to use the wormhole in Wormwood, or—"
"Stop!" Gliss exclaimed. "We can't just rush off through the closest wormhole."
"Again," Darb added, tickling Zing under his chin.
Perda frowned. "Are you two saying you don't want to help Ello?"
"He saved us when we got stuck on Skellia," Zann said.
Gliss shook her head. "That's not what I'm saying at all." Her voice was shaky, but she sounded certain. "I'm saying that if we're going into the vortex, we need to be sensible about how we do it."
"Okay then," Zann said. "So what should we do?"
Darb spoke up. "I have an idea. What about that guidelink Zann's parents invented?"
Perda gasped. "What a great idea! They said it might help people navigate the vortex."

"It should be able to help us find sources of magic too," Zann said. "On Skellia the gulpers usually eat wormholes as soon as the wormholes appear. But the guidelink might help us find more wormholes. Then we can all get away."
Darb nodded. "That's exactly what I was thinking."
Zann smiled at him, impressed again. Darb didn't have any magic, but he was one of the smartest people Zann knew.
"Do you think your parents would let us use the guidelink?" Gliss asked Zann.
"No way," Zann replied. "Not if they knew we were planning to travel in the vortex. We'll have to take it from the lab without telling them."
Zann felt bad saying that. He didn't want to deceive his parents. But they were so worried about other things. He didn't want to add to their worries now by telling them about Ello.
"It's a good thing the adults are distracted by politics," Perda said. "We can probably rescue Ello and get back before they notice we're gone."
Zann hoped she was right. Navigating the vortex was tricky, and they wouldn't have Wyssa to help them find their way home this time.
Gliss looked out the window. "It's getting pretty late. Let's get a good night's sleep and then find an excuse to visit the lab in the morning."
"Are you going to the lab today?" Zann asked his parents and Boz at breakfast. He was nervous about how he and his friends would sneak the guidelink out of the lab.
"Yes." Nax helped himself to a goofruit muffin. "We need to store the relics safely until after the election."
"I still can't believe Laddno wants to be king," Boz said.
Once again the adults started talking about politics.
A few minutes later, Perda and Gliss arrived with Saffa.
"Ready to get to work?" Saffa asked the other adults.
"Can we tag along?" Perda asked. "I'd love to see more of the lab."
"Of course," Asta agreed. "You'll have to stay out of the way though. We have a lot to do."
When everyone arrived at the lab, Perda and Gliss distracted the adults with questions. Meanwhile Zann and Darb slipped off to the room where the guidelink sat.
Zann grabbed the device from the shelf.
"Uh-oh. Someone's coming!" Darb whispered.
Mari had just walked in. Zann tucked the guidelink into his pocket.
"Sorry I missed your party, Zann," Mari said. "I had to do something with my family instead."
"Oh, that's too bad," Zann said. "It was fun."
Just then Zann's mother hurried over. She looked serious.
Zann felt the guidelink in his pocket. Had she seen him take it?
But Asta was looking at Mari. "I'm glad you're here, Mari. We need your help."
Zann cleared his throat. "I guess we'll get out of your way then," he said. He shot his friends a meaningful look.
His parents and Saffa barely seemed to notice his comment. But Boz looked up as Zann and his friends headed toward the door.
"Hold on," Boz said. "I'll zap home with you. I have some work to take care of at the house."
Zann gulped. "Um, you're coming home now? But you just got here."
Nax heard him and looked over. "It's better if your grandfather is with you. These are unsettled times in First City, and there's safety in numbers."
Zann sighed. This wasn't part of their plan! How were they supposed to sneak away from Boz long enough to get to a wormhole?
Boz was already rubbing his hands together, preparing to zap away. Just then Mari approached Darb.
"I almost forgot," she said, smiling at him. "I heard about a Void Rights meeting that's happening today. People will be talking about some new breakthroughs in magic sharing."
"Magic sharing?" Perda echoed.
Mari nodded. "It's the future of equality for Voids," she explained. "You should go to the meeting, Darb!"
"Um, I probably won't have time," Darb mumbled.
"Here's the information, in case you change your mind." Mari told him when and where the meeting would be taking place. Then Saffa called her, and she went over to get instructions from her.
"Ready, kids?" Magic was sparking from Boz's fingertips. "Let's zap!"
Zann rubbed his own fingers together, trying to hide his dismay. How were they supposed to save Ello now?
Zann peeked into Boz’s room. He was hunched over his notebook, writing furiously.
"I wish he would go back to the lab," Zann told his friends.
Perda sighed. "We'll never save Ello if we're stuck here."
The kids listened to some music until Boz poked his head into the room. "Keep it down in here. I'm trying to concentrate!"
"Sorry," Zann said. "Um, can we go for a walk?"
"All right," Boz said. "But don't be long. I'll conjure us some lunch in an hour."
The four friends hurried outside.
Perda groaned. "We only have an hour," she said. "That's not nearly enough time to save Ello."
Zann nodded. "So let's do something else for an hour," he said. "Maybe Boz will decide we're safe on our own and then go to the lab after lunch."
Gliss looked at Darb. "That Void Rights meeting should be starting around now," she said. "What if Mari was right, and there really are new ways for Voids to get magic?"
Darb stared at the ground. "That might be interesting," he mumbled.
Perda shrugged. "Let's check it out."
"Do you really think Gliss and I will be welcome there?" Zann pointed to his hair.
"I wish I knew how to do a Masking spell," Perda said.
"What's a Masking spell?" Zann asked.

"I read about it in an old book in the Swamp Bottom library," Perda said. "The spell was discovered in another world. It can make a person look exactly how he or she wants to look. You two could get rid of your red hair."
"I'll just conjure a wig for myself," Gliss said.
Zann conjured a large hat.
The meeting had already started when Zann and his friends arrived. A large crowd filled the room. Several people stood on the stage, including a young man with wild black hair.
Perda had noticed someone else. She elbowed Zann. "Look, there's Jev," she whispered.
Zann looked. Jev was standing near the stage with his parents.
"Now we'll demonstrate some of the Void magic we just told you about!" the young man with the black hair announced.
"Void magic," Gliss repeated softly. "I guess Mari knew what she was talking about."
Zann nodded and watched as the young man held up a wooden cane.
"This came from a world called Atmo," the man said. "It allows someone to leap long distances."
"Atmo is the world my parents were talking about," Zann whispered to his friends. "I wonder how these people got their hands on stuff from other worlds."

He watched as the young man used the cane to leap from one end of the room to the other. The crowd gasped. After that the young man and his friends showed off some other items. They had a canteen that stayed full no matter how much someone drank from it. They displayed a shirt that could expand or contract to fit anyone of any size.
Two of the presenters held up a pile of rubbery fabric. "This is a boat that comes to life without magic," one announced. "I'm a Void, and even I can make it work. Watch!"
The Void pulled a little tab. The audience gasped again as the fabric expanded. A minute later it had taken the form of a small boat.
"Wow!" someone cried. "How did you do that?"

The young man smiled. "Once Laddno is king, he'll explain everything. He already vowed to share all this magic and more with everyone—including Voids." Cheers rang out around the room. "Laddno will have control of all those relics from the Cave of the Unknown," the man continued. "And he will share that immense power with everyone in Magica. The Red Council will no longer be allowed to hoard the relics for its own purposes."
"That's not what the Red Council is doing," Zann muttered.
"Soon we'll have magic of our own!" an excited Void shouted. "Hooray for Laddno!"
"Hooray for Laddno!" several others cried.
Then a man raised his hand. "But I heard the Red Council is trying to destroy all the relics. What if the members succeed before Laddno takes power?"
"No!" several people shouted.
"Maybe we should storm that lab right now!" someone yelled.
A few people cheered, though others looked troubled. Zann gulped. Should he zap to the lab to warn his parents? He started rubbing his fingers together just in case.
But the young man onstage raised both hands for attention. "That might not be necessary," he said. "Laddno is working on something big—something that could render the relics unnecessary."
Murmurs arose from all around the room. Zann couldn't help feeling curious about Laddno's work himself.
The young man smiled at the crowd. "Surely everyone here has heard the tales from the Old Times," he said. "Including stories about the Source?"
Zann blinked. The Source? That sounded familiar, but he couldn't quite remember what it was.

"The Source is where all of Magica gets its magic," the man said. "It's where our world's native magical power comes from. It's where that power is stored until you snap your fingers or rub your hands together to summon it."
"But I thought the Source was a myth," a woman called out.

The young man smiled. "I did too. But Laddno knew better. He's sure he can find the Source and figure out how to control it. That way he can share its power fairly." He clasped his hands together. "Just think! Soon every Void in Magica will have as much access to magical energy as the most powerful Magic Masters!"
"Hooray for Laddno!" someone shouted again.
The room erupted with cheers and excitement.
Darb leaned closer to Zann. "Can we get out of here?" he whispered.
Zann nodded, already backing toward the door. "Exactly what I was thinking."
Zann and Darb headed out of the meeting. Perda and Gliss followed them.
"What's wrong?" Gliss asked. "Darb, I figured you'd want to stay and find out more. Just think—soon you might have magic of your own!"
"I'm not sure I want that," Darb said softly. "I mean, sometimes I think it might be nice to conjure my own food instead of asking someone else to do it. But . . ."
"But what?" Gliss sounded perplexed.
"All I want to do when I grow up is become an animal caretaker," Darb blurted out. "What if having magic gets in the way of that?"

Now Zann understood why his friend looked conflicted. Most Voids were limited to a few simple jobs that required no magic. One of those jobs was animal caretaker. Darb had dreamed of doing that for as long as Zann had known him.
"I understand," he told Darb. "But Magica will still need animal caretakers even if all the Voids get magic."
"Maybe," Darb said. "But . . . I'm used to being a Void. I actually don't mind it."
Zann was shocked. How could anyone not want magic?
Still, Darb was his friend, so Zann didn't question him. Instead he flashed a smile at Darb and changed the subject. "Do you think Laddno can really do what he's promising?"
"I doubt it," Gliss said. "That guy says Laddno has some secret knowledge. But nobody knows for sure if the Source is real."
"I read that it might be deep beneath Mount Mystery," Perda said. "Or maybe inside the Cave of the Unknown."
"If the Source is in the Cave, then Laddno is out of luck," Zann pointed out. "The Cave was destroyed, remember? Let's get home before Boz starts to worry about us."
When the kids reached Zann's house, a magical note was floating in the living room.
"It's from Boz," Zann said. "Venna called another meeting. Boz won't be back for several hours."
Perda's eyes widened. "This is our chance to help Ello!"

Zann swallowed. He knew Boz would be furious if he ever found out that the kids had gone out again. Zann quickly pushed that thought out of his mind and checked his pocket to make sure the guidelink was still there. "Let's go."
They headed back outside. Zing tried to come with them, but Darb convinced the dragon to stay behind.
"Maybe I should stay too." Gliss looked pale. "I swore I'd never go near a wormhole again!"
"You'll be fine." Perda grabbed her hand. "Let's zap straight to Wormwood."

Wormwood was as creepy as ever. A variety of makeshift huts huddled around the central green where a gnarled and ancient tree grew. The wormhole at the tree's base wasn't visible, but Zann remembered exactly where it was.
On the way to the tree, they passed Wyssa's old hut. An older man with gray hair sat outside. He stared suspiciously as the kids went by.
Suddenly there was a growl from the tent next door to Wyssa's hut. A small silver dragon leaped out, spitting shards of ice.
"Eek!" Gliss cried. "Stay back!"
"Sorry!" A young man hurried out of the tent and grabbed the dragon. "She won't hurt you."
"Hey, it's you!" Perda blurted out. "The guy from the meeting."
The man brushed his wild hair to the side. "Oh, were you there?" he asked in a friendly voice. "I hope you enjoyed it—especially you." He smiled at Darb. "You're a Void, aren't you?"
"You live here?" Zann said before Darb could answer. He peered past the man. Piles of strange items filled the tent. Other items lay in the grass outside the tent.
"Yes, home sweet home." The young man noticed Zann's red hair and frowned. He turned back to Darb and Perda. "Some mess, hmm? I brought home a bunch of stuff from the meeting."
"We should go." Gliss sounded nervous as she glanced toward the tree.
The man ignored her. "Are you interested in joining our group?" he asked Darb. "We can use more help to get the word out about Void Rights."
Zann expected Darb to mutter "no thanks."
Instead Darb cleared his throat. "Did you say you brought back some things from the meeting?" he said. "I'd, uh, love to see that boat again."
"Of course!" the man exclaimed. "Our mission is to share new kinds of magic with everyone. Come in and look at it all you like."
"Actually I was hoping to borrow the boat for a while," Darb said. "I'd like to study it."
The man looked uncertain. "It's the only one we have. Laddno went to great personal trouble to acquire it."
"I wouldn't need it for long," Darb added quickly. "I'd be happy to bring it back to Laddno campaign headquarters tomorrow to discuss how I can help the cause."
The man still looked hesitant. But finally he smiled. "I suppose that would be all right."
Soon the deflated boat was draped over Darb's shoulders. The kids hurried toward the tree.
"What was that all about?" Zann asked.
Darb smiled slyly. "We're going to Skellia, right? A drowning world with weak magic? I thought a boat that doesn't require magic might come in handy."
"Good thinking, Darb!" Perda said. "Now we won't have to use magic to create a raft."
"And that means we won't attract the gulpers." Zann shivered, thinking of the magic-eating creatures that swam in Skellia's waters.
When Zann and his friends approached the tree, the wormhole spun open.
"I was hoping the wormhole had disappeared," Gliss joked weakly.
"Not this one," Zann said. "It's been here for a long time."
Perda laughed. "Hey, maybe the Source is located right here under this spooky old tree with its super powerful wormhole!"
"Who knows?" Zann snapped his fingers. A Shackle spell linked the friends' hands together.
Zann stepped toward the wormhole. "Let's go!"
Zann felt dizzy as he and his friends tumbled through the vortex. Lights flashed and strange worlds passed by. Slowly he reached into his pocket and pulled out the guidelink.
"Give me that!" Perda called over the whooshing sound of the vortex. "I think I can make it work."
"I hope you're right!" Zann placed the device in her hand. He wished he'd paid more attention when his parents were explaining the device's abilities.
Perda fiddled with the guidelink.
"What are you doing?" Gliss asked her.

"I'm supposed to rub it to create friction," Perda said. "Then I focus on what type of magic I want it to find. It should pull us toward any world nearby that matches my thoughts." She frowned. "But so far nothing is happening!"
"You have to figure it out!" Gliss sounded frantic. "Otherwise we could end up flying through the vortex forever!"
Suddenly Perda swerved toward one of the wormholes, dragging her friends with her. Zann grabbed the wormhole’s edge. Instantly the wormhole pulled them in and spat them out on the other side.
Zann held his breath, expecting to splash into the stormy waters of Skellia. Instead he landed on wet ground. "Oof!" he blurted out.
Gliss sat up and rubbed her head. "Ouch," she said. Then she looked around. "Hey, this isn't Skellia."
"Not unless the oceans disappeared since we were here," Darb said.

The world they'd landed in looked similar to Magica. They were in a forest clearing, with tall trees shading the light of a bright orange sun. Birds swooped overhead, and an insect buzzed in the grass nearby.
"Oh well." Perda sighed. "I guess I'm still figuring out how the guidelink works."

"At least this world looks nice and peaceful." Gliss peered around. Then she wrinkled her nose and looked down. "It's kind of soggy right here though. Let's find a drier spot to rest and regain our energy."
Zann nodded. It took a lot of energy just to stay conscious in the vortex. They usually had to rest before they could travel again.
"Wait! Don't go anywhere yet," Darb said. "We need to pay attention to landmarks so we can return to the wormhole when we're ready."

"Oops. Good point," Zann said. As usual, the wormhole had spun shut as soon as they'd moved away from it. Now it was only visible as a tiny ripple in the air. If Zann hadn't known it was there, he wouldn't even have noticed it.
"I see a crooked tree over there, and some blue flowers," Gliss said.
"Good," Perda said. "We'll definitely be able to spot that tree again. Now let's go uphill. It should be dry there." She led the way up a gentle slope.
Soon they reached a sunny clearing. Zann flopped onto the dry ground and looked at Perda. "So why didn't the guidelink work?" he asked.

She shrugged and sat down beside him. "I think I know what I did wrong," she said. "I was focusing on the gulpers from Skellia, since they probably have the most magic on that world. But when Gliss said the thing about flying through the vortex, I thought about birds."
Darb watched a bright purple bird land nearby and peck at some yellow flowers. "There definitely are a lot of birds here," he said. "Maybe they're the source of this world's magic."
"They could be," Zann agreed. Then he frowned. "Uh-oh. Do you think our magic will work here?"
"I hope so, or we won't be able to open the wormhole!" Gliss' eyes widened. "We'd better test it. I'll conjure us something to drink."
She snapped her fingers. Blink!

Zann felt a sudden surge of magic energy. At the same time, the entire landscape around them changed! The sunny meadow had disappeared. They were now sitting in the shade of several large trees. A small flock of multicolored birds perched on a squat shrub with shiny blue leaves.
Zann gasped and jumped to his feet. "What happened? Did we accidentally zap somewhere else?"
"I don't think so." Darb looked around. "We're still on a hill. And the position of the sun hasn't changed. I think we're in the same exact spot."
"But everything around us looks different!" Perda said. "The trees, the birds . . ."
"That must be how magic works in this world," Darb said. "Gliss' magic friction changed the landscape around us."
"Yeah." Zann gulped. "I wonder if it made that crooked tree move around too. We might not be able to find the wormhole without it."
"Oh no," Gliss said. "What about the wormhole itself? What if it moved? What if it's gone?"
Perda held up the guidelink. "This is supposed to be able to locate strong sources of magic, right? Maybe it can lead us back to the wormhole."
"Do you know how to make it do that?" Darb asked.
"No." Perda bit her lip. "But I'll figure it out."
She rubbed the guidelink. Blink!
The landscape changed again. Now the kids found themselves standing among bushes with spiky leaves. Nearby several large, six-legged creatures with shaggy fur sniffed around in the grass.
"Hmm," Perda said. She rubbed the guidelink again. Blink!
Now a deep, tangled forest surrounded the kids.
Blink!
Again the scenery changed. Now the open meadow was back. But instead of birds, there was a swarm of large insects buzzing around a tree with purple bark.
"Stop!" Gliss grabbed the guidelink out of Perda's hand. "Every time you create friction, the landscape changes!"
"Sorry." Perda looked nervous.
Zann knew how she felt. It seemed like they couldn't use magic in this world at all—not without getting lost. So how were they going to find their way back to the wormhole?
While Zann, Perda, and Gliss were beginning to panic, Darb appeared calm.
"Don't worry," he said. "I think I can get us back to the wormhole."
"How?" Gliss cried. "We can't use magic!"
Darb smiled. "I can't ever use magic. I'm used to living without it. Give me a minute." He squinted up toward the sun and then glanced around.
"What's he doing?" Perda whispered.
Zann shrugged. "Let's wait and see."
Darb looked up again. Then he closed his eyes and just stood there for a moment. "Okay," he said at last. "I think it's this way."
Zann and the girls followed as Darb led the way. After a moment Darb paused. He looked around and then closed his eyes again. When he opened them, he made a turn and then walked some more.
"I think he's using his non-magical senses to try to find his way back to the wormhole," Zann told the others softly.
"That's right," Darb said. "The sun was just above our left shoulders when we were walking up the hill, so now I'm trying to keep it just to our right."
Within minutes Zann spotted a slight shimmer in the air up ahead.
"The wormhole!" he shouted. "There it is!"
"Whew!" Gliss sounded relieved. "We're lucky you found it, Darb. Our landmarks are nowhere in sight!"
Zann nodded. The scenery looked very different than it had when they'd arrived. But he didn't really care about that anymore.
"Let's get out of here," he said.
"Are you sure we've rested enough?" Gliss asked.
"No," Perda said. "But I agree with Zann. We need to get to Skellia and help Ello."
They shackled themselves together and dived into the wormhole. Almost immediately Zann realized they should have rested for longer. He felt weak. He and his friends careened wildly around.
"This is terrible!" Gliss shouted. "We have to find a place to rest."
"Just grab the first world we pass," Darb called out.
"No!" Perda cried. "What if we end up back in Fardark?"

"No way that's happening!" Zann declared. Fardark was a creepy world full of horrible creatures, like scatter beasts. Perda was right—they couldn't risk landing somewhere like that. But they had to stop soon.
"Give me that," he blurted out. He grabbed the guidelink from Perda.
With the last of his energy, he focused on soothing, intelligent magic. A second later he felt the device tugging him toward an upcoming wormhole.
Moments later they tumbled out into another world. This one looked similar to Magica too. But it smelled completely different.
"Ugh!" Gliss held her nose. "It's Niffia!"
Zann grabbed his own nose. He'd recognize Niffia anywhere. It was the stinkiest world he'd ever smelled!
"I wish we could try again." Perda glanced at the wormhole. "But I think we'll have to make the best of it until we're rested."
"At least the people in this world are friendly." Darb pointed. "Look, here come some Niffians now."
The Niffians smiled brightly. "Welcome back, my young friends!" the leader said. "We're so happy that you've chosen to return to our beautiful world."
Zann forced a smile. He'd stopped holding his nose when the Niffians had arrived. "Thank you," he said. "We needed a nice place to rest and restore our energy."
"You've come to the right world," another Niffian said, beaming. "Please come with us and share some food and drink."
The kids followed the Niffians to the nearest town. As they ate, Zann and his friends told the Niffians about their adventures since their last visit to Niffia.
When Zann mentioned Wyssa, the Niffians looked more delighted than ever.
"Ah, Wyssa!" one of them cried. "How is our most esteemed friend?"

"We're not sure." Zann traded a look with his friends. During their first visit to Niffia, they'd been surprised to find out how much the Niffians liked Wyssa. She'd never seemed very friendly to Zann or the others.
"We haven't seen her since she left Magica with Morb," Perda said.
"Morb." One of the Niffians frowned slightly. "Ah, yes. I believe that was the name of her, um, companion during her most recent visit."
Zann was surprised. "Wyssa brought Morb here?"
"Only briefly," another Niffian said. He and the others suddenly looked much more solemn than usual. "She stopped only long enough to collect a bit of pupu leaf."
"Pupu leaf?" Perda echoed. "What's that for?"
The Niffians exchanged glances. "We didn't ask why she needed it," one said.
"However," another added, "the pupu is mostly used for spells involving immobilization."
Zann shuddered as he remembered Wyssa's threat to feed Morb to a scatter beast. Was that why she'd needed the pupu? To immobilize him long enough for the fearsome creature to find him?
"So," the Niffian leader said. "Why are you four traveling through the vortex again?"
Zann told the Niffians about their current mission to find Skellia and help Ello.
"We'll fetch you some oogberry," one Niffian said, while another rushed off toward the forest. "That's an important ingredient in searching spells."
"Just relax for now though." The Niffian leader smiled. "We'll take care of everything."
For the next hour, Zann did his best to rest and ignore the stink. He and his friends were talking about Niffia when Zann's head exploded in pain. Clutching his forehead, he groaned.
"Zann!" Perda cried.
Zann hardly heard her. He fell to the floor, landing on the guidelink. Ello's frightened face appeared in his mind.
"Help!" Ello wailed. "Please, hurry!"
Zann grabbed the guidelink. "We're coming!" he cried, even though he knew Ello couldn't hear him.
Or could he? Immediately Ello's face brightened. "Hurry!" he said again, before fading away.
Laddno frowned as a female member of the Red Council droned on about election details. The businessman had wandered to the back of the room ten minutes earlier.

He glanced toward the group. Boz was sitting up front with his non-Red daughter and her husband. All three were listening carefully to what the Red Council member was saying. Laddno glared at Boz, but the old Magic Master didn't even look his way.

Laddno began pacing. He didn't like being ignored, especially by a bunch of snooty Reds and their cronies. But that would all change soon. Once he was elected king, Laddno planned to make some big changes. He'd start by hanging an enormous portrait of himself in the palace. Then no one could ignore him—or his power!

He was thinking about what color to paint the throne room when the familiar pain filled his head again. He held his head and staggered out of the room. He collapsed against the wall, panting as the pain subsided slightly.
The voice in his head spoke.
"What?" Laddno replied. "How soon?"
He paused and listened again. Then he frowned.
"Are you sure they're really coming?" Laddno asked. "What if they can't do it?"
Once again he fell silent as the voice raged on. Finally Laddno nodded.
"All right," he said resolutely. "I'll begin immediately."
"Hold still," a Niffian said as he dabbed purple goo on Zann's fingers.
Perda stared at her own fingers, which were already coated with the stuff. "How does this work again?" she asked.

"This oogberry paste will work with your magical friction," the Niffian explained. "All you need to do is think of the place you wish to visit. When the paste glows, it means you're near your destination."
"That sounds sort of like the guidelink." Gliss glanced at the device sticking out of Zann's pocket. "With that, we need to think about a certain type of magic."
The Niffian smiled. "With the paste, you just need to think of a person or place."
"That will make things easier," Zann said. He looked at his hands. "Okay, I think we're ready."
He was grateful to the Niffians for helping them. But he was eager to get away from their stinky world as soon as possible. Besides, he was worried about Ello.
Soon Zann and his friends were back in the vortex.
"Think about Skellia, everyone!" Perda called.
Within seconds the paste began to glow.
Zann spotted an approaching wormhole. "That must be Skellia up ahead!" he shouted.
Moments later they plunged through the wormhole and into cold water. The water was so rough, Zann was glad that the Shackle spell was holding them all together.
Suddenly something large glided past beneath them.
"A gulper!" Perda yelled. "Quick, inflate the boat!"

Darb spit out a mouthful of water. Then he pulled down the boat, which had been draped over his shoulders, and yanked the little tab. Soon the boat was bobbing on the waves. By now the gulper had moved away. Zann was relieved. Since they hadn't used magic, the creature hadn't been interested in them.
When they were all on the boat, Zann collapsed and caught his breath. "We did it," he said.
"Thanks to the Niffians." Perda looked at her hand. "My oogberry paste washed off."
"Mine too," Gliss said.
Zann saw that his fingers had also returned to their normal color. "Oh well. Hopefully the guidelink will help us find our way back to Magica."
"First we have to find Ello," Darb said.
Zann sat up and looked around. From horizon to horizon, all he could see were churning gray waves. There was no sign of land anywhere.
Gliss peered at her hand. "Maybe there's some oogberry paste stuck under our fingernails."

"I have a better idea," Perda said. "Let's use the guidelink. Since it tracks magic, we might be able to find Ello with it. We just need to focus on whatever type of magic Ello is using to communicate with Zann."
Gliss frowned. "But we don't know what type that is."
"It's worth a try," Zann said.
He rubbed the guidelink and focused on Ello. He thought about the magic that Ello had used during their last visit to Skellia.
At first nothing happened. So Perda and Gliss put their hands on the guidelink too and added their own thoughts to Zann's. Finally something tugged on the boat.
"I think it's working!" Perda cried.
The boat floated along, pulled by the guidelink's magic. Suddenly a gulper rose out of the water!
"Oh, no!" Gliss wailed. "The guidelink attracted a gulper!"
"Everyone, stop using magic," Darb called out. "Let's just sit here until the gulper swims away."
When the gulper was gone, they tried again. Two more gulpers appeared, drawn by the energy of the guidelink.
"What are we going to do?" Gliss said. "This isn't working!"
"Let's try once more," Perda suggested. "This time, don't focus on Ello. Just think about finding the strongest magic source around." She looked at Zann. "Your parents said it could do that, right?"
"I think so," Zann said. "Let's try it."
This time the guidelink responded almost immediately. The boat sped over the waves.
"Whoa!" Perda cried.
"Wow," Darb said. "The guidelink must have found a really strong power source!"
"Yeah," Zann said slowly. "That's weird though. I thought Skellia didn't have much native magic."
"Look!" Perda shouted. "It's another boat."

Zann peered through the sea spray. Something was bobbing on the waves up ahead. When they got closer, he laughed with relief. It was a rickety houseboat with a small figure waving to them from the deck.
"It's Ello!" he cried. "We found him!"
"You came!" Ello cried as the inflatable boat bumped against the houseboat. "I thought you wouldn't!"
"Of course we came," Zann said. He was happy to finally see Ello's face in person. "Help us up."
Ello held out his hand. Everyone climbed up onto the houseboat's deck, and then Zann and Darb pulled up the inflatable boat.
Gliss turned to smile at Ello.
"We're glad you're safe!" she cried, flinging her arms around him.
"Hey!" Ello shook off her hug and took a quick step back.
Perda frowned at him. "What's wrong?"
"Nothing," Ello said quickly. "Uh, I'm sorry. I've been alone so long. I guess I've forgotten how to act around people."

Zann glanced around. "Wow, this houseboat is bigger than it looked from a distance." He bent to peer at an odd stain on the floor. The boat was missing a few chunks of wood here and there too. But for the most part, the vessel seemed sturdy.
"Why are you alone?" Gliss asked Ello. "What happened to your people?"
Ello scratched his head. He was wearing a pair of dark gloves. That seemed a little odd to Zann, but he soon forgot about it. There were more important questions to be answered.
"Wyssa said she was going to come back and rescue you," Zann said. "Didn't she do that?"

Ello frowned. "She did come back to Skellia. She promised to take all of them—uh, I mean us—to an unoccupied world where we could resettle. But when they left, I was at the back of the group. They accidentally left me behind."
Gliss gasped. "That's horrible! Didn't she come back for you?"

Zann was wondering the same thing. Wyssa might be kind of cranky and unpredictable, but she had very strong magical powers. She could have easily come back and rescued Ello once she realized he was missing.

"Obviously not." Ello frowned, looking around the houseboat. "I figured a gulper must have eaten all the wormholes after they left. Or maybe she just didn't bother to come back for me." He shrugged. "Wyssa probably had other things on her mind besides helping me."
Ello sounded bitter. Zann was surprised. The last time Zann had met Ello, the Skellian boy was kind and optimistic despite his people's dire situation.
But Ello had been alone for a long time now. He'd been left behind and apparently forgotten. Anyone in his situation would be bitter.
Darb was peering through a door leading to the interior of the houseboat. "This place is pretty nice," he said. "Where did it come from?"
"Where did what come from?" Ello fiddled with the tips of one glove, not looking at Zann or his friends.
"The houseboat," Perda said. She sounded impatient. "Where did you get this houseboat?"
"I made it, of course," Ello said.
"Really?" Darb stared at him in surprise.
Zann and the girls walked over to Darb and looked through the door too. The interior room contained a bed, a table, and various other necessities.
"But your people don't have much magic," Gliss blurted out. "How in the world did you make all this stuff?"
"Yeah," Zann said. "Uh, no offense. But last time we met, you could barely conjure food or water. So how did you manage to conjure this boat all by yourself?"
Ello looked away from them and bit his lip. "Um . . . I'll tell you about it later, okay? Right now we have to get out of here. A storm is coming, and my boat just sprang a leak this morning. See?"
He knelt down and placed his gloved palm on the deck. At that moment Zann was distracted by the guidelink, which jumped in his pocket. He glanced down and wondered what had set it off.
Then he noticed a gulper glide by. Perhaps that creature's magic had caused the guidelink to jump?
He turned his attention back to Ello. Ello had just stood up again. In the spot he'd touched, water was welling up through a crack in the boards.
"Yikes!" Perda stared at the leak. "I didn't see that at first. You're right—we need to get out of here."
"Especially if Ello’s correct and there's going to be a storm." Darb squinted up at the sky.

Zann looked up too. As usual on Skellia, the sky was filled with foreboding clouds, though the sun was peeking through in a few spots. It didn't look particularly stormy to Zann. But he assumed Ello knew the weather on Skellia much better than he did.
"Okay, let's take our boat," he said. "We can use the guidelink to find a wormhole."
"The what?" Ello sounded curious.

While Darb and the girls tossed the boat back into the sea, Zann quickly told Ello about the guidelink. "Its power will attract gulpers," Zann said. "But if we're quick, we can get through a wormhole before they catch up."
By then the other three kids were already in the boat. "Hurry up!" Perda called.
"Coming!" Zann jumped into the smaller boat. Then he looked up. "Come on, Ello!"
Ello hesitated, looking fearful as he stared down at them.
"Hurry!" Gliss cried.
Finally Ello jumped off the deck. Just then a large wave pushed the small boat away. Ello let out a cry as he plunged into the sea between the two vessels.
"Oops," Zann said. "Get ready to help him aboard when he surfaces."
He leaned over the side, ready to grab Ello's hand. But when Ello's head finally popped into view, he was too far away.
"Swim this way!" Perda called.
Ello's arms flailed. He gurgled and sank underwater again.
"Oh no!" Gliss cried. "I think he's drowning!"
"I'm coming, Ello!" Perda cried. She dived into the water.
Zann plunged into the chilly sea too. He dived down into the murky water and spotted Perda just below him. When he reached her, she had Ello by the arm.
Zann grabbed Ello's other arm and helped Perda drag him back to the surface. Ello coughed and spit out water.
"Over here!" Gliss called.
She and Darb reached out to pull Ello aboard. Then they helped Zann and Perda as well.
"Whew! That was close," Perda said breathlessly.
"What happened?" Darb asked Ello. "Can't you swim?"
"Of course I can." Ello was shaking. "I suppose I must be weak from my long solitude. Let's find a wormhole and get out of here."
"Okay." Zann pulled out the guidelink and handed it to Perda. "How should we do this?"
Perda rubbed the device. "Think about wormholes, everyone," she said. "Or the vortex. Either one might work."
Several gulpers surfaced nearby. Then there was a tug on the guidelink.
"This way," Perda said. She held on tightly as the device pulled the boat along. The gulpers followed.
Darb eyed the gulpers. "I hope the guidelink helps us get to the wormhole first. Otherwise all it's doing is helping those things find a snack."
"Maybe we should all hold the guidelink," Gliss suggested.
Everyone put a hand on the device. Zann glanced at Ello's hand. "Ello, it might work better if you take off your gloves," he said.
Before Ello could respond, the boat rocketed forward. The guidelink vibrated under their hands. The gulpers were soon far behind.
Perda pointed ahead. "There's a wormhole!"
Zann nodded. "Get ready to jump, everyone!"
"What about the boat?" Darb said.
"We'll have to leave it behind." Zann glanced over his shoulder and saw that the gulpers were gaining on them. "There's no time to deflate it."
Darb nodded, but he looked uneasy.
Perda performed a Shackle spell. With everyone shackled together, Zann got ready for the leap into the wormhole.
"Now!" Zann cried.
Everyone jumped. Whoosh! A moment later they were spinning through the vortex again.
"We did it!" Gliss exclaimed. "I've never been so happy to be in this crazy place."
Perda laughed. "I know what you mean." She glanced at Ello, who was shackled between her and Zann. "Welcome to the vortex, Ello."
"What?" Ello looked around. "Oh, right. This is my first time in the vortex."
"That's weird," Zann thought. Ello sounded flat and unimpressed. Usually people were freaked out during their first time in the vortex.

"Let's see if we can find your people," Zann said. "Did Wyssa tell you anything about the world where she was bringing them? If we know what type of magic it has, maybe we can use the guidelink to find it."
"I have no idea," Ello said. "Wyssa didn't tell us anything. Maybe I should just come back to Magica with you. I've always wanted to visit."
Gliss raised an eyebrow. "Don't you want to find your family?"
"I'm sure you know some powerful people in Magica who can help me get home," Ello said.
Zann was surprised. When his parents were lost in the vortex, Zann wanted more than anything to be reunited with them. But Ello didn't seem to be in much of a hurry to find his own family.
Perda gave Ello a suspicious look. "Why wouldn't Wyssa tell your people where she was taking them?"
"She might have been distracted by Morb," Gliss suggested before Ello could respond. "Maybe she was still trying to figure out what to do with Morb."
"That's it!" Ello said quickly. "She did seem distracted. And Morb kept trying to escape. That's probably why she didn't tell us anything."
"She brought Morb with her to Skellia?" Zann was surprised again. "Why would she do that?"
"And didn't your people ask any questions?" Perda persisted. "Your mother or Rellu weren't curious?"
"Who?" Ello said.
Zann stared at him. "Rellu," he repeated. "The elder from your village."
"Oh, him." Ello cleared his throat. "Of course. I, uh, didn't hear you."
Zann couldn't ignore his uneasy feelings anymore. Something about Ello was odd. And judging by the suspicious look on her face, Perda felt the same way.
Perda gestured to an approaching wormhole. "Let's exit here. I think we need to have a talk."

Zann grabbed the edge of the wormhole, peeking through to make sure it didn't look like Fardark or any other unpleasant world. The landscape was covered in ice and snow, but otherwise didn't seem dangerous. When they'd landed in the soft snow, Perda dissolved the shackles.
"Brr!" Gliss said. She snapped her fingers to conjure a warm coat. "Hey, our magic seems to work here."
Perda was staring at Ello. "So, Ello, tell us again exactly how you got left behind."
"And where that houseboat came from," Zann added.
Ello frowned. "Why are you interrogating me?" he whined. "I just want to get back to the safety of Magica."
"But you've never even been to Magica," Perda said. "Why don't you want to find your family instead?"
"Yeah," Gliss said. "That does seem weird."
Ello scowled. "Fine," he said. "You want answers? Here you go!" He snapped his fingers.
Ello's familiar face began to change appearance. Zann watched with confusion. Then he gasped. Ello's face was gone. In its place was a different, even more familiar one.
"Morb!" Zann cried.
Perda's eyes widened. "You used a Masking spell!"
"Clever girl." Morb glared at the kids. "All of you really are too clever for your own good."
Before the kids could react, he plucked the guidelink out of Perda's hand. With a triumphant cackle, he disappeared through the wormhole.
Zann and his friends stood silently for a moment. Perda was the first to speak.
"We just rescued Morb!" she cried.
"But how is he even still alive?" Darb blurted out. "Wyssa said . . ."
"And how did he get enough magic to send Zann those messages?" Gliss said. "Or do that Masking spell? Or even make the houseboat?"
"Never mind all that," Zann said. "We have to get back to Magica and warn everyone!"
"How?" Gliss glanced toward the wormhole. "We don't have the guidelink to help us anymore."
Zann realized she was right. He gulped. Still, they had no choice. "We'll get home," he said, trying to sound confident. "Now let's get out of here. This world is freezing."
They shackled themselves together and returned to the vortex.
"Now what?" Darb asked.
"Let's just check every wormhole we pass," Perda said. "We have to pass Magica eventually."

Each time they passed a wormhole, they grabbed the edge and looked in. First they saw a world with grass taller than their heads. Another world had three white suns shining over pale yellow trees. The next wormhole revealed a world with thick purple fog.
Finally they reached a wormhole with a view of a beautiful spired city.
"That looks like Pax," Perda said.
Zann remembered the pleasant world they'd visited before. "Let's stop here for a while. We can regain our strength before continuing."
Pax was just as nice as Zann remembered, but it was hard to enjoy it when they were so anxious about finding their way home. As soon as they'd rested enough, the group returned to the vortex.

After that, Zann lost track of how many worlds they passed. But none of them was Magica. When they came to another world they recognized, called Gabble, they stopped to rest again. Then they continued on.
More worlds followed—worlds with blue suns, polka-dotted trees, odd-looking creatures. None looked anything like Magica.
Zann felt his magical energy faltering again. "We need to stop for another rest," he said. "Here's a wormhole—" He froze with fear.
"It's Fardark!" Perda cried.
Zann pushed himself away from the wormhole, and again everyone tumbled through the vortex.
"We definitely don't want to stop there," he said. "We'll try the next world."
But they recognized the next world too.
"Ugh," Gliss said. "It's that weird place where nasty dragons are in charge."
"Drac," Darb added. "We can't stop here either."
"Okay." Zann felt exhausted. "We can't go much longer without a rest though."
The next wormhole revealed a bustling city. People hurried along, carrying shopping bags or talking with friends. A trio of small boys kicked a ball in the street.
"This one looks okay." Perda sounded tired.
Zann started to pull himself through.
"No!" Darb cried. "It's the no-magic world! Remember our last stop here? We won't be able to open the wormhole once it closes."
Zann looked more closely, wondering how Darb had recognized it. "How do you know it's the no-magic world?"
Darb pointed. "That black-and-white ball. It's just like the one we saw last time."
Zann hesitated. The ball did look the same. But lots of objects ended up traveling from one world to another.
"We can't risk it," Gliss said.
Zann knew his friends were right. "Okay, let's keep going. But whatever world we come to next, we're going to have to stop. No matter what."
When the next wormhole came into view, Zann took a deep breath and pulled himself and his friends through. They landed on a gnarly tree root.
Zann sat up and looked around. When he spotted several tiny houses, he felt a surge of hope.
"We're in Rood!" Gliss cried. "Hooray!"

Zann's friends talked excitedly. But Zann was too relieved to speak. Rood had once been known as World X. It was the only world where the outgoing wormholes led directly into other worlds, bypassing the vortex entirely. Morb had come here to try to destroy Magica, but Zann and his friends had stopped him.
"We got lucky," Darb said.
