Perda nodded. "All we have to do is find the queen of Rood. She can find a wormhole back to Magica! Then we can warn everyone about Morb!"
A short while later, the kids stood before the tiny Queen of Rood.
"I'm so glad your travels brought you back to Rood," the queen said. "I've been hoping to thank you again for ridding my peaceful world of Morb's evil influence."
Zann looked down and so did his friends. Nobody wanted to tell the queen that they'd just accidentally released Morb!
"Um, thanks," Zann said. "We were happy to do it."
The queen smiled up at them as she summoned a wormhole with a wave of her hand. She waved again, and the wormhole spun open.
"This wormhole will take you directly into the palace in First City," the queen said.
"Really?" Perda exclaimed. "But last time we were here, you told us you can't summon individual wormholes."
"Your friend Wyssa stopped by with a potion," the queen said.
Zann and his friends thanked the queen and then stepped through the wormhole. They emerged into a shadowy corner of the palace throne room.
The scene there was chaotic. People hurried back and forth, shouting frantically. For a second Zann wasn't sure what was happening.
He spotted his parents and Boz. Near them were Venna, Teplo, and Gliss' uncle, Gar.
"This is an outrage!" Boz shouted. He hadn't noticed the kids in the corner.
Zann gasped as he realized his grandfather was immobilized by magical shackles. So were his parents and Teplo.
"I'm sorry, sir." A palace guard stepped toward the shackled adults. Several other guards followed. "We're going to have to lock the four of you in the dungeon until we get to the bottom of things."
"Listen to me!" Venna shouted.
But nobody was listening to her. The guards dragged the prisoners away. Zann started to rush forward, but Darb held him back.
"Let them go," he whispered. "Otherwise the guards might grab you too."
Zann sighed. He knew Darb was right. The guards had already taken his family away. There was nothing he could do right now.
Laddno strode to the middle of the room. He whistled for attention, making the sound even louder with a Swelling spell. Everyone stopped talking and turned to stare at him.
"Don't panic!" he shouted. "I'll get to the bottom of what's happening here, believe me."
"Why should we believe you?" Venna snapped. "This is probably your fault. Everyone knows you're anti-Red."
"That's not true." Laddno puffed out his chest. "I care about all of Magica's citizens. That's why I want to lead Magica."
Laddno snapped his fingers and zapped out of sight. As soon as the businessman was gone, Zann broke free of Darb's grasp. He rushed toward Venna.
"What's going on?" he cried. "Why did those guards take away my parents, Boz, and Teplo?"

"Zann? What are you doing here?" Venna sounded surprised, and a little shaken. "Where did you kids come from? Never mind—it doesn't matter." She sighed. "Your parents and Boz were accused of stealing several important items from their lab. They're being held in the dungeon while the guards search their homes. Teplo tried to stop the arrest, so he's being held too."
Zann gulped, immediately thinking about the guidelink.
"Why are my parents being accused of stealing?" he blurted out. "I mean, it could have been anyone."

Perda shot him a worried look. Zann guessed that all of his friends were thinking the same thing he was. This was all their fault! They had taken the guidelink, but Zann's family was in trouble for it. And the kids couldn't even give it back now, since Morb had taken it!
"Yeah, who accused Zann's parents and Boz?" Perda put in. "There's no way to prove they took that thing."
"What thing?" Venna looked confused.
"The guidelink!" Gliss cried. "Zann's parents didn't steal it!"
"What's a guidelink?" Venna shook her head. "Never mind, I don't care. Whatever it might be, the other items that are missing are much more important."
"Huh?" Now Zann was confused. "What items are you talking about? What's missing from the lab?"
"Several of the relics." Venna sounded grim. "Including the Mask of Zanta."
Perda gasped. "Really? That's the most powerful relic there is!"

"Yeah. But why would anyone think my parents would want to steal it?" Zann stared at Venna. "Now that I think about it, you were the one who didn't want the relics destroyed. Why didn't they accuse you?"

Venna frowned at him, looking angry for a second. Then she sighed again. "Because I have an alibi," she said. "I was in a meeting at the palace when the relics disappeared. Otherwise, I'd probably be in the dungeon right now too."
"Venna!" a woman called from across the room. "We need you!"
"Coming!" Venna called back. She looked at the kids. "You four should lie low for the moment," she said quietly. "I'll get in touch when I figure out how to help the prisoners."
She rushed away. Gliss looked around nervously before pulling the others into the hallway. "Venna's right," she whispered. "We should get out of here."
Perda didn't seem to hear her. "Who would steal the Mask of Zanta?" she asked.
"And why?" Zann added. "It's such a dangerous relic—the most ancient and powerful one in Magica."
Perda nodded. "At least since the Horn of the Otherworld has been destroyed."
Zann thought back to their last adventure and shuddered. Morb had stolen the Horn of the Otherworld and used it to give himself an incredible amount of power.
Gliss seemed to be thinking the same thing. "What if Morb stole the mask?" she said, her eyes widening. "He might have made it back here to Magica before us."
"He probably did," Perda agreed. "It took us a while, because he stole the guidelink from us."
Zann glanced back into the throne room. Venna was huddled with Gliss' uncle and several other people. They all looked very serious.
"We should have asked exactly when the relics went missing," he said. "Maybe we should ask Venna right now."
Darb spoke up. "You heard what she said. She wants us to lie low."
"But we should warn her," Zann said. "I mean, if Morb really is back, she should know, right?"
"We don't know for sure that Morb is back," Gliss argued. "Maybe he—"
Suddenly a Red popped into view from a nearby doorway. "Hey!" The man grabbed Gliss by the arm. "What did you kids just say?"
"What?" Gliss tried to yank her arm away, but the man's grip was strong.
"Let go of her!" Zann shouted. "Otherwise we'll call for help!" Zann was angry, but he was also confused. He had seen this man before. But where?
"Hey, I know you," Darb blurted out. "We saw you at Zann's parents' lab." Darb glanced at his friends. "Remember?"

Now Zann did remember. The man had been with Venna and the king and queen when they'd whisked his parents away to that important meeting on his birthday. Zann had thought the man looked familiar back then too.
The man ignored Darb. "I heard you say my brother's name," he said, glaring at Gliss in an accusing way. "Why?"
"Huh?" Gliss blinked in surprise. "What are you talking about?"
"Yeah," Zann added. "Who's your brother?"
The man turned and stared at him. "My brother . . . is Morb."
"What?" Perda cried. She stared at the mysterious man. "Morb is your brother?"
"That's why you look familiar," Zann said. "You look kind of like him."
"What were you saying about my brother?" the man demanded.
Zann's heart pounded. What if Morb's brother was just as evil as Morb? What if Morb had sent him to capture the kids?
"None of your business," Zann blurted out. He grabbed Darb with one hand and Gliss with the other, hoping that Perda saw what he was doing. "Zap!"
Splash!
They landed in a courtyard fountain just inside one of the palace entrances. Several guards hurried toward them.
"Where did you kids zap from?" the biggest guard demanded. "The use of magic within palace walls is forbidden without permission!"
Zann stepped out of the fountain. "Since when?"
"Since yesterday." The guard narrowed his eyes. "Who are you anyway? You look familiar."
"Nobody," Zann said quickly. "We were just trying to leave."
The guard snapped his fingers, and the Directory appeared. A second later he was reading Zann's page.
"Oh, I see," the guard said. "Your parents and grandfather are in the dungeon. Maybe we should take you there as well."
Zann gulped. He tried to figure out how they could escape. At that moment Morb's brother zapped into view nearby.
"It's all right," he told the guard in a stern voice. "These rascals slipped away from me, but it won't happen again."
"They're with you, Maff?" The guard sounded surprised.
"Yes. Laddno wishes to speak with them." Maff rubbed his hands together. Magical shackles appeared around the kids' arms. "Thanks for catching them for me."
"Hey!" Perda cried.
"But . . ." The guard sounded slightly suspicious.
"That will be all, sir." Maff turned away. "Come, all four of you. It's this way."
Zann didn't trust Morb's brother, but he didn't want to end up in the dungeon either. So he followed Maff out of the courtyard, pulling his friends along.
"Are you sure this is a good idea?" Perda whispered. "What if he's working with his brother?"
Zann wondered the same thing. "Are you really taking us to see Laddno?" he asked Maff.
Maff glanced at him. "Of course not. I hold no loyalty to that bully. He's as crooked as the Wormwood tree itself."
"What do you mean?" Gliss said. "He's running for King of Magica."

"Yes, and we can only hope that Venna crushes him in the election," Maff said grimly. "Who knows what Laddno has in mind for Magica if he's elected. His entire business empire is based on shady deals and black market goods, mostly from other worlds."
"Really?" Perda's eyes widened. "How do you know that?"
"I have my ways," Maff said. "I found out Laddno provided several of the items my brother used in his evil contraptions."
"I thought Wyssa brought Morb all that stuff from other worlds," Zann said.
"She brought most of it," Maff said. "But there were a few things that even she wasn't willing to help Morb with."
"Wow." Zann was stunned. He hadn't paid much attention to Laddno, or worried much about the election either. But now it sounded as if Laddno was really bad news!
Then again, how could he be sure that Maff was telling the truth? After all, he was Morb's brother.
"If you're not taking us to Laddno, where are you taking us?" Darb asked.
"Wherever the guards won't find you," Maff replied. "If they dump you in the dungeon, you won't be able to tell me why you were talking about my brother just now."
Zann traded a look with his friends. Perda was frowning.
"We're not going to tell you anything while you're holding us prisoner," she said.

"What?" Maff blinked and then glanced at the magical shackles still holding the kids together. "Oh, the Shackle spell. Sorry, I only conjured that to trick those guards. If I release you, will you promise not to zap away again?"
"We won't promise you anything!" Gliss cried.
Maff grinned and snapped his fingers. Zann braced himself for some horrible new spell to hit them. Instead the shackles disappeared.
Perda rubbed her arm where the shackles had been. "I thought you'd only release us if we talked."
"I'm not my brother," Maff said. "I hope you'll tell me what I want to know. If not, I'll still help you escape."
"Really?" Perda shot Zann an uncertain glance.
Zann wasn't sure what to say. He was surprised that Maff had released them before getting what he wanted. That wasn't a very Morb-like thing to do. Maybe Maff wasn't much like his brother after all.
"Come in here." Maff stepped into a nearby room. "We should stay out of sight."
Zann hesitated. Then he shrugged and followed Maff into the room. "We might as well trust him," he told his friends. "Maybe he can help us free my parents and the others."
"Okay." Perda still sounded uncertain. "So should we tell him about, you know, Morb?"
"Please do," Maff urged. "Then I'll tell you what I know."
"Okay." Zann took a deep breath. "It started several days ago. I thought I was receiving a Red Share . . ."

He went on to tell Maff the whole story, with his friends chiming in now and then. Maff looked more and more alarmed. When he heard that Morb seemed to have magic power again, his eyes widened. And when the kids described how Morb had grabbed the guidelink and disappeared into the vortex, Maff went pale.
"This is terrible!" Maff exclaimed.
"We didn't mean to release Morb," Gliss said.
"He tricked us," Perda added.
"I know." Maff nodded wearily. "You kids shouldn't blame yourselves. This is all my fault!"
"What do you mean?" Perda asked Maff. "How can it be your fault?"
"Yeah, we're the ones who rescued Morb from that houseboat," Zann added.
"But I was the one who created the houseboat," Maff told them.
"What?" Gliss exclaimed. "How?"

Maff sighed. "I didn't want Wyssa to kill my brother," he said. "I know what Morb did. I know he deserved his fate. But he's my brother." His eyes had a faraway look. "Maybe if my brothers and sisters and I had been a little nicer to him, things would have been different. We should have included him more often, even though he was a Void . . ."
Zann glanced at his friends. "Okay," he said. "But how did you stop Wyssa from doing what she planned to do?"
Maff blinked. "Oh. That was easier than I expected. When she left Magica with Morb, I tracked her through the vortex."
"You did?" Perda said. "How?"
Maff shrugged. "I've made a lifelong study of off-world magic," he said. "I used a difficult spell."
Zann nodded. He guessed that Maff was a very powerful Red. Otherwise he wouldn't be hanging around at the palace with Venna and the other important people in First City.
"I expected the spell to lead me to Fardark," Maff went on. "That's a terrible world where—"
"We know," Zann broke in. "We've been there."
Perda shuddered. "Yes. Wyssa had threatened to feed Morb to a scatter beast."
"I thought that was her plan too," Maff said. "But instead I ended up on Skellia."
"So Ello—I mean Morb—was telling us the truth?" Gliss asked. "Wyssa brought Morb along when she rescued the Skellian people?"
"Not exactly," Maff said. "Apparently she left him immobilized in an unpopulated world while she transported the Skellians to their new home. Then she retrieved Morb and brought him to Skellia."
"Why?" Zann asked. "Did she want to feed him to a gulper?"
Maff smiled faintly. "I doubt a gulper would be interested. Morb had no magic left."
"Right," Darb said. "Gulpers eat magic. Morb was back to being a Void."

Maff nodded. "Wyssa had decided that a scatter beast would provide too quick and merciful an end to Morb," he said. "So she decided to strand him on Skellia. She'd discovered that Morb is terrified of deep water and can't swim."
"Oh!" Now Zann understood Wyssa's plan. "So she left him there with no magic, which means no way to reach a wormhole or navigate the vortex."

"Exactly," Maff confirmed. "There was only a small island left, and the waters were still rising. She knew that eventually he would drown, but that he'd have plenty of time to ponder his own demise in the meantime."
"Wow, that's horrible," Gliss said. She glanced at the others. "Even for Morb."
"Yeah." Zann shuddered. "So then you found him there?" he asked Maff.
"That's right," Maff said. "He begged me to take him away from Skellia. I wouldn't do that—he still had to pay for his crimes. But I couldn't help taking pity on him. I didn't want him to die."
"So you created that houseboat," Zann said.
"Yes. I also provided him with a pair of infused gloves. They contained just enough self-refreshing magic to allow Morb to create food and other basic necessities."
"Self-refreshing magic?" Perda sounded curious. "What do you mean?"
"It's a very simple type of off-world magic," Maff explained. "It's rather weak though. That's why I chose it, given Morb's, er, talents for manipulating magic."
"Wow," Gliss said. "Now a bunch of stuff makes a lot more sense."
"But not all of it," Zann added. "Morb only had a weak pair of infused gloves. So how was he able to do Masking spells and send me weird messages from another world?"
"Good question," Perda said. "Masking spells take a lot of magic energy. At least that's what the books say. And who knows what kind of spell he used to communicate with Zann."

"I have no idea." Maff shrugged. "I thought I'd considered every possibility, but clearly my brother is even cleverer than I realized. He must have harnessed some sort of native Skellian magic source to increase the gloves' power."
"Maybe he caught a gulper or something," Perda suggested.
Darb winced. "I hope not," he said. "Or if he did, I hope he treated it better than he did those blue leeches he brought here."
Zann was a little surprised that Darb was so concerned about the gulpers, which were kind of scary. But Darb did love all animals, from panic bugs to the biggest, nastiest dragons.
"This is looking bad," Gliss declared in a shaky voice. "We have to tell someone that Morb is on the loose!"
"Who can we tell?" Perda said. "First City is in chaos. Nobody even knows where the king and queen have gone!"
"Yeah, and my parents and Boz wouldn't even listen to us," Zann said. "That is, before they got tossed in the dungeon." He looked at Maff. "Do you think you could get us in to see them?"
"Are you sure that's a good idea?" Gliss said. "What if the guards throw us in a cell too?"
"It might be worth the risk," Maff said. "Boz and Teplo might have a good idea for stopping Morb."
"You mean you don't know how to stop him?" Perda said.
Maff shook his head and looked grim. "I'm sorry, I don't. But I'm willing to do whatever it takes if someone else has a plan."
Zann stared at Maff in alarm. If Morb's own brother didn't know how to stop him, what chance did they have?
But he tried not to lose hope. "Okay, let's go to the dungeon," he said.
"We're not supposed to use magic unless absolutely necessary," Maff told Zann and his friends. "We'd better walk to the dungeon."
"Who banned magic inside the palace?" Zann asked.
"I'm not sure." Maff looked troubled.
The ban sounded strange to Zann. With the king and queen gone, who was in charge at the palace? Normally it would be the Red Council. But why would they ban magic? It didn't make sense.
A huge guard stood outside the dungeon's entrance. He wasn't dressed like the other palace guards. His uniform was entirely black.
"Who are you?" Maff asked the guard. "Why are you dressed like that?"
The guard ignored Maff's questions. "What's your business here?" he demanded.
"I want to see my parents," Zann said. "They're in the dungeon."
The guard looked him up and down. "Go ahead," he said, stepping aside to let them pass. "But don't use any magic."
"That's odd," Maff said as the group walked down the steps. "That guard wasn't wearing a typical uniform. I wonder what's going on."
Zann spotted more guards below. They were dressed just like the guard upstairs.
Zann pushed past them, eager to see his family.
"Zann!" his father exclaimed. "What are you doing here?"
"We wanted to see you." Zann hurried closer. His mother was in the cell next to Nax. Boz and Teplo were nearby.
"Uncle Gar!" Gliss cried suddenly. "How did you end up in there?"
Zann quickly scanned the cells. Gliss' uncle was right beside Teplo. Other members of the Red Council were locked up too.
"I don't see Venna," Perda whispered. She shot a careful glance at the nearest guard.
"Or Saffa," Zann murmured back. "That's good."
The scene reminded Zann of the time when Morb had imprisoned most of the Reds in Magica.

But Morb wasn't doing this, or someone would have seen him. The thought made Zann feel a little better. But only a little. How could he talk to his parents and the others with all these guards listening?
Maff seemed to be thinking the same thing. "May we have a moment of privacy?" he asked the guards. "The boy wishes to speak with his parents."
"Sorry," a guard said, not sounding sorry at all. "We have our orders. We must stay."
Maff opened his mouth as if to argue. But Zann's mother leaned forward.
"It's all right, kids," Asta said. "It's good to see you, but you don't need to worry about us."
"That's right," Uncle Gar added. "This will all get sorted out after Venna is elected."
"Just stay safe, all right?" Nax said.
Before Zann could answer, footsteps pounded down the stairs. All the guards spun around and saluted as Laddno stepped into the room.

"At ease, fellows," he told the guards. His hands clasped behind his back, he strolled toward the cells, ignoring Maff and the kids. "Hello, citizens," he said. "I'm sorry to see you in such dire straits."
"Hmph," Boz said. Nobody else made a sound.

Laddno wandered up and down the row of cells. "I wish to inform you that your happiness is very important to me," he said. "If you are all innocent, as you claim, I'll make sure you're released once I've been elected king."
"Why not release them now?" Perda said boldly. "Nobody seems to be in charge now that the king and queen have disappeared. I bet you and Venna could join together to free the prisoners right away."
Laddno peered at her. "Who are you?" he asked.
"Never mind her," Boz said. "We're okay, kids. We can wait until after the election."

"Yes," Teplo added. "But if you're worried, you should recite my favorite poem. It's called 'Ode to a Turnip.'" He cleared his throat. "'Such a fine fruit, ah! Happiness attends the chewing herewith.'"
Laddno scowled at him. "Enough with the poetry," he snapped. "I never could stand that nonsense. What's the point of it?"
"What's the point, indeed?" Teplo beamed at him and then winked at Zann. "Now, be off with you. Children and turnips both require fresh air, hmm?"
Zann exchanged confused looks with his friends. Teplo had always been a little strange. Had prison finally made his mind snap?
"You heard the man." Laddno gestured to the guards. "Take them outside."
Zann was soon outside the palace walls with his friends.
"Where's Maff?" Perda asked.
"I'm not sure." Zann looked around. The guards had zapped them outside, but Maff was nowhere in sight. "I guessed he stayed in the palace."
"I've got it!" Darb blurted out.
The others stared at him. "What?" Gliss asked.
"The poem." Darb grinned. "I know what Teplo was trying to tell us."
Zann had already almost forgotten about that silly turnip poem. "What are you talking about?"
"It's an acronym," Darb explained. "The first letters of each word of the poem are S-A-F-F-A-H-A-T-C-H."
Perda gasped. "Saffa hatch!" she exclaimed. "That must mean that Saffa is hiding out in the hatch at Teplo's house."
"She must be afraid she'll be taken prisoner too," Zann said.
"And Teplo wants us to hide with her!" Darb added.
"Shh." Zann glanced around, hoping nobody had heard them. He didn't want to wind up in prison.
"What are we waiting for?" Gliss said. "Let's go!"
All was quiet at Teplo's house. Zann checked to make sure nobody was nearby. Then he knocked on the hatch outside the front door.
It creaked open, but there was no other sound.
"Should we go down?" Gliss asked, sounding nervous.
"I'll go first." Zann tried to look brave. He sat down on the edge and lowered himself into the darkness below.
Abruptly he let out a scream—his entire body was engulfed in flames!
"Zing, stop that!" a voice cried from the darkness.
A light flared. Gasping in pain, Zann dropped to the floor. Zing flew around his head, whistling irritably.
"Sorry about that." Saffa hurried forward and touched Zann's arm, instantly healing the burns. "He's been a little excitable ever since we brought him down here."
"Sorry you got burned, Zann." Teplo's assistant, Fala, stepped into view behind Saffa. "We zapped your dragon here as soon as we realized you kids had disappeared."
"That's okay. I'm used to getting burned." Zann scratched Zing on the head. Then he looked up. His friends were peering down anxiously. "It's okay!" he called. "I'm fine."
Once the others were inside, Fala closed the hatch with a snap of her fingers.
"I'm glad you're here," Saffa told the kids. She chuckled as Zing snuggled up to Darb. "I think Zing's glad too."
"Thanks." Zann eyed Teplo's sniffer goose, which had just waddled into sight. "Teplo sent us."
"Are the prisoners okay?" Fala asked.
"They seem to be," Gliss said. "My uncle is with them now too."

"Oh dear." Saffa shook her head. "It seems as if anyone who was close to Boz or Zann's parents is being taken into custody. Fala and I were afraid we'd be next on the list. That's why we went into hiding. I'm just glad my husband is traveling far from First City right now."
"Is Venna in the dungeon?" Fala asked.
"No, we didn't see her there," Perda replied.
"Good." Saffa paced around the small room. "Let's hope it stays that way."
"She said she had an alibi for the time when the relics went missing," Zann said.
Saffa nodded. "That may be true. But this situation seems to be about more than the missing relics."
"What do you mean?" Darb asked. "Who's ordering the guards to take all those prisoners?"
"We have no idea," Fala said. "That's what troubles us the most."
"We might know," Gliss blurted out. "I hope we're wrong. But we need to tell you something."
"What is it?" Saffa asked.
The kids explained what had happened with Morb.
"Uh-oh," Fala muttered. "This is bad."
"Do you think Morb could be imprisoning Reds again?" Gliss asked.
"I doubt it," Saffa said. "Reds were already being imprisoned before Morb escaped from you." She started pacing again. "But he's no doubt up to something."
"Yes." Fala sounded grim. "And Magica is extremely weak right now with all the political turmoil. If Morb shows up, he'll have a good chance of carrying out his evil plans—whatever they are."
"He probably wants to take over Magica again," Perda said.
Gliss shuddered. "Or destroy it!"
Saffa hardly seemed to hear them. "We need to find out if he's back in Magica yet." She snapped her fingers, and the Directory appeared. "Morb!" she said.
The Directory showed Morb's page. It hadn't been updated since Wyssa had taken him away several months earlier.
"Hmm." Fala scanned the entry. "That's good. But we shouldn't be too happy. Morb might have tampered with his entry somehow."

"That sounds like something he'd do," Perda said. "Maybe he put a Disguising spell on himself so the Directory didn't recognize him when he returned to Magica. Or maybe he put a spell on the Directory itself, so it couldn't update his entry. A Dousing spell might work for that."
"If we don't trust the Directory, how can we find out if Morb is here?" Zann said.
"Let's do a Tracking spell." Saffa glanced at Fala. "Do we have access to anything Morb owned?"
Fala nodded. After digging through a drawer for a moment, she pulled out a ring with a glowing stone.
"What's that?" Zann asked.
"It's from another world. After Morb's first defeat, the Magic Masters searched his lair. Teplo found this and decided to keep it as a souvenir."
"Perfect," Saffa said. "We can use it as our focusing object."
"Oh, I've read about this kind of Tracking spell!" Perda looked excited. "If you have an object that belongs to someone, you can use it to draw you toward that person."
"I thought using magic to track other people was illegal." Gliss sounded worried.
"It is," Saffa said. "But this is more important than any law."
Zann nodded. "If Morb is back in Magica, we need to know. Let's do it!"
He and his friends watched while Saffa and Fala prepared the spell, creating a mixture of powders and liquids.
"That looks like one of Wyssa's potions," Perda whispered to Zann.
Soon the potion was ready. Saffa carefully dipped the ring in it.
"Now the ring will pull us toward its owner," Saffa told the kids. "In this case, Morb."
Fala snapped her fingers; the hatch popped open.
Saffa glanced at the kids. "You kids should stay here. It'll be safer."
"No way!" Zann said. "We were the ones who released Morb."
"By accident," Gliss mumbled.
Zann nodded. "By accident. But we still want to help find him."
"And stop him!" Perda added.
Saffa eyed them for a moment and then nodded. "All right. But let's leave the dragon and the goose here. They'll only attract attention."
"Sorry, little buddy," Zann said as Zing tried to follow them. "You need to stay here."
Once outside, the group walked along, following the pull of the ring. The object led them out of Teplo's neighborhood, across the river, and along several winding streets. Soon they were in Wormwood.
Fala looked around. "Maybe Morb is here trying to procure some magic items from the locals."
But the ring didn't lead toward any of the huts. Instead it pulled them straight to the Wormwood wormhole!
"Now what?" Zann stared at the wormhole, which had swirled open at their approach.
"I guess the Directory was right," Darb said. "Morb isn't in Magica."
"Yet." Saffa reminded everyone. "This could be our chance to find him and stop him before he gets here."
Fala nodded. "We should tell Venna what's going on."
"Good idea," Saffa said. "But this news is too important to entrust to a message moth. Someone might intercept it."
"You're right," Fala said. "I'll go speak to Venna in person." She rubbed her hands together and zapped away.
As the others waited, they heard shouts from the area near Wyssa's old hut. There was a burst of magical energy. People peeked out from nearby shelters to see what was going on.
Saffa looked uneasy. "I hope nobody starts wondering what we're doing by the wormhole."
Fala reappeared. "Things are getting worse," she said breathlessly. "I spoke to Venna. She's still safe—for now. But the guards are looking for you, Saffa." She turned. "And you too, Zann."
Zann gulped. Then he glanced at Saffa. "Sounds like it'll be safer for all of us in the vortex. We should go now."
"What about Zing and the goose?" Darb said. "We can't abandon them in the hatch."
"I'll stay behind with them," Fala said. "I can use the Remote Eye to keep an eye on things."
Zann remembered the Remote Eye. It was an old-fashioned magical device that could be used to see long distances. "Good idea," he said.
Another series of shouts and shrieks rang out from the huts.
"Let's not waste any more time," Saffa said anxiously.
"Be careful." Fala patted Zann on the shoulder and then nodded to the others. "I'll see you when you return."
She zapped away. Saffa stepped toward the wormhole. "Let's go."
"Wait!" Perda said. "Shouldn't we do a Shackle spell?"
"Why?" Saffa looked confused.
Zann and his friends looked at each other. "Have you ever been in the vortex before?" Zann asked Saffa.
She shrugged. "I've read about it. And of course I've discussed it with Nax and Asta and others."
Zann winced. He remembered how overwhelming the vortex was during his first adventure through it. But then again, Saffa was a Magic Master. Maybe it would be easy for her.
"We always use a Shackle spell in the vortex," Zann explained. "That way we're sure to stay together."
Once they were shackled, they dived into the wormhole with Saffa leading the way.
"Whoa!" she cried as soon as they were in the vortex. She waved her arms, which sent the whole group spinning wildly.
"Stop that!" Gliss called. "Just let it pull you along."
"I—I can't!" Saffa sounded breathless and scared.
Zann glanced at his friends. "Maybe we'd better stop for a rest."
Perda nodded.
Zann grabbed the edge of the next wormhole. The world they were passing looked safe, so he pulled the group through. After landing on solid ground, he undid the Shackle spell.

Saffa took a few deep breaths and then sat up. She looked around. "Oh my! Look, there are five suns. This must be Illumos. Apparently the multiple suns have a multiplying effect on the magic here. Let's try it!"
She rubbed her fingers together. A second later a hat appeared, followed by several more!

Saffa laughed with delight. "It's just as Nax and Asta said!" she exclaimed. "Oh, this is marvelous! I can't believe I'm really here." She clapped her hands. "I wonder if we could find Chronos next? I've always wanted to see that world. It sounds so relaxing."
Zann glanced anxiously at his friends. "Shouldn't we focus on finding Morb?"
Saffa's smile faded. "You're right, Zann. Sorry for getting distracted."
"It's okay." Darb grinned. "We all got kind of distracted our first time visiting new worlds."
After a short rest, Perda redid the Shackle spell.
Saffa handed the glowing ring to Zann. "Maybe you'd better handle this," she said. "You have much more experience in the vortex than I do."
"Thanks," Zann said. "But actually, Perda is better with that kind of stuff than I am." He handed over the ring.
Perda slipped it onto her finger. "Okay, let's go!"
This time Saffa was between Zann and Perda. That seemed to help her stay calm as they flew through the vortex. Zann glanced forward at Perda, who was leading the way.
"Is the Tracking spell working?" he called.
"Yes," Perda replied. "It's leading us this way!"
They sped past several wormholes without slowing. Then Zann felt the ring pulling them toward a wormhole up ahead.
"This must be where Morb is!" Gliss exclaimed.
"Hold on, everyone!" Perda cried.
Zann didn't have time to look at the world before being sucked through the wormhole.
"Oof!" Zann grunted as he landed hard.
Perda stood up and looked at all the trees. "Whew!" she said. "At least we're not in Fardark."
Zann grinned. "I was thinking the same thing."
"Where are we?" Gliss asked as Perda unshackled everyone.
Zann didn't recognize the world. But he could feel magic energy snapping through the air.
"I recognize those trees from the books," Saffa said. "I think we're in Atmo."
Zann remembered that his parents had mentioned Atmo. Suddenly he noticed that Perda was several dozen strides away and moving fast. "Hey, Perda, wait up!"
"I can't!" she called breathlessly. "The spell is really strong here!"
Everyone rushed after her. They nearly crashed into her when she abruptly stopped near an enormous tree.
"Careful!" Saffa whispered. "Morb must be nearby."
A cloaked figure stepped out from behind the tree. "What in all the worlds are you doing here?" an irritated voice asked. The figure threw back its hood.
Zann gasped. "Wyssa!"
Wyssa glared at Zann and the others. "I thought I'd seen the last of you when I left Magica."
"We weren't looking for you, Wyssa," Perda said. "This brought us here."

Wyssa's eyes widened when Perda held up the ring. The old woman snatched it away. "This belonged to my sister," she blurted out. "She gave it to me as a last gift just before . . ." Her voice trailed off, and her eyes narrowed. "Where did you get this?"
"The ring is yours?" Saffa said. "We thought it belonged to Morb."
"Ah." Wyssa's expression shifted into a frown. "I should have known that dirty rat was the one who stole it from me. He probably planned to use it to blackmail me."
"Oh dear," Saffa said. "If Morb stole the ring from you, it never really belonged to him."
Zann nodded as he figured out what had happened. "So the Tracking spell worked," he said. "But it led us to the ring's true owner, not its most recent possessor."
"That makes sense," Perda said. "Otherwise it would have led us to Teplo, because he had it last."
Wyssa held up a hand. "Silence," she said. "What's going on here? Why are you tracking Morb? I told you I'd make sure he never bothers Magica again."
Zann bit his lip and flashed a guilty look at his friends. "Actually, Morb seems to have a new plan."

After he and his friends told Wyssa everything that had happened, the old woman looked furious. Wyssa whirled away, muttering under her breath, and stomped over to a nearby bush. She began plucking berries from its branches.
"What are you doing?" Saffa asked.

Instead of answering, Wyssa pointed at Zann. "You, boy," she ordered. "Go up the lung tree, the one over there with the gray bark. Break off three twigs from near the top. Make sure they're small ones, so the tree isn't hurt."
"That's a lung tree?" Zann remembered his parents saying that they'd used a piece of wood from a lung tree to power the infusinator.
"Hurry!" Wyssa shouted.

Zann levitated to the top of the tree. The air sparked around him, magic energy bouncing off him in ticklish little bursts. He remembered his parents saying that Atmo's magical energy came from the air. It felt very strange to be surrounded by that much magic all the time!

When he reached the top of the tree, he broke off the twigs, as Wyssa had requested. Far below he could hear her barking orders at the others. Zann glanced down to make sure she wasn't looking up. Then he broke off another few twigs, which he stuck in his pocket. Maybe they would help his parents with their experiments, if things ever went back to normal.
"Hurry up, boy!" Wyssa shouted. "What's taking you so long?"
"Coming!" he called quickly and floated back down.

When he reached the ground, Zann saw Wyssa scowl. She grabbed the twigs out of his hand without saying thank you. But Zann didn't mind. He was glad that they'd found her, even if it had been an accident. She might be the only person who could help them find and defeat Morb for good.
Wyssa was crouching down by the pile of stuff she'd been gathering.
Saffa wandered over to look. "Aha!" she exclaimed. "I just figured out what you're doing, Wyssa. It's a Locator spell, isn't it? A much more sophisticated one than the one we used though."
Wyssa didn't respond. She was assembling the twigs Zann had brought her into a tepee shape, tying them together with some vines she'd gathered.
"Are you building a contraption like the Secret Eye?" Perda asked.
"Or like those things Morb is always building?" Gliss asked uneasily.
"It does look like Morb's contraptions, only smaller," Zann agreed. "Where did you learn how to make it?"
Wyssa glanced up. "I need to concentrate," she growled. "Stop your incessant chattering."

The group fell silent while Wyssa continued her work. Soon the little contraption resembled a pyramid. It was filled with various leaves and stones. Green berry juice ran down its sides. Finally Wyssa tied the glowing ring onto it.
"The ring is part of the magic?" Saffa asked with interest. "Will it help you locate Morb because he stole it from you?"
Zann expected Wyssa to ignore that question too. But she glanced up at Saffa.

"No," Wyssa said firmly. "I didn't attach the ring because of Morb. This ring has been in my family for generations. That gives me a special connection with it, which will boost the spell's magic power."
"Cool," Perda said. "I've read about that kind of thing. It's sort of like using a relic."
"Silence, please." Wyssa sprinkled a handful of sparkly powder over the contraption. "Morb!" she intoned loudly. "Show us Morb!"
Zann held his breath as a puff of pale green smoke emerged from the contraption. It slowly formed into a ghostly image of Morb.
"It's him!" Saffa cried.
Zann stared at the image. It showed Morb standing in a sandy landscape with a jagged ridge behind him. He was scowling at something Zann couldn't see.
A second later a gust of wind blew the image away.
"Aah!" Gliss cried in frustration. "We didn't see enough to know where he is!"
"Yeah," Zann said. "There must be lots of desert worlds out there."
Wyssa's eyes met Saffa's. "I know exactly where that is," Wyssa said.
Saffa was nodding slowly. "I recognized Dragonjaw Ridge in the background. It's one of the most recognizable features in the Far Frontier."
"The Far Frontier?" Zann said with a gasp. "But that means . . ."
"Yes," Saffa said grimly. "Morb is already back in Magica."
Wyssa snatched the ring from the contraption she'd built. "Don't worry," she said. "I'll deal with Morb." She stomped off, but Zann and the others caught up with her.
"We're coming too," Zann said.
"No." Wyssa shoved him aside. "It's my responsibility. Now get out of my way."
"But we want to help!" Saffa said.
"Yeah," Perda said. "Besides, you can't just leave us here. We might not be able to find our way back to Magica without you. Morb took our guidelink, remember?"
Darb nodded. "And even if we do find our way back, First City isn't safe for us right now."
"That's fine," Wyssa said. "Atmo is pleasant and safe. You can relax here, and I'll return for you once I'm done with Morb."
Saffa nodded. "Perhaps that's for the best."
"No!" Zann cried. "You can't leave us here!"
"Yeah, what if you need our help?" Perda exclaimed.
Wyssa's eyebrows shot up in surprise. "What?" she cried. "I don't require help from anyone, especially a bunch of chattering children."
"You might." Zann didn't back down. "We were the ones who stopped Morb before, remember?"
"That's right!" Perda chimed in. "We couldn't have done it without your help. But you couldn't have done it without our help either."
"The kids have a point," Saffa said. "They've done more to stop Morb's terrible plans than anyone."
Wyssa glowered at them all. Finally she shrugged. "Fine," she snapped. "But I'm not babysitting any of you, all right? Now let's go. I need to gather more ingredients on our way back."

She grabbed more twigs and plants on the way to the Atmo wormhole. But she didn't stop there. Once they were in the vortex, she led the way into world after world. Zann and his friends had visited a few of the worlds before, but there were several that they'd never seen. They stayed in each one just long enough for Wyssa to gather a few ingredients. Zann and his friends barely had time to rest and recover their magic energy before they were zooming through the vortex again.
After landing in one world, Zann felt weak and out of breath. He breathed deeply, and right away he regretted it.
"Ugh," Perda exclaimed. "We're back in Niffia!"
"Oh my!" Saffa looked startled. "I've read about this place, but the stench is worse than I ever could have imagined!"
"Definitely," Gliss agreed.
"Hush," Wyssa scolded. "Here come our hosts. Don't embarrass me by insulting their lovely world."
Zann rolled his eyes. Niffia might look lovely, but it sure didn't smell lovely!
As usual, a greeting committee was hurrying toward them with big smiles on their faces, which lacked noses.
"Greetings, dear friend!" one of the Niffians cried, beaming at Wyssa. "It's an honor as always to have you here!"
"Thank you, my friends." Wyssa smiled. "With your permission I'm here to gather some ingredients for a spell."
"Of course—everything we have is yours." A Niffian waved toward the fields and forests surrounding them. "Please help yourself."
"Thank you." Wyssa bowed. "While I'm gathering what I need, perhaps you would be so kind as to look after my friends?"
"It would be our honor," another Niffian assured her, bowing to the kids and Saffa. "Come with us for some rest and refreshment."
Zann and the others did their best to ignore the smell as the Niffians took them back to their town and gave them food and drink.
"This world would be perfect if it didn't stink!" Zann whispered to Darb when the Niffians weren't listening.
"And Morb might be perfect if he wasn't evil," Darb replied. "I wonder what he's doing in the Far Frontier."
Zann shrugged. "Look, here comes Wyssa."
"I trust you found what you needed, my friend?" one of them asked.
"I did indeed." She smiled and bowed. Then she turned to survey Zann and the others. "You look comfortable," she said. "Perhaps you should stay here while I, er, take care of things back in Magica."
"No!" Zann blurted out, horrified at the thought of being stuck in stinky Niffia for a long time. "You promised we could come with you."
"I promised no such thing," Wyssa retorted.
Meanwhile the Niffians looked even happier than usual. "It would be our honor if you stayed!" one of them exclaimed.
"Yes," another added. "That would give you a chance to see even more of our beautiful world!"
"We can't stay," Zann said, trying desperately to think of a way to convince Wyssa not to leave them behind. "Wyssa needs our help."
"Yeah, we haven't even had a chance to tell you about everything else that's happening in Magica," Perda told Wyssa.
"Like what?" Wyssa sounded skeptical.
"Like you shouldn't just go barging back into Magica without knowing that the king and queen quit and disappeared," Gliss said.
Wyssa raised one eyebrow. "Interesting. But not relevant."
"And how about Zann's parents being accused of stealing those missing relics?" Perda added.
"Missing relics?" This time Wyssa's voice was sharper. "What missing relics?"
Zann shrugged. "A few of the things in the lab disappeared, and nobody knows where they went or who took them," he said. "Like the Mask of Zanta, and—"
"All right, that's enough chatter," Wyssa interrupted. "I've changed my mind. You're coming with me." She bowed quickly to the Niffians. "Thanks again, my friends. We must depart."
Moments later the whole group was back in the vortex. Zann was relieved. But why had Wyssa changed her mind so abruptly after hearing about the relics?
Before he could ask, he saw a wormhole spinning toward them up ahead.
"Hang on," Wyssa called, yanking them toward it. "We're here."
Zann could tell they'd landed in First City, though he didn't recognize the area. A light green rain was falling, casting a lime-tinted glow over the whole scene.
"Where are we?" Gliss asked.
"Edgewood," Saffa said, sounding perplexed. "It's a neighborhood on the far northern border of First City. But why did you bring us here, Wyssa?"
Zann wondered the same thing. He realized that it was probably too risky to use the palace wormhole right now. But why wouldn't Wyssa bring them out in Wormwood? After all, she used to live there.
"There's no time for idle chitchat." Wyssa snapped her fingers. "Zap!"
This time Zann recognized the spot where Wyssa had taken them. "The zoo?" he said, staring at a pair of nibblers in an enclosure nearby. "Why are we here?"
"Are we going to borrow a dragon to ride to the Far Frontier?" Darb asked.
Gliss glanced toward the dragon pen with a nervous expression. "The dragons here aren't very tame."
Wyssa didn't seem to be listening. She peered through the green rain, which was falling harder now. "My errand here won't take long."
Saffa stepped toward the zoo entrance, looking restless. "We should check on Venna," she said. "She might have been taken prisoner by now."
"There's no time for that," Wyssa said. "We need to find Morb before he gathers more power!"
"The election is less than a month away," Saffa said, sounding stubborn. "If things get any worse, it could be a disaster for all of Magica."
Zann wasn't too worried about the election. But Saffa's words had reminded him of his parents. "We should check on the prisoners too," he said.
"Yes!" Gliss exclaimed. "I want to see my uncle."
Wyssa sighed. "Go," she said. "Make sure they're all okay. I'll wait for you here."
Zann looked at the others. Could they trust Wyssa? Or would she take off for the Far Frontier on her own as soon as they zapped away?
"Wyssa, we might need your help getting into the palace," Saffa said.
Wyssa didn't look happy. But she agreed to go to the palace with them. "We have to hurry," she said.
Everyone joined hands. Zap!
They landed at the edge of the palace square. It was still raining, and Zann had to wipe water from his face before he could see clearly. When he did, his eyes widened.
The square looked much different than usual. Dozens of guards were marching around, all of them wearing that new dark uniform they'd seen on the guards in the dungeon.
"What's that all about?" Saffa muttered.
"Who knows?" Perda said. "Maybe we can figure out a way to sneak in without the guards seeing us."

"We don't have time for that." Saffa sounded impatient. "This is still Magica, isn't it? We have the right to visit the palace anytime we like without fearing imprisonment. I'm tired of sneaking around!"
"But—" Zann began.
It was too late. Saffa was already marching toward the main entrance.
"Should we go with her?" Gliss asked.
"No." Wyssa snapped her fingers, and a glowing wall appeared in front of them.
"Hey." Zann was annoyed. "You can't stop us with a Shield spell."
"It's for your own good," Wyssa said.
Just then Darb poked Zann on the shoulder. "Look!"

Saffa had reached the closest group of guards. While the kids watched, she appeared to argue with the guards. A moment later a guard clapped his hands. A large bubble enclosed Saffa! She yelled and struggled to get out, but it was no use. The bubble was already floating toward the palace.
"No!" Zann blurted out, louder than he'd meant to.
His voice attracted the attention of a guard. The guard turned and peered toward them, his face suspicious.
Zann felt panic flash through him. If they all ended up in the dungeon, there was no way they'd be able to stop Morb!
He grabbed Perda with one hand and Darb with the other. "Zap!" he yelled.
Splash!
They landed in a deep puddle in the gutter outside Teplo's house. Zann glanced around to make sure his friends were there.
Perda, Gliss, and Darb were there, but someone else wasn't.
"Where's Wyssa?" Perda asked.
"I don't know," Zann said. "I guess she didn't zap with us."
Gliss glanced up and down the street nervously. "We should get out of sight while we decide how to find her."
Moments later they were in the hatch. Zing danced around Darb's head, shooting happy flames. Fala seemed relieved to see them.
"Where's Saffa?" she asked.
"The dungeon, probably." Zann told her what had just happened.
"Oh no!" Fala twisted her hands together. "This isn't good. Especially given everything that's happened while you were gone."
"What happened?" Perda asked.
"For one thing, the palace guards found the Mask of Zanta in Zann's house."
"What?" Zann cried. "How did it get there? I'm sure my parents didn't steal it!"
"I know they didn't," Fala said. "But now your parents and Boz are in real trouble."
Zann gulped. "What kind of trouble?"
"I'm not sure yet." Fala said. "They're being kept in the dungeon until the election is over. Then the new king or queen can figure out what to do."
"What about my uncle?" Gliss asked. "Did they let him go?"
"No. All the prisoners are staying until after the election," Fala said.
"It's okay," Zann said. "At least this gives us some time to deal with Morb first. After all, the election is almost a month away."
"No, it's not," Fala said. "That's another thing that happened while you were gone. Laddno is insisting on holding the election next week!"
"The election will be next week?" Gliss blinked in surprise. "Laddno can't do that, can he?"
"He did it," Fala said grimly. "Venna wants this to be over, so she didn't object. Neither did anyone else."
"That makes sense," Darb said. "The longer the campaign goes on, the more time Laddno has to get people all riled up. So Venna probably wants the election as soon as possible."
"I suppose you're right." Fala looked troubled. "It doesn't give us nearly as much time to stop Morb though."
"Yeah," Zann said. "Maybe we should try to rescue my parents before we go to the Far Frontier."
"No," Perda said. "I'm sure Venna won't let anything bad happen to the prisoners, no matter what happens with the election."
"But—" Zann began.
"Think about it," Perda urged him. "Morb is a much bigger threat to everyone, including your parents, than anything that might happen with this election. We have to stop him."
Darb nodded. "Besides, Wyssa won't wait for us if we try to rescue them. For all we know, she already left for the Far Frontier."
"I'll check." Fala hurried over and grabbed the Remote Eye from a shelf. She put it to her eye.
"Check the palace square," Perda suggested. "That's where we saw her last."
Fala nodded. "I don't see her there," she reported after a moment. "I'm checking the streets nearby too."

Zann was only half listening. He was still thinking about his parents and Boz. What if the election took place before Zann and the others returned from the Far Frontier? And what if Laddno won? Maff had told the kids that Laddno couldn't be trusted. What would he decide to do with the prisoners?
Suddenly Zann had an idea. "Can you use that thing to look inside the palace?" he asked Fala.
She lowered the Eye. "Sure," she said. "I've been checking on Venna whenever she's there, just in case something strange happens."
"What about the dungeon?" Zann asked.
"Oh, I see." Fala scratched her chin. "I'm not sure about that. There are probably spells protecting it from spies."
"Can we try?" Zann asked.
"I suppose it wouldn't hurt." Fala raised the Eye again. After a moment she smiled. "Hey, it does work! I can see everyone. They all look fine." She gestured to Zann. "Take a look."
Zann eagerly peered into the Eye. He gasped as he saw his parents, Boz, Teplo, and the others. They were talking quietly to one another from their cells.
"I can't believe there are no Shield spells on the dungeon," Gliss said, reaching for the Eye. "Can I check on my uncle?"
"There probably are spells," Perda said. "But the Remote Eye is a very old form of magic, remember? Maybe the spells don't protect against stuff like that."
"That's probably the case," Fala agreed. "Now let's see if we can locate Wyssa."
The kids took turns scanning the city with the Eye. Meanwhile Fala tried a few other Search spells, but nothing worked.
"Maybe she really did leave without us," Gliss said.
"Now what are we going to do?" Perda exclaimed.
"I know one place we haven't checked," Darb said.
Zann glanced at his friend, who was scratching Zing with one hand. The sniffer goose was cuddled up against Darb's other side, honking softly as she drifted off to sleep.
"Where?" Fala asked.
"The zoo," Darb replied. "That's where she took us before, remember?"
"Let me check." Fala raised the Remote Eye to her face. As soon as she looked through it, she gasped. "There she is—in a dragon pen! But what's she doing?"
Perda grabbed the Eye. "It looks like she's cleaning up dragon scales," she reported. "That's weird."
"Not if she needs the scales for some kind of travel spell," Fala pointed out. "We'd better hurry. She could decide to leave at any moment."
"We?" Zann glanced at Fala. "Are you coming with us?"
She shrugged. "I'd love to see the Far Frontier."
"But what about the animals?" Darb asked.
"I thought you might want to stay with them this time," Fala told Darb, smiling.
"No!" Zann blurted out. "We can't leave Darb behind."
"But he's so good with animals," Fala said. "This is where he can be most helpful."
Gliss shook her head. "He's most helpful with us," she said firmly.
"That's right," Perda agreed. "I've lost count of how many times Darb has helped us during our travels."
Zann nodded. "He might not have magic, but he has skills the rest of us don't have."

Fala looked surprised, but she raised both hands in a gesture of surrender. "All right," she said with a smile. "You've convinced me. Darb can go with you, and I'll stay here. But be careful, all right?"
"We will," Zann promised, reaching for his friends' hands. "Zap!"
They landed in a little fountain filled with moon minnows and other fish.
"Ugh, what is it with you and water, Zann?" Gliss complained. She climbed out and used magic to dry herself and Darb.
"Never mind that." Zann jumped out of the fountain and looked around. "Which dragon pen was Wyssa in when you saw her?"
"It wasn't the big one with the mean dragons," Perda said. "I think I saw a cloud glider in the background."
"That pen is this way." Darb led the way along a path and around a large display of animals native to the Magica Mountains.
When they rounded the corner, Wyssa was just letting herself out of the dragon pen. She frowned when she spotted the kids.
"It's about time you got here," she snapped. "I hope you're ready, because we're leaving for the Far Frontier right now."
"We're going to the Far Frontier now?" Gliss sounded nervous.
Wyssa nodded.
"But how?" Perda asked. "We can't just zap there."
"Why not?" Zann asked.
"Why do you think it's called the Far Frontier?" Perda rolled her eyes. "It's really far away!"

"She's right, Zann," Darb said. "Your parents wrote about the Far Frontier in their book. The place is much farther from First City than the Cave of the Unknown, or the Misty Marshes, or anywhere else you've ever heard of."
Perda nodded. "It was really hard for them to get there—that's why they only went once. Didn't you read your parents' own book, Zann?"

Zann shrugged. He'd flipped through the book about the Far Frontier, but mostly just to look at the pictures. His parents' journey there had happened long before he was born. It wasn't that exciting to him. He'd always been more intrigued by their travels through the vortex.
"So how did they get there?" he asked.
"We don't have time for this," Wyssa muttered.
Perda ignored her. "Your parents zapped as far as they could," she told Zann. "They zapped dragons with them and rode them for the next part of the journey."
"But the dragons refused to go past a certain point," Darb said. "Your parents think it's because there wasn't enough steady magic for them."
"So your parents released the dragons and walked the rest of the way," Perda added. "It took them more than a week to reach the edge of the Far Frontier."
Gliss wrinkled her nose. "Do we have to do all that?"
"No," Wyssa barked. "Now be quiet so I can focus."
Zann saw that she'd pulled out a small contraption made of twigs and pebbles and various other things.
"What's that?" he asked.
Wyssa didn't answer. She leaned over the contraption, carefully pouring the dragon scales she'd gathered into the top.
"Will that contraption zap us all to the Far Frontier?" Gliss asked.

Wyssa ignored the question. "You'll have to be careful about what magic you do while we're in the Far Frontier." Wyssa brushed a few stray scales off her hands. "It's probably better if you check with me before doing any magic at all, actually."
"But—," Perda began.
She fell silent as Wyssa started muttering under her breath and waving her hands over the contraption. A moment later a puff of purple smoke emerged from the top.
"Join hands." Wyssa grabbed Zann's hand. "Then close your eyes and breathe in."
Zann grabbed Perda with his free hand and closed his eyes. He felt light-headed—almost as if his mind had left his body. He could hardly feel Perda's hand in his.
That made him panic. What if he'd lost hold of his friends?
He opened his eyes and screamed in terror. He was hurtling through the air so fast he could barely see a thing! It was even more terrifying than being in the vortex.
"Close your eyes, boy!" Wyssa snapped. She gave his hand a sharp squeeze.
Zann obeyed, though his heart was pounding. What kind of spell had Wyssa created?
A moment later he felt his feet hit the ground hard. He staggered forward, almost losing his balance as the ground shifted below him.
"Oof!" He grunted as he fell onto his hands and knees. The ground was soft—and hot! Zann snatched his hands away immediately.
He opened his eyes. He was in a sun-scorched desert. An endless expanse of sand stretched in every direction. His friends were sprawled nearby. They looked confused.
Wyssa gazed into the distance, one hand shielding her eyes from the bright sun.
"What are you waiting for?" she said when she noticed Zann looking at her. "Let's get moving."
Zann stood, his legs shaky. "Is this the . . . Far Frontier?"
"Of course." Wyssa nudged Perda with her foot. "Up!" the old woman ordered.
Perda groaned and pushed herself upright. "Wow," she said. "This place is even weirder than it looks in the book."

Zann had to agree. The Far Frontier appeared to be nothing but sand dunes, with only a few distant rocky areas dotting the horizon. The sun seemed closer and hotter than elsewhere in Magica. Zann glanced up and saw a dragon soaring lazily far overhead.
Gliss spotted it too. "I thought you said dragons couldn't fly here."
"Regular ones can't," Wyssa replied impatiently. "I suppose some local species must have developed here."
"That makes sense." Darb peered upward with interest. "Different types of animals can adapt to different environments."
"Enough chitchat," Wyssa said sharply. "We need to hurry."
"Why?" Gliss said. "I mean, it only took us like five minutes to get here."
"Wrong." Wyssa glared at her. "Our journey took almost two days."
"What?" Perda exclaimed. "What kind of spell was that, anyway?"
Wyssa didn't respond. She stepped forward, squinting into the distance. "We must locate Morb."
"Okay." Zann brushed sand off his legs. "How are we going to do that?"
"With almost no magic," Gliss added.
Zann waited for Wyssa to answer, or maybe to pull out another mysterious powder or contraption. But she merely shrugged and took a few steps forward.
"It's hard to walk on this soft sand," she muttered.
Zann noticed that she sounded surprised. "Wait," he said. "You have been to the Far Frontier before, haven't you?"
"What gave you that idea, boy?" Wyssa snapped.
Perda gasped. "You've never been here before?"
"Of course not." Wyssa scowled at the kids. "Now be quiet so I can figure out what to do."
Zann gulped. Wyssa didn't have a plan to find Morb!
It was a strange thought. Wyssa usually knew everything.

Perda looked stunned for a second too. Then she cleared her throat. "I've read every word of Zann's parents' books," she told Wyssa. "In the one about the Far Frontier, they talked about how hard it was to walk on the shifting sand."
"Yes, and what's your point?" Wyssa sounded irritated. "We can't zap while we're here. The magic is too unpredictable."
"Nax and Asta befriended some of the nomads who live here." Perda waved a hand at the desert surrounding them. "The nomads taught them to summon something called a hoof beast."
"A hoof beast?" Gliss echoed. "What's that?"
"It's a native desert animal," Darb said. "I've read about them."
Perda nodded. "The nomads taught Zann's parents to control them using just a little bit of magic. That way they could ride them instead of fighting the sand."
"Of course." Wyssa cleared her throat. "I was just going to suggest summoning a few of those beasts."
Zann traded a look with his friends. Had Wyssa really planned to suggest that?
He decided it didn't matter. Wyssa was already pulling some dried leaves and twigs out of her pockets. Whether it was her idea or not, she seemed to know how to summon the beasts.
"Hold out your hands," Wyssa ordered the kids. "Create friction while I sprinkle this on you. But be careful."
Zann and his friends did as she said. Soon magic energy was sparking around them. Wyssa muttered under her breath and closed her eyes, waving her hands to direct the energy.
"Whoa." Perda blinked as a tiny spark exploded in front of her eyes. "This is crazy."
Gliss nodded. "It reminds me of the unstable energy near the Cave of the Unknown."
Zann glanced at Wyssa, but she was ignoring them as she continued to murmur and wave her hands. "Maybe there's a powerful source of magic near here too," he said to his friends.
Gliss gasped. "Like the Source?"
Zann nodded. "What if that's why Morb came here? Maybe he's trying to find it."
"And control it," Perda added grimly. "And I thought it was scary when it was only Laddno who wanted to find the Source!"
"The Source might not even exist," Gliss said.

Before Zann could respond, he heard thundering hooves in the distance. Half a dozen strange creatures appeared on the horizon. They stopped some distance away and peered at the humans with large, dark eyes.
"Are those hoof beasts?" Gliss whispered.
Darb nodded. "They look just like the pictures in the book I read."
Perda took a step forward, shading her eyes for a better look. "They look sort of like desert donkeys, but bigger," she said.
"Prettier too," Gliss put in. "Look at their long manes and tails!"
Zann had to agree. The beasts had multicolored hair in shades of gold, brown, and yellow.
"Their hair helps them blend into the desert," Darb said. "And those wide hooves help them get traction in the shifting sand."
Wyssa frowned. "Why aren't they coming closer?" she muttered. "I know I did the right spell."
"Maybe Darb could try to tame them," Zann suggested. "He's great with animals."
Darb didn't respond for a second. He was still watching the hoof beasts carefully.
"They look nervous," he said. "Actually they look scared."
"Of us?" Perda wondered. "Why?"
Before anyone could respond, one of the hoof beasts let out a sharp whistle. The entire herd wheeled around and galloped off across the sand.
"Stop!" Wyssa cried. She flung magic energy after the animals. "Get back here!"
But the beasts were already gone. "I wonder what scared them," Gliss said.
"Maybe they . . . ," Zann stopped as the sand rumbled beneath his feet. "What was that?"
Perda took a step back. "The ground is moving!"

Zann glanced around. The sand was shifting everywhere he looked. A few dozen strides ahead, a sinkhole appeared to be forming. Suddenly sand shot upward as an enormous, lumpy head burst out of the ground! It looked almost like a dragon—but much bigger. Its snakelike neck was the same color as the sand, and its mouth held two rows of jagged teeth.
"Oh, no!" Perda gasped. "It's a sand beast!"
"What's a sand beast?" Gliss cried.
"I'll tell you later." Perda spun around. "We have to get out of here!"

She took off as fast as she could in the shifting sand. Zann raced after her and almost crashed into her when she skidded to a stop. The sand beast's forked tail had just emerged from the sand ahead of them!
They spun around. But several legs with claws were popping into view all around them.
"How many arms and legs does this thing have?" Gliss cried.
"Enough," Darb said grimly. "We're surrounded!"
The beast's giant head dived at Zann, and he ducked. Saliva sizzled as it hit the hot sand.
"Gliss, look out!" Darb yelled.

Zann spun around and saw one of the creature's claws moving toward Gliss. He snapped his fingers and sent a bolt of energy toward it. But instead of zipping toward the clawed arm, Zann's magic energy burst into a fireball!

That distracted the sand beast just long enough for Gliss to dart away from its claws. Darb grabbed her and pulled her closer to the others. The group huddled together as the beast's multiple limbs all moved toward them.
"We have to get out of here!" Zann cried. "Join hands!"
"Don't try to zap!" Wyssa shouted. "Your magic will—"
Zann didn't wait for her to finish. As soon as he and his friends were touching, he screamed, "Zap!"
"Oof!"
Zann landed so hard that his head spun. He stayed still for a moment to catch his breath. Finally he was able to sit up.
There was no sign of the sand beast. That was a relief. But there was no sign of Zann's friends or Wyssa either.
"I guess that's why Wyssa didn't want us to zap," he muttered.
Looking around, he realized he'd landed in some kind of deep gully. It looked like a dry riverbed.

"That figures," Zann told himself. Whenever he zapped without focusing on his destination, he always seemed to land in water. He supposed that this gully was the closest thing there was to water in the dry expanse of the Far Frontier.
Thinking about water made him thirsty. But he tried to ignore that feeling. He needed to find his friends before he did anything else.
Zann climbed to his feet with a groan. The rocky gully hadn't been as soft a landing as the sand!

He approached the gully's bank. When he tried to climb it, every rock he touched came loose and tumbled to the ground. He grabbed a gnarled shrub that was growing out of the bank. But the shrub's branches were lined with sharp thorns. Soon he was filthy, sore, and totally discouraged.
"This is ridiculous." Zann pulled a thorn from his palm. "Maybe zapping didn't work exactly how I expected it to, but it still worked."
That meant using magic wasn't out of the question. It didn't matter what Wyssa had said.
Zann snapped his fingers. "Levitate."
For a second nothing happened. Zann frowned, and then he rubbed his hands together. Magic energy began to spark weakly around him.
"Levitate!" he said loudly.
This time he felt his feet lift off the sand. He kept rubbing his hands, and slowly he rose into the air. Then he felt himself sinking again.
"Levitate!" he cried again, rubbing his legs together too.
Finally he managed to levitate all the way out of the gully. He landed on the sand at the edge.
"Whew," he said. "Hey!"
A swarm of insects buzzed around him, stinging his arms and face. Zann swatted at them, but they kept attacking. When he tried to zap them with magic energy, he missed.
"Ouch!" he yelled, trying to smack one of the insects. But it was too fast.
Zann rubbed his hands together, ready to zap away. He hesitated. What if he ended up even farther away from his friends?
He danced in place, trying to avoid the stinging insects. His feet kicked up some sand, which gave him an idea.
Zann dropped to his hands and knees and started to dig. He dug his way into the soft, warm sand until he was almost completely covered. Fewer insects could reach him now.
The sand was hot, and after a few minutes, Zann couldn't stand it. He didn't hear any more buzzing, so he carefully dug his way back out. The insects were gone!

"Thank goodness," he muttered, quickly healing the stings with magic. It took a few tries, since his magic energy kept fizzling out before he could touch the right spots. But finally his skin stopped burning and itching.
But then Zann was thirstier than ever. Since his healing magic had basically worked, he snapped his fingers to create a drink.
"Yuck!" he exclaimed as something soft and squishy appeared in his hand. Instead of a cup of refreshing airberry juice, he'd conjured a handful of squashed, overripe airberries!
"Ugh!" Zann tossed the berries away and wiped his hand. Then he tried again. He focused carefully.
This time it worked! He gulped the cup of airberry juice, which made him feel better.
But why was magic so difficult here? At the Cave of the Unknown, it was partly because of all the powerful relics that had been hidden there. Could there be relics nearby now?
"Maybe Morb stole the relics and hid them out here where nobody would find them!" Zann thought with a shiver.

Just then he heard a sound. He spun around and saw Darb riding toward him on a hoof beast. Perda was sitting behind him, looking nervous. Two more hoof beasts were trotting along behind the first one.
"I knew you could tame those animals!" Zann called, smiling, as his friends reached him. "Where's Gliss?"
"We don't know." Perda jumped down. "We hoped she was with you."
"We haven't seen Wyssa, either," Darb added. "Luckily Perda and I landed near each other."
Perda nodded. "I ended up on a rocky little bluff. I looked around and spotted Darb on some grassland below me."
"Grassland?" Zann looked around at the sand and rocks.
"The grass was pretty brown," Darb said with a smile. He patted one of the hoof beasts. "But these guys were eating it."
"Yeah, and as usual Darb made friends right away!" Perda said with a laugh. "So we decided to ride around and look for everyone."
"You were only a ten-minute ride from where we landed," Darb said, scratching the hoof beast on the neck. "This guy must have smelled you or something, because he led us this way."
"Good," Zann said. "Maybe that means he can help us find Gliss and Wyssa. They're probably nearby too."
"I hope so." Darb whistled for the other two hoof beasts. "I'll show you how to ride these guys, and then we can start searching."
Riding a hoof beast was like riding a dragon, except that the hoof beasts were furry instead of scaly, and they didn't fly. Zann held onto the creature's long, silky mane as he settled onto its back.
"Come on," he told his hoof beast. "Let's find our friends."

The hoof beasts carried Zann and his friends away from the rocky gully into more sand dunes. Then they passed some scrubby trees. After that they crossed the grassland Darb and Perda had mentioned. More hoof beasts were grazing there.
"Let's look over there," Perda called, pointing to some hills.
They rode to the hills, which at first were gently rolling and mostly sand. Then the slopes got steeper and rockier, with a few plants dotted here and there.
Perda peered into a cave. "How are we supposed to find two people around here?" she said. "They could be anywhere. Maybe we should try using magic."
"Maybe," Zann said, remembering what had happened with the levitation spell and the airberry juice. "But we'll have to be careful because—"
A Red Share hit Zann, almost knocking him off his hoof beast. It was from Gliss. She was terrified!
"Zann!" Darb halted his hoof beast. "Are you okay?"
Zann gulped for breath as the Red Share started to fade. "I'm fine," he said. "But I'm not sure about Gliss." He told them about the Share.
"Oh, no!" Perda cried. "We have to find her!"
"Could you tell where it was coming from?" Darb asked.
Zann closed his eyes. He could still feel Gliss' terror in the back of his mind. He turned his head, and it faded. When he turned his head the other way, the Share got a little stronger.
He opened his eyes. "That way, I think," he said, pointing.
"I hope Gliss is all right." Darb sounded worried.
"I wonder if Wyssa is with her," Perda said. "If not, then maybe that's why she's scared."
Darb nodded. "I'd be scared too, if I were all alone in the Far Frontier."
Zann didn't say anything. Gliss hadn't just felt scared—she'd felt terrified. Would she feel that way just from being alone? He wasn't sure.
They emerged from the hills. Ahead of them the desert stretched into the distance. Perda shaded her eyes against the blinding sunlight.
"I don't see anything," she said. She looked anxious. "Or anyone. Do you really think Gliss could be anywhere out there?"
"Look." Darb pointed. "There are more hills over there."
Zann squinted through the hot, hazy sunlight. "That's the direction the Share seems to be leading us," he said. "Come on, let's hurry."

The hoof beasts seemed to sense the kids' urgency. The animals broke into a faster gait. Their hooves pounded the sand, kicking up clouds of dust. Zann held on to his beast's long, silky mane, hoping he wouldn’t bounce off.
"At least Morb can't sneak up on us out here—there’s nowhere for him to hide," Perda joked weakly.
"Why do you think he came here?" Zann glanced around at the sun-bleached sand. "Could he really be searching for the Source?"
"Maybe." Darb shrugged. "That sounds like something he'd do."
"Laddno will be mad if someone else finds it first." Zann tried to laugh at his own remark. But he was too worried about Gliss to do more than cough.
They were nearing the next set of hills. The hills were steep and rocky, with spiky plants clinging to them and a few scrawny trees growing sideways out of pockets of soil.
Perda looked up. "I'm not sure these beasts can climb these hills."
"They won't have to climb them." Darb pointed. "I see a trail that leads up to the top."

Zann followed as Darb and his hoof beast led the way into a narrow opening between two hills. The shade of the trail felt good after the searing heat of the desert sun. But Zann felt a little nervous. It was hard to see more than a few strides ahead. What if they ran into another sand beast in here? What if they ran into Morb?
The hoof beasts seemed nervous too. Zann's beast, looking alert, had its head way up in the air. Its ears swiveled, and it let out a loud snort.
Perda cried out as her beast suddenly jumped forward with its ears pricked. "Why are they acting like this?" she exclaimed.

Darb patted his beast. Then he glanced back at the others. "Maybe the hoof beasts don't like being in such an enclosed space," he said. "They're used to being out in the open desert or grasslands. They're probably worried that—"
He broke off with a strangled cry. Zann started to call to him. But before he could, he felt something tighten around his chest. It was a rope!

"Hey!" Zann shouted. He tried to shake off the rope, but it was pinning his arms to his sides. A second later he felt the rope jerk him right off the hoof beast's back. He slammed into the rocky ground with a grunt.
Out of the corner of his eye, Zann saw that both of his friends were in the same situation. He squirmed desperately, trying to free himself. But the rope was too tight—and it was thick and strong.
"Someone lassoed us!" Perda cried. "Who was it? Hey, show yourselves!"

Several people stepped out of the shadows of the rocky hills. The people were tall and lean. Their loose clothes were the same color as the sand. Wide-brimmed hats hid part of their faces, though Zann was pretty sure those faces were painted with clay or paint. He'd seen pictures of such tribes in his parents' book. They were nomads who were able to survive in this rough land.
Zann watched nervously as one of the strangers stepped forward.
"You should not have come here," the man said darkly. "Your friend has caused us great sorrow, and now you must die."
Zann's heart pounded as more nomads stepped into view. They didn't look friendly. "Whatever she did, we're sorry," he said. He assumed they were talking about Wyssa.
"Silence!" an older nomad said.
"What could she have done that was so terrible, anyway?" Perda cried. "Magic barely works here."
Zann nodded. "And she only arrived an hour ago!"
"An hour?" The first nomad frowned. "Telling lies will not help you."
Another nomad stepped forward. "Your friend has been troubling us for days with his magic."
His magic? Zann was confused. "Wait," he said. "The only friends we have here are an old woman and a Red girl around our age. Who are you talking about?"
A nomad woman scowled. "Don't try to trick us," she snapped. "Your friend Morb tried that already."
Perda gasped. "Morb?"
"Morb definitely isn't our friend!" Zann cried.
Darb nodded. "We came here to stop him."
The nomads exchanged a skeptical look. "What would make a bunch of kids think they could stop Morb?" one asked.
"Because we've done it before," Perda retorted.
"That's right," Zann said. "We stopped him when he tried to take over Magica. And when he tried to destroy it after that."
A nomad stepped forward and peered carefully at Zann. Then she moved over to examine Perda and Darb too. Finally she nodded.
"They're right," she said. "These are three of the young heroes from First City. I recognize them now!"
"Untie them at once," the older nomad ordered the others.
Soon Zann and his friends were on their feet. Now Zann could see the hoof beasts they'd been riding. They were grazing on some plants a little farther down the trail.
Zann rubbed a spot on his wrist where the rope had bitten into his skin. He was tempted to magically heal it, but he decided that using magic right now probably wasn't a good idea.
"Please." The older nomad, who appeared to be the leader, gestured toward a cave nearby. "Come inside and rest."
Another nomad glanced around. "You shouldn't be out in the open where Morb might spot you," she said. "He is a dangerous man."
"We know," Perda said. "That's why we can't rest. Our friends are still out there!"
A nomad put a hand on her arm. "Perhaps we can send out a search party. Why don’t you tell us about them."
Zann and the others followed the man into a surprisingly spacious cave. One nomad lit some candles while others brought out some food and drink.
Zann and his friends told the nomads about Gliss and Wyssa. Half a dozen nomads stood up. They promised not to rest until they’d found the pair.
"How will they find them?" Zann asked after the search party had left. "I thought it was hard to use magic here."
"It is," the nomad leader said. "But we have learned to compensate for our home's unpredictable and weak magic."
"What do you mean?" Darb asked.
A woman stepped forward. "We know how to read the wind and the sound waves," she said. "And how to communicate with the creatures of the desert, who see and hear even more than we can."
"Really?" Darb looked impressed. "Wow."

Zann was confused. He'd seen for himself that magic could be unpredictable here in the Far Frontier, just like it was near the Cave of the Unknown. But why had the nomad called it weak? If the Source was here, shouldn't magic be stronger than normal?
