He opened his mouth to ask the nomads about the Source, but Perda spoke before he could.
"You said Morb was causing your tribe lots of trouble," she said. "What did he do?"
"He's been using magic carelessly," the leader said with a frown. "He has no concern for how the stray energy affects others."
Another nomad spoke up. "Yes, and he destroyed an ancient tree that was important to the history of a neighboring tribe."
"Don't forget the Seeing Stone," a woman said. She looked at the kids. "Morb appears to be building something on a plateau that we use for seeing long distances."
"What is he building?" Zann asked. He thought about the terrible magical contraptions Morb had built before.
"And why would he be building it way out here?" Darb added.
"Maybe he's trying to build a device that will help him find the Source," Perda said.
"Or to control it," Zann said.
"The Source?" a nomad said. "What do you mean?"
"The Source of all magic," Perda explained. "That's where the legends say all of Magica—"
"We know what the Source of all magic is," a woman interrupted with a chuckle. "But if it actually exists, I can assure you it's nowhere in the Far Frontier!"
Most of the other nomads were smiling or chuckling now too.
Zann frowned. "How can you be so sure?"
"There's no strong magic power here at all," the leader explained. "That's why this part of Magica was never heavily populated."

Another nomad nodded. "We can barely muster enough magic energy to stay fed and clothed," she said. "We must rely on our own feet, and those of the hoof beasts, for transportation. We can't even create trees for shade!"
"Trust us," the leader said. "We know better than anyone that there isn't a whole lot of magic nearby."
Zann was pretty sure that the nomads were telling the truth. But he felt more perplexed than ever.
"If Morb isn't looking for the Source, then what's he doing here?" he said.
Before anyone could respond, a breathless nomad burst in. "I came as fast as I could," he exclaimed. "We think we've found your friend!"
"Really?" Zann leaped to his feet. "Where?"
"Come, I'll show you!" The nomad was already rushing out again.
When Zann and his friends burst out of the cave, the nomad was whistling for the hoof beasts, which were still grazing nearby. Several of the beasts trotted over.
"Did you find both Gliss and Wyssa, or just one of them?" Perda asked as she climbed onto one of the hoof beasts.

"I'm not sure," the nomad messenger admitted. "My group of searchers was nearing an area where there are several deep caves. Ripples of magic energy were coming from that direction. We assumed it was coming from your friends. The others continued on while I returned to fetch you."
"Are you sure it wasn't Morb sending out the energy?" Zann asked.
The messenger grimaced. "Quite sure. We saw him atop the Seeing Stone when we passed. Luckily he didn't notice us."
Soon Zann, Perda, Darb, and several nomads were galloping across the desert. The messenger led them to some rocky hills. Two nomads were crouched by a large, dark hole in the side of a big hill.
One of them turned when she heard Zann and the others coming. Her face was ashen. "She's in trouble!" the nomad called. "Hurry!"
Zann jumped off his hoof beast and ran to the mouth of the cave. He gasped when he looked inside.
Just inside the cave was a deep, wide pit. Looking down, Zann saw Wyssa. She was standing on a huge boulder. All around her, filling every bit of the floor, were hundreds of cave hissers!
Zann felt his blood run cold. Cave hissers were among the most dangerous creatures in all of Magica. They lived underground, and their bite could immobilize even a large dragon.
"Oh, no!" Perda cried as she knelt beside Zann. "Can those hissers reach her?"
"Not quite," a nomad said grimly. "But she can't reach us either."
"Why can't she just levitate out?" Perda said. "Or magically immobilize the hissers so she can get by?"
Wyssa had heard them by now. She squinted up at Perda with a frown. "I tried both those things, but my magic isn't working," she snapped. "Do you have any other brilliant ideas, girl?"
"The lower half of this cave seems to be a natural vacuum," a nomad said.
Now Zann understood the problem. Magic didn't work in a vacuum.
Wyssa was still staring up at them. "If I had all of my potions and ingredients, I could blast these hissers into oblivion."

Zann nodded. Wyssa came from a world with little natural magic. Her people had learned to combine various ingredients to create magic energy. Once she'd even managed to open a wormhole in a world with no magic at all!
"Maybe we can find the ingredients you need," Zann said.
A nomad cleared her throat. "I don't think there will be time for that." She pointed.
The cave hissers were piling atop one another. "What are they doing?" Zann asked.
"They're forming a pyramid," Darb said. "I've heard that hissers will cooperate with one another to reach—" He gulped. "Food."
Zann gulped too. They didn't have time to look for magical ingredients. If they didn't figure out how to get Wyssa out of there soon, she would become the cave hissers' lunch!
He glanced around, desperate for ideas. His gaze fell on the hoof beasts standing nearby. A couple of them had the nomads' long lassoes looped around their necks.
"I know!" Zann exclaimed. "We can pull Wyssa out with your ropes! They're strong enough, right?"
A nomad nodded. "Strong enough, yes. But not long enough."
"That's okay." Zann grabbed a couple of the lassoes. "We'll tie them together."

Soon the lassoes formed one long rope. But when Zann tried to toss it to Wyssa, he couldn't get it to land anywhere near her. Wyssa was too far away from the cave mouth. A couple of the nomads tried too, but it was no use. The end of the rope kept falling onto the hissers. On one try, a hisser clung to the rope, and the nomad struggled to shake it off.
"This isn't working!" Perda cried. "We need a new plan."
Zann bit his lip. How could they get the end of the rope out to Wyssa? He studied the cave. A large stalactite hung down right above the pit.
"If I could get out there and hang on, I could lower the rope to Wyssa," he said, thinking aloud. "Then the rest of you could pull us both out."
"What?" Darb looked out at the stalactite. "How are you going to get there?"
Zann shrugged. "I think I can jump that far."
Perda looked alarmed. "What if you miss?"
Zann tied the rope around his waist. "I'll keep the rope short enough so that if I do miss, I can't fall all the way down."
"It seems dangerous," a nomad argued. "There must be another way."
Zann glanced down just in time to see Wyssa kick a cave hisser off the top of the boulder. Others were creeping toward her feet.
"There's no time," Zann said. "I'll be fine."
The others tied their end of the rope to a sturdy rock. Zann took a deep breath, trying to gauge the distance out to the stalactite. Could he do this?
He took a running start and leaped. He reached the stalactite. "I did it!" he cried. "I—" Suddenly he felt his grip slipping. He began to slide downward and clawed furiously at the slippery rock.
"Levitate!" he cried without thinking.
"Zann, no magic!" Perda yelled.
It was too late. Zann's magic energy bounced against the vacuum below.
Bam!
A strong shock wave of magic energy knocked Zann upward. He felt himself bump against the stalactite and slam against the cave's ceiling. "Ow!" He grunted.

He twisted around and hugged the stalactite. His hand found a deep crack to hold onto, and he settled his feet on a small bump near the bottom of the stalactite. Feeling secure, he sighed with relief. Then he untied the rope.
"Careful, boy!" Wyssa called up to him.
Zann lowered the rope to Wyssa.
She grabbed it, gave it a tug, and yelled, "I'm ready!"

The nomads yanked the rope, and Wyssa was lifted off the boulder. She swung over the cave hissers, kicking furiously as claws snapped at her feet. Up and up she went until she reached the top. Two nomads pulled her to safety.
Next a nomad threw the rope back to Zann. He caught it with one hand while still gripping the stalactite with the other.
Zann breathed deeply. He let go of the stalactite and quickly grasped the rope with both hands. Immediately he swung downward. He used his feet to brace himself as he slammed into the wall.
"Oof!" he cried. Soon he felt himself being raised up and out of the pit.
"Wow!" Perda exclaimed as a nomad helped Zann onto the ledge. "I can't believe that worked."
"Your bravery is inspiring, young man," the nomad said.
"Yes, well . . ." Wyssa brushed off her clothes and shot Zann a grumpy look. "I suppose you did save my hide, boy. It's about time you repaid me for all the times I've saved yours."
"You're welcome." Zann grinned. But then his grin faded. "What happened to Gliss?"
Wyssa glanced around. "I assumed she was with you."
"The others are still searching," a nomad said. "We should join them."
"I can help." Wyssa pulled a handful of purple berries from her pocket.
"Are those oogberries?" Zann asked.
Wyssa didn't answer. She crushed the berries and then rubbed them onto her fingers. "This way," she said, exiting the cave.
"What are you doing?" one of the nomads asked. "Is that magic from another world?"
"Yes. It senses magical sources." Wyssa headed toward one of the hoof beasts. "Someone help me mount this creature, and I'll lead the way."
Soon they were all riding across the desert. Wyssa was in the lead, occasionally changing direction slightly.
"Are you sure you're following the right energy?" a nomad asked. He sounded nervous.
When Zann looked around, all the nomads looked rather grim.
"What's the matter?" Perda asked.
The nomads exchanged a look. "We're heading toward the Seeing Stone," one said. "That's where Morb was last seen."
Zann looked at Wyssa. "Do you think your spell is leading us toward Morb instead of Gliss?"
"It's possible," Wyssa said. "But we need to be sure. Unless you wish to abandon your friend out of fear?"
"Of course not," Zann said.
One nomad soon called for a halt. "We're definitely nearing the Seeing Stone," he whispered. "We should proceed with caution."
Everyone dismounted the hoof beasts and tiptoed past some outcropping.
Zann spotted the Seeing Stone immediately. It was a huge stone plateau with gently slopping sides and a flat, wide top. No wonder the nomads used it to view long distances.
But he wasn't really thinking about that. He was focused on the ugly contraption standing in the middle.
"Look!" Perda whispered. "It's one of Morb's contraptions!"

Zann nodded. The contraption was an awkward jumble of bones, stones, and other things Zann couldn't recognize from this distance. It was smaller than some of the villain's previous contraptions, but it looked just as evil.
"I don't see the girl," Wyssa murmured. "The spell locked onto the magic energy coming from Morb's contraption."
"So how will we find Gliss?" Darb said.
"We'll have to move away from here and try again," Perda said. "Maybe once we're away from that thing—"
"We're not going anywhere yet," Wyssa said. "We must destroy it before Morb returns to finish it."
"How can you tell it's not finished yet?" Zann glanced at the contraption again. "Is it because it's smaller than the other ones?"
"That, and other reasons." Wyssa stepped forward. "Come with me. We're going to need a lot of friction."
"But what about Gliss?" Darb said.
"We'll continue looking for Gliss soon," Wyssa said. "First we must stop Morb."
"But—," Perda began. Wyssa was already walking away.
Zann and his friends traded a glance. "I don't think we have a choice right now," Zann said.
They all hurried after Wyssa. Zann, Perda, and the nomads rubbed their hands together to create magic friction. Finally Zann felt their energy sparking and buzzing around them.
Meanwhile Wyssa had climbed atop the plateau. "Send it to me!" she called, rubbing her hands together.
They sent all the energy up toward her. She held out her arms, and when the energy reached her, it burst into an enormous fireball.
"Wow," Perda said.
Wyssa lifted the fireball and turned toward the contraption. Zann held his breath.
But then the old woman glanced down. Giant beetles were swarming toward her.
"Darb, what are those things?" Zann asked.
"I don't recognize them," Darb said. "They don't look very aggressive though."
The beetles marched in tidy lines, clicking their antennae in time to their steps.
Zann glanced at Wyssa, who was still gaping at the beetles. The fireball was beginning to fizzle out.

"Quick!" Zann cried. "We have to send more energy up to Wyssa!" He and the others furiously rubbed their hands together again. But before they could get enough energy sparking, the fireball had disappeared.
A second later Wyssa snapped her fingers and zapped out of sight.
Zann looked at the nomads, who seemed just as perplexed as the kids were. "What kind of insects are those?" he asked the nomads. "Are they dangerous?"
"I've never seen such creatures before," one nomad responded. "They aren't native to the Far Frontier."
"Hey!" Darb pointed. "They all just disappeared!"
"That's weird." Zann felt uneasy. "What if those beetles are some kind of strange off-world creatures that Morb is using to guard his contraption? They might be more dangerous than they look."
"Dangerous enough to scare off Wyssa?" Perda sounded skeptical. "She's not even scared of a scatter beast!"
"Let's climb up there and see what happens," Darb said. "Maybe we can break the contraption apart without magic."
"We'll stand guard and alert you if Morb is approaching," one of the nomads said.

"Okay." Zann could tell that the nomads wanted to stay far away from that contraption. He didn't blame them. Morb was awfully scary, and so were his contraptions. But Zann knew that this could be their best chance to stop the evil villain's plans.
Zann, Perda, and Darb climbed up to the top of the plateau. Zann walked toward the contraption. But after just a few steps, he found his path blocked by an invisible wall of energy.
"There's a Shield spell here," he said.
Perda nodded. "We should have known that Morb wouldn't leave his contraption unguarded."
Darb glanced around. "There's no sign of those beetles. Why would he need them if he has a Shield spell?"
Perda shrugged and poked at the invisible shield. "Should we try to break through this?"
"How?" Zann said. "Our magic barely works here. Besides, I'm sure Morb used a strong spell."
"I bet that fireball would have broken through." Perda frowned. "I wonder what made Wyssa zap off like that."
"Who knows?" Darb started walking toward the edge of the plateau. "But come on, we should get out of here before Morb comes back."
Zann had to agree with that. They climbed back down and told the nomads about the Shield spell.
"Is your friend coming back?" one of the nomads asked.
"You mean Wyssa?" Zann shook his head. "I don't know. Maybe we should try to contact her. Are there message moths out here?"
"No," a nomad replied. "But we can send her a message."
"How?" Darb asked.
"A sound message," another nomad said. "We send sound waves through the air and the ground to form thoughts and feelings."

Zann wasn't sure that Wyssa would understand that kind of message. But he didn't have any better ideas, so he stood back and watched while the nomads sent their message. They stomped their feet and danced in a circle, waving their arms and rubbing their hands together to form spurts of magic energy. Even the hoof beasts stopped grazing and watched the nomads with interest.
"That magic is cool," Darb whispered. "I can feel it!"
Zann could feel the nomads' magic message too. The nomads were saying, "Where are you? We wish you were here with us."
"I hope Wyssa feels it and comes back soon," Perda said after the nomads finished sending the message. "We need her help to find Gliss."
"Maybe we should split up and keep searching for both of them," Darb suggested. "We could cover more ground that way."
"No, you might get lost," a nomad said. "In any case, people from our tribe are still searching for your friend Gliss. They will send a message when they find her."

The hoof beasts had gone back to grazing after the message had been sent. But suddenly one of them let out a sharp whistle. The other hoof beasts abruptly raised their heads. Their ears swiveled around, and their nostrils flared. Then they all took off at a gallop.
"Hey! Where are they going?" a nomad exclaimed.
Another nomad whistled sharply. But the hoof beasts ignored the sound. They soon disappeared over the horizon.
"That was strange." One nomad frowned. "What frightened them?"
"Look!" Darb pointed. "Here comes Wyssa!"
"Oh, good!" Zann said.
"Maybe she startled the hoof beasts," Perda said.
Zann opened his mouth to respond. Instead he gasped as a Red Share struck him so strongly that he staggered and almost fell. It was from Gliss, and she was still terrified!
The others didn't notice his reaction. They were hurrying to meet Wyssa. Zann staggered after them, his head throbbing with the Share.
"Why did you zap off like that?" Perda asked Wyssa. "You were about to destroy Morb's contraption!"
"Was it the insects?" Darb asked. "They looked harmless, but maybe—"
"They are harmless," Wyssa said with a short laugh. "I apologize for being such a coward earlier. After all, what kind of fool is afraid of a few silly blank bugs? I must have been losing my mind!"
"Blank bugs?" Darb said with interest.
The Share was still distracting Zann, but he also couldn't help noticing that Wyssa was acting oddly. She wasn't the type of person to apologize for anything or to call herself a coward.
"Are you okay?" he asked, doing his best to ignore Gliss' terror for the moment.
"Good question," Wyssa said with a smirk. "Actually, I'm better than ever. Much better."
Perda blinked. "What do you mean?"
Wyssa let out a wild cackle. Suddenly there was an evil glimmer in her eye. "I thought you children were supposed to be clever! And yet you're always so easy to trick!"
Before Zann could figure out what that meant, Wyssa snapped her fingers. Her face and body shimmered and started to change.
A shiver ran down Zann's spine as a new face took shape. Zann gasped. "Morb!"
"Let's get out of here!" Zann shouted to his friends.
He ran, with Darb and Perda on his heels. Out of the corner of his eye, he noticed the nomads disappearing into some scrubby brush in the other direction.
"Stop!" Morb snarled. "I wish to speak with you." There was a flash of magic energy.
"Oof!" Zann grunted as he crashed into a glowing green wall. He and his friends spun around.
Morb stalked toward them with a sneer. "Aren't you happy to see me?" he asked. "How about your friend?"
Morb stepped aside, revealing someone who had been hidden behind him.
"Gliss!" Darb cried.
Gliss looked terrible. Her face was streaked with tears, and her hair was messy and tangled with twigs and leaves.
"What did you do to her?" Perda cried, rushing toward Gliss.
Morb snapped his fingers. The sand between Perda and Gliss turned into molten lava. Perda barely stopped in time to keep from getting burned.
Zann's heart raced. How did Morb have this much power, especially in the Far Frontier?
"Your little friend is just fine—for now." Morb smirked. "I was sick of hearing her cry, so I used an Immobilization spell on her."
Zann wished that Wyssa would return. She was the only one who might be strong enough to fight Morb.

"But don't worry." Morb was still talking. "I've kept your friend healthy and strong. I want her magic energy at full force when I feed her to my new contraption. And then you kids are next!" He glanced toward Darb. "Well, maybe I'll spare the Void. After all, he's got no magic to contribute."
Zann gulped. This was bad! He'd seen what happened when Morb "fed" people and creatures to his contraptions. They all ended up drained of magic. And often dead!
Zann's only hope was for Wyssa to show up. Maybe if he kept Morb talking, he could buy some time.
"So what is this new contraption supposed to do, anyway?" Zann asked. "I mean, if our magic is going to power it, we deserve to know, right?"
Morb chuckled. "That's my little secret. All of Magica will find out its purpose soon enough."
Perda seemed to catch on to what Zann was doing. "But why build it way out here in the Far Frontier?" she asked.
"To avoid prying eyes, of course." Morb smirked again. "But don't worry. My associate in First City is already preparing for its arrival."
An associate? Zann exchanged a surprised look with his friends. Who was Morb talking about?
"It seems right that you kids will be the ones to provide the power to transport my contraption to First City," Morb continued. "After all, you were the ones who delayed my plans so greatly."
"We delayed your plans?" Perda exclaimed. "What are you talking about?"
Morb pointed a bony finger at her. "By taking so long to rescue me from Skellia! I thought you were cleverer than that. Clearly I overestimated you."

That gave Zann another idea to keep him talking. "How did you survive in that world anyway?" he asked. "And how were you able to send me those messages? Your brother said he left you with only a weak pair of infused gloves."
"Unless he was lying," Perda muttered. "Maybe Maff is Morb's associate."
Zann's eyes widened, and he wondered uneasily if Perda was right. Could Maff have been working with his brother all along?

"Ah, my brother ." Morb spat out the word as if it tasted bad. "Yes, he tried to hold me back, just as my entire family has done all my life. But I was too smart for him. My travels have taught me more about magic than you silly Reds will ever know."
"What do you mean?" Darb asked.
"Didn't your friend Wyssa tell you?" Morb cackled. "She was the one who taught me the spells and secrets of her home world—the ones that even a Void can master."
"What?" Perda blurted out. "Wyssa taught you how to do magic?"

"At first." Morb shrugged. "Of course, I soon surpassed her basic lessons and continued learning on my own." He chuckled. "Although I made a few mistakes while I was learning to control my new power. That's why Wyssa can never return to her home world."

Zann's head was spinning with everything that Morb had just said. He already knew that Wyssa used to work for Morb, procuring off-world objects and creatures for him. But he didn't know she was the one who'd given Morb his first taste of magical power!
"Speaking of Wyssa," Morb said, interrupting Zann's thoughts, "I hope you're not keeping me talking in the hope that she'll come back to rescue you."
"W-what do you mean?" Perda asked.
"She's of no use to me anymore." Morb shrugged again. "So I put her out of her misery."
Zann gasped. Was Morb saying that Wyssa was dead?
Morb crooked a finger toward Gliss. She jerked toward him, like a rag doll being pulled by a string. Morb dragged her up the side of the plateau.
"Stay there," he ordered Zann and the others. "I'll be back for you."

When he reached the invisible shield, he snapped his fingers and stepped through the spot where it had been. Zann guessed that meant he'd disabled the Shield spell. Morb snapped his fingers again. Gliss let out a gasp and collapsed to her knees.
"Morb released Gliss from the Immobilization spell." The color drained from Perda's face. "Morb is going to feed her to the contraption!"
"Go ahead, girl." Morb nodded toward Gliss. "If you have any last words to say to your friends, do it now."
Gliss' eyes filled with tears. "Please don't hurt my friends," she whimpered.
"I didn't tell you talk to me," Morb snarled. "Talk to them. Or would you rather get this over with quickly?"
Gliss looked at Darb, Zann, and Perda. Suddenly her eyes widened, and she stood straight up. "Yes, I want to say something."
"Fine. Hurry up," Morb said, turning away to fiddle with his contraption.

"I just want to say you've been the best friends ever," Gliss said loudly. "It's been fun going on adventures with you and stuff. Perda, you're the bravest person I know, and probably the smartest too. Although Zann is awfully smart too. He always seems to figure things out. And Darb, well, you probably know how special I think you are." Her voice softened for a moment. Then she cleared her throat and continued talking, describing all the adventures they'd had over the past few months.
Zann stared at her, astonished. What had come over her? Gliss never talked this much!
Even Morb seemed surprised. He turned away from the contraption to gaze at Gliss with his mouth hanging open.
"What's wrong with her?" Perda muttered in Zann's ear.

Before he could answer, he spotted sudden movement out of the corner of his eye. A rope flew out of the rocks at the base of the Seeing Stone. It looped over Gliss and yanked her off her feet and right over the edge of the plateau!
A nomad popped into view. "Catch her!" she shouted.
Several other nomads jumped out and broke Gliss' fall. They quickly untied her. Now Zann knew why Gliss had started babbling. She saw the nomads sneaking up on the group; she was distracting Morb!
Morb roared with fury.
"Give her back!" Morb shouted. He rubbed his hands together.
More nomads appeared behind him. They threw rocks and branches at the contraption, which was now unprotected by any kind of Shield spell.
Morb spun around. "No!" he cried. He conjured a new Shield spell. At the same time, the glowing green shield in front of Zann and his friends blinked off.
A couple of nomads helped Gliss up onto a hoof beast. More hoof beasts appeared, wild-eyed and terrified. But they stopped long enough for Zann and the others to fling themselves onto their backs.
"Stop!" Morb cried.
Zann bent low over his animal's neck as he felt magic energy zinging around him. The entire group was already galloping off in a cloud of dust.
Zann watched several nomads pack tools and clothing into a sack. "Thank you again for all your help," he said. "I hope the rest of the search party returns soon."
"We hope so too." A nomad shot a worried look toward the mouth of the cave.
The kids and their rescuers had been hiding in a cave since escaping from Morb about an hour earlier. Most of the other nomads had now returned. Only a few were still missing.
"Are you really moving on so soon?" Darb asked.
The nomads all nodded. "It's what we do," one said.
"Besides," another added, "we want to get as deep into the Far Frontier as we can before . . ." Her voice trailed off, and she exchanged a look with some other nomads.
"You want to stay far from whatever is going to happen," Zann finished for her. "We understand."
A nomad stepped over and put a hand on his shoulder. "You could come with us," he said. "Trust me, we know how to remain hidden."
Zann glanced at his friends. Gliss was huddled beside Darb, still looking relieved to be free.
"We can't," she said, her voice shaking a little. "We have to try to stop Morb."
"Yes," Zann said, while Perda and Darb nodded. "I don't know what sort of horror Morb is planning for Magica. But we have to get back to First City and warn everyone."
"Right," Perda said. "But how will we get back without Wyssa?"
"What?" a voice rang out from the cave entrance. "You're planning to leave me behind? Ungrateful brats!"
"Wyssa!" Perda cried as the old woman strode in.
"Wait," Zann said, his eyes narrowing. "Is it really Wyssa this time? What if . . .?"
He didn't bother to go on, but now everyone looked suspicious.
"Morb told us you were dead," Darb said.

Wyssa rolled her eyes. "It would take more than a sand beast to take me out," she snapped. "Obviously Morb didn't do his research. Everyone knows sand beasts can be tamed if you tickle them in just the right spot on the lips."
Zann felt uncertain. This person certainly sounded like Wyssa. But Morb had already tricked them twice.
Just then several nomads burst in. The others greeted them with relief.
"Now we are all here!" one cried. "We can depart."
One of the newcomers nodded. "We found your friend," he told the kids, gesturing toward Wyssa. "Although I imagine she would have found you on her own."
"Yes," another newcomer said with a laugh. "Anyone who can tame a sand beast can surely do anything!"
That made Zann relax a little. Perda elbowed him. "Look at her ring," she whispered. "That's the ring that Wyssa always wears!"
Perda was right. The glowing stone peeked out from Wyssa's gnarled hand.
Zann grinned, feeling reassured. "It must be the real Wyssa."
"Thanks for everything," Wyssa told the nomads. She pulled some dragon scales out of one pocket and her small contraption out of another. "We have to go."
She sprinkled the scales over the contraption. Suddenly Zann and his friends were hurtling back toward First City.
Zann crashed hard into the ground. "Ow!" he yelped. He opened his eyes and rubbed his knee, which had slammed into a rock. He, his friends, and Wyssa were in a forest clearing.
"Where are we?" Perda asked.
"I think we're near Wormwood," Darb said. He glanced toward Wyssa.
The old woman snapped her fingers and zapped out of sight.
"Hey!" Gliss cried.
"Where did she go?" Zann asked.
"Maybe she'll come back," Perda said.
They waited for a few minutes to see if Wyssa would return. After several minutes passed by, they decided to give up, and walked the short distance into town.

When they got there, they saw election ads everywhere. Magical posters floated above almost every street corner. Words and images flashed on and off. Automatons marched around, squawking out names and slogans.
"Vote Venna!"
"Laddno for king!"
Zann glanced up and saw Laddno's name written in the sky in glowing letters.
"This is crazy," he commented.
"It sure is." Gliss gasped and pointed at another ad. "Look—the election is tomorrow!"
"Tomorrow?" Zann said. "We must have lost even more time traveling back and forth to the Far Frontier than we realized."
"We'd better get to Teplo's house and see what's going on," Perda said. "I hope Fala is still free. She could help us get word to Venna about Morb."
Zann nodded. "I hope so. Maybe it's good that the election is tomorrow. As soon as it's over, Venna can focus on stopping Morb's evil plans."
"Whatever those plans are," Darb added. "We still don't know what his new contraption is supposed to do."
Gliss shivered. "I'm sure it's something bad. Come on, let's zap."
They zapped to Teplo's neighborhood. Shouts rang out from a park nearby.
"There's another Void Rights rally going on," Gliss said.
"Is Laddno there?" Perda asked. "Maybe we should try to warn him about Morb. He should be able to get word to Venna and the others at the palace."
They stepped closer. Gliss levitated to get a better look over the crowd. "I don't see Laddno," she reported. "Hey, I think that's Jev's father speaking now!"
"Is Jev there too?" Darb asked.
"Uh-huh." Gliss quickly lowered herself to the ground. "We should leave before Jev sees us."

"Wait." Zann had just spotted his friend Mari standing near the back of the crowd. He sent his voice toward her with a Sound-shifting spell. "It's Zann. Meet me behind the crooked tree on the corner."
"Why do you want her to come meet us?" Perda asked as Zann led the way to the spot he'd mentioned.

"She can probably tell us about anything important that happened while we were away," Zann said. "What if the prisoners got released or something? Now that we're back, we should find out what to expect."
Moments later Mari arrived. She looked happy to see everyone. "I was wondering what happened to you guys," she said. "I haven't seen you in days."
"We, uh, were out of town," Zann said.
"Out of town?" Mari sounded surprised.
"Yeah." Perda shot a warning look at the others. "Um, we just wanted to stay out of sight for a while. We were afraid Zann might get locked up because his parents are under suspicion."

Zann was a little surprised that Perda didn't want to tell Mari why they'd really left town. Maybe she thought it would take too long to explain. After all, they might not have much time to stop Morb. His contraption had appeared to be almost finished. And it probably wouldn't take Morb long to repair any damage the nomads had done to it.

"Oh, right, that makes sense," Mari said, shooting Zann a sympathetic smile. "I don't blame you for hiding out in Swamp Bottom for a while. Anyway, you've missed a lot. People are really going crazy over this election."
"We saw all the ads and automatons," Gliss said. "I've never seen so many!"

Mari nodded. "Like I said, people are going crazy these days. I just hope I can continue keeping the remaining relics safe until the election is over tomorrow," she said. "Venna helped me put a Security spell on your parents' lab, just in case."
"Good," Perda said with a laugh. "Now you can say the future queen helped you create a spell."
"Maybe." Mari shrugged. "Actually, most people think Laddno is going to win."
"Laddno?" Zann said. "I can't believe—"
"Hey!" a new voice interrupted.
It was the young man from Wormwood—the one who'd loaned Darb the boat. He hurried toward them, looking annoyed.
"Where's my boat?" the young man demanded. "You were supposed to bring it back!"
"Uh-oh," Zann muttered. They definitely didn't have time to try to explain that they'd left the boat behind in another world. "Let's get out of here. Zap!"
Splash!
"Ugh!" Perda cried. "Zann, why do you always zap us into water?"

"Never mind." Gliss stepped out of the shallows of the river where they'd landed. She snapped her fingers to dry her clothes. "Look, we're near the palace. Let's see if we can sneak in and see our families."
"Good idea," Zann said. "I want to make sure my parents and Boz are okay."
Zann and Gliss conjured large hats to hide their red hair. Then all four kids crept around the corner until they could see into the palace square.
"Zann, are you sure this is a good idea?" Darb whispered.
"Everyone is distracted by the election right now," Zann whispered back. "This might be our best chance to . . ."
His voice trailed off, and he gasped. Several trolls had just stepped out of the palace!
"Trolls!" Perda hissed in Zann's ear.
The four friends hid behind a hedge.
"I haven't seen a troll in First City since Morb was defeated!" Zann whispered.
Darb peeked through the hedge. "Laddno just came outside."
Zann watched in shock as Laddno talked to the trolls. Zann was too far to hear what the man was saying. But he could hear the trolls' loud grunts in response.
"Forget about trying to see your families," Perda murmured. "It's not safe here."
They returned to Teplo's house. Zing was flapping around, shooting flames everywhere.
"Why is he so excited?" Perda asked.
"He's probably just happy to see us," Zann said.
"I hope Fala didn't get captured," Darb said. "What if Zing was trapped here while we were gone?"
Teplo's pet sniffer goose waddled into sight, honking with displeasure.
"Zing's food looks fresh," Perda said. "That must mean Fala has been here recently."
"Good." Zann summoned a message moth. "I'll let her know we're back."
Moments later Fala zapped into view. "You've returned!" she cried. "I was starting to worry about you."
"How's my uncle?" Gliss asked. "And Zann's family?"
"They're fine." Fala handed Gliss the Remote Eye so Gliss could see for herself. "Now tell me about your trip. Did you find Morb?"
Gliss peered through the Eye and then handed it to Zann. He looked through it and saw his parents, Boz, and the others sitting in their cells. They looked okay.
"We found Morb," Perda said. "We have a lot to tell you."
The kids described their trip to the Far Frontier. The more they talked, the more worried Fala looked.
"Oh, dear," she said. "So it's true—Morb really is up to no good."
"As usual," Perda said grimly. "But that's not all. We were just at the palace, and we saw a bunch of trolls in the square!"
"Yes." Fala nodded. "Laddno brought them to the palace a couple of days ago. He's using them as bodyguards."
"Why?" Gliss asked.
Fala shrugged. "He claims he needs them because his life has been threatened."
"Who threatened him?" Zann asked.
"He won't give any details," Fala said. "He also won't explain how he's controlling the trolls."
Zann traded a look with his friends.
"What if Morb is the one who's threatening Laddno?" Perda said.
Zann had been thinking the same thing. "Laddno might remember that Morb used trolls once," he said. "Maybe Laddno thinks he can use them to stop Morb."
A message moth fluttered into the room. It was from Mari.
"She wants to know why we disappeared so suddenly earlier," Zann told his friends. He started to write a response, but Fala stopped him.
"It's better to keep your movements quiet," Fala said. "At least until after the election."
"Okay." Zann stared at the moth. Thinking about Mari gave him an idea. "Let's go to my parents' lab. Maybe we can get some ideas there about ways to stop Morb."
"Good idea," Perda agreed. "Don't tell Mari we're going, though. As Fala said, we should keep our movements quiet."
"We have to tell Mari," Zann insisted. "She told us there's a spell on the lab. We won't be able to get past it without her."
"What spell?" Fala sounded surprised.
They told her what Mari had revealed about the Security spell.
"She said Venna helped her with it," Gliss said.
"Venna didn't mention anything about that to me," Fala said. She looked at Zann. "But go ahead and contact her."
Zann quickly inscribed the moth. "Okay," he said. "Let's go."
"Are you coming, Fala?" Perda asked.
"I'll meet up with you later," she replied. "I want to check on Venna again. She's received some threats too. But she refuses to go into hiding."
Zann whistled for Zing. Then he and his friends zapped to the street outside the lab. To his surprise, Mari was already waiting for them.
"You got here fast," Zann said.
Mari smiled. "I was on my way here to check on the relics when I got your moth."
"What kind of Security spell did you put on this place?" Perda asked.

"A special kind of Shield spell." Mari rubbed her hands together. "It's pretty cool." She explained how the spell worked, though Zann didn't pay much attention. He just wanted to get inside the lab and figure out how to stop Morb.
But once inside, Zann wasn't sure where to start. Mari wandered into the back to check on the relics.
Zann looked at his friends. "Let's just look around for anything that might be useful," he whispered. He wanted to trust Mari, but he remembered Fala's warning.

Perda was already opening record books. "This one's about the Mask of Zanta," she said. "The relic is gone, but your parents wrote a lot about it." She scanned the page. "Mostly about its immense power and its connection to the very early days of Magica history."
Zann bent closer to see. Something in his pocket poked him. He reached in and pulled out the twigs he'd collected on Atmo.
Mari came back into the room. "What are those?"
"I found them in another world," Zann said. "They're supposed to contain lots of magic energy."
"From another world?" Mari stepped closer. "Cool. I bet my uncle would love to see those!"
"Why would your uncle want to see them?" Gliss asked.
Suddenly Mari looked uncomfortable. "He's a, um, researcher."
Zann was confused. If Mari's uncle was a researcher, why had she been so eager to work for his parents?
He opened his mouth to ask. But at that moment, the entrance to the lab flew open and several trolls burst in!

At the sight of the trolls, Zann grabbed Zing and zapped away. He landed near Wormwood, which reminded him of Wyssa. They needed to find her; she might be the only person who was powerful enough to stop Morb.
There was a flash as Perda, Darb, and Gliss zapped into view.
"Good!" Zann said. "I didn't know if you guys would get out of there." He looked around. "Where's Mari?"
Perda shook her head. "She zapped out on her own. I barely had time to grab Darb and Gliss before zapping out of the lab."
"How'd you find me so fast?" Zann asked.
Perda grinned. "I learned a new spell."
"Is it some sort of Tracking spell?" Zann was intrigued.
"It's called a Uniting spell," Perda said. "I read about it in a book about magic from other worlds. The spell can only be used to find someone who wants to be found."
"Can you use the spell to find Wyssa?" Zann asked.
Perda shrugged. "I can try."
She rubbed her hands against her forehead and closed her eyes. Then she muttered a few words that Zann couldn't hear.
Perda opened her eyes and looked around. "Sorry, it's not working."
"I guess Wyssa doesn't want to be found," Darb said.
Zann sighed. "We need to find her."
Gliss glanced around. "We're pretty close to Wormwood. Maybe someone there has seen her."
"Let's go," Zann said.
When they arrived at Wormwood, a familiar voice called out.
"Don't bother walking any farther!" It was Hap.
Zann stopped. "Why not?"
"You can't get in." Hap waved a hand toward the collection of huts. "Someone put a spell over the whole place. I can't even get in to check on my valuables!"
"Why would someone put a spell over Wormwood?" Perda asked.
"I don't know," Hap grumbled.
Zann took another step forward. He couldn't see any sort of shield.
Suddenly his leg became stuck. "Hey!" Zann cried. It felt as if he'd stepped into a wall of gooey glowberry pudding.
"What's wrong?" Perda rushed forward and then stopped. "Ack! I'm stuck too!"
"Pull us out!" Zann called to Gliss and Darb. "Don't come too close though."
"I warned you," Hap said once Zann and Perda were freed.
Zann rubbed his leg, which still felt sticky. "What a weird spell."
"I already sent a message moth to Laddno to alert him." Hap chuckled. "He'll be our king soon. He might as well get to work now, right?"
"Do you really think he'll win the election?" Zann asked.
Hap shrugged. "I don't know. But I hear he's going to bring in extra magic energy. Soon we'll all have enough magic to create our own palaces!"
"Is Laddno really telling people that?" Gliss asked. "I doubt it's true."
"Never mind." Zann tugged on her arm. "Let's go."
It was starting to get dark, so the kids returned to Teplo's place. Fala was waiting for them.
"Good news," she said. "Many people think Venna will win the vote easily tomorrow."
Gliss smiled. "Once Venna is queen, she's sure to release the prisoners."
"And then she can help us figure out what to do about Morb," Perda said.
"Right," Fala said. "Now let's all get some rest, and we'll deal with everything else tomorrow."
The next day the kids came out of the hatch and found a large, multicolored toad waiting for them.
"Vote! Vote!" it croaked loudly.
"We know," Zann said with a smile. He touched the toad on the head, and his fingers tingled. A second later the toad spit out a voting ballot with Zann's name on it.
Zann picked it up and magically inscribed "Venna" on it. Then he tossed it to the toad, which caught it on its long tongue and gulped it down.

One by one, Zann's friends and Fala cast their votes the same way. Vote toads had been in charge of elections ever since Zann could remember. Up and down the street, he could see other people voting through other toads. Once every vote in Magica had been swallowed, the toads would gather in the palace square to present the results.
"What should we do for the rest of the day?" Gliss said as the toad hopped off in search of more voters.
Perda shrugged. "Let's look for Wyssa again."
They spent the next few hours wandering around the city. Vote toads were everywhere, and so were voters. Everyone seemed excited that the election was here at last.
Eventually the kids wandered past the palace square. There were no trolls in sight at the moment. Only one vote toad was there, accepting votes from several palace workers.
Then the door opened and Laddno hurried out, flanked by a pair of trolls. "I'd like to vote, please!" he announced loudly, pushing past a woman who was about to touch the toad.

The toad croaked, casting a wary eye toward the trolls. Laddno patted the toad on the head. He wrote on his ballot in large, glowing letters. Then he tossed it back to the toad, which gulped it quickly.
"Thank you!" Laddno glanced around at the palace workers as if he expected applause. When nobody said anything, he frowned and went back into the palace. The trolls remained in the square.
"Let's get out of here," Zann whispered. "We haven't found Wyssa, so let's go to Venna's campaign headquarters to hear the election results."

Later they waited with Fala, Venna, Maff, and various other adults. Finally a glowing image of a vote toad appeared in the sky. The toad's tongue flicked out, inscribing a number beside a picture of Venna and another number beside a picture of Laddno.
A gasp went up from the crowd. Laddno had won!
Shock rippled through Zann. "I can't believe Laddno won."
"Those numbers can't be right!" a man shouted.
"I demand a recount!" a woman cried.
Venna zapped away, along with Maff and a few others.
"Do you think Laddno cheated?" Perda asked.
Fala shook her head. "Nobody can tamper with a vote toad. At least I don't think anyone can." She zapped off without another word.
Gliss frowned. "Now that Laddno is king, will he release the prisoners soon?"
"I'm sure he will," Darb assured her. "There's no reason for him to keep them locked up."
"You're right." Zann felt restless. "But we need to tell someone about Morb. The longer we sit around here doing nothing, the more time he has to finish that contraption!"
"Let's go back to the lab and keep looking for ideas about what to do," Perda suggested.
They all agreed. But when they were standing outside the lab, Zann remembered the Shield spell that Mari and Venna had put up.
"How are we going to get in?" he said. "Should we try to find Mari?"
"There's no need to." Perda stepped forward. "I remember how she unlocked it."
Seconds later they were inside. Zann grinned at Perda, impressed again by how adept she was at learning magic.
"It's a good thing you guys are here," he said. "If it hadn't been for my birthday, you'd all be stuck in Swamp Bottom with no idea about Morb or missing relics or any of the rest of—"
He stopped talking and gasped as a strong wave of magic energy hit him. An invisible force was pulling on him.
"Hey!" Gliss grabbed a table for support. "What's happening? Is this part of the Shield spell?"
"I don't think so," Perda said. "Not unless Mari forgot to mention this part."

"It's pulling me toward the door!" Zann tried to hang onto a chair, but the magic was too strong. It pried his hands from the chair and dragged him outside. The magic herded Zann and his friends along the street.
Only Zing didn't seem to be affected by the spell. The dragon followed, whistling frantically, as Zann and his friends were dragged toward the center of the city.
Zann heard other people shouting; they too were being herded in the same direction.
"What kind of spell is this?" Gliss cried.

"I read about something like this in that book about off-world magic," Perda said. "I think it's a Compel spell. These spells were banned during the Days of Discipline, along with Flash Freezes and human search spells and the rest of the stuff that's illegal now."
"Could Morb be doing this?" Gliss said.
"I guess we'll find out," Darb said. "It's guiding us toward the palace."
Moments later the kids were in the palace square, which was crowded with people. Most of them looked angry or confused.
"This is outrageous!" a woman shouted.
"Why have we all been dragged here?" a man yelled.
Zann spotted Mari. He stepped toward her, relieved to find that the Compel spell had released him.
"Hey, Mari! Do you know what's happening?"
Mari turned to face Zann and his friends. She smiled. "You mean the weird spell? I don't know. But this is pretty exciting, huh?"

Zann was surprised that she looked so happy. Before he could ask why, there was a commotion at the front of the crowd. Suddenly a tall, gold-colored stage appeared. Laddno walked onto it with a big grin on his face. He was wearing a ceremonial robe.
"Welcome, citizens!" A Swelling spell allowed his voice to be heard over the noise of the crowd. "Thank you for coming!"
"We didn't have much choice, did we?" a man yelled.
"I'm honored to be your new king," Laddno said. His voice became louder as people booed. "Together we shall create a wonderful new future for Magica!"

As Laddno continued to talk, Zann didn't pay much attention. He was too busy wondering how they could get word to the new king about Morb's return. Maybe when Laddno let Zann's parents and Boz out, the adults could help to get Laddno's attention.
Suddenly Perda elbowed Zann. "Who's that?"
A figure had appeared beside Laddno. A dark cloak hid the person's face from view.
Laddno glanced at the figure. "Oh, right, I almost forgot," Laddno said. "The reason I called you here is to introduce you to my new associate, Brom. He will be, er, assisting me as I rule Magica."
"Associate?" Gliss sounded confused. "What does he mean?"
"And who's Brom?" Perda added. "I've never heard of him."
Zann shrugged. Curious, he leaned forward as the stranger threw back his hood.
Laddno smiled. "I'm sure everyone in Magica will enjoy getting to know my good friend Brom," he said. "You'll especially enjoy his vast and creative magical powers."
"No way!" a woman shouted. "I don't even believe you won the election. I demand a recount."
"Bring out the voting toads!" someone else yelled.
The square erupted in noise. A few people started chanting Venna's name. Others continued to yell at Laddno.
"Maybe we should get out of here," Gliss said. "Things are getting out of control."
Perda's eyes were still on the stranger. "There's something about that guy," she muttered. "He has a weird look in his eyes."
"Who? Laddno?" Zann asked.
"No, Brom." Perda sounded uneasy. "Something about him reminds me of Ello." She gulped. "Not the real Ello, but when—"
Just then Brom pushed forward, almost knocking Laddno off the stage.
"Hey!" Laddno protested.
"Enough of this charade," Brom said. He snapped his fingers, and suddenly his face changed.
"Oh, no!" Gliss cried. "It's Morb!"
Morb's gaze swept the crowd. The citizens were frightened and confused. Good. That would make things easy.
"Settle down, people!" Laddno cried. "Listen to me! I'm the king!"
Morb rolled his eyes. He was growing weary of that fool. Laddno had been useful, but Morb didn't need him anymore.
"Having trouble controlling your subjects, King Laddno?" Morb said mockingly. "Perhaps it's time to let your associate take over."
"Huh?" Laddno blinked at him.
Magic energy sparked from Morb's fingertips. "To me!"
The crowd gasped as the ceremonial robe flew off Laddno.
"How dare you do that!" Laddno cried.
Morb ignored him, magically settling the robe over his own head. Yes, that was better. Much, much better.
"We have to get out of here!" Zann whispered to his friends. "We can't let Morb see us!"
When he turned to push through the crowd, he saw Mari with her mouth open in shock. "No!" she whimpered. "He promised my uncle that they would rule together!"
"What did you say?" Perda asked.
"Laddno is your uncle?" Zann said in shock.

Mari's eyes filled with tears. "I didn't tell you before—I wasn't supposed to tell anyone." A tear trickled down her cheek. "I'm sorry I lied to you, Zann. Uncle Laddno didn't tell me that his secret partner was Morb. Otherwise I never would have . . ." Her voice trailed off.
"You never would have what?" Perda demanded.
Zann's eyes widened as he guessed what Mari had been about to say. "It was you, wasn't it? You stole the relics from the lab!"

"I'm sorry," Mari whimpered. "I thought I was helping my uncle, not Morb! That's why I couldn't come to your party. I was helping with Uncle Laddno's big rally." She glanced over her shoulder at the stage, where Laddno was cowering behind Morb. "I'd better go and try to help him now."
She rushed away. Zann took a step after her, but Darb stopped him with a hand on his arm. "Forget about her," he said. "We have bigger problems."
Perda nodded. "Let's go to Teplo's house and see if Fala’s there. Maybe she has some ideas for what to do next."
They zapped into the hatch. The sniffer goose greeted them with an irritated honk and a peck at Zann's leg. There was no sign of Fala.
Darb glanced at the animals' food dishes. "I think Fala forgot to feed the goose this morning," he said.
"I'll take care of it." Gliss snapped her fingers, and food appeared in one of the bowls.
Darb watched the goose eagerly snap up the food. "Maybe we should let her go. If things get bad and we can't make it back—"
"Don't say that!" Gliss said with a shiver.
But Perda nodded. "No, he's right. We shouldn't leave her trapped here—just in case."
As soon as the goose finished eating, Perda opened the hatch. Darb honked at the goose in her own language. She cocked her head and flew out.
Zann felt strange as he watched her go. Did Darb and Perda really think things were going to get that bad? Then again, with Morb in power, things weren't looking good.

They decided to zap to Venna's campaign headquarters to see if Fala and the others had returned. But when they arrived, the place was nearly deserted. Maff was one of the few people there. He hurried over when he spotted the kids.
"Good, you're safe," he said. "Fala sent me to look for you earlier. We have a plan."
"Great! What is it?" Zann asked.

"The only chance we have to stop my brother is for everyone to join their magic together to defeat him," Maff explained. "I was about to send an invitation for the entire city to join us again at the palace square to confront him. Maybe you kids can help me."
"Sure." Zann exchanged a worried look with his friends. "But do you think that will work? Morb seems really strong."
Maff sighed. "It's our only chance."

He held out his hands. The kids joined him to form a circle and rubbed their palms together. Zann could feel Maff's strong Red magic mingling with theirs. Even so, they were all exhausted by the time the Invitation spell was finished.
"Whew!" Maff wiped his brow. "All right, I think we reached everyone. Let's get back to the square."
When their group arrived outside the palace, the golden stage was gone, and Morb and Laddno were nowhere in sight. But the square was still crowded. The mood in the air felt dangerous and uncertain.
"Maybe this will work," Zann said to his friends. "Morb can't use his magic against all of us, right?"
Suddenly a murmur ran through the crowd. Zann turned to see that Morb had just appeared, standing atop an even taller stage than before.
"Welcome, dear citizens!" he cried in a mocking tone. Then he bowed. "I see my dear brother Maff has called you back to congratulate me."
"That's not why we're here, Morb!" Maff yelled. "You are not the true king!"
Morb snapped his fingers, and his brother suddenly froze in place. Gasps and shouts rang out from all around.
"Who's next?" Morb rubbed his hands together. "Oh wait, I know what you're looking for. What's a celebration without confetti?"
He snapped his fingers again, and confetti rained down over the square.
"Ow!" Perda cried. A piece had landed on her arm.
"It burns!" someone nearby yelled.
Zann ducked as a spark nearly ignited his hair. The confetti was bursting into flames!
People were running around screaming. "Let's get out of here!" Gliss cried.
Zann grabbed Darb with one hand and Zing's tail with the other. "Zap!"
Splash!
Zann, Darb, and Zing landed in a fountain across the street from Venna's campaign headquarters. Perda and Gliss appeared nearby a second later.
Immediately several trolls ran out of the headquarters.
"Run!" Zann cried.
The kids quickly outran the trolls and hid in some bushes.
"Should we go back to Teplo's house?" Gliss said, panting.
Darb nodded. "I don't think we should zap though. If there are more trolls out there, we don't want to accidentally zap into them."
"And with Morb back in town, I'm betting there are plenty of trolls wandering around," Perda said grimly.
"When we saw the trolls at the palace, we should have known that Laddno was plotting with Morb," Zann said.
"Really? I never would have guessed that," Gliss said. "It's crazy."
"Shh." Perda took a step out of the bushes to check for trolls. "Come on, let's go."

When the kids got to Teplo's house, trolls were patrolling the street. Next the kids tried to go to Zann's parents' lab. But they had to stop behind another building near the lab. More trolls were lurking in front of the lab.
"Now where should we go?" Gliss whispered.
"This can't be a coincidence," Perda said. "Morb probably sent those trolls out to look for us. Or for Zann, at least."
Zann gulped. Was that true? "We need a place to hide and figure out what to do," he said. "Follow me. I think I know a place."
He led the way down one street after another.
"Where are we going?" Darb asked.
"You'll see." Zann led his friends into a large park with a playground in the middle. "I used to play hide-and-seek here all the time when I was little. And I was always the last one to be found."
He glanced around to make sure no trolls were nearby. Then he ducked into a large playhouse shaped like a small version of the palace.
"No way, Zann!" Perda said. "If a troll looks in here, we'll be trapped!"
"No, we won't." Zann grinned and ran his hands over the back wall. Soon he found the secret door he remembered. Beyond was a small room with a few buckets and rakes.
"Wow." Gliss looked around. "I never would have guessed this was here!"
"Neither will the trolls." Zann closed the hidden door behind them. "We should be safe in here while we figure out what to do."
His smile faded as he realized he had no ideas. How were they going to stop Morb this time?
"We need to find Wyssa," Perda said. "She might be our only hope."
Darb nodded. "But how can we find her if she doesn't want to be found?"
Perda sighed. "Good question. I can try my Uniting spell again, but I doubt it will work any better."
"What if she already left Magica?" Gliss said.
Zann hadn't thought of that. "I don't think she'd leave," he said slowly. "She seems to feel responsible for helping Morb reach this level of power."
"True," Gliss said. "She seemed pretty determined to stop him too." She frowned. "At least when those weird beetles in the Far Frontier weren't around. We never did ask her what those were."
"Never mind that," Darb said. "If Wyssa is still in Magica, she's probably looking for that new contraption."
"Do you think Morb brought it to First City already?" Gliss wondered.
"Probably," Zann said. "I'll bet that's what's giving him so much power."
"If we find that contraption, we might also find Wyssa," Darb said.
"Or at least we could try to destroy the contraption ourselves," Perda said. "Okay, so where do we look for the contraption? The palace?"
"Maybe." Gliss shrugged. "I wish we had the Remote Eye with us."
"Or the guidelink," Perda added. "That might be able to guide us to a strong source of power like the contraption."
"Forget all that," Zann said. "How are we going to search without being caught by Morb's trolls?"
They were all silent for a moment, thinking. Darb was the first to speak.
"Why not the Directory?" he said.
"Huh?" Zann blinked at him. "The Directory?"
Darb nodded. "Morb is pretty busy right now with taking over Magica and everything. He might not think to block or alter his Directory entry."
Perda gasped. "The Directory automatically updates everyone's information!" she exclaimed. "It'll have Morb's current address!"
Zann grinned and clapped Darb on the shoulder. "I'm sure that's where Morb keeps his stuff, including that contraption!"
"It's worth a try!" Gliss snapped her fingers. The Directory appeared, glowing brightly in the dim little storage room.
"Morb," Zann said, and the Directory zeroed in on a particular entry. At the top was a picture of a sneering Morb, along with his name.
"Current occupation: Tyrant and usurper," Darb read as Zann scrolled down the page. "Current residence: the palace in First City. Previous residence: Number 11 Twisted Branch Avenue, Wormwood."
Perda gasped. "Of course! That explains the invisible shield over Wormwood. It must be there to protect Morb's contraption!"
"I wonder how he got it there from the Far Frontier," Darb said. "And why would he bring it to Wormwood instead of to the palace?"
Perda shrugged, not seeming too worried about that. "Maybe he brought it in through the wormhole or something, so it was easier just to leave it there," she said.
Gliss frowned. "But there are no wormholes in the Far Frontier."
"Never mind that," Perda said. "How are we going to get into Wormwood, past that weird, sticky Shield spell?"
Zann grinned. "You just answered your own question," he told her. "We can go in through the wormhole!"
"The wormhole is dangerous!" Gliss cried. "There must be another way into Wormwood."
"No, Zann is right," Perda said. "We can't waste time. Morb is already taking over Magica!"
"How will we reach a wormhole?" Darb asked. "There's one in the palace, but there's no way we can sneak in there."
"There's one in Edgewood," Perda said. "Wyssa brought us there once."
"Perfect," Zann said. "Let's zap there now."
A moment later they stood in front of the Edgewood wormhole.
"Are you sure this is a good idea?" Gliss asked. "We don't have the guidelink anymore. How are we going to navigate through the vortex?"
Perda frowned. "Good question. It could take a long time to find our way to the Wormwood wormhole."
"If we can find it at all," Darb said.
Zann shrugged. "Do you have a better plan? We're wasting time arguing about this."
"We'll waste even more time if we get lost in the vortex," Gliss said. "I think we should—Wyssa!"
The old woman had just zapped into sight nearby.
"There you are!" Wyssa exclaimed. Surprisingly, she seemed glad to see everyone.
"What are you doing here?" Zann asked. "Are you trying to escape through the wormhole?"
"No, I was looking for you, actually," Wyssa said. "I have something important to tell all of you—especially you." She jabbed a finger toward Zann.
"Okay, what is it?" he asked.
Wyssa opened her mouth to reply. But just then Gliss let out a scream. "Trolls!" she cried.
Zann spun around. Half a dozen trolls were charging toward them.
"Let's get out of here!" Wyssa shouted. She grabbed Zann with one hand and Darb with the other. Zann had just enough time to grab Zing's tail before the whole group dived into the wormhole.
They weren't in the vortex for long. Before Zann could catch his breath, Wyssa tugged them toward another wormhole. Seconds later they emerged in Wormwood.
"Whew!" Gliss exclaimed. "That was quick."
Zann looked around. "Uh-oh," he said. "More trolls are coming!"
Several trolls had been lounging in the shade of the Wormwood tree. Now they hurried toward Zann and the others.
Zing flew up and whistled his distinctive song. The trolls slowed down and craned their necks toward the little dragon.
"Hurry!" Perda whispered. "Let's hide while Zing distracts them."
She led the way into a large hut nearby. A moment later the trolls seemed to lose interest in Zing. They blinked, looked around, and then wandered off and disappeared into a different hut.
"They're so stupid that they forgot what they were doing," Zann whispered.
"Never mind that." Perda was peering out the door. "There's the contraption!"
Zann couldn't believe he hadn't noticed it right away. It was near the gnarled old tree, just to one side of the wormhole.
"It looks so evil!" Gliss whispered with a shiver.
Darb nodded. "It doesn't look much different than it did when we saw it in the Far Frontier."
"Yes." Wyssa sounded relieved. "It's still not finished. Otherwise we would be too late to stop Morb."
"How do you know it's not finished?" Perda asked.

"That's what I started to tell you." Wyssa glanced at Zann. "I'm pretty certain that Morb plans to place the Mask of Zanta in the empty space on top. That's the most powerful relic there is. If we don't stop him, the results will be—"
"Don't give away the surprise, Wyssa," a voice interrupted.
Zann spun around. "Morb!" he exclaimed.
The villain had just stepped out of the shadows at the back of the hut. Zann turned again, planning to run. But several trolls now blocked the hut's one opening.

"Don't even think about trying to zap away," Morb warned. "The spell I've placed over Wormwood won't allow that." He pointed a finger toward Zing, who was already whistling again. The little dragon dropped like a rock.
"Hey!" Darb cried. "Immobilization spells are illegal!"
"Haven't you caught on yet?" Morb sounded amused. "The old rules don't apply anymore. I'm in charge now, and that means that I make the rules!"
He reached into his robe and pulled out the Mask of Zanta.
Wyssa gasped. "You can't!"
"Silence, old woman." Morb held up the Mask, studying it. "It's beautiful, isn't it? Terrifying, but beautiful."
"It's beautiful," Wyssa snapped. "But it's wasted on that thing out there."
"My contraption?" Morb raised an eyebrow. "What do you mean?"
"I thought you would try to take over Magica again," Wyssa said. "But there's no way you can do that with a travel contraption."
"A travel contraption?" Perda echoed. "Is that what it is?"

Morb chuckled. "Yes, the crazy old woman is correct," he said. "But don't fret. I doubt anyone will be disappointed by what I have planned. Horrified, yes, but not disappointed. The only thing that contraption has to do is get me safely through the wormhole." He pointed one bony finger toward the tree. "And then pull the Wormwood tree in after me."
"No!" Wyssa blurted out.
Zann was confused by Wyssa's panic. Did it really matter if Morb took the Wormwood tree through the wormhole?
Morb laughed. "So you finally figured it out, hmm?" He taunted her. "It sure took you a long time, Wyssa."
"What is it?" Gliss asked. "What did you figure out?"
Wyssa looked grim. "That tree. It's the Source."
"Huh?" Zann said. "The source . . . You mean the Source of all magic?"
"The Source is real?" Perda said.
"Oh, yes, it's real." Morb sounded pleased with himself. "That tree pulls all of Magica's energy from the vortex."
"But that means . . ." Zann began slowly.
"It means," Wyssa said, "that removing it would leave Magica with no magic energy at all!"
Zann's head spun. Morb was going to steal all of Magica's magic energy!

Morb chuckled. "I can understand why you're all upset." He turned to face Darb. "Except for you, perhaps. Voids like you can rule Magica now. You'll never have to put up with being mistreated again." He scowled for a moment, his eyes angry and faraway. Then he glanced at Wyssa. "By the way, you can mark this off as another world that you've destroyed."
"Huh?" Zann said. "You can't blame her for what you're doing."
"Oh, but I can." Morb smirked. "She taught me everything she knew about magical contraptions."
Zann traded a confused look with his friends. What was Morb talking about?
"I thought magical contraptions were invented right here in Magica, during the Old Times," Perda said.
"Don't they teach you kids any real Magica history?" Morb rolled his eyes.
Zann turned to Wyssa. "What is he talking about?"
Wyssa looked pale. "It's true. During the Old Times, the vortex was much smaller. Many worlds had yet to develop, or to connect to the others."
"Yes," Morb said. "That made the vortex much easier to navigate."
"Indeed." Wyssa nodded. "Back then people from different worlds shared their ideas and techniques. Many of the relics from the Cave of the Unknown came from other worlds."
"Like the Horn of the Otherworld," Darb said. "It came from a beast from another world, right?"
"Yes," Wyssa said. "And many forms of magic originated in other worlds, including the contraptions that Morb has built."
"But the idiots who took over during the Days of Discipline banned those types of magic," Morb said. "They didn't want magic to be available to everyone. They wanted to control it."

"That's not why they banned those types of magic," Wyssa said. "It was because old King Zanta, the last king of the Old Times, was an evil tyrant. He used magical contraptions to control people. He caused all sorts of chaos in Magica."
"I've read about that," Darb said. "The people rose up against King Zanta. That's how the Days of Discipline began."
"There's something else." Wyssa focused on Zann. "You are a direct descendant of King Zanta himself."
Zann gasped. "Really?"
His friends looked stunned. Even Morb seemed surprised.
"Are you inventing lies to distract me, old woman?" he demanded.
"Not at all. That's why their names are similar," Wyssa said.
Zann shook his head slowly. "Mom said my name was an old family name." He gulped. "I never asked where it came from though."
"She probably doesn't know its full history," Wyssa said. "Most of that era has been long forgotten."
"Enough of this talk," Morb spat out. He touched his fingers together and sent a sizzling blast of energy toward Wyssa.
Gliss screamed and the others gasped. But Wyssa raised her hand and the blast bounced away, hitting a troll. As the troll raced off, wailing in pain, Wyssa smirked.
"Nice try, Morb," she said. "You'll have to work harder than that to . . ."
Her voice trailed off as the sudden clicking of antennae filled the air. Zann spun around. The hut was swarming with the same beetles he'd seen in the Far Frontier.
"No," Wyssa whispered, backing away. She tripped over a rough spot of ground and fell.
"Wyssa!" Perda cried as the beetles swarmed over the old woman.
"Get them off!" Zann yelled. He grabbed at one of the insects. But the beetle slipped away before he could get a grip.
"Use a Blast spell!" Perda rubbed her hands together to create friction. But suddenly her movements slowed.
Zann tried to rush over to Perda. But his body was moving in slow motion too!
"It's a spell." Gliss lifted a hand slowly and pointed at Morb.
Morb threw back his head and laughed. "Oh, why didn't I think to use a Sloth spell on you kids before? That would have saved me a lot of trouble!"
Zann slowly turned to look at Wyssa. She was completely covered in bugs.
"What are those things, anyway?" Darb asked.

Morb smiled. "Ah, it's nice to see a Void with some curiosity. Blank bugs are loosely related to dragons, though they have none of a dragon's cunning or individuality. They're mindless drones with little intelligence and even less free will. They only follow their basic instincts: move, eat, sleep." His smile widened. "And thanks to Wyssa, every person on her home world now lives as a blank bug."
"What?" Perda said.

Morb grinned. "I lived there for a time, remember? At first they welcomed me. But as I gained knowledge and power, they turned against me. So I tricked Wyssa into helping me build a contraption. She had no idea what my plan was. But I was able to use that contraption to alter the entire population. Now they are all blank bugs!"
Gliss looked horrified. "Now we know why Wyssa freaked out when she saw those things earlier."
Zann shivered, imagining what it would be like to live as a mindless blank bug, or to know that people he cared about had to live that way.
"Maybe that's why she's so cranky all the time," Darb murmured.
Morb waved a hand. "Enough chitchat. I have work to do." He strode out of the hut, throwing up a glowing green wall to block the entrance. As soon as he disappeared, Zann felt the Sloth spell lift.
"Whew!" Perda shook out her arms. "That spell felt weird. Now what are we going to do?" She glanced at the beetles crawling over Wyssa. The old woman wasn't moving.
"I don't know," Zann said. "But we have to stop him, or Magica will lose all of its magic!"
Zann and his friends tried blasting through Morb's Shield spell, but it was too powerful.
Perda peered through the translucent green wall. "Morb seems to be adjusting something on the contraption," she said. "We have to stop him before he puts the Mask on it."
"I know." Zann paced around the hut. "But how do we do that?"
Darb looked at Zann. "Wyssa said you're descended from King Zanta. Since the Mask got its power from him, maybe you have some sort of connection to it."
Perda gasped. "That would be just like Wyssa's ring!"
Darb nodded. "Wyssa said her ring had been in her family for generations. She used it to make her spells stronger. Maybe you could control the Mask, Zann."
Zann didn't like being related to such a terrible tyrant. But what if his friends were right? He had to try.
Zann stepped closer to the shield. Morb was now carrying the Mask to the contraption. Zann rubbed his hands together and focused on the Mask.
"Come to me," he murmured. The relic jumped in Morb's hand!
"What's going on?" Morb grumbled.
Zann focused all of his energy on the Mask. "Come to me."
This time the relic wiggled free of Morb's grip and flew halfway back toward the hut!
"Stop!" Morb roared. He sent a blast of magic after it. The Mask hung in midair for a second and then flew back to him.
Morb glared at Zann. "Give up, boy! My powers are much greater than yours." With a snap of his fingers, Morb shackled himself to the Mask.
Zann concentrated hard on the Mask.
"Wow!" Perda cried.
Morb's entire body slid backward toward the hut. "How are you—oh, never mind!" He rubbed his fingers together. Sparks flew.
Zann groaned as he felt Morb's magic fight back against his own. "I can't drag him anymore," Zann grunted. "His magic is too strong!"
A moan rose nearby. The pile of insects shifted slightly.
"Wyssa's still alive!" Perda exclaimed. She tried to shove some of the blank bugs away, but more kept swarming in.
Zing woke up from the Immobilization spell. He flew over, shooting flames at the blank bugs. But they hardly seemed to notice their own bodies smoking.

"Stop, Zing! You'll burn Wyssa." Darb glanced thoughtfully from the dragon to the blank bugs. "But I have an idea. Morb said these insects are related to dragons, right? Perda, can you try one of your fancy new spells to summon Teplo's sniffer goose?"
"Sure," Perda said. "Why?"
"That goose is a natural enemy of dragons," Darb said. "Maybe she'll recognize these bugs as dragons too!"
"Do it quickly!" Zann cried. A magic blast hit him, knocking him down. He sat up and saw Morb bent over, breathing heavily. "I've tired him out," Zann thought.
Perda rubbed her hands together and murmured under her breath.
Suddenly the sniffer goose burst in through an opening in the hut. When she saw the bugs, she honked and flapped toward them. The blank bugs clicked with alarm and scurried out of the hut.
Slowly Wyssa sat up, moaning.
"Morb is walking toward the contraption again!" Gliss cried.
That seemed to bring Wyssa back to her senses. She staggered to her feet and sent out a blast of magic energy. The green wall blocking the hut’s entrance vanished.
"We have to stop Morb," she croaked.
Zann was already at the hut’s entrance, racing toward Morb.
"Get back, boy!" Morb snarled. "You can't—"

Zann leaped forward and shackled himself to the Mask and Morb. When he touched the relic, a jolt ran through his body, almost knocking him over. He braced himself, remembering how another relic had taken over his mind and almost driven him crazy.
But that didn't happen this time. Zann was flooded with a power that felt perfectly natural.
He glanced toward his friends. The trolls were blocking them from helping him.
"Zap!" he cried. He was hoping to zap himself, the Mask, and Morb away from the contraption. He felt a tug, but he was unable to zap away.
Morb smirked. "Give up, Zann. You can't beat me—not this time."

Gritting his teeth, Zann tried to drag Morb away from the contraption with both his muscles and his magic. Despite the extra energy surging into him from the Mask, he was tiring fast. Morb was too powerful!

Morb sneered. "See what I mean? But perhaps my triumph can wait a few moments. It will be a pleasure to watch all the energy drain out of you first. Soon all of Magica will know how that feels!" He cackled with delight.
Darb finally managed to dodge around the trolls. He edged closer. Morb spotted him and smiled.

"Ah, the little Void," he said. "I like you, boy. You don't babble incessantly like your friends. Why don't you come with me when I leave Magica? I could use a servant." He winked. "If you prove loyal enough, perhaps I'll even teach you a few of the tricks Wyssa taught me."
"Really?" Darb said.
Zann's jaw dropped. Could Darb actually be considering Morb's offer?
"Darb, no!" Gliss cried.
Morb chuckled. "Ignore them, boy," he said, reaching out toward Darb. "Join me. You won't regret it."
"No, I won't," Darb said. He stepped closer. "But you might regret some things soon!"

He yanked something out of his pocket and tossed it to Zann, who caught it automatically with his free hand. Only then did he see what it was: the infusinator! Suddenly more energy flowed into Zann. This could be his chance!
"Zap!" he shouted with every bit of energy he could muster.
Splash!
As Zann had hoped, he landed in the middle of the river near the palace, with Morb and the Mask still shackled to him.
"No!" Morb cried. "I can't—" A wave washed over his head.
Zann yanked him up. "What's the matter?" he said. "Can't swim?"
Morb glared. Then panic filled his eyes as he began to sink again. "Save me!"
Zann pulled the villain up out of the water. "I'll rescue you, but only if you unshackle yourself from the Mask."
Anger burned in Morb's eyes. But as more water splashed over his face, he looked nervous. "How do I know I can trust you?"
"You don't know that," Zann said. "But what choice do you have? I'll let us both drown before I let you steal all the magic from Magica."
Morb glared at him again. But when another wave washed over him, he whimpered and then snapped his fingers.

The magic shackles fell away. Zann hesitated for a second, letting one last ripple of strong, wonderful energy run through him. Then he unshackled himself from the Mask too. The relic drifted away with the current. Zann winced as the Mask smashed against a rock and broke into a dozen pieces. The current swept them away.
"Help me!" Morb gurgled. "You promised!"
Zann dragged Morb out of the current to the shallows. Then he rubbed the fingers of his free hand together to create energy for a Swelling spell, to make his voice louder.
"Help!" he called to the people in the palace square nearby. "I need the palace guards over here!"
"Why don't we zap to the university instead of walking?" Gliss said.
Zann grinned at her. "I want to walk," he said. "I never really got a chance to show you guys around First City before everything happened."
"True." Perda laughed. "This has been the craziest visit ever!"

Zann had to agree. It was hard to believe that life was nearly back to normal less than two days after Morb's defeat. Just hours after Morb's capture, the king and queen had reappeared and explained why they'd quit so abruptly. Laddno had kidnapped one of the queen's young nephews and threatened to toss him into the vortex if the king and queen didn't step down.
Still, Zann couldn't help feeling sad. Gliss' uncle Gar was planning to zap Gliss, Perda, and Darb back to Swamp Bottom the next day. When would he see his friends again?
"It was fun watching Queen Venna's inauguration yesterday," Gliss said.
Perda nodded. "I'm glad they figured out that Laddno tampered with the vote toads."
"He never could have done it without Morb's help," Darb said.
Even though the king and queen had returned to the palace, they'd decided to retire. They promised to do everything they could to support Queen Venna.
Gliss took Darb's hand. "I think Venna will make a good queen. For one thing, she's promising to meet with the leaders of the Void Rights groups."
"Not Laddno," Perda said. "The real leaders."
"We're here," Zann said as they reached the entrance to the university campus. "Are you sure you want to see this?"
Perda nodded. "I want to see for myself that he can't get free."
Gliss and Darb nodded too.
