At one end of the campus, there was an enormous, clear cube. A small island sat in the middle of it, surrounded by deep water. The island contained a chair, a table, a cot—and Morb. He sat slumped in the chair, looking miserable.

The prison cube had been Teplo's idea. It was laced with spells—some that provided Morb with food and other basic necessities, and some that ensured that he couldn't break out or communicate with anyone.
"If he tries anything evil, we'll know right away," Zann said. "Let's go. My parents are expecting us at the lab."
"Why do they want us to come to the lab, anyway?" Gliss said as they walked.
"Maybe they need our help cataloging the relics, now that Mari isn't around anymore," Perda said.
Zann felt sorry for Mari, who'd gone into hiding along with most of her family. Queen Venna had sentenced Laddno to a year of hard labor on the slopes of Mount Mystery.
"I'm glad all the relics were recovered," Perda said. "Boz says they even managed to fish all the pieces of the Mask of Zanta out of the river."
"I wonder what they'll do with the relics now," Gliss said.
When they stepped into the lab, there was a burst of lights and music.
"Surprise!" many voices cried.
Zann grinned. The place was packed. His parents and Boz were there, along with Teplo, Fala, Gliss' uncle, and many other people. Even Maff was there.
"We wanted to throw your friends a going-away party," Nax explained. "And also a thank-you party for saving Magica."
"Again!" Fala added.
"Thanks," Zann said. "You didn't have to do this."
"Sure we did. And there's more. These are for you." His mother handed each of the kids a silver twig with a crystal on the end.
"Are these from Atmo?" Zann asked.
His father grinned. "It's our latest invention."
"Wyssa helped us before she left Magica," Asta said.
"They're called zap accelerators," Boz said. "They'll allow you to travel between First City and Swamp Bottom with a single zap. Now you kids can visit each other whenever you like!"

Zann was so stunned that he couldn't speak for a second. The past couple of weeks had been strange and often scary. But this was the best happy ending—and surprise extra birthday gift—that he could ever have hoped for!
"Wow, thanks!" he exclaimed at last. His heart swelled with good feelings. "Now let's party!"
Zann stood at the top of the waterfall. Mist rose from a deep, sparkling pool far below.
"You're not scared, are you?" a teasing voice said behind him.
It was his friend, Perda. She smiled at him, and Zann noticed that the mist made her look even prettier than usual.
"I'm not scared," he said with a laugh. "Here I go!"
He leaped off the edge of the cliff. A second later he heard Perda yell, "Look out below!"
He glanced up and saw her falling along with the sparkling water. "Whee!" he shouted as they both hurtled toward the pool.

At the last second, Zann snapped his fingers and used magic to slow himself down. He splashed into the pool gently. A moment later Perda splashed down beside him, spraying him with water. She hadn't slowed herself as much as he had. That was typical. She was pretty brave.
"Here come Darb and Gliss," Perda said, pointing up.

Their two friends were at the top of the cliff. They jumped together, holding hands. That was partly because Darb was a Void, which meant he couldn't do magic. He needed Gliss' magic to keep him from falling too fast.
But it was also because Gliss and Darb held hands a lot lately. Zann thought it was nice that they were a couple now, but it also made him feel a little bit uncomfortable.
Splash! They landed together nearby.
"That was fun, wasn't it?" Darb said, swimming over to Zann.
"Yeah," Zann agreed. Then he spotted a boy around their age hurrying toward the pool. "Look! Ello's back."
Zann swam to the edge of the pool, with his friends following. Ello had stopped to look at a tiny creature with silvery wings that had landed on a rock at the edge of the pool.
Darb climbed out of the water. "Is that a dragon?" he asked. He was very interested in animals of all kinds.
Ello carefully picked up the tiny creature and handed it to Darb. "Isn't it cute? There were no dragons in Skellia, but there are several species here in Mistafar."

Gliss climbed out of the pool for a better look, squeezing water out of her bright red hair. She and Zann were the only Reds in the group—their red hair was a sign that they had especially strong magic.
"It's cute," she said. "And it's definitely much less scary than the gulpers from your old world!"

Zann agreed with that. They'd first met Ello in Skellia, a world of rising seas and constant rain. The Skellian people had wanted to escape before all of their land disappeared beneath the waves. However, the only way to leave was through the vortex that connected all the known worlds. Reaching the vortex required going through a wormhole. But magic-eating sea creatures called gulpers ate the wormholes as fast as they appeared.
"True. None of us miss the gulpers," Ello said with a shudder.
"Do you miss anything about Skellia?" Darb asked.

Ello looked thoughtful. "I liked sailing on the open sea. And it's hard getting used to a whole new place." He smiled. "But Mistafar is great! Everyone is grateful that you convinced Wyssa to move us here."

Wyssa was a mysterious woman with strong magic powers. Zann and his friends had met her during some earlier adventures. She'd brought the Skellians to Mistafar. This was the first time Zann and the others had traveled from Magica to visit.
Suddenly Zann noticed that Ello's hands were empty. "Hey, I thought you were bringing snacks," he said with a grin.
"Oh! I almost forgot to tell you—it's time for Perda's birthday cake," Ello said.

Perda's birthday was the reason for the visit. Back in Magica, Zann lived with his parents in First City, while the other three kids lived in his former hometown of Swamp Bottom. They were able to visit one another occasionally with the help of zap accelerators, magical devices that helped them to travel long distances quickly. But Zann still missed seeing his friends every day like he had when he lived in Swamp Bottom.
"Great! Waterfall jumping made me hungry," Perda said. "Let's go and have cake!"
They walked back to the Skellians' village. Zann's parents were in the main square, chatting with some other adults. A platter of small, beautifully decorated cakes was sitting on a wooden table.
"Happy birthday, Perda!" Ello's mother said. "Help yourselves to cake, kids."
Zann and his friends each took a cake. Then they sat down to eat. "I'm glad your parents brought you to visit us," Ello said.
"Perda talked them into it since it's her birthday," Zann said. "They know she's interested in being an explorer someday."
"Or maybe a researcher," Gliss said. "She's absolutely obsessed with the ancient history of Magica!"
"You are?" Zann looked at Perda in surprise. The last time he'd spent time with her, she had been more interested in studying other worlds.
Perda took a bite of cake and then nodded. "Yes, it's really interesting. But it's hard to find much information about the Old Times."
Gliss shuddered. "That's probably because everyone wants to forget about the Old Times. My parents say it was a time of dark magic and danger."

Perda licked frosting off her fingers. "There's even less information about the time before the Old Times," she said. "Hey, Zann, remind me to ask your parents if they have any books about that period."
"Okay." Zann nodded.
Just then his parents came toward them. "Finish your cake, kids," his mother, Asta, said. "It's time to go home."
Zann sighed. He wasn't sure what to think about Perda's new interest. "It's so strange," he thought. "I hardly know anything about my friends anymore!"

Perda gazed at the swirling lights and colors all around her. Some people, like Gliss, thought the vortex was scary and dangerous. Perda knew it could be both of those things, but she also thought it was beautiful and interesting.
"I wonder how long it will be until I can travel through it again," she thought.
"This trip was fun, wasn't it?" Perda said to Gliss, who was magically shackled to her. The whole group was shackled together in a line so they wouldn't be separated in the vortex.
Gliss nodded but she looked nervous. "Are we there yet?" she asked.
Zann's father, Nax, was shackled to Perda's other hand. "Yes, almost home," he said. "Hang on, kids!"
He grabbed a wormhole, pulling the whole group through it. Perda landed on her feet and then looked around.
"Oh," she said. "We're in Edgewood."
Zann's mother, Asta, snapped her fingers. "Release," she said.
All the shackles disappeared.
"Let's zap back to the lab and get Zing," Zann said to Perda and the others. "Then we can figure out what to do for the rest of the afternoon."
Perda nodded, feeling a pang of dejection. She, Gliss, and Darb were scheduled to return to Swamp Bottom right after dinner. "I wish we could stay longer," she said.
Perda reached for Darb's arm, planning to zap the two of them across town to Zann's parents' lab. Before she could, Gliss grabbed Darb's other hand.
"Zap!" Gliss said, snapping her fingers. She and Darb disappeared.

Zann's parents zapped away too. "Ready?" Zann asked, looking over. For a second Perda thought he was going to grab her hand. But that would be silly. Unlike Darb, she was perfectly capable of zapping herself.
"Zap!" she said, snapping her fingers to create magical friction.
She landed on the street in front of the lab. A second later Zann appeared nearby with a splash.
"Drat," he muttered, stepping out of a puddle of purple rainwater.
Perda laughed. Zann was good at magic, but he could be a little careless. Sometimes that meant he didn't land quite where he meant to when he zapped somewhere.
They went into the lab where Zann's parents conducted their research. The others were already there.
"Look out, Zann!" Darb called. "I think Zing is a little annoyed . . ."
Perda ducked as a dragon flew toward them, shooting flames out of his mouth. Zann clapped his hands and yelled, "Shield!" just in time to avoid getting roasted.
"Sorry you couldn't come with us, Zing," Perda said with a laugh, watching the dragon chase his master around the room. "Don't take it out on Zann, though—it wasn't his fault."
"You wouldn't have liked Mistafar anyway, little buddy," Darb added with a grin. "It's very wet."

Zing snorted a plume of smoke in their direction and then returned to chasing Zann. The others continued joking around, but Perda was distracted by everything in the lab. She always found it fascinating to see what Zann's parents and the other researchers were doing.

There were several adults in the lab. Nax and Asta were chatting with a few of them about the trip to Mistafar. Meanwhile a young research assistant was shuffling through papers on a desk. A metal-and-glass case sat nearby. A big lock secured it. Perda wandered over to look into the case, which held several ancient-looking items.
"Where are the rest of the relics?" she asked the research assistant.
The young man looked over. "The most powerful ones were moved to the palace, where they can be guarded full-time," he said. "We kept only a few here to study further."
Perda peered at the relics. She recognized some of them, since she and her friends had gone on the mission to retrieve them from the Cave of the Unknown.
"That's the Dragontamer's Charm, right?" she said, pointing to a dented metal amulet. "I read that it supposedly dates back to the earliest of the Old Times."
"That's right," Zann's mother said. She'd come over just in time to hear Perda's comment. "And the relic beside it may be even older!"
Beside the Dragontamer's Charm was a cracked old pottery cup.
"That looks familiar," Perda said. "I think I remember seeing it in the cave. What's it called?"
Asta shrugged. "It doesn't have a name. All we know is that it's very, very old. We plan to study it to figure out more."
The research assistant handed Asta some papers and then hurried away. Asta set the papers down beside a chunk of wood that was sitting on the desk.
"What's that?" Perda asked, stepping closer for a better look.
"It's a piece of the Wormwood tree," Asta replied. "Now that everyone knows that the tree is the Source of magic, we plan to study it more closely too."

"Cool," Perda said, wishing she could stay in First City to help. Most people were afraid of the neighborhood known as Wormwood. They thought it was seedy and possibly even dangerous. But Perda was fascinated by the recent discovery that all the magical energy in Magica came from the gnarled, ancient tree that grew there. When Magicians snapped their fingers or rubbed their hands together to create friction, they were using energy from that tree.
"How cool is that?" she whispered, staring at the chunk of wood.
"Zing! No, look out!" Zann's father cried.

Perda spun to see Zing speeding across the room, shooting flames. Zann had just ducked out of the way, and Perda could see that the little dragon was flying too fast to stop. He was heading straight toward an old, dusty book lying open on a table. Flames were pouring from his snout.
"The book!" Nax cried. "No, Zing, no!"
Zann heard the horror in his father's voice and realized the book must be very important. He leaped toward it, hoping to grab it before Zing charred it.
But Perda was closer—and faster too. She yanked the book away a split second before Zing's fiery breath set the wooden surface of the table aflame.

"Bad boy, Zing," Asta scolded, snapping her fingers and magically dousing the fire. "Thanks, Perda. That's the only known copy of that book. It would have been tricky to restore it, even using magic."

Zann was relieved that the book was safe. The last time Zing had burned something important, Zann had been grounded for a whole week. And even though Magicians could do a lot of things with magic, they couldn't do everything. That book looked really old, which meant it was possible that nobody still living had read the entire thing. If that was the case, even the most powerful Restore spell couldn't bring it back if it was destroyed.

"We should probably get out of here," Zann said, snapping his fingers to create a dragon harness. He grabbed Zing, who struggled and spit flames at him. But Zann ignored the burns and strapped on the harness. When it was secure, he quickly healed his burns with magic.
"Okay, let's go," Darb said, and Gliss nodded.
But Perda seemed to be totally focused on the book she was holding. "Hey, what is this?" she asked, peering down at the open page. "It looks like a poem or something."

"We think it's a riddle," Zann's mother replied. "Those words used to be carved into the trunk of the Wormwood tree. Bark grew over the words long ago. But before that happened, a historian copied it into that book about the history of Wormwood."
"That's cool," Zann said. "What does the riddle say?"
"I'll read it out loud," Perda said. She cleared her throat and then began:
"Bygone days lost to time's haze
Yet visible to careful gaze
Rooted in the depths of time
Touch and see—no need to climb."
"What in the worlds does that mean?" Gliss asked, furrowing her brow in confusion.
"We're not sure yet," Nax said. "Zann's mother just found that book buried in an old trunk in the basement of the university library."
Asta nodded. "I was beginning our research into the Wormwood tree."
That was enough of an explanation for Zann. He wanted to have fun with the last few hours of his friends' visit. He didn't want to hear about another of his parents' work projects.
"So where do you want to go?" he asked his friends. "Maybe we should check out the new other-worlds exhibit at the zoo."
"Hold on." Perda was still peering at the book. "May I take a blink image of the riddle? It would be fun to try to puzzle it out."
"Sure, go ahead," Nax said with a smile. "Let us know if you have any ideas!"
Perda held the book up to her face. "Blink," she murmured as she blinked her eyes. A second later a sheet of paper appeared. She grabbed it, folded it, and put it in her pocket.
Then the kids said good-bye and headed outside. The rainstorm that had left puddles in the street earlier had cleared away, and it was a warm, beautiful day.
"So are we going to the zoo?" Darb asked eagerly.
"We could," Gliss said. "But we should probably go to the palace first. Venna invited us to visit the next time we came to First City, remember?"
Venna had been elected queen of Magica a few months earlier. Zann and his friends had helped her stop a plot to take over the government. Because of that, they were welcome at the palace anytime.
Just then a large spotted rat raced past. Zing whistled and dashed after it. Zann was taken by surprise and ended up being dragged by the little dragon.
Zann's friends laughed and chased both of them.
"Zing, leave that poor rat alone!" Darb cried.

Zann finally managed to yank his pet to a stop. "Now do you see why you weren't allowed to come with us today?" he said with a grin. "Who knows how many new creatures you would have decided to chase in Mistafar!"
"Zing could use some exercise," Darb said. "Maybe we should take him to the park."

Zann nodded. Wandering through one of the city's lovely parks with his friends sounded like a nice way to spend the afternoon. Gliss and Darb would probably hold hands and walk off by themselves. That would leave Zann with Perda, which sounded even nicer.
But when he looked at Perda, she was shaking her head. "I have a better idea," she said. "Let's go to Wormwood."
"Wormwood?" Gliss wrinkled her nose in distaste. "Ugh, why?"
"I want to take a look at the tree." Perda pulled the blink image out of her pocket. "Maybe we can figure out what this riddle means. Wouldn't that be cool?"
Zann traded a dubious look with Darb. Staring at the Wormwood tree didn't sound like a very good way to spend the last few hours of his friends' visit.
"Well, Perda is the birthday girl," Darb said slowly.
Gliss sighed. "That's true. She should get to choose what we do." She glanced at Perda. "Are you sure you really want to go to Wormwood?"
"Absolutely." Perda smiled. "Thanks, you guys. I'll see you there! Zap."
With a snap of her fingers, she disappeared. Zann shrugged. "Okay, let's go," he said to the others. "Maybe she'll get bored soon and we can spend the rest of the day at the zoo or the park."
He made sure he was holding on tightly to Zing's leash. Then he snapped his fingers and zapped away.

Perda landed in front of the Wormwood tree, near a rickety hut where a skinny old woman was stirring an enormous metal pot of foul-smelling stew. Or was it a potion of some sort? The people of Wormwood were known to practice some strange magic. A furry striped creature was stretched out beside the pot, soaking in the warmth of the fire that heated it. Perda recognized it as an itchetch, a creature from another world that some people kept as a pet.
But Perda wasn't interested in the woman or her stewpot or even the itchetch. She stared at the tree. Its gnarled old branches stretched over the entire area, casting weird-shaped patches of shade.
"It's strange to think that all the magic in Magica came from one tree," Perda thought. "I can't wait to find out more!"
As she took a step toward the tree, she heard a loud splash right behind her.
"Ouch!" Zann cried.
She turned to see that Zann had landed with one foot in the old woman's stewpot. "Drat," Zann muttered, pulling his foot out of the bubbling stew.

Zing was just outside the pot beside Zann. When the itchetch spotted the dragon, it growled and jumped to its feet. Zing spit out a burst of fire in return. Zann grabbed Zing to keep him away from the itchetch. "Sorry," he added when he noticed the old woman glaring at him.
"That's just like a Red," she spit out. "Carelessly ruining a poor old Void's dinner!"
Perda hurried over. "Please forgive him," she said to the old woman. "We can fix your, um, soup?"
Just then Gliss and Darb landed, holding hands. "What's going on?" Gliss asked.
The Void woman rolled her eyes. "Great, just what I needed," she said. "Another Red! Would you like to come into my hut and destroy my few lowly belongings, missy?"
Gliss looked confused. "Um, no?"
"Is that an itchetch?" Darb said. "Cool!"
"Yes," the old woman said. "Be careful of your dragon. My itchetch hates all scaly creatures. And now that our dinner is ruined, he'll be looking for something else to eat." She glared at Zing.

"I'd better do something," Perda thought. She rubbed her hands together to make lots of magic friction. Then she quickly created a whole new pot of delicious-smelling stew, along with a platter of fruit and cheese.
The old woman's eyes lit up. "Ah, that's more like it," she said, greedily stuffing a piece of fruit into her mouth. "Apology accepted."
"Good. Let's get out of here." Zann hurried away, carrying Zing, who was still glaring at the itchetch.
Perda walked closer to the tree's giant trunk. "Look out for the wormhole," Gliss warned.

Perda nodded, sidestepping the spot so she wouldn't accidentally open the wormhole. Unlike many of the wormholes in Magica, which appeared and disappeared from time to time, the Wormwood wormhole had been in the same spot in front of this tree for as long as anyone could remember.
Zann set Zing down and dropped the harness. Then he snapped his fingers and healed the burns the hot stew had left on his leg. He also dried his pants and shoe.
"Look out," Darb said. "Here comes that itchetch."
Zing saw the creature coming too. He flapped his wings, flying toward the itchetch before Zann could grab his leash.
"Will that thing really try to eat Zing?" Gliss asked, looking worried.

"I doubt it," Darb said. "For one thing, they're about the same size. See? They're just chasing each other around." He reached over and took her hand. "Don't worry, we can keep an eye on them and intervene if we need to."
Gliss smiled at him. "Okay."
The itchetch tried to tackle Zing. But the dragon flew up, shooting flames. Then he turned and chased the itchetch, causing it to snarl angrily.

Darb knew a lot about animals, so Perda figured Zing would be all right. She pulled out the blink image again. "I wonder if this riddle could help to explain how the Source of magic works, like Asta said."
"Maybe," Zann said, leaning in for a look at the words.

He was the only one paying attention to Perda. Nearby, Darb bent to pick a wildflower, and then he tucked it into Gliss' red hair while she giggled. Zing and the itchetch stopped running around and started growling at each other.
"'Touch and see,'" Perda said. "I wonder what we're supposed to see?"
Zann shrugged, stepping toward the tree and putting a hand on its trunk. "And what are we supposed to touch?"
"It says 'no need to climb,'" Perda pointed to the words. "So it's probably something low enough to reach."
"Maybe we should—Zing, look out!" Zann cried.
The itchetch had just leaped at the dragon again. Zing was flying backward, shooting flames.
"Huh?" Perda thought. "The itchetch's claws look sharp, but Zing is pretty tough."

Then she noticed the wormhole swirling open. For a second she wasn't sure why. None of them were close enough to open it the regular way. And none of them were doing magic, which might cause it to open from farther away.
But that wasn't true, she realized. It took magic energy for Zing to create fire. His energy was causing the wormhole to open—and now he was hurtling straight toward it!
"Grab him!" Darb shouted. He started running, but he was too far away to reach Zing in time.
Luckily Zann was closer. He grabbed Zing's leg just as the wormhole sucked the little dragon in.
"Zann!" Perda cried as she saw him teeter on the edge, trying to pull his pet out of the swirling wormhole. She leaped forward, hoping she was fast enough.

Zann felt the wormhole's intense magic power pulling at him and began to panic. Then a strong pair of hands grabbed his shoulders. There was a yank, and the wormhole released him and Zing. He tumbled back onto the ground near the Wormwood tree, with the little dragon landing on his stomach.
Zann grunted. Looking up, he saw Perda staring down at him.
"Phew! That was close," she said.
Darb and Gliss hurried over. "Good going, Perda," Darb said. "It looked like Zann and Zing were both going to get sucked in!"
"We were, until Perda grabbed me," Zann admitted. "Thanks."
"Can we get out of this creepy neighborhood now?" Gliss complained. "There's probably still time for a walk in the park or a boat ride or something nice like that before dinnertime."
"Soon." Perda glanced at the huge tree. "I want to study the riddle a little more."
As Zann pushed Zing off him and stood up, he noticed the itchetch creeping closer with its yellow eyes locked on Zing. The dragon spit a burst of flame at the other creature.
"Stop it, you two," Zann scolded. "Or if you won't stop, at least move away from the wormhole."
He grabbed Zing's leash and dragged the little dragon around to the opposite side of the huge tree trunk. The itchetch followed.
Zann released Zing and looked around.

"I've never been to this side of the Wormwood tree before," he thought. Based on the rocky, rough ground, he guessed few people wandered here. Several large roots stuck out of the ground, and Zann noticed that one had a particularly interesting shape.
"Come look at this, you guys!" he called.
Perda appeared a moment later. "What is it?"
"Where are Darb and Gliss?" Zann asked, stepping aside as Zing chased the itchetch past him.
Perda rolled her eyes. "I don't think they heard you," she said. "They're looking for another flower to put in Darb's hair so the two of them will match."
Suddenly Zann couldn't stop wondering what would happen if he tried to put a flower in Perda's hair. Would she like it, or would she think it was silly?
"What did you want to show us?" she asked, interrupting his thoughts.
"Check out that root." Zann pointed. "Doesn't it look like an angry troll?"
Perda laughed. "Yeah, a little bit!" Then her smile faded, and she leaned forward. "Wait—do you see something in there?" She pointed to a hole in the root that looked like the troll's open mouth.
Zann hadn't noticed it before, but now he did. The sunlight shining through the tree's branches glinted off something metallic.
"Careful," he said as Perda crouched down for a closer look. "I heard that the people in Wormwood sometimes leave stuff for one another near this tree. Illegal stuff from other worlds, even."
"I know." Perda stared into the hole. "But what if it's not that? The riddle says 'rooted' in one line, remember? Maybe that's a clue, and whatever's in the hole is important somehow."

Zann wasn't sure about that. It seemed much more likely that the glinting object was an illicit stone from another world or something like that. Then again, Perda was one of the smartest people he knew. Maybe she was right.
"Let's try to get it out, then," he said. "But we should be careful. Don't touch it."
Perda nodded. "Let's try a Levitation spell to lift it out."
She tried the spell on her own first, but nothing happened. So she and Zann joined their friction by rubbing their hands together. The metal item didn't move.

Perda sat back on her heels. "We could ask Gliss to help," she said, peering around the trunk. "Or we could spend all day trying to figure out other spells to use. Or . . ." She leaned forward and stuck her hand into the hole.
Zann bit his lip. "Perda, don't—"
"Got it!" Perda pulled her arm out, clutching something tightly.
At the same moment, Zann felt a shock wave of magic energy burst over him. He gasped and Perda's eyes went wide. Even Zing and the itchetch noticed and stopped chasing each other for a moment.
"What was that?" Zann asked. "It happened right when you pulled your hand out." Then he gasped again. "Look!"
A wormhole suddenly spun open at their feet, nestled between two large, gnarled roots.
"Whoa," Perda said. "Is that a wormhole? It looks . . . different."
"I've never seen one on the ground before," Zann said, taking a step back from the swirling hole. "And how can it exist so close to the other one? I thought that never happened."
Perda nodded, looking a bit pale. "Do you think it opened because of this?" She opened her hand to reveal a small, dirty scrap of metal.
"It looks like a leaf," Zann said. "What if it's a powerful relic, like the Dragontamer's Charm or something like that?"
Before Perda could answer, they both heard a loud snarl. Zing had just slapped the itchetch with his tail. The itchetch responded by leaping forward and giving the dragon a shove.
Zing tumbled backward—right into the new wormhole!
"Zing!" Zann shouted, barely managing to grab one of the dragon's wings before it disappeared.
"Oh, no! Not again!" Perda cried, grabbing Zann's arm.
Zann was relieved—but only for a second. Because this time, even though Perda was pulling as hard as she could, the wormhole kept sucking them farther in.
"Help!" he shouted frantically as his whole arm disappeared after Zing. "Guys, we need help over here!"

There was an answering shout. But Zann barely caught a glimpse of an alarmed-looking Darb and Gliss. As they appeared from around the tree, he, Zing, and Perda were sucked all the way into the wormhole.
Perda knew she should probably be panicking. But she couldn't help being happy about returning to the vortex.

Except . . . this time the vortex seemed different. It was darker than usual, with fewer swirling lights. A deafening roar made Perda wish she could cover her ears. But she was using both hands to cling onto Zann's arm because they seemed to be tumbling faster than ever before.
"Hold on!" Zann yelled over the noise. "I'll try to grab a wormhole."
Perda looked around. "Where?" she cried. "There are hardly any wormholes here!"

For the first time, she felt a twinge of panic. Normally there were lots of wormholes in the vortex. The only tricky part was finding the one you wanted—or at least not accidentally pulling yourself out into a scary, dangerous world. But now a wormhole passed by only once every few minutes.
"There's one!" she yelled.
"Got it!" Zann had managed to wrap Zing's leash around his waist, so he used both hands to grab at the edge of the wormhole.

Perda grabbed it too. She saw a steep mountainside covered with dark, dripping trees. The sky was dark, and jagged flashes of lightning lit up the scene every few seconds, glaring off the craggy cliffs overhead.
"Weird," she commented. "This wormhole is in the ground too."
"Never mind that," Zann said. "Are you thinking what I'm thinking?"

Perda nodded. "That looks a lot like Fardark," she said with a shudder. They'd visited the terrifying world a couple of times and barely escaped alive. It was home to nothing but horrible, violent creatures who wished to harm any traveler unlucky enough to end up there.
"I never saw mountains like this in Fardark though," Zann said. "And those trees look like some I've seen in Magica. Maybe it's not Fardark after all."

"It's not worth the risk," Perda said. "We'll try the next world. But first, let's make sure we don't lose each other." She rubbed her fingers together to create friction. Then she touched Zann's arm. "Shackle," she said.
Magical shackles appeared, binding them together. Zann quickly shackled himself to Zing as well.
They let go and tumbled on through the strange, noisy vortex. For a long moment, they didn't pass any wormholes, and Perda felt panic creep through her again.
Finally a glowing wormhole appeared up ahead. Once again Zann grabbed the edge with both hands and managed to pull himself and Perda halfway through. They paused and looked around.

This time the world before them was rocky and charred, with almost no foliage. Then there was a screech of fury, and an enormous purple dragon flew into view. A second, bright red dragon was pursuing it. It was spitting fireballs as the first dragon dodged to try to avoid them. The purple dragon screamed in pain as a fireball hit it in the back of the head. The dragon spun around and leaped toward the other dragon with deadly claws extended. The two huge creatures were locked in battle. They tumbled to the hard ground with a thump that nearly shook loose Perda's grip on the wormhole.
"Oh, no," she said, her heart sinking as she realized where they must be. "I think . . . this is Drac!"
Zann looked pale. Drac was another dangerous world they'd barely escaped. There, dragons were the dominant species. They treated humans as servants—and sometimes as food.
Zing was peering out through the wormhole. He shot out a puff of smoke in the direction of the dragons.

"That red dragon looks like a much larger version of Zing," Perda thought. "Maybe it's a type of fire whistler." She liked Zing just fine, but he could be a little destructive. That's why Zann was one of the few people in Magica who chose to keep a fire whistler as a pet. She couldn't even imagine what kind of damage a huge version of Zing could do!
"Let's get out of here before they notice us," Zann said as the wrestling dragons rolled closer to the wormhole.
Once again he and Perda let go and continued through the vortex.
"We've got to find a place to stop and rest soon," Zann said.

Perda realized he was right. Already she could feel the last bits of magic energy ebbing from her body. That was weird. Traveling through the vortex always used a lot of energy. But she'd never lost this much energy this quickly before.
"We have to stop at the next world, no matter what," she said as another wormhole appeared up ahead.
"Yeah," Zann agreed, sounding tired. "At least we already found the two scariest worlds possible."

"Not quite," Perda said. "What about that world we found with no magic at all?" She shuddered just thinking about it. That world had been full of interesting sights, smells, and people. But there was no natural magic energy there at all. Perda and her friends were helpless to do even the simplest things, like create food or zap from place to place. Plus, since magic energy was required to open a wormhole, they'd almost been trapped there forever!
"What are the odds we'd end up there again?" Zann said.
He grabbed the next wormhole as it swirled past. Perda pulled herself up beside him to take a look.
"At least the sun is shining here," Zann said, glancing around.
Perda nodded. The land before them was drab and barren, with wispy, brownish grass covering a flat plain. A few boulders and prickly shrubs were the only other things breaking up the boring scene.
"This doesn't look like a very exciting world," she said. "But I suppose it's a safe place to rest and figure out how to get back to Magica."
"I agree," Zann said. "Let's go!"

Zann realized this wormhole, too, was on the ground. He yanked on the edge of the wormhole as hard as he could, propelling himself upward. He flew out and landed on his feet, but he forgot that Perda was still shackled to him.
"Hey!" she cried. "Whoa!"
She crashed into Zann, and the two of them collapsed on the ground in a tangle of arms and legs. Zing landed on Zann's face.
"Oof!" Zann grunted, embarrassed to realize that his elbow was in Perda's ear.
Perda quickly snapped her fingers. "Unshackle," she said, undoing the spell. She jumped to her feet and looked around. "I wonder where we are?"
Zann glanced back just in time to see the wormhole swirl shut and disappear. He also realized his arm hurt.
"Ow," he said, noticing a scrape. "I think I landed on a rock."

He unshackled himself from Zing. Then he snapped his fingers and touched the wound on his arm to perform a simple Healing spell. But nothing happened. The scrape still stung, and it still looked red and raw.
"What's wrong?" Perda asked.
Zann rubbed his hands together to create more friction. Then he tried again. "My Healing spell isn't working!" he exclaimed. "What if we did land in that no-magic world again?"
"This doesn't look anything like that world," Perda said. "It's probably not working because the vortex sapped your energy. You should rest and then try again in a few minutes."
Zann nodded. "I hope she's right," he thought. "My arm doesn't hurt that much. But I do not want to be stuck in a world without magic!"

To distract himself, he looked around. The land was just as flat and colorless as it had appeared from the vortex. Now that he could see more, though, Zann spotted mountains rising in the distance. He also saw a crooked, weak-looking sapling growing very close to where the wormhole had been. It cast only a few jagged slivers of shade that didn't do much to combat the heat of the blazing sun.
"Look over here." Perda had wandered a short distance away. She was staring down at some limp greenish gray sprouts. "This looks like some kind of garden. See? These plants are growing in rows."
"That means there must be people nearby." Zann noticed a shallow hole in the ground. A crude stone shovel with a wooden handle was lying next to it. "Look, they left one of their tools."
Perda walked over to look. "Someone dug this hole recently," she said. "See? The dirt on the shovel is still a little damp, even though the air here is really dry."

Zann was impressed that she'd noticed something like that. Perda really was one of the smartest people he knew. She would make a great researcher someday, if that was what she decided to do for a career.
"I wonder where they went," he said. Then he noticed Zing creeping toward a patch of thorny bushes. "Hey Zing, don't you dare start chasing something! That's what got us into this mess, remember?"
He grabbed the dragon's leash. Zing opened his mouth as if to shoot flames at him, but only a little steam came out.
"Uh-oh," Zann said. "Zing's magic isn't working either. That's a bad sign."

For a second, Perda looked worried. Then her expression brightened. "Wait—we undid our Shackle spells after we got here, remember? That means there's at least some magic energy. It just must be really weak. Or maybe it works differently here than it does in Magica."
Once again Zann was impressed. Before he could respond, Zing yanked on his leash, which made Zann's arm hurt again. "Ouch," he complained. "What are you—oh!"
A girl stepped into view from behind the shrub Zing was watching. She was about their age, with reddish brown hair and a few freckles. She was dressed in a drab, simple outfit of rough-looking cloth.
"Hello," she said, her voice shaking a little. "Where did you come from? One moment I was alone, and then . . ." Her voice trailed off uncertainly.
"I'm Perda, and this is Zann," Perda said. "What's your name?"
"Mellis," the girl replied. "But where did you come from?"
"We came through the vortex from a world called Magica," Zann said.
Mellis blinked in confusion. "You came here from another world?"
"Yes, that's right," Perda said.
"Oh." Mellis looked as if she didn't believe them. But she didn't say so. Instead she said, "Well, wherever you came from, welcome to Terrica."
"Terrica?" Perda looked thoughtful. "I don't remember seeing that world mentioned in any of your parents' books, Zann."
Zann shrugged. "They say there are lots of worlds that haven't been discovered yet," he said. "I guess we just discovered one."
He felt his arm throbbing and lifted it for a better look. Mellis noticed his scrape.
"Oh, you're hurt!" she exclaimed.
"I almost forgot." Perda stepped closer. "Our energy must be returning by now."
She rubbed her hands together and touched the sore spot on Zann's arm. Nothing happened. She tried again, rubbing her hands on her legs this time.
"Heal," she said as she touched the scrape again. Then she shook her head. "Still nothing—not even when I used a focusing word!"
"Let's both try." Zann and Perda rubbed their hands together, and then both of them touched Zann's arm.
But still the scrape remained, oozing a little bit of blood.
Mellis looked perplexed. "What are you doing?" she asked.
Zann tried to control the panic rising within him as he turned to her. Maybe Perda was right—maybe magic worked differently here. "Mellis," he said. "How does magic work here in Terrica?"
Mellis blinked in confusion. "Magic?" she echoed. "What's that?"
Perda could see the panic on Zann's face. She felt a flash of fear herself.
But then she thought again about that Shackle spell.
"It takes magic to reverse that spell," she thought. "There must be some magic energy here—at least a little."
"Maybe they don't call it magic here," she said to Zann. "They might use a different word." She turned to face Mellis. "How do you create things here? Do you use friction or some other way?"
"Friction?" Mellis sounded distracted. "I'm not sure what you mean. But please, tell me—what is that creature? I've never seen anything like it!"
She pointed to Zing, who was sniffing at an insect.
"That's Zing," Zann replied. "He's a dragon. I guess you don't have dragons in Terrica."
Perda shrugged. "Lots of worlds don't have dragons," she reminded him. "Mellis, how do you create food when you're hungry?"

Mellis looked confused again. "You mean, how do I prepare it?" she asked. "I usually cook it over a fire, like everyone else. Although my uncle and I grow some fruits and vegetables that are edible without cooking."
Perda and Zann traded a glance. Zann was looking panicky again. But Perda was still thinking about that Unshackle spell.

"I bet this world has very weak magic," she said. "Wyssa's home world was the same way, remember, Zann? That's why she learned all about mixing potions out of berries and stuff—that's how they do magic there."
"So you think we're in Wyssa's home world?" Zann said.
Perda shook her head. "This doesn't look like that world at all," she said. "I'm just saying that Terrica might have weak magic too."
"Maybe," Zann agreed. "Come to think of it, the teachers at school are always saying that healing magic takes lots of energy. That's why they stopped letting me bring Zing to school."
"Let's try something easier than a Healing spell," Perda said. "It's awfully hot out here. I'd like a nice, cool cup of airberry juice."
She closed her eyes and pictured the juice. For a moment nothing happened.
"It's not working," Zann said.
Perda focused even harder on the image, rubbing one hand on her leg to create more friction. Finally she felt something land in her other hand. But it didn't feel like a cup.
When she opened her eyes, it didn't look like a cup either. It was a single airberry, shriveled and dry.

"Oh my goodness!" Mellis cried, her eyes wide with amazement. "You just made that berry appear out of nowhere! You must be nearly as powerful as Zira, the head of our village council! She can perform incredible feats with her potions."
"Potions?" Perda tossed the airberry to Zing, who chomped it down eagerly. "Aha! That must be the only kind of magic here."
Zann shrugged. "I guess so. At least now we know there's some magic energy in this world, even if it's not strong enough for Healing spells." He glanced at his scraped arm. Then he gasped.
"What is it?" Perda stepped toward him, concerned. "Is your injury getting worse?"

"No, it's not that." Zann gulped. "The magic here isn't strong enough for Healing spells. Well, opening a wormhole takes a lot more energy than healing a scrape, doesn't it? What if we can't get it to open? How will we go home?"
"What's a wormhole?" Mellis asked.

But Perda barely heard her. She and Zann rushed to the spot where they'd arrived. The dirt and scrubby grass looked the same there as everywhere else. Luckily Perda remembered that the vortex had spit them out close to the scraggly little tree.
"This is the spot," she told Zann. "I'm sure of it."

"Back in Magica, all you have to do to open a wormhole is step close enough to it," Zann said. "Your own natural magic energy joins with the energy in the air to open it. So why isn't this one opening?"
Perda wiped sweat from her brow and glanced around. "Maybe I'm wrong about the spot," she said. "Let's try over this way."
But no wormhole appeared. "The magic is weak here, right?" Zann said. "Maybe we have to create more energy to get it to open."

"It's worth a try," Perda agreed. What Zann had said made sense. Back in Magica, magic energy was everywhere. Friction was a way of focusing it to do what you wanted it to do. If the energy here was very weak, it would probably take much more friction to gather enough magic energy to open a wormhole.
She and Zann spent a few minutes creating as much friction as they could. Zann got Zing to rub against his leg to add a little more friction. They even convinced Mellis to help.
"Why are we rubbing our hands together?" she asked at last.
"It's a way to bring magic energy to us," Zann explained. "When there's enough, the wormhole should open."

But a short while later, their hands were sore and nothing had happened. "Too bad we don't have one of those relics from your parents' lab," Perda said. "The reason they're so powerful is that they're full of superconcentrated magic energy. That would definitely help us open the wormhole!"

Zann flopped down on the ground to rest. Then he sat up straight. "Hey!" he exclaimed. "What about that weird metal thing we found in the Wormwood tree's root? It looked kind of like a relic. I bet that's what opened the wormhole there. Maybe it will work here too!"
Perda felt a surge of hope. But just as quickly, her heart sank again. "Maybe," she said. "But I dropped it when I grabbed you to stop you from falling into the wormhole. It's still in Magica."
Zann saw Perda's anxious look and felt even more anxious himself.
Mellis stepped closer. "Your arm looks painful," she said. "The entire village council is meeting at my house today. I can take you there to see Zira. Her potions will heal you."
"Great! Let's go." Zann whistled for Zing, who flew over.

Mellis looked worried. "Perhaps we should leave your pet behind. Zira is the most accomplished scientist in this part of Terrica. If she hasn't seen such a beast before, she might want to study him further."
"Mellis doesn't believe we're from another world," Zann thought. What if Zira and the other adults felt the same way? Then again, what if they did believe them? Zira might want to study them too!
"We probably shouldn't mention where we're from," he said to Perda. "We could tie Zing to that tree to wait for us."
Zing let out an angry whistle and shot a puff of steam in Zann's face.
"That tiny tree? He'd yank it right out of the ground if he doesn't feel like staying," Perda said. "Maybe we could disguise him somehow."
Mellis looked thoughtful. "He's about the same size as a chupo."
"What's a chupo?" Zann asked.
"A creature that lives in the mountains." Mellis pointed toward the mountain range Zann had noticed earlier. "Chupos are pretty rare since they're a favorite snack of rock trompers." She shuddered.
"Rock trompers?" Perda echoed.

"Yes. They're terrifying and dangerous creatures that also live in the mountains." Mellis looked at Zing again. "Everyone has heard of chupos, but few in this area have seen one. Let's see if we can turn your, um, dragon into a chupo."
First Mellis said they had to hide Zing's gleaming red scales. She had a bottle of water in her rough cloth bag, and the kids mixed it with dirt to create a muddy paste.
Zing wasn't happy about having mud rubbed on him. Zann was glad that he couldn't shoot fire at the moment, only hot steam. Even so, it was difficult to keep him still.
"I wish Darb were here," he muttered, dodging a slap from Zing's wing. "He can convince Zing to do almost anything."
Perda nodded. "Hold still, Zing. We missed a spot."
Finally Zing was the same drab color as the landscape. "Chupos don't have wings though." Mellis studied the dragon. "And you can still tell he's covered in scales, not fur."
Perda glanced at Mellis' bag. "Maybe we could wrap him in that," she suggested. "We could say he's injured, and it's a bandage."
"Good idea!" Mellis dumped a few items out of the bag. Then she pulled off the rope belt that cinched in her loose tunic. "We can use this to tie it on him."
Soon Zing was fully disguised. Zann wasn't sure what a chupo looked like. But he doubted it looked like a dragon covered in mud and draped in a bag.
"Let's hope nobody looks too closely," Mellis said. "It's the best we can do. Follow me—the farm is this way."
Zing's legs and wings were restricted by the bag so the kids took turns carrying him.
"How far away is your house?" Zann asked after they'd been walking for several minutes.
"At our current pace, we should be there within an hour," Mellis replied.
Zann and Perda traded a dismayed glance.
"I wish we had enough magic to create more comfortable shoes," Zann said.
Perda rolled her eyes. "If we had magic, we wouldn't need better shoes," she reminded him. "We'd just zap there!"
Zann shifted his grip on Zing. The little dragon felt heavier with every step.

Mellis distracted the visitors by telling them more about herself. She'd lost both her parents to a famine when she was very young. Her uncle Vilkor had taken her in, and now the two of them eked out a living on their large but arid farm.
"It's not easy," she admitted with a sigh. "Especially now that our main well has run dry. That's why I was out there when you arrived. Uncle Vilkor had sent me to dig a new well."
Zann was amazed by Mellis' tale. Life without magic sounded really difficult!
Finally they spotted a few buildings on the horizon. There was a small barn, a separate building for storing dried grains, and a modest one-story house.

Three people were sitting in the yard. By now Zann was so exhausted from the long walk that he barely took in the names when Mellis introduced them. Uncle Vilkor was tall and handsome, with a big smile and a strong handshake. "Welcome, welcome," he said. "Visitors from far away—what fun!"
Then there was a man named Krub, who was broad-shouldered and rough-looking. He didn't say much, but when he did speak, his voice was loud and gruff.
Finally Mellis introduced Zira, a small, lean woman with steely gray eyes.

"Let's have a look," Zira said, examining Zann's scrape. "Yes, this should be a simple matter. Let's go indoors so the dust doesn't contaminate my potion. It's quite rare and difficult to make, you know."
She sounded proud of her work. Soon Zann found out why. The moment Zira rubbed her purple paste-like potion onto his wound, it stopped hurting.

"Wow, thanks!" he said. Then he noticed Krub watching Zing with narrowed eyes. None of the adults had paid much attention to the dragon when Mellis had said he was an injured chupo. But now Zing was nosing at the fire in the hearth, obviously trying to figure out how to regain his powers.
"What's the chupo doing?" Krub said, sounding suspicious.
"Nothing." Mellis grabbed Zing. "Er, Uncle, our guests are tired from their long trip. Shall we show them to their beds?"
Perda awoke after a restless night. When she opened her eyes, she was confused. "Where am I?" she thought. Then she remembered. "Oh yeah. Zann and I are trapped in Terrica."
The evening before, Mellis had taken them to her bedroom, which contained only a thick mat stuffed with straw. She and Vilkor had brought in similar straw beds for Perda and Zann.
Perda sat up and yawned. Zann was still asleep. But Mellis was awake. She was searching the floor in the corners of the room.
"What are you looking for?" Perda asked sleepily.
Mellis straightened up, looking anxious. Before she could answer, the door flew open.
"Time to get moving," Vilkor announced. "Mellis, you quit digging earlier yesterday. I hope you'll make up the time today."
Zann finally woke up. "Where am I?" he mumbled.
"Zann and I will help her dig the well," Perda told Vilkor. "After all, it was our fault she had to stop yesterday."
"You will?" Vilkor looked impressed. "Wonderful! I'll make sure you all have a double helping of porridge for breakfast."
"Thanks," Mellis said after her uncle left. "You don't really have to help dig."
"We don't mind." Zann appeared fully awake by now. He nudged Zing with his foot to wake him up.

After two helpings of porridge, they started the long hike to the well site. Zann carried Zing until they were out of sight of the farmhouse and then released him from the bag. The girls carried an assortment of tools.
"Why did you decide to dig your new well so far from the farmhouse?" Perda asked. "Won't it be difficult to haul water so far?"

"Yes, but water is scarce in this part of Terrica," Mellis explained. "My uncle noticed that small tree and figured there must be water in that spot. He suggested I pull out the tree and dig the well exactly where it was growing. But I didn't have the heart to do that. I dug next to it instead."
Perda shook her head. "It's strange to think how different things are here from back home in Magica. We just conjure whatever we need."
Mellis shot her a sidelong look. "Will you tell me more about Magica? I still don't understand where it is or how you got here."
"Sure," Zann said. "Magica is great! Well, it usually is. Not long ago this evil guy named Morb decided to take over, and . . ."
He told Mellis the whole story, with Perda helping. Mellis' eyes grew wide as she listened. Perda wondered if she believed what they were telling her.
Finally they reached the well site. The day was growing hotter. Zann mopped his brow with the back of his arm.
"We'd better start digging," he said.
"Wait." Perda dropped her shovel. "First let's try to open the wormhole again."
She and Zann went to the spot where they'd emerged from the wormhole. But it still didn't appear.
"Let's stop wasting energy," Perda said at last.
Mellis was already digging. Perda and Zann each picked up a shovel and joined her. Soon the three of them had scooped out a wide but shallow hole.
By the time they stopped to eat lunch, the hole was as deep as the height of a tall man.
"This is great." Mellis peered into the dark, damp hole. "With all three of us working, we might strike water today! Uncle Vilkor will be so pleased if that happens."
"Uncle Vilkor could make it happen faster if he picked up a shovel himself," Zann grumbled.
Perda was too tired to say anything. Every muscle in her body was sore. Her throat ached with thirst. She imagined gulping down a tall, cool glass of airberry juice.
Mellis finished her lunch quickly. "I'll take a turn in the hole," she said. "Can one of you please help me get down there?"
Zann climbed to his feet and held onto Mellis' hands, lowering her into the hole until she could safely drop down.
"I wonder if there's enough magic energy to make a pitcher of airberry juice," Perda said as Zann flopped down beside her again. "Should we try?"
Zann groaned. "I'm not sure I have enough strength to create friction," he said. "It does sound tasty though, so—"
"Hey!" Mellis called up from the hole. "Could one of you hand me the ax? I've hit a big root."
That made Perda curious enough to stand up and grab the ax from Mellis' bag. "A root? From what?" she asked as she peered into the hole.
Mellis looked up and shrugged. "I'm not sure. It's too big to belong to that tiny tree. Maybe there was a larger tree here once."
Perda carefully handed the ax down to Mellis. "Have you hit any water yet?"
"No," Mellis said. "But the dirt is getting quite damp. I think we're very close."
"Cool." Zann kneeled next to Perda. "I'll take the next turn down there if you want."
Mellis nodded. She hoisted the ax and swung it at a gnarled root at the bottom of the hole. Once, twice, then . . .
"Whoa!" Mellis cried, falling back.

Perda felt something come rushing up and out of the well. It wasn't water, but a mighty swirling rainbow of light and air. It roared up and filled the air so that Perda could barely see Zann beside her.
"What's happening?" Zann shouted.
Perda couldn't answer. For a second she was terrified.
Then she gasped as she felt sudden strength course through her. Could it be . . . ?
Acting on a hunch, she snapped her fingers. An overflowing pitcher of airberry juice appeared in front of her. And then another, and another, spilling juice onto the dusty ground.
"Zann!" she cried. "It's magic energy!"

Zann felt hope surge through him, along with new energy. He ripped the bandage from his arm. Zira's purple goo had made the scrape feel better, but the injury was still visible. With one snap of his fingers, Zann healed it completely.
"It's true!" he cried, dancing around. "Our magic . . . is back!"

Zing whistled and flew around in a circle, shooting blasts of flame. Perda laughed and started dancing along with Zann. They jumped and spun as the geyser of magic energy poured out of the well, drifting across the land.
Suddenly Perda stopped and pointed. "Look!"

Zann's gaze had been focused on Perda, who looked prettier than ever as she laughed and danced. Now he glanced around. The drab landscape surrounding them was changing. Bright green grass sprouted rapidly, replacing the dry brownish stuff. Flowers began to bloom. Moss crept out to cover the boulders with soft green. Even the scrawny little tree looked stronger and taller.

"Careful, Zing!" Zann exclaimed as the little dragon zipped past the tree, almost setting it alight with his fiery breath. But the tree didn't burn. Zann wondered if that was because the air felt different now—moist and pleasant, with none of the baking heat of moments before.
"This is amazing," Perda said. "It must have something to do with that root. The magic started pouring out as soon as Mellis chopped through it."
"That makes sense," Zann agreed. "Oh! Speaking of Mellis, I hope this isn't freaking her out too much."
Perda looked into the hole and gasped. "Mellis! Are you okay?"
Zann hurried over. Mellis was huddled at the bottom of the hole. At first Zann thought she was watching the magic energy pour out from the severed root. Then he saw that her eyes were closed.
"Oh no," he said. "All that magic energy must have knocked her out!"
"We have to get her out of there." Perda held out her hand. "Grab my arm and lower me down there, and maybe we can—"
"Wait—we have magic again," Zann reminded her. "Let's try to levitate her out."
Perda's eyes widened. "You're right!" she exclaimed with a sheepish laugh. "I almost forgot."
They created friction and focused on lifting Mellis.
"Levitate," Zann murmured.
Slowly and carefully they brought Mellis up and out of the hole. Zing flew around, whistling anxiously until Mellis landed gently on the ground.
"Mellis!" Perda leaned over her. "Can you hear me?"
Mellis' hand twitched, and her eyes fluttered open. "Wh-what happened?" she asked.
"You released a bunch of magic energy," Zann said. "Look around and see!"
Mellis sat up. She gasped as she took in the scene around her. "Where are we?" Her voice was shaking.
Perda smiled. "We're in the same place," she said. "I guess the energy made stuff grow. And Zann and I can do magic again. Watch!"
She snapped her fingers and created a glass of water, which she handed to Mellis. Mellis stared at it, seeming afraid to drink it.
Zann was still thinking about what had happened. "That root contained magic," he said. "But how?"

"Different worlds get their magic energy in different ways," Perda reminded him. "Like in Atmo—remember? There, magic energy is created by the air itself. But in Magica it comes out into the air through the tree, or maybe from the vortex itself through the tree. Other worlds are all different. Some have weak energy, like Wyssa's home world—"
"Or Terrica, before now," Zann added.
Perda nodded. "Then there are worlds with extra strong magic, like Galvan. Remember how weird it felt to do magic there?"
Mellis looked overwhelmed. "But how could things change so suddenly?" She carefully set down the glass of water. "It's like we're not even in Terrica anymore!"
"Oh, we are," Zann assured her. "But now we can do magic."
"Maybe you can too," Perda said. "Give it a try—let's see!"
Mellis looked nervous. "Me, do magic? But I don't know how!"

"It's not that hard," Zann said. "Even really young kids can do basic stuff." He frowned as Zing zipped past. The little dragon was obviously happy to have his fire power back. He shot out a burst of flames that knocked over the water glass. "Hey, stop that, you overgrown swamp rat," Zann scolded him.

Perda smiled encouragingly at Mellis, ignoring Zing. "Just create friction. Rub your hands together like this." She demonstrated. "While you do that, picture what you want to create in your mind. It can be anything—maybe another glass of water?"

Mellis looked uncertain. But she rubbed her hands together and then squeezed her eyes shut, looking very focused. For a moment nothing happened, and Zann wondered if Terricans were like Voids—unable to do magic at all.

He shouted in surprise as rain abruptly began pelting down, as if a giant waterfall had just burst into existence overhead. He quickly snapped his fingers to create an umbrella. Perda did the same. Zing flew down to huddle beneath Zann's umbrella, chirping irritably about getting wet.
Perda moved over to cover Mellis with her umbrella.
"I think you just created rain," Perda said.
"I can't believe I did this." Mellis was staring, wide-eyed, at the puddles forming all around them. "And why is the rain pink?"
Zann shrugged. "Pink rain isn't as common as green or purple, but it's not that rare, either."
"Not in Magica," Perda said. "Things might be different here."
"Green? Purple?" Mellis looked baffled. "Rain isn't usually a color at all! It's just clear, like regular water."
"Hmm." Perda looked thoughtful. "We've seen other worlds with colorless rain."
Zann knew she was right, though he couldn't remember exactly which worlds.
"Mellis!" he exclaimed in alarm as Mellis' eyes fluttered shut again and she keeled over with a splash.
Perda leaned over Mellis, concerned. Then she looked over at Zann.
"She must be shocked by all of this," Perda said. "It was too much for her, especially after hours of hard digging."
"Yeah. Look! The rain is stopping," Zann said.
Perda lowered her umbrella. Zann was right. The pink downpour stopped as quickly as it had started. After a moment Perda and Zann were able to revive Mellis, though she seemed weak and disoriented.
"We'll take you home," Perda told the other girl. "You should probably lie down for a while."
Perda and Zann helped Mellis to her feet.
"Let's leave the tools here," Zann said. "We can come back for them later."
Perda nodded, putting an arm around Mellis. Zann did the same on the girl's other side.
"Lean on us while we walk," Zann told her.
Perda blinked as she realized what Zann had just said. "Walk?" She grinned. "We don't have to do that anymore. We can zap her home!"
Zann laughed. "Now I'm the one who's forgetting we can do magic again!" he said. He grabbed Mellis by the arm. "Got her?"
"Yep." Perda took hold of her other arm. "Ready?"
"Zap!" Zann shouted.
Splash!
The three of them landed in a large pink puddle in front of Mellis' house. Vilkor was standing outside, staring in confusion at the puddle.
"Aah!" he screamed when he saw them. "Where did you kids come from? You shouldn't sneak up on me like that!"
Perda immediately noticed that, aside from the pink rainwater, the magic energy hadn't reached this area. The landscape around the farm buildings was still drab and brown.
"Maybe the magic only works near the well," she said to Zann.
Zann was staring past her. "No, I think it's still coming," he said. "Look!"
Perda turned and saw a wave of green rolling toward them over the scrubby fields. Vilkor saw it, too, and screamed again.
"It's all right, Uncle," Mellis said weakly. "It's just, um, magic. It came out of the new well."
"What are you talking about?" Vilkor narrowed his eyes, seeming to forget about everything else. "We just need water from that well! Didn't you find any yet?"
"Not exactly," Zann said. "Instead of water, we struck magic energy. It's like your friend Zira's potions but better!"
"You won't need a well now," Perda added. "You should be able to create all the water you need through magic."

She hoped that was true. After all, she didn't know exactly how magic worked on Terrica or how good Terricans could be at performing it. Mellis had tried to create a glass of water and wound up creating an entire rainstorm.
Perda thought again about Galvan, the world with magic energy so strong that a simple spell could have unpredictable results.
"I wonder if Terrica will be like Galvan," she thought.

"Don't be ridiculous," Vilkor said. "Zira's potions are one thing. But the sort of thing you're talking about is impossible . . ." His words trailed off as the wave of magic energy reached them. Grasses and other plants sprang up around their feet, and a flower sprouted right under Zing. Surprised, the little dragon jumped and shot flames at it. The flower collapsed in a pile of ash, but dozens more soon grew to replace it.

Perda and the others took a few steps back as the pink puddle expanded into a small pond. The scrawny fruit trees in the orchard leafed out, and a flowering vine crept up the wall. It soon covered the farmhouse with sweet-scented pink blossoms.

Vilkor watched all of it. "How can this be happening?" he cried, smacking his forehead in confusion. He rushed to the little kitchen garden near the house. "My cabbages! I nearly turned them back into the soil yesterday because they were so small and weak. But look! They're now ready to eat!"
Zann scratched his head. "I guess the magic energy is helping everything, not just people," he said. "It doesn't work that way where we're from."
"Where you're from?" Vilkor's eyes went sharp and curious. "Come to think of it, I don't believe you kids ever told me exactly where that is."
Perda traded a glance with Zann. Should they tell the truth? Zann shrugged and opened his mouth as if to do so. But Perda spoke first.
"Just a faraway area, where we have magic," she said. She waved a hand vaguely in the direction of the well.

"Ah. The distant land beyond the mountains, eh?" Vilkor said. "I hear things are strange there indeed." He tapped his chin thoughtfully. "Zira never would tell anyone where or how she learned to make her potions. Perhaps she traveled to that part of Terrica in her youth."

Zann shot Perda a surprised look. She knew what he was thinking. He was wondering why she didn't just tell Vilkor they were from a different world. But even though Mellis already seemed like a friend, Perda didn't quite trust Vilkor. After all, what kind of man would force his young niece to dig a well all by herself?
Perda noticed that Mellis still looked pale. "Mellis needs to lie down," she told Vilkor. "She was caught in the stream of magic. We think it overcame her."
"It did, did it?" Vilkor shot his niece a slightly sour look. "Or is she trying to get out of finishing that well?"

Perda sighed. The entire world around him had changed. But Vilkor still didn't understand that he didn't need to worry about his silly well anymore. If they didn't do something to convince him, she was afraid he'd order poor Mellis back to digging right now!
Zann could see that Perda was feeling frustrated with Vilkor.
"I don't know why she didn't tell him that we're from Magica, not Terrica," Zann thought. "But I'm sure she had a good reason."
Perda tried once again to convince Vilkor that he didn't need a well anymore. Zann decided it was easier to show him how magic worked than to try to explain it.

"Watch this," Zann said. He rubbed his hands on his legs to create plenty of friction. Then he used an Enlarging spell to double the size of the pond in front of them. Next Zann turned the water blue and created a small wooden dock and a rowboat.
He glanced at Vilkor. The man's jaw had dropped in astonishment.
"How did you do that?" Vilkor asked, sinking onto a bench as if he didn't trust his legs to hold him upright.
"Easy. I used magic." Zann rubbed his hands together and then added an elaborate fountain to the middle of the pond. He shot a look toward Perda, wondering what she thought of his efforts.
"This cannot be happening." Vilkor glared at Zann suspiciously. "I must be asleep and dreaming."

Zann added a pretty shrub to the edge of the pond. "Anyone can do this, now that Terrica has magic." Thinking about Mellis' failure to create water, he added, "At least we think so. Why don't you give it a try?"
"Maybe he shouldn't," Perda whispered. "The magic energy seems kind of unpredictable so far, and besides—"
"No, it's fine," Zann assured her. "I didn't have any trouble with the spells I just did." He glanced proudly at the lovely pond.
Vilkor stood, looking intrigued. "What do I need to do?" he asked cautiously.
Zann quickly explained about friction and focusing words and the other basics of creating items. "Go ahead," he finished. "Try to create something, like a glass of water."
Vilkor still looked suspicious. But he followed Zann's instructions, rubbing his hands together. "Mmm . . . water," he said.
A rough pottery cup of water appeared in his hand. The man was so shocked, he nearly dropped it.
"It worked!" Vilkor exclaimed. "Can it really be true? Can I create anything I want?"
"Almost anything," Perda said. "You can't create people or animals. And you shouldn't create anything that might hurt others or . . ."
Vilkor was already rubbing his hands together again. "Wheel of fine cheese!" he shouted.
A large chunk of cheese landed with a thump in front of him. After that, Vilkor created a pair of silk pants for himself, along with a matching hat.
"Oh," he said, looking disappointed. "I wanted a feather in the hatband, but it's not there."
"Slow down," Zann said with a chuckle. "You're new to this, and your magic energy might be running low. Don't worry. It'll return after a short rest."
He noticed that Perda was watching Mellis and looking worried.
"Mellis still looks pale," Perda said. "All that magic energy might have made her ill. Maybe we should take her to see Zira."
"Zira?" Vilkor stopped playing with his new hat. "No! I don't want her to know what's going on here."
"What do you mean?" Zann asked.
Vilkor stroked his new silk pants. "This special magic thing is on my land," he said. "I don't want anyone else to know about it until I've figured out how best to, er, deal with it."
"It's okay," Mellis said. "I'm feeling better already."
"Hear that? She's fine." Suddenly Vilkor gasped. "What is that thing?" he cried in alarm.
Zann spun around, thinking about the rock trompers Mellis had told them about. And who knew what other wild, dangerous creatures might be in this world?
But all he saw was Zing. Until now, the little dragon had been resting in the shade of the flowers that had grown up around him. He'd finally stood up and walked to the bank of the pond.
"Oops," Zann whispered, realizing that they'd forgotten to refresh the chupo disguise.

But that was no big deal now, he realized. He rubbed a hand against his side. He had no idea what a chupo looked like, but he did his best. He used a Visual Confusion spell to make Zing look like the mud lizards he and Darb used to search for in the swamps of Magica when they were little kids.
Vilkor blinked, looking more startled than ever. "What's happening?" he said.
Mellis laughed and glanced at Zing. She really did look stronger now. The color had returned to her cheeks, and her eyes were bright. She snapped her fingers.
"Chupo," she whispered just loudly enough for Zann and Perda to hear her.
The Visual Confusion spell shifted. Now Zing looked brown and furry, with a pair of curved fangs emerging from a blunt snout.
"See, Uncle?" Mellis said. "It's just a chupo. You're probably a little light-headed from doing all that magic. It's not surprising if you're imagining things."

"Hmm." Vilkor looked suspicious again. Just then he noticed a plump purple fruit hanging from a nearby tree. "Would you look at that!" he exclaimed. "I thought that tree would never bear fruit. And the fruit is so large! I can charge a premium for those at the village market . . ."
He was still muttering with delight as he rushed over to pick the fruit.
"Are you sure you don't want to see Zira, just in case?" Perda asked Mellis.
Mellis shook her head. "I'm feeling better and better," she said. "Besides, I don't really trust Zira—or her right-hand man, either."
Zann wasn't sure what she meant by that. Before he could ask, though, Zira strode into view.
"What in Terrica is going on here?" she asked.
Perda stared at Zira, thinking about what Mellis had just said about not trusting her. "Er, nothing," she said.
But Vilkor rushed over to Zira, clutching the purple fruit. "Look!" he cried. "Everything is growing! And it's all because of my new well!"
Zann leaned closer to Perda. "So much for keeping everything a secret," he whispered. "I guess Vilkor is too excited to stay quiet."

Perda nodded, though she was only half listening to Zann. She was still watching Zira. The woman listened to Vilkor's babbled explanation and then looked around. Perda saw something in her gaze change.
"There's something about her eyes," Perda thought. "They look suspicious, like she's plotting something."

"I see," Zira said, her voice suddenly less confused and more amiable. "Congratulations on your good fortune, dear friend." She patted Vilkor's arm. "Perhaps if you show me this magical well, I can help you protect it from the greed of others."
"Thanks, Zira." Vilkor grinned at her. "You've always been a true friend to me. That's no surprise, as the two of us are clearly the smartest people in the village. Here—have a new hat."

He rubbed his hands together. A moment later another fancy hat appeared. Zira stared at it and then glanced at Vilkor's hands. Perda could see what the woman was thinking. She was noting exactly what Vilkor had done to make the hat appear.
"Thank you, Vilkor," Zira said. "Now, shall we visit your well?"
Zann leaned closer to Perda again. "Let's go with them," he whispered eagerly. "Now that there's all this magic energy around, I bet we can open the wormhole and go home."
"I suppose you're right." Perda couldn't shake the idea that Zira might be planning trouble. "Mellis said she didn't trust Zira though. What if she tries something sneaky?"
Zann shrugged. "Like what? Now that magic is spreading in this world, nobody can control it."
"I guess that's true," Perda said. "Maybe we should give Mellis a few more magic lessons before we leave though."
"Sure," Zann said. "But let's make it quick. We've already been missing for more than a day, and I'm sure our families and friends are worried."

Perda nodded. She wondered how long it had taken Darb and Gliss to rush back to the lab and tell everyone about the weird new wormhole in Wormwood. Would Nax and Asta try to come through it to rescue her and Zann?
She pushed aside those thoughts as she realized Vilkor was pointing at them. He was telling Zira how they'd arrived suddenly at the farmhouse, seemingly out of thin air.
"You did that with magic, right?" Vilkor said. "Perhaps that magic would save us from needing to walk all the way to the well?"
"Sure," Zann said. "We can zap there immediately."
Perda could tell he was about to explain how to do it. "Join hands," she said before he could say anything else. "Zann and I will transport everyone to the well."

Zira looked curious, and Vilkor looked a little nervous. But they did as Perda said. Soon all five of them were holding hands in a line, with Zann and Perda at either end. Zann held onto Zing's tail with his free hand.
"Ready?" Perda said. She rubbed her free hand against her side. "Zap!"

When they landed, the adults immediately started babbling about the Zap. But Perda barely heard them. The place looked so different! There were more shrubs and trees now. And the original tree wasn't a scraggly sapling anymore. It had grown into a strong, medium-size tree, large enough to shade the well. The well itself was now filled with sparkling, rainbow-colored water.
"Is that water?" Vilkor asked. "It looks strange!"

Perda saw that he was still clutching the pottery cup he'd created earlier. "Scoop some out," she said. She was a little curious about the colorful water. "You should be able to tell if it's regular water by the taste."
"I'm not tasting that!" Vilkor looked alarmed. "What if it's poisoned or enchanted with evil spells?"
Zira stepped forward. "I'll taste it."
She snatched the pottery cup from Vilkor's hand and then dipped it into the overflowing well. She lifted the cup toward her lips. Before she was able to take a sip, the cup cracked down the side.
"Oh, dear," Vilkor said as the water dribbled onto the ground.
Zira frowned. "Perhaps you were right after all, Vilkor." She tossed the cup away. "There's something very wrong with this water. Perhaps dangerously so."
Perda stared at the cracked cup on the ground. For some reason it looked vaguely familiar, but she didn't spend much time thinking about that. She was focused on Zira.
"Am I imagining things," she thought, or had the woman squeezed the cup with her hand to make it crack?
"What good is a well if you can't drink the water?" Vilkor complained. He glared at Mellis as if he blamed her for the whole situation.
Zann rolled his eyes. "He still doesn't get it," he whispered to Perda.

Before Perda could answer, Zira spoke again. "Never mind that, my friend," she said to Vilkor. "We'll get to the bottom of it. In the meantime we should post guards immediately to keep everyone else away until we figure out what's—"

She was interrupted by a wild howl that sent chills down Perda's spine. A moment later a creature Perda had never seen before stepped into view from behind a shrub. It was the size of a small human, covered in rough brown fur. Sharp, crooked teeth stuck out of a wide mouth that was dripping with slime. The creature walked on four legs, though its crooked hind legs were much shorter than its forelegs, which barely touched the ground as it lurched along.
Mellis gasped in terror. "Oh, no!" she cried. "A gorzog!"
The gorzog crept closer, growling and spitting foul-smelling mucus.
"Gorzogs are the most dangerous creatures in this part of Terrica," Mellis warned Zann and Perda, her voice shaking. "They're totally fearless and will eat anything—or anyone—they can grab."

The gorzog was ugly, but Zann didn't think it looked that scary. It wasn't even very big. But Zann's travels to other worlds had taught him that creatures didn't have to look scary to be very dangerous.
"Find a weapon," Vilkor said, grabbing one of the shovels the kids had left by the well.
Mellis darted toward another shovel. At that moment the gorzog leaped in the same direction. Its hind legs propelled it farther than Zann expected.
It landed in front of Mellis, who screamed and tried to grab the shovel. The gorzog blocked her, growling loudly.
"I'm coming!" Perda cried, rushing forward.
"No, stop!" Vilkor cried. "It's too late for my niece, but we can still save ourselves!"
Zann shot the man a disgusted look. "He isn't even going to try to rescue her!" he thought.
Perda reached Mellis' side. "Shield!" she shouted, clapping her hands.
A translucent, glowing, green wall appeared between the girls and the gorzog. The creature lunged forward, hit the shield, and fell back with an irritated shriek.

Zann gulped as the frustrated gorzog turned to face him. He thought about creating a Shield spell to protect himself and the two adults. Before he could, Zing flew past him, shooting fire in the gorzog's direction.
"Go, Zing!" Zann shouted as the gorzog flinched at the flames. Perda and Mellis looked hopeful.
But the two adults looked perplexed. "A flying chupo?" Zira muttered, narrowing her eyes. "Impossible!"
"Is that chupo shooting fire out of its mouth?" Vilkor scratched his head, seeming to forget about the gorzog for a moment.
