The gorzog crouched low to the ground, tracking Zing with its yellowish eyes. Suddenly it jumped up and spat a huge wad of goo at the little dragon.
"Zing! No!" Zann cried as his pet fell to the ground. The dragon tried to free his legs and wings from the gorzog's sticky spit.
"Zing! Try singing!" Perda called.
"Good idea," Zann said. "Sing, little buddy, sing!"
He wasn't sure if the fire whistler's distinctive song would work the same way it did in Magica. There, it hypnotized most creatures, though humans and other dragons were immune.

Zing wriggled and writhed. His red tongue flicked in and out as he tried to clear the sticky spit from his snout. Zann held his breath. The gorzog was creeping closer, eyes locked on the helpless dragon.
Finally Zing managed to whistle a weak tune. The gorzog stopped, though Zann couldn't tell if it was because it was hypnotized or merely surprised.
Out of the corner of his eye, Zann noticed that Perda had dismissed the Shield spell. Mellis was backing away, but Perda was tiptoeing closer to the gorzog.
"What is she doing?" Vilkor said. "The gorzog is distracted by that chupo. This is our chance to run away!"
"Or perhaps we could use magic to get away," Zira said. "What did you call it? A Zap?"

Zann ignored both of them. "Sing louder, Zing," he said. He wasn't sure what Perda had in mind, but he planned to back her up if he could. He took a step closer to the gorzog, hoping to distract its attention away from her and Zing.
The gorzog growled at Zann. It stared at him and then at Zing. It seemed to be trying to decide which prey looked tastier.
Suddenly Perda leaped forward. Zann guessed she'd used magic to propel herself farther than she could have jumped on her own. She landed right next to the gorzog.
"Perda!" Mellis cried. "What are you doing?"
Perda didn't look around or even flinch as the gorzog spun to face her. She reached out and tapped the monster on the head, while rubbing her side with her other hand.
"Shackle," she said loudly.
The gorzog tried to leap at her. But as it did, magical shackles appeared on its legs, binding all four limbs together. It flopped forward, its gnashing teeth only an inch from Perda.
"Whoa!" Zann laughed and hurried forward. "That was awesome!"
"Thanks." Perda glanced down at the gorzog. "Wow, this thing is even uglier up close."

Zann kneeled beside Zing, who was still struggling against the sticky spit. "Hold still, buddy," he said. He rubbed his hands together and used a Cleaning spell to remove the disgusting goo. Zing immediately leaped into the air and flew around the helpless gorzog. The dragon spat angry flames, though Zann noticed he didn't get too close to the creature.
"Quite impressive, young lady," Vilkor said. He hurried forward to give Mellis a hug. "I'm glad you're safe. I don't know what I'd do without you, Mellis."
Zann stepped closer to Perda. "He wasn't worried about that a few seconds ago," he whispered. "He was ready to run away and let her become the gorzog's lunch!"
"That's why we have to make sure she knows how to do magic before we leave," Perda whispered back.
"Okay. But how are we going to get her away from those two?" Zann shot a glance toward the adults. Vilkor was still patting his niece on the shoulder, while Zira was watching Zing fly around.
"That's not really a common chupo, is it?" Zira asked loudly, turning toward Zann and Perda. "I've never seen nor heard of one that could fly and breathe fire."
Zann gulped, thinking fast. "Um, maybe the magic from the well gave it new powers?"
"No, I think there's something you're not telling us." Zira folded her arms over her chest, her steely gaze taking in Zann, Perda, and Zing. "I think you traveled to Terrica from another world!"
Perda was startled by the certainty in Zira's eyes as she accused her and Zann of being from another world.
"How do you know there are other worlds?" Zann blurted out.
Zira smiled. "So it's true?"
"Other worlds?" Vilkor let out a snort. "What a ridiculous idea!"
Zira kept smiling. "It explains everything: their magic abilities, the flying chupo . . . And the way you kids defeated the gorzog was quite impressive. How did you do it?"
Perda still didn't trust Zira. She shot Zann a glance, hoping to stop him from answering. But he didn't notice.

"First, Perda used a Shield spell," he began. "Then she used a Shackle spell." He quickly explained how both spells were done. Zira asked several questions. Zann gave her more basic magic tips about friction, focusing words, and directing the mind.
"I wish Zann would stop talking," Perda thought. But now it was too late. She tried to tell herself she was worried for nothing. After all, soon everyone in Terrica would be able to do magic anyway.
"I see," Zira said at last. "Perhaps I'll try it myself."
She rubbed her hands together, glancing around the area. Her eyes landed on the well, and she smiled.
"Protect," she murmured.

Suddenly a tall stone wall appeared, completely surrounding the well. The only thing Perda could see was the top of the tree sticking out over the wall. Well, that and the magic energy still seeping out in all directions. Now instead of drifting along the ground, it slid over the wall and dissipated.
"Very impressive!" Vilkor said. "But now how am I supposed to reach my well?"
"The water is dangerous, my friend," Zira said. "Remember? This will keep our fellow villagers safe until we figure out how to purify it."
"Wow, Zira is learning fast," Perda whispered to Zann and Mellis, feeling a little unnerved. "How did she figure out how to do such a large spell so quickly?"
"She is known to be very wise," Mellis whispered back.
"She must be," Zann murmured. "She's the only one in Terrica who believes other worlds exist."
"She doesn't just believe it," Perda said. "We never mentioned being from another world to anyone here except Mellis. Zira must have known about other worlds even before we arrived!"
Zing, who was still flying overhead, whistled loudly.
A moment later Vilkor let out a shout. "Gorzogs!" He pointed toward the horizon. "A whole herd of them is headed this way!"
"Let's get out of here!" Zann said, whistling for Zing.
"Wait." Perda said. The shackled gorzog still struggled against the magical restraints, drooling and snarling. "We can't leave it here like this."
Vilkor shrugged. "Why not? When the other gorzogs arrive, they'll see that it's helpless and devour it. That will decrease the local population by one."
He obviously considered that a good thing. Perda hesitated, wondering if he was right.
But Mellis pulled her hand out of her uncle's. "No!" she cried. "A gorzog can't help its nature. It would be cruel to leave it to be torn apart."
She came closer, flinching when the gorzog growled at her. "Unshackle," she said, rubbing her hands together.
The gorzog's shackles remained intact, though sparks bounced off them, exploding in the air. Mellis ducked, and the gorzog whined fearfully.
"You can't remove someone else's Shackle spell," Zann said. "Only the person who created it can undo it."
Perda stepped forward. "And that is me." She looked back at the others. "Get ready to zap away as soon as I release the gorzog."
She unshackled the gorzog, and then everyone held hands.
"Zap!" Zira shouted.

They landed in a village. The street was narrow and unpaved and lined with shabby huts. However, the magic energy had clearly arrived. Green grass and bright flowers sprouted everywhere, and colorful fruit hung from the trees. A bush covered in vibrant purple berries was visible over the walled yard of the nearest hut.
"I wish Darb were here to identify those berries," Perda thought. "I feel as if I've seen them before, but I can't remember where."
"Oh!" Vilkor looked around. "You've brought us to your home, Zira. I thought we were heading to my house."
"I thought so too," Zann said. "I was about to zap us there, but Zira was faster."
Perda nodded, surprised once again. Zapping was pretty basic magic, but it took time to learn how to land in a specific spot. Zira had done it on her first try!
Zira had a sly smile. "Let's step inside, Vilkor. We have much to discuss."
The two adults disappeared into the hut.
"I guess we're not part of the discussion," Zann said. "Let's zap back to the well and try to open the wormhole."
"We can't go now." Mellis looked nervous. "Those gorzogs will still be sniffing around."

"They can't climb that wall, can they?" Perda asked. "We could zap ourselves inside it." She grinned at Zann, remembering all the times he'd carelessly landed in a puddle or pond. "Zann is good at zapping into water."
Just then several people raced into view on the street.
"What's happening?" cried a wild-eyed woman.
A tall man tore at his hair. "The whole world is changing!" he wailed. "It's the end of time!"
"Where's the council?" A stout man shoved past the others. "We need to know what they plan to do about all of this!"
Vilkor and Zira came back outside.
"Calm down, everyone!" Vilkor cried.

"There's no need to panic," Zira added loudly. "Everything is under control. Go home, and I'll update you as needed." She noticed the three kids and Zing. "That goes for you too. Return to Vilkor's house and stay there."

Zann woke up the next morning to the sound of a bird singing outside the window. For a second he thought he was back in Swamp Bottom. The bird's song sounded a lot like one he'd heard most mornings there.
But when he opened his eyes, he sighed. "I'm still in Terrica," he thought. He sat up and looked out the window, but the bird was hidden in a lush tree outside.
"I guess birds are similar in every world," he said with a yawn.
The room was empty. Zann dressed quickly and then headed out to the main room. He found Perda and Mellis eating breakfast at the table.
"Here's something you might like," Perda was saying. She snapped her fingers, and a platter of puckerberry pancakes appeared.
Mellis took a bite. "Wow!" she said. "These taste a lot better than porridge."
Zann joined the girls at the table. "After breakfast, we'll give you a few more magic lessons," he said. "Then Perda and I can head to the wormhole."
Mellis took another bite of the pancakes. "My friend Anso from the village loves sweet things," she said. "Will you teach him to make some of these foods before you leave?"
"Sure," Perda said. "We'll zap to the village after we finish eating. We'll teach you and your friends everything you want to know."
"No, you won't." Vilkor strode into the room just in time to hear her. Zira was right behind him. "We don't want you to tell anyone about magic."
"What?" Zann traded a confused look with Perda and Mellis. "It's not like magic is a secret. Everybody can see that things are changing."
"They see only that plants are growing and there's more water around," Zira said. "They don't know why. And it's better that way."
"What do you mean?" Zann asked.

Vilkor's eyes gleamed. "Who knows what would happen if everyone could use magic?" he said. "It's better for everyone if Zira and I are in charge. We can provide magical services for anyone who needs them."
"Right," Zira said. "It's safer if only Vilkor and I and perhaps a few additional people—"
"What?" Vilkor glanced at her. "We didn't talk about including anyone else."

Zira patted his arm. "Not yet. First, we need to determine how far this magic energy has spread from the well. If it has reached beyond our village, we'll need local deputies in other villages to help control—er, I mean, manage things."
"That's not fair," Perda said with a frown. "Magic should be for everyone. Besides, people will figure it out on their own soon enough."
Zira narrowed her eyes at Zann and Perda. "Weren't you visitors talking about going back to your own world?"
Vilkor laughed. "Stop humoring them with this silly talk of other worlds."
"Well, wherever they came from, I think they should return there soon," Zira said.
"Or what?" Perda demanded.
Vilkor frowned. "How dare you speak so insolently, girl!"
Zira didn't say a word to Perda, but Zann saw her gray eyes grow narrow. A second later Perda gasped.
"Let's get out of here," Perda said. She grabbed Zann and Mellis and dragged them toward the door.
Once they were outside, Zann turned to face her. "What was that all about?" he asked. "I thought you were going to tell Zira off. Instead you ran away! That's not like you."
"I know." Perda slumped onto a bench. "But I was too startled to stay. Zira sent me a mental message!"
Zann was startled now too. "But that's really advanced magic! We haven't even studied it in school yet."
"I know. I don't know how she did it, but she did." Perda bit her lip. "She said that if we tell anyone the truth, she'll send a pack of hungry gorzogs after Mellis!"
"What?" Mellis cried, looking horrified.

"Don't worry. We won't let her do that." Perda glanced at Zann, looking troubled. "Normally, mental messages can only be done at very close range. I wasn't standing that close to Zira, and I wasn't looking directly at her either. So how was she able to send that message into my mind?"

Zann thought about that. His grandfather, Boz, could send mental messages from a distance to his Magic Master friends. But most ordinary Magicians didn't bother with the difficult spell at all. It was much easier to use message moths or other methods to communicate.
"Zira is catching on to magic so fast that it's scary," he said. "Do you think she'd really try to hurt Mellis?"
"I don't know." Perda stood and grabbed Mellis by the hand. "But don't worry, Mellis. Zann and I won't leave Terrica until we're sure you're safe."
"Th-thanks." Mellis still looked nervous.
"And we'll figure out a way to make sure those two are going to share magic with everyone too," Perda said.
"Do we really need to get involved in that?" Zann asked. "Like you said, people will figure it out on their own."
Mellis nodded. "You're right. And your families must be terribly worried about you. You should go home. Zira will have no reason to hurt me if I go along with their plan."
"But their plan isn't right!" Perda exclaimed.

"I know." Mellis shrugged. "But I doubt it will last long. My uncle can be shallow and greedy—and cowardly—but he's not evil. Besides, he's terrible at keeping a secret." She chuckled. "He'll probably accidentally tell people about magic before long. What's the harm in letting him and Zira play magic rulers until then?"
Zann thought Mellis had a good point. But Perda shook her head.
"You may be right about your uncle, but I don't trust Zira one bit," she said. "We're staying."
By the next afternoon, Perda knew she'd been right to insist on staying in Terrica. "This is wild," she whispered to Zann and Mellis.

The three of them were at the edge of the village green. Vilkor was in the center of the green, standing on a golden dais he'd created. Zira was seated behind him. Dozens of villagers were gathered around the dais, chanting Vilkor's name.
"Next, please!" Vilkor shouted. He pointed at a woman in the crowd. "You there. Come forward and tell me what you wish me to provide for you."
The woman shuffled forward. "Thank you, Vilkor," she said. "My cloak is old and worn." She fingered the tattered garment she was wearing. "May I please have a new one?"

"Yes, I will do this for you." Vilkor closed his eyes, waved his arms dramatically and chanted a few nonsense words, and then clapped his hands. A beautiful cloak appeared. The crowd gasped. The woman dropped to her knees as Vilkor stepped forward to drape the cloak around her thin shoulders.
"Thank you, Vilkor!" the woman cried. "Thank you so much!"
"This is ridiculous," Perda muttered, feeling annoyed. "He's trying to fool everyone with all that muttering and arm waving. It's the clap that creates friction."
"I know that, and you know that," Zann said. "But we can't tell anyone or Zira might punish Mellis."
Perda glanced toward Zira. The woman had stayed close to Vilkor all day, but she was letting him get all the attention. "Hmm," Perda thought. "I wonder why."
Another villager stepped forward.
"That's my friend Anso's father," Mellis said.
"My family has run out of bread," the man said. "We have no grain to make more. Please help me."
"Oh no," Mellis said.
"Of course, of course." Vilkor went through his routine again, ending with a clap and the appearance of a small loaf of bread.
"Thank you," the man said as he accepted it. "But you see, I have a growing son, and my wife is ill. Could I have more bread so we all might have enough to eat?"

Vilkor frowned. "How do I know you will share it with your family, rather than bartering it away to your own benefit? If your wife and son wish to have more to eat, they can come and beg me for bread themselves."
"But my wife is ill, as I said," the man protested. "My son is staying with her in case her condition grows worse."
"Begone!" Vilkor insisted. "Do not question my decisions, or next time you might receive nothing at all!"
Mellis gasped.
Zann winced. "Wow! All this power is really going to Vilkor's head."
"I have to help Anso and his family," Mellis said.
Perda nodded as she watched Anso's father make his way through the crowd. The man looked sad. "Come with me," Perda said.
She hurried to intercept the man as he reached the edge of the green. Zann and Mellis followed.
The man saw them coming and smiled, but his eyes remained worried.
"Hello, Mellis," he said. "I hope you'll come to visit Anso soon. He's been busy helping his mother, but I know he'd love to see you."
"We saw what just happened," Perda said before Mellis could respond. "Come with us and we'll help you."
The man looked surprised. But he followed Perda to a deserted alley. She created several loaves of bread, along with cheese and fruit and a bag to carry it in.
"Thank you!" The man looked overwhelmed. "But how are you doing that? I thought only Vilkor had gained the power of magic."
"That's what he wants you to think," Zann said.
Perda nodded. "Anyone can do magic. All you have to do is create friction, and then—"
"Perda! No!" Mellis looked frightened. "What if Zira finds out?"
"Heads up!" Zann hissed. "Isn't that Zira's friend, what's his name?"
"Krub," Perda said, recognizing the man. He walked past the end of the alley without noticing them.
"Whew," Mellis said. "That was a close call. Krub always does everything Zira says. He probably would have told her about seeing us here."
Anso's father looked nervous too. "Thank you, young friends," he said, clutching the bag of food to his chest. "I'd better go home and check on my wife."
He scurried away. Perda was disappointed that she hadn't had the chance to teach him basic magic. But she could tell that Mellis was relieved.
"I know you're scared," she told the Terrican girl. "But surely by now you see that we have to stop this. What your uncle and Zira are doing is wrong."
"I know." Mellis looked miserable. "I hate seeing my uncle force everyone to grovel before him. But what can we do?"
"We can stand up to them," Zann said. "We have to."
Perda smiled at him, glad that he was backing her up. She'd thought he might not, since he was so eager to return to Magica the day before.
She wanted to go home too. She missed her family and friends, and she hated that they were surely worried sick about her and Zann. But they would understand when they heard the whole story.
"What do you say?" Perda asked Mellis. "Will you help us put a stop to this?"

Mellis hesitated. "I'll try. But I still don't believe my uncle will be able to keep up this charade for long. In the meantime, will you teach me more magic? Then I can start teaching Anso and some of the other kids in secret. That way we'll be ready once the truth finally comes out."
It wasn't quite the plan Perda would have chosen. But she had to admit it sounded a lot safer for Mellis, at least while Vilkor and Zira were in charge.
"Okay," she said. "Let's do it."
"Are you sure this will work?" Mellis stood, trembling, on the roof of an abandoned building at the edge of the village.
Zann gave her a thumbs-up. "Just do what we taught you," he called. "Deceleration spells are pretty easy."
"And don't worry," Perda added. "If it looks like you're in trouble, Zann and I will stop you before you hit the ground."
Zann smiled at Perda. It was fun working with her to teach Mellis basic magic skills. They'd been at it since seeing Vilkor at the village green the day before.
"Okay, here I go!" Mellis glanced at Zing, who was flying in lazy circles nearby.
She stepped off the edge of the roof. Zann held his breath. "Can she do it?" he thought. He rubbed a hand against his leg, just in case he needed to save her.
But halfway down, Mellis' fall slowed—and then stopped. She floated in midair.
"Hey!" she cried, sounding surprised and delighted. "I did it! I decelerated!"
"You did more than that," Perda said. "You decelerated so much that now you're levitating! I guess we don't need to bother teaching you that now."
Zann laughed. "Yeah. You're a fast learner, Mellis!"
Mellis floated the rest of the way down. "Thanks," she said. "Magic is fun!"
Zann grinned. "Okay, here's a pop quiz. Create a chair so I can sit down."
Mellis laughed and snapped her fingers. A lounge chair appeared. Zann flopped onto it.
"Now do a Vanishing spell," Perda said.
Mellis snapped her fingers again. The lounge chair became invisible, but Zann could still feel it.
"Now do a Shackle spell," Zann said.
"Okay," Mellis said.
Suddenly Zann felt shackles on his wrists.
"Hey!" Zann laughed. "Unshackle me!"
Mellis smiled as she pretended to be confused. "Hmm, I'm not sure I remember how to do that."
Perda laughed, and Zing flew down and shot a playful spurt of flame at Zann.
Zann laughed too. But then he noticed Zira walking past. He quickly hid the shackles and stood up.
"Oh, hello, kids," Zira said. "It's a lovely day, isn't it? But I'm afraid I have no time for small talk. I'm late for a meeting with Krub."
She hurried on and disappeared around a corner. Zann and the girls exchanged a worried look.
"Do you think she guessed what we're doing?" Mellis wondered.
Perda shrugged. "I doubt it. She was walking pretty fast. But never mind her. Unshackle Zann, and then we'll teach you more."
By the next morning, Zann and Perda had taught Mellis every spell they knew. After breakfast they reviewed a few things.
"Try displacing the water from the pond," Zann suggested. "But don't worry if you're only able to move part of it. Displacement spells are difficult, and they use lots of energy."
Mellis rubbed her hands together, causing sparks to fly. Then she pointed at the pond.
Zann and Perda gasped and jumped back as all the water flew up in the air. It disappeared into the sky.
"Yikes!" Mellis said. "Did I do it wrong?"
"No." Perda looked impressed. "But you might have used a little too much energy."
Zann squinted upward. After a moment the pond water reappeared. "Look out!" he cried.
The water splashed down, splattering everywhere.
"Oops," Mellis said.
"Don't worry," Perda said. "You'll soon have better control of your magic energy."

Zann nodded. "When I was younger, I once tried to create a cookie under the table because I didn't like my dinner. But I accidentally created ten cookies, and my parents caught me." He grinned sheepishly at the memory.
Then he sighed. Thinking about his family made him miss them.
Perda seemed to be feeling the same way. "I think we've taught you everything we can," she told Mellis. "Now you just need to practice."

Mellis looked sad. "Does that mean you're leaving Terrica? I understand. You must miss your home world. Can I come along to say good-bye? I've been meaning to visit the well anyway. I think I lost something out there."
Just then Zira and Krub zapped into view. "Is your uncle home?" Zira asked.
"He's inside," Mellis said.
The two adults disappeared into the farmhouse.
"I wonder if Krub knows the truth about magic," Perda said. "He and Zira seem pretty close."
Before Zann could respond, they all heard raised voices inside. Vilkor seemed to be arguing with the other two.
"Let's go while they're distracted," Mellis said. "I don't want my uncle to ask where we're going."
They zapped to the well. Zann was startled to find the area mobbed with people.
"What's going on?" Perda asked as an excited-looking woman bumped into her.
Zann glanced at the wall Zira had created around the well and the tree. Lots of people were touching it or gazing at it.
"I guess people heard where the magic energy came from," he said. "I wonder if Vilkor and Zira know that."

Mellis looked worried. "They'll be angry when they find out." She cleared her throat. "Attention, everyone!" she said, using a Swelling spell to make her voice louder than normal. "This is private property. Please disperse!"
Only a few people seemed to hear her. But none of them listened.
"Just get out of here as soon as we leave," Perda suggested. "That way nobody can blame you for this."
Zann nodded and grabbed Zing. "We'll miss you, Mellis," he said. "Maybe we'll visit again some time."
"That would be great," Mellis said. "I'll miss you both. Thanks for everything!"
They all hugged. Then Zann and Perda created a Mutual Shackle spell so either of them could undo it. Zann also shackled himself to Zing.
"You should zap us inside the wall," Zann said. "You're much more accurate at that sort of thing."
Perda nodded. "Zap!"
Thump!
"Oof!" Perda cried out as she, Zann, and Zing fell back onto the ground just outside the wall.
"A Shield spell!" Zann rubbed his shoulder where he'd bumped it. "It felt like a strong one too."
Perda frowned. "Zira saw me create the Shield spell to stop the gorzogs. She must have figured out how to do one herself."
Mellis hurried forward. "Are you okay?" she asked. "What happened?"
Perda and Zann quickly explained.
"But why would she want to shield the well?" Zann said.
"She wants to control the source of magic," Perda said grimly. "This makes me worry that Mellis isn't going to be safe here without us."
Zann shrugged. "So let's take her back to Magica."

"That's exactly what I was thinking," Perda said. "What do you say, Mellis? You can practice your magic even more easily in Magica. We can tell Zann's parents and grandfather what's going on here and ask them to help."

Mellis didn't say anything for a moment. She appeared to be thinking. "Thank you," she said at last. "I'd love to see your world. But Terrica is my home, and if it's in trouble, I need to stay and try to help."
"I understand," Zann said. "Anyway, none of us can go anywhere until we figure out a way past that Shield spell."
Perda realized he was right. "Let's levitate up and look into the well from above," she said. "Maybe the shield goes only as high as the wall does."
Mellis looked around at the crowds of people. "Are you sure we should levitate where people can see?" she asked. "Surely Zira will hear about it if we do."
"Good point." Zann squinted up at the tree, which Perda noticed had grown even larger. "A few branches are sticking out over the wall. We could try to grab them and climb up that way."

Zing helped by flying up and perching on a branch to make it sink lower. Then Perda climbed onto Zann's shoulders. That lifted her high enough to grab the branch. Soon all three kids were scrambling up toward the center of the tree.
The shield stopped them before they reached the trunk. But they could look down over the wall.
Perda gasped when she saw the well. "The water is clear now," she said. "I wonder if that means most of the magic energy has escaped."
"Maybe," Zann said. "Look! You can see to the bottom of the well. It looks like lots of roots have grown out over the bottom!"

They all stared down at the tangled mass of large roots. Did they belong to the tree? Before Perda could figure it out, Krub and Zira zapped into view below. Vilkor was with them. He looked sulky. Perda also spotted three muscular men she'd never seen before.
"Attention!" Zira shouted, glaring around at the crowd. "You all must leave this area immediately."
Nobody paid any more attention to her than they had to Mellis. Zira waited a moment, tapping a foot impatiently.
Then she snapped her fingers. A tall wall of fire sprang up, surrounding the entire crowd.
People screamed and shouted, coughing from the smoke. The flames crept inward, trapping everyone in a smaller and smaller area.
"Oh, no!" Perda exclaimed. "We have to stop her!"
Zann glanced into the well. "Let's use this water to douse the flames."
"How can we do that?" Mellis cried. "It's behind the Shield spell!"
"Most Shield spells work in only one direction," Perda explained. "They're usually meant to keep people out, not in."
Zann nodded. "A two-way shield is much more difficult to create. Let's hope Zira hasn't figured out how to do that yet."

They all rubbed their hands together and focused on the well water. It rose up and out of the hole. For a second Perda was afraid they might send it flying into the sky, like Mellis had done with the pond water.
"Easy, easy," she said. "Focus on keeping it where we want it."
Mellis and Zann nodded, their expressions focused. Perda held her breath until the water broke through the shield.
"It is one-way only," she said in relief. "Now follow my count of three—one, two, three, go!"
They magically flung the water onto the ring of flames.
Whoosh!
The people were soaked, but the fire went out. Everyone ran away.
Perda slumped with relief. Then Zira spotted them.
"Come down here," Zira ordered. "Now!"
Mellis looked nervous. But Perda wasn't scared of Zira.
"Zira is an adult, and she's a fast learner," Perda thought. "But Zann and I have much more experience with magic."
"Come on, Zing," Zann said, whistling. The little dragon stayed where he was, hidden in the branches. Zann shrugged. "Suit yourself," he said with a touch of annoyance.
"Let's levitate down," Perda whispered. "Maybe that will make her realize who she's messing with."
They floated down, landing in front of Zira.
"We're glad you're here," Zann said boldly. "You're the one who wants us to leave Terrica, right? We can't do that while your Shield spell is blocking the wormhole."

"Actually, I've changed my mind about you leaving," Zira said. "I've learned a lot of magic by spying on you two. And you might have still more to teach me." She rubbed her fingers together and then pointed at them. "Shackle!"
Magical arm and leg shackles appeared on Zann, Perda, and Mellis. Their hands were bound behind their backs.
"Stop!" Perda cried. "You can't do this!"

Zira smirked. "Yes, I can. I'd like to keep you around. But you three are too much trouble when you're together." She gestured to Krub and two of the other men. "Take them away—to three separate far-flung corners of Terrica!"
"Take them away!" Zira shouted again.
"I can't believe this is happening!" Zann thought, outraged.
"Release us right now!" Perda cried, struggling against her shackles.
Zann saw one of the large men heading toward him. "Don't touch me!" Zann yelled.
Zira smirked. "You look like a sturdy kid, Zann." She glanced at the goon. "Take him to the mines in the mountains beyond the lowland swamps. He can make himself useful there. Krub, go with them."
"No, stop!" Zann said.
The goon grabbed one of Zann's arms, and Krub grabbed the other. Zann struggled, even though he knew it was no use. As they dragged him away, he glanced back at Perda and Mellis.
Perda's eyes met his. Zann wished he could break away and save her.
Suddenly he felt words forming in his mind. "Perda is sending me a mental message!" he thought. "She must have been inspired by the message she got from Zira."
Her words were faint and muddled, but Zann was pretty sure he understood them: Look for other wormholes. I'll find you and Mellis when I can get away.
Zann nodded and Perda smiled. Zann smiled back, glad that they were a team.

"What are you grinning about, you weird kid?" Krub growled, yanking on Zann's arm. "In case you didn't notice, you're a prisoner. And you're about to learn what hard work is like!" He laughed nastily, and the goon joined in.
Zann ignored them. Now he was looking for Zing, but he couldn't see him anywhere.
"We have a long walk ahead of us," the goon said. "Might as well get started."
Krub smirked. "No walking for us today, my friend. Zira taught me how to travel by magic."
"She did?" The goon looked impressed and a little nervous. "Is it safe?"
"Safer than hiking through lands occupied by gorzogs and rock trompers," Krub replied. "Rub your hands together, like this . . ."
He and the other man dropped their hold on Zann and created friction. Then they grabbed him again.
"Zap!" Krub shouted.
They landed in a patch of brambles.
"Ouch," the goon said, yanking a thorn from his hand. "Where are we?"
Zann wondered the same thing. All he saw were trees, rocky land, and scrubby plants.

Krub looked around. "I recognize this place. We're only a third of the way to the mines. Zira said it might require several zaps to get to them." He frowned. "I guess she was right. It's late and I'm tired. We'll camp here tonight and zap the rest of the way tomorrow."
"Camp?" Zann thought with a shiver. He didn't relish the idea of camping out with these two. But he didn't have a choice.
Krub used magic to create simple tents for himself and the goon. But Zann was left to sleep outside on the hard ground.

The men built a fire and ate the food they'd brought. They also pulled out flasks of foul-smelling liquid that they swilled with enthusiasm. Krub gave Zann a piece of jerky and a few sips of water. The jerky tasted like dirt, and the water was stale.

After the sun went down, strange creatures made noises in the trees all around the camp. Zann flinched at every grunt and howl. But he did his best to ignore them, along with the men's talk and laughter as they continued drinking from their flasks.
"I need to get some rest," Zann told himself, trying to get comfortable on the rough, rocky ground. "I want to be ready for anything tomorrow."
He was drifting off to sleep when a howl woke him. A second later an animal stepped into the firelight. It was the same size as Zing, with brown fur and sly red eyes.
"A chupo!" Krub exclaimed.
The goon picked up a large stick. "I'll chase it away."
"No—wait." Krub grinned. "It isn't interested in us. Just the boy. Maybe we should let it have him, eh? Even chupos have to eat."
Zann sat up, struggling against the shackles. "Come on, guys. This isn't funny."
Krub and the goon laughed as the chupo crept closer.
"Look, here comes the rest of the pack," Krub said.
Several more chupos appeared out of the darkness. One stopped and stared fearfully toward the fire. But the rest were focused on Zann. He gulped as one of the creatures licked its chops.
Zann could tell the two men were enjoying watching his terror. For a second he felt helpless.

Then he realized something: He wasn't actually helpless. The shackles stopped him from moving freely. But they couldn't stop him from doing magic. Even if they were too tight to allow him to rub his hands together, he could still snap his fingers. He did so several times to build up friction.
"Get back!" he blurted out, creating a fireball that shot toward the chupos.
They ran away, howling with fear, and disappeared into the darkness.
"Look at that!" Krub crowed with a hearty laugh. "The boy has some fire in him after all. Get it? Fire?" He grinned.
The goon came over and slapped Zann on the back. "Well done, boy," he said. "That kind of courage deserves a drink."
He held out his flask. Whatever was inside smelled even worse up close.
"No thanks," Zann said. "Let's just get some sleep."
The goon shrugged and took another drink. "Maybe the boy's right," he said. "It's getting late."
Krub yawned. "One of us should stand guard in case those chupos come back. You can take the first watch."
"Why me?" the other man complained. "You do it."
Zann lay down and closed his eyes. It had been a long day, and he was tired. As the two men continued to argue, he quickly fell asleep.
"This is ridiculous," Perda thought as she dunked a dirty dinner plate into a basin of soapy water.
She shuffled over to the kitchen door. Her legs were still shackled together. Zira had released her hands after they'd zapped to her house an hour or two earlier.
Zira was in the courtyard garden. Just as Perda looked out, Zira snapped her fingers and created a tall, golden fence around the bushes with purple berries that Perda had noticed before.

Those bushes were almost the only thing about Zira's house that hadn't changed since Perda had first seen it. Thanks to Zira's magic abilities, the house was now the largest and grandest in the village.
"What do you want?" Zira asked, frowning when she noticed Perda in the doorway. "I told you to wash the dishes."
"Yes, you did. But as I keep telling you, it would be much faster and easier with magic," Perda said.

Zira shrugged. "Too bad. As I keep telling you, you're forbidden from using magic. If you ever want me to remove those shackles from your legs, you'll remember that. Now get back to your chores. I expect you to be finished with the dishes by the time I return from the village green." She rolled her eyes. "Vilkor wishes to bestow more magical favors on the townspeople this evening. I should be there to supervise."
Perda was interested to hear that Zira was leaving. "All right," she said, trying to sound humble. "I'll get back to work."
She shuffled back inside. Zira followed, pausing to watch as Perda picked up another dirty dish.
"I'll be back in an hour," Zira said. Then she snapped her fingers and zapped out of sight.
Perda set down the dish. With her hands free, it was easy to create friction. She quickly cleaned the rest of the dishes with magic.

"Zira will be gone for an hour," she thought, looking around. "That means I have an hour to look around this place. Maybe Zira left some clues about what she has planned for Terrica. Or maybe I can figure out where she sent my friends."

For a second Perda was tempted to zap away to try to find Zann and Mellis on her own. But she realized that her shackled legs would slow her down too much. Besides, someone might see her and tell Zira.
"First, I'll figure out what's going on," she murmured as she shuffled into the next room. "Then I'll figure out how to rescue my friends."

By the next day, Perda hadn't figured out either of those things. She'd searched as much as she could while Zira was away. But she hadn't found any clues. Then Zira had returned and forced her to sweep the whole house. By the time she finished, Perda was exhausted. Doing chores without magic was hard!

To make things worse, Zira had woken her up early to do more hard work. At the moment Perda was busy dusting all the fancy statues, furniture, and knickknacks Zira had created to decorate her enormous reception room.
There was a knock on the door. It was Vilkor.
"Oh, hello, young lady," he greeted Perda. He peered around, wringing his hands. "Is my niece here with you? I haven't seen her since she was dragged off by those large fellows yesterday."
Perda was surprised to see that he actually looked worried. "I haven't seen her, either," she said. "You'll have to ask Zira."
Zira entered the room. "Ask me what?"
Vilkor repeated his question about Mellis. "She's quite useful around the house," he added, glancing into the next room. "She could keep this place spotless for you."

"Your niece isn't here," Zira said. "She's making herself useful at a friend's plonk farm outside of town." As she spoke, she snapped her fingers. A large fireball appeared, hovering above her hand. She played with it as if it were a ball spinning on her finger. "Why do you ask? Do you have a problem with my assignment of duties?"
Vilkor gulped, his gaze trained on the fireball. "No, of course not. Mellis always was fond of animals . . ."
Perda rolled her eyes. She could tell that Vilkor was intimidated by Zira's display of magical power.
"That's how she's keeping him and everyone else in line," Perda thought. "But I'm not afraid of her. And now I know where Mellis is!"
"Say," Vilkor said, still watching the spinning fireball. "Can you teach me how to do that?"
Zira noticed that Perda had stopped dusting to listen. "Back to work, girl!" she said. "And put some effort into it. This room is still a mess!"
Perda stared at her defiantly. Then she rubbed her hands together and magically removed everything from the room. The dust and dirt were gone, along with the furniture and everything else.
"Clean enough for you now?" Perda asked with a smirk.
Zira gnashed her teeth. "How dare you! Shackle!"
Tight shackles appeared around Perda's wrists.
Vilkor bit his lip. "Oh, dear."
Zira pointed. "To your room, girl," she snarled. "I'll decide your punishment later."
Pretending to be scared, Perda slunk off toward her sleeping chamber. Unlike the rest of the house, it wasn't large or fancy at all. It was barely big enough for a rough mattress on the floor.
Once inside, Perda stood up straight and smiled. Her plan had worked. She wasn't sure how long it would be before Zira decided on her punishment, but she wasn't going to waste a moment.

It wasn't easy to create friction with her wrists so tightly shackled. Plus, it seemed that lots of energy was required to zap out of Zira’s house. So she rubbed her shoulder against the wall and her feet on the floor until she had built up enough energy. Then— zap!
"Aren't we ever going to zap again?" Zann thought.

Krub and the goon had slept late that morning. After a leisurely breakfast, Krub had zapped them all to this grassy hillside. Since then Krub and the goon had been drinking from their flasks again. Zann just wanted to get going.
Finally Krub took an extra-long swig from his flask and let out a loud burp. "Let's move on," he said. "Get over here, kid."
Zann shuffled over. The two men grabbed him.
Krub rubbed his free hand against his leg. "Zap!"
They landed in a swampy area. The air was humid, and streams and puddles were everywhere.
"We're almost there." The goon peered into the thick, dripping trees. "The mines are a short hike from here."
He and Krub set off. Zann shuffled after them, but the shackles on his legs made it difficult to walk.
"Hey, wait up!" he called.
Krub frowned. "Oh, right." He snapped his fingers and muttered something under his breath.
The shackles on Zann's legs disappeared.
The goon looked impressed. "How'd you do that?"
"Never mind," Krub said. "Let's go."
Zann didn't need Krub to tell him what had happened. He guessed that Zira had put a password on her Shackle spell. That would allow anyone who knew the password to remove or replace the shackles.
"Zira probably heard me and Perda telling Mellis about magical passwords," Zann thought. "I wish I'd heard the password Zira put on my shackles."
He was sure Krub would put the shackles back on at night. He would listen more carefully then.
They hiked through the swamp and then headed uphill. Finally they heard voices nearby.
"It sounds as if others are here," the goon said.
Krub nodded. "Don't tell them about magic."
They entered a large clearing. Several people were hurrying in and out of a cave, while others sorted through piles of rocks and dirt.
"I found flint," a man called out. "Let's go back in for more!"
"Flint?" Zann said. "Why are they so excited to find that?"
Krub shot him a surprised look. "To make fire, of course. It's a lot faster than rubbing sticks together."
"Why are we bothering with this, anyway?" The goon scratched his head. "Can't we just have Zira and Vilkor make fire now?" He shrugged. "We might even be able to do it ourselves if we really try."
Krub looked intrigued. "Zira made magic sound too difficult for anyone except her. But I can transport us long distances and create food. How can making fire be that much harder?"
"Let's try!" The goon rubbed his meaty hands together and then pointed at the ground. "Fire!"
A wisp of smoke appeared briefly. Zann rolled his eyes. They were out of the swamp, but the ground here was still pretty moist.
Krub tried next. He created friction and then held out his hand. "Fire!"
A small fireball appeared in his hand. Krub's eyes widened, and his jaw dropped. But as the fireball got a little larger, he quickly tossed it away.
"Ouch!" He shook his hand. "It burned me!"
Zann tried not to laugh. Meanwhile the men's shouts were attracting attention. Several miners came over when the goon set a small shrub on fire.
"What's going on?" a miner asked. "Did you do that?"
The goon tried to stamp out the burning bush. "None of your business!"
"Does this have something to do with the way plants are growing and the land is thriving?" a woman asked.
Another miner nodded. "It's strange but also wonderful! My orchard was barren until a few days ago. Now I have more fruit than my family can eat!"
"It's magic!" the goon blurted out. He went on to tell the miners everything.

Krub looked angry at first. But when the miners stared at him in awe, he couldn't resist showing off. "I can do magic too!" He quickly rubbed a hand on his side, and then waved his arms. "Drink for everyone!"
Several flasks appeared. The miners grabbed them eagerly, tasting the contents.
"This is a miracle!" one cried. "Will you show us how to do it?"
"No." Krub frowned. "And don't try to do magic on your own. It's forbidden by the owner of the well from which the magic came!"
The miners didn't look intimidated by the warning. Already some were waving their hands around, trying to imitate what Krub had done.
"They didn't notice Krub creating friction," Zann thought. "They won't be able to do magic until they figure that out."
He was tempted to shout out the truth. After all, magic should belong to everyone.
But then he glanced down at his shackled hands. He needed to get that password before he did anything else. Maybe it would release Perda and Mellis too.
To distract himself, he looked around. This part of Terrica reminded him of the hills near Swamp Bottom. That made him miss Magica more than ever—and Zing.
"Ow!" he blurted out as an insect landed on his arm and gave him a painful bite. He tried to swat it, but the shackles stopped him.

"I'm glad we don't have those nasty bugs in Magica," he thought. "Still, a lot of the trees and stuff look so familiar. I wish Darb were here. He'd notice all the little differences between here and home."
The goon grabbed his arm. "Time to get to work."

Zann had no choice but to stumble after him. As the goon dragged him past a crooked tree surrounded by a tangle of brush, Zann noticed something in the clearing beyond. Was it a cloud of those biting insects coming for him?
Then he blinked in surprise. No, it wasn't insects. It was a shimmer in the air. Could it be . . . a wormhole?
Perda landed in a rural area. The village was visible in the distance.
"I see that ugly tower Zira added to her house," she thought.
Then she looked around. She'd chosen her landing spot at random. Now she had to find that plonk farm. But she didn't even know what a plonk was!
A woman was walking past with a basket under her arm.
"Excuse me," Perda said, shuffling toward her. "Is there a plonk farm around here?"

"A plonk farm?" the woman asked in a friendly way. Then she saw Perda's shackled wrists and legs. "Oh dear," she said quickly. "You must be one of Zira's prisoners. If I help you, I might meet the same fate! I'm sorry."
She hurried off before Perda could say anything else. Perda shuffled along the road. It was hard to walk in the shackles. She tried hopping instead. That was faster but much more tiring.
A man came into sight. He was humming happily and juggling a loaf of bread and a couple of pieces of fruit.
"Hello!" Perda said. "Could you please point me toward the nearest plonk farm?"
The man was so surprised that he dropped the fruit, though he managed to hang onto the bread.
"Who are you?" he asked. Then he, too, noticed the shackles and looked suspicious. "Why are you asking about the plonk farm?"

Perda sighed, realizing it wouldn't be easy to find her friends if she was shackled. For a moment she was tempted to give up and zap back before Zira noticed she was missing. Zira would have to remove the shackles the next time she wanted Perda to do chores. Maybe then she could try to escape again.
But then she noticed the man glancing nervously toward a side road.
"Is that the way to the plonk farm?" she blurted out.
"You didn't hear it from me." The man quickly grabbed the fruit he'd dropped, hugging all his food to his chest. "I don't want Sir Vilkor to take back my stuff!"
"You got that food from Vilkor?" Perda asked. "He should have told you that you can create all the food you want yourself."

The man looked suspicious again. "What are you talking about? Sir Vilkor and his assistant, Zira, warned that troublemakers would be envious of their power and tell lies about them. Keep away from me, troublemaker!"
"Wait!" Perda cried as he rushed away. "At least let me show you how you can—"
"No!" the man snapped. "You're lucky I don't run back to the village and tell Sir Vilkor about your mischief!"
Perda watched him go. Then she shuffled toward the side road, hoping she could find the plonk farm on her own.
A few minutes later, she spotted a boy her age on the road ahead. She hopped to catch up to him.
"Hi," she said. "Is there a plonk farm around here?"
The boy stared at her. "Um, I don't know." His eyes were shifty and nervous.
"Please, don't worry," Perda said. "I won't tell anyone you spoke to me." She took a closer look at the boy. "Hmm, you look sort of familiar. Do I know you?"
"No, I don't think so," he said. "Excuse me, I have to go."
Suddenly Perda realized why he looked familiar. He resembled someone she'd met a couple of days earlier—the father of Mellis' friend. "Are you Anso?" she asked.
The boy looked startled. "How do you know my name?"
"I'm Perda," she said. "Mellis is my friend. I'm searching for her. Do you know where she is?"

"Shh!" Anso glanced around. But there was nobody in sight. "Yes, I'm going there now." He showed Perda a loaf of bread hidden in his shirt. "Her new boss won't give her any food. He says she has to eat with the plonks she's taking care of."
"Please bring me to her," Perda begged. "I need to see her so I can figure out how to rescue her. You can trust me. I promise!"
Anso hesitated, and then nodded with a small smile. "Any friend of Mellis is a friend of mine. Come! We'll have to sneak past Trof, the owner of the farm. He's not a nice man."

They headed down the road as quickly as Perda could shuffle. As they went, she told Anso everything that had happened since she and Zann had arrived in Terrica. Anso looked a bit skeptical when Perda said she came from another world, but he seemed willing to believe her.
Finally Perda saw the farm. Anso led her into a grove of trees. They sneaked through them to the back fence of the farm.

It was hard to climb the fence in shackles, but with Anso's help, Perda managed it. They crept across a dirty yard and into a pen where a dozen large, short-legged creatures snorted and squealed and fought each other for scraps of smelly food.
"So those are plonks," Perda thought.
And then she spotted something else. Perched on a barrel was a dirty and disheveled Mellis. Her face lit up when she saw Perda and Anso.
"You came!" Mellis cried.
She rushed toward them. Suddenly a young plonk dashed in front of her, its beady eyes fixed on a half-eaten vegetable. Mellis tripped over the animal, sending it tipping over into the muck.
The plonk squealed loudly, and within seconds the rest of the plonks took up the cry.
"Hey!" a man shouted. "What's going on out there?"
"We have to hide!" Anso hissed in terror.
But the sticky muck of the plonk pen made it even harder for Perda to move. Before she could hide, a large, mustached man with a ruddy face stomped into the pen.
"Who dares to sneak onto my property?" he roared, grabbing Anso by the arm.
Zann stared at the shimmer. "It looks like a wormhole!" he thought. "I wish I could get closer. Then I could tell for sure."
But the goon was still dragging him toward the cave.
"Zira wants you to put in a hard day's work here," Krub said. "So that's exactly what you're going to do."
"How am I supposed to work like this?" Zann held up his shackled hands as he followed the men.
"Once we're inside, I'll remove those shackles," Krub replied.
"What?" The goon looked surprised. "There will be nothing to stop him from zapping away."
"He won't dare." Krub looked smug. "Zira told me she's figured out how to use magic to track people. She'll know immediately if he leaves this area."
Zann felt skeptical. He'd never heard of such a spell.
Then again, Zira was learning magic at a fast pace.

"Back in Magica, we can find someone using a Uniting spell," he thought. "But that's only if they want to be found. Otherwise the only option is to use the Directory to find out where they live, or maybe use a spy fly to spy on them."
He thought about telling Krub that. If Krub knew that Zira couldn't magically spy on him, maybe Zann could convince the man to rebel against her. After all, Krub already defied her by making fire.
"So watch yourself, boy," Krub warned Zann with a nasty smile. "And if you're thinking about escaping, think again. Because if you misbehave, Zira might punish your friends."
Zann gulped. Would Zira really hurt Perda or Mellis if he didn't do as she wished? He wasn't willing to take that chance.
"Don't worry, I'll behave," Zann said.
"Good." Krub murmured a word under his breath, and Zann's arm shackles disappeared.
Zann was disappointed. Once again he'd failed to hear the password.
Next Krub rubbed his hands together and created a shovel. He handed it to Zann. "Now start digging."
"Why?" Zann said. "It should be easy to extract whatever you want by using magic."
"That's not how Zira wants you to do it." Krub's smile was nastier than ever. "Get to work!"
An hour later Zann was sweaty, exhausted, and covered in dust and grit. He also felt frustrated. He kept trying to tell Krub that he could do what Zira wanted better and faster with magic.
"Why does she want us to find this stuff anyway?" he asked. "What did you call it? Crumblestone?"
"That's the stuff," Krub said. "It's very delicate. That's why you have to dig it out the old-fashioned way. Zira is afraid that using magic might damage it."
"But why does she want it?" Zann asked again.
Krub shrugged. "It's one of the main ingredients in those potions she's famous for. She thinks it will make her new magic even stronger."

"But that's not true," Zann said. "Regular magic is caused by friction—that's all. Potions don't have any effect on it." He frowned, trying to remember his lessons from school. "At least I don't think they do."
The goon rolled his eyes. "What do you know? You're just a kid." He wiped his brow and turned to Krub. "It's hot in this cave. Let's go outside for a drink."
Krub nodded and then glared at Zann. "Don't try anything, kid. Remember, Zira is watching!"
Zann was glad to see them go. There were no other miners in this part of the cave. So he rubbed his hands together to create friction. "Crumblestone," he said as a focusing word.
A large chunk of soft stone appeared. It looked exactly like the smaller chunks of crumblestone he'd dug out so far.
"That should satisfy them," he thought. "And they'll never know I didn't dig it out by hand!"
He snapped his fingers to create food and a glass of airberry juice. Then he sat down on a rock to eat.

He couldn't stop thinking about his friends. He wondered where Zira had sent Perda and Mellis. And what had happened to Zing? The last time Zann had seen his dragon, Zing was hiding in the tree by the well. Was he still there, or was he searching for Zann? Zann hoped the dragon was okay.

"This world seems like Magica in some ways," Zann thought as he chewed his food. "But in other ways it's so different! It reminds me of tales about the Old Times, when Magica wasn't as modern and peaceful as it is now."

He glanced around the cave. It looked a little like some parts of the Cave of the Unknown back in Magica. But it was much less scary. The Cave of the Unknown had all sorts of unpredictable magic energy humming in the air.
"I guess every world has a mix of dangerous stuff and harmless stuff," he thought. "Except for Fardark or Drac. Those places are totally dangerous!"
Zann took a sip of airberry juice.
"At least Zira hasn't figured out how to control dark magic like old King Zanta did," Zann thought. "He was totally evil, ruling the entire land from his spooky old fortress deep in the mountains."
Zann was surprised to realize how much he remembered about Magica's history from his school classes.
"Some of it is actually pretty interesting," he thought. "No wonder Perda is obsessed with it lately."
Thinking about Perda made him miss her even more. She'd said she would try to find him and Mellis. But how long should he wait before trying to find the two girls himself?
He was so lost in his own thoughts that he failed to notice the men had returned.
"Stop slacking, boy!" Krub roared. "Get back to work!"
"Let him go!" Perda shouted as Trof yanked Anso's arm.
"Don't tell me what to do!" The plonk farmer sneered. He grabbed Mellis with his free hand and glared at her. "Did you bring your friends in to do your work for you?"
"No, of course not!" Mellis cried in terror.

Trof narrowed his eyes. "Zira warned that I'd have to keep an eye on you to make sure you were working hard enough. It seems she was right. You're the laziest and sneakiest worker I've ever had! You're lucky I don't feed you to the plonks."
Perda gritted her teeth. "What do I do now?" she thought. "I can zap out of here anytime. But I can't leave Mellis and Anso in the hands of this brute."

She was tempted to send a Blast spell at the farmer. But she held back. For one thing, it would be difficult to create enough friction for that kind of spell while shackled. Besides, it wouldn't be right to hurt him, even though he was holding her friends as prisoners. There had to be another way to save them.
"Please, sir, listen to me," Perda said. "If you let us go, I can teach you how to use magic."
Trof laughed. "What could a child like you possibly teach an adult like me?"

"I may be young, but I've been doing magic my whole life," Perda replied. "I come from a world where magic has existed forever. And the magic here in Terrica seems to work the same way as it does in my world."
"Another world?" The man looked skeptical. "That's a very creative story, young lady. But don't expect me to believe it!"

"I can't prove that I'm from a different world. But I'll prove I can do magic. Watch!" Perda snapped her fingers a couple of times, since she couldn't rub her hands together while shackled. A piece of fruit appeared in her hand. "See?"

Trof looked surprised, and then suspicious. "Where did that come from?" he asked. "I was told that only certain people can perform magic. You must have had that fruit hidden in your clothes or something."
"No, I created it with magic." Perda tossed the fruit to the plonks. A large one grabbed it and gobbled it up, snorting happily. The other plonks squealed hungrily.
"I can teach you how to do it too," Perda said.
She quickly created more food, making sure there was enough for all the plonks. Soon the creatures were chomping, chewing, and grunting with joy.

Trof's eyes narrowed. "Are you trying to trick me? If you truly can create something out of nothing, why not create something more useful? Perhaps a new board to replace the one the plonks broke yesterday?" He gestured to a cracked section of the rickety wooden fence.
"Sure, I can do that," Perda said. She created more friction, and moments later a board appeared in front of Trof.
His eyes widened. "You did that by snapping your fingers?"
"Basically, yes." Perda briefly explained how friction worked. "Go ahead and try it," she said. "You can create anything you need—more boards, nails, food . . . anything except humans or animals."
Trof still looked suspicious. But he dropped his hold on Anso, who sidled a short distance away. Trof didn't notice. He was busy snapping his fingers.
"Nails!" he shouted.
Several nails appeared in his hand.
He gasped. "It worked! I did magic!"

Perda smiled and nodded. She wished that Trof would let go of Mellis. Then she could grab her and Anso and zap them all away. But the farmer was keeping a tight hold on Mellis' arm, even as he continued snapping with the other hand. He went on to create a new hat for himself, a hammer to help him fix the fence, and several more boards.
"But wait!" he exclaimed as a board dropped at his feet. "Why should I waste my time building the fence myself? Can I make one by magic?"
Perda shrugged, still trying to figure out how they could all escape. "Sure," she said. "You'll need a little more friction for that though. You could try rubbing both your hands together."
She hoped that would make him drop his hold on Mellis. Instead he rubbed his free hand vigorously against his belly. "New fence!" he cried. "Tall and strong, so the plonks can't break out!"
A tall, sturdy fence appeared around the plonk pen.

"Very nice." Perda was still trying to come up with a plan. "Er, did you say your worker is sneaky? I can show you how to control her better. I'll demonstrate on this boy." She pointed at Anso. "Shackle!"
Loose shackles appeared on Anso's wrists. "Hey!" he cried.
Trof's eyes lit up. "I bet I can do that," he said, turning to Mellis.

Perda's heart sank. She'd planned to offer to shackle Mellis' arms as well, so that Trof would let go of her. Then Perda could zap the three of them away and release Anso and Mellis from their shackles once they'd landed. But if Trof was the one to put a Shackle spell on Mellis, only he could undo it.
The man was already rubbing his hand on his belly again. "All right, what was the word you used again?" he asked.

Before Perda could figure out how to respond, there was a loud whistle from overhead. A second later the new fence burst into flames. Startled, the plonks ran all around, squealing. Trof cried out in surprise and fear, and Mellis and Anso both looked scared.
But Perda felt a flash of hope when she looked up and saw a little, red dragon dive-bombing another section of fence.
"Zing!" she cried.

Zann pried a rock loose with his shovel. "I assumed they'd let me stop working when they saw that big piece of crumblestone," he thought tiredly. Instead Krub and the goon had told him to keep digging. Now they were lounging nearby, sipping from their flasks. Finally Krub came over to see what Zann was doing.
"There's no more crumblestone here," Krub said. "Crawl through to the next chamber and dig there for a while. We'll check on you soon, so don't slack off."
Zann had to get on his hands and knees to fit through the tunnel. But he didn't mind. At least he'd get a break from the two men.
The next chamber was long, with a low ceiling. A short, wiry man was chipping away at the wall.
"Hello." Zann greeted him. "Do you mind if I dig too?"
"Be my guest." The man peered at him. "Hey, you're the kid I saw doing magic earlier. You pulled a whole chunk of stone out of thin air!"
"What?" Zann was alarmed. He didn't think anyone had seen him create the crumblestone.
"Don't worry, I won't tell your bosses." The man leaned closer and lowered his voice. "Especially if you tell me how you did it."
Zann was relieved. "Of course. Magic should be for everyone. I'm happy to teach you."
Zann showed the man how to create friction by rubbing his hands together. "That's basically all you need to do. Then you can create anything, even food. Use a focusing word to start with. Cookie!"
A wiggle root cookie appeared in Zann's hand.
The man stared in awe. "Amazing!"
"Now you try it," Zann said with a smile. "Just think of your favorite food as you create friction."
The man successfully created a sandwich. Then he made himself new boots. Finally Zann showed him how to zap from one place to another.
"You're doing great," Zann said as the man zapped from the far end of the cavern back to where Zann was waiting. "Keep practicing, and soon you'll be doing all kinds of magic."
"Okay," the man said. "Now show me how I can punish my enemy."
"What?" Zann said, surprised.

The man's expression darkened. "Another miner poached a valuable vein of glowstone from me last week. But he's twice my size, so I couldn't fight him for it. I want to punish him! How can I do that with magic?"
Zann was alarmed. "That's not how magic is supposed to be used! The main law in my world is 'do no harm to others.'"
The man rolled his eyes. "Your world sounds boring, kid. That guy harmed me by stealing my vein. Why shouldn't I harm him back? He deserves it!"
Zann shook his head. "I'm sorry. I can't help you."
"Can't, or won't ?" The man glared at him. "If you won't teach me what I want to know, maybe I won't keep quiet about the magic you've been doing. I'm sure your bosses would love to hear about it."
Zann gulped, not sure what to do. Luckily, at that moment, two other miners entered the chamber. Still, Zann knew he had to do something to stop the first man from talking to Krub.
"Um, okay," he whispered. "Meet me in the woods by the crooked tree at midnight, and I'll teach you what you need to know."
For the rest of the day, he couldn't stop thinking about the encounter. What was he going to do?
"That man will be looking for me at midnight," Zann thought. "And I'll be at the camp, shackled! Maybe Perda and Mellis will arrive before then. Then we can escape together."

But as night fell, there was still no sign of his friends. Krub and the goon camped in the clearing. They invited some other miners to share their smelly beverage. As the evening passed, the men drifted off to sleep. Krub forgot to shackle Zann.
"What luck!" Zann thought with relief. He thought about zapping back to Vilkor's village. Then he remembered Perda's words again: "Look for other wormholes!"
He glanced into the dark woods. The crooked tree wasn't far away. Was that a wormhole he'd seen earlier? He decided to find out.
"If the others do show up here, we can escape back to Magica," he thought as he sneaked away. "My parents and Boz can help us figure out what to do after that."

Soon he spotted the crooked tree looming ahead in the darkness. Seeing it reminded him of his arrangement with the miner. How long did he have until midnight? And what would he do if the man showed up early? The thought made him nervous.
"Just focus on checking for that wormhole," he told himself.
He stepped past the crooked tree into the small clearing beyond. Zann stepped closer to the shimmer, and a wormhole swirled open!
He stared into the swirling depths with amazement. All he had to do was step closer, and the wormhole would pull him into the vortex.

"Maybe I should go now, on my own," he thought. "That way I won't have to worry about the miner or anything else. I can find my way back to Magica and ask the adults to help save Perda and the others."
He took another step.
Then he stopped. He couldn't abandon Zing or his friends, especially Perda. Besides, she had mentioned that Terrica wasn't in any of his parents' books. What if he couldn't find his way back here?
The wormhole continued to swirl, almost hypnotizing Zann. He snapped out of it when someone cleared his throat nearby.
It was the miner. "Hello, kid," he said with a nasty smile. "I'm ready for my lesson now."

178.title: A Battle of Wits and Magic

paragraphs.text: Perda thought fast. While Zing flew around, sending blasts of flame everywhere, she snapped her fingers. "Open," she murmured.
The gate in Trof's new fence burst open. Perda hopped toward a large plonk and waved her shackled wrists. "Go! Be free!"
The plonk spotted the open gate. With a loud squeal, it raced through. Several other plonks charged after it.
"Hey, get back here!" Trof cried. He ran after them, finally letting go of Mellis.
"Unshackle," Perda said to free Anso. "Quick! Grab Mellis, and then hold onto me."
Anso looked confused. But Mellis was running toward them. "Grab Perda's arm and hold on tightly!" she said. "Hurry!"

Mellis and Anso held onto Perda, who whistled for Zing. The dragon flew toward her. But Trof spotted him passing overhead. The farmer reached up and grabbed the dragon out of the air, slinging him into a large crate nearby and slamming it shut.
Perda gasped. "Zing!"
Mellis squeezed her arm. "Trof is coming! We have to go!"
Trof ran toward them, looking furious. Perda couldn't stand the thought of leaving Zing behind. But if she hesitated, they would all be trapped again.
"Zap!" she cried.
When she, Mellis, and Anso landed, she looked around. She'd been in such a hurry that she hadn't specified a location. They appeared to have landed back in the village.
"We're near Anso's house," Mellis said, sounding relieved. She reached over and hugged him. "Go home before you get into even more trouble because of me."
Anso hugged her back, looking uncertain. "Are you sure?"
"Yes, you should go home," Perda said. "Thanks for your help."
Anso said good-bye and disappeared into a house down the street.
"Thanks for coming to rescue me," Mellis said. "Where's Zann?"

"I'm not sure," Perda said. "I didn't even know where Zing was until just now." She bit her lip, feeling worried. "We need to figure out how to rescue him from Trof. We also need to find out where Zira sent Zann."
Just then several people hurried into view, talking loudly. "I heard Sir Vilkor is giving away special golden staffs to celebrate the creation of his new home!" one woman exclaimed.
A man clapped his hands eagerly. "Let's go—I want one!"
"Sir Vilkor is so generous," another man said. "Life is better, now that he can bless us with his magical abilities!"
Perda scowled as she listened. How dare Vilkor and Zira keep the secret of magic to themselves! She was tempted to jump out of hiding and teach those people to do magic just as she'd done with Trof.
"Wait," Mellis whispered, seeming to guess what she was thinking. "Let's follow them to this new house they mentioned. Maybe Zann is there."
Perda wondered if she could be right. Zira had ordered Krub to take Zann to work in a mine. But what if he'd returned? If they could find him, he could help them rescue Zing.
She and Mellis sneaked along behind the group. They walked to a huge, fancy mansion near the town square.
Mellis looked surprised. "That wasn't there before. My uncle must have built it in the past couple of days!"

"He probably used up all his magic energy doing so," Perda said. "Either that, or Zira helped him." She still couldn't believe how powerful Zira seemed to be. That made it even more important to make sure Zira didn't keep the secret of magic from the citizens of Terrica. Nobody should have that much power.
"We can worry about that once we're all together and safe," Perda told herself. "I'm sure we can come up with a plan to reveal the truth to everyone."
Perda and Mellis hid behind a tree and watched people lining up in front of Vilkor's new mansion.
"Maybe we should go inside and ask him to help us," Mellis whispered. "My uncle isn't a bad person."
Perda wasn't so sure. Vilkor might not be evil, but he was willing to go along with Zira's evil plan. The only thing he seemed to care about was making his own life nicer.
"What if Zira is in there with him?" Perda whispered.
Mellis looked worried. "I didn't think of that."
"I'm not sure we . . ." Perda's voice trailed off. She'd just felt an invisible tug, as if a giant hand was pulling her farther down the street.
"Hey, what's going on?" Mellis took several steps in that direction. "I didn't mean to walk this way!"
Perda gasped, recognizing the feeling. "It feels like a Compel spell! They're not allowed in Magica." She struggled to stop herself from moving, but the spell forced her to follow Mellis.
"Let's zap away!" Perda said. "That might free us from the spell!"
Just then two large goons burst into view.
"It's them!" one goon shouted. "Grab them!"

Perda lunged for Mellis, hoping to zap away. But her shackles prevented her from moving fast enough. The goons grabbed both girls. As she struggled against her captor, Perda noticed he had odd purple marks on his face. The other goon had similar marks.
"I can't zap while he's holding me," she thought. "Not without taking him with me, anyway. And I can't leave Mellis behind!"
She glanced at the other girl just in time to see Mellis snap her fingers. A rock appeared in her hand, and she threw it at the goon holding Perda. It hit him in the shoulder.
"Ow!" he yelped, letting go of Perda.
"Go, Perda! Zap away!" Mellis shouted. "Save yourself!"
Perda hesitated. She hated to abandon Mellis so soon after freeing her from Trof. Still, she couldn't help anyone if she was trapped herself.
As the goon reached for her, Perda snapped her fingers. "Zap!"
Zann gulped. "What should I do now?" he thought.
The miner stared at him, his expression eager and cruel. "You promised to teach me how to get my revenge. Let's get started."

Zann didn't know what to say. Sure, he could teach the man how to do a basic Immobilization spell. Most kids in Magica learned that one in case they were ever attacked by a dragon or other dangerous creature. But Zann couldn't imagine using it on any human or animal that wasn't threatening his life. It wouldn't be right.

There were other spells the man would probably like too. Nasty, dark spells that nobody in Magica ever used for anything. Back in the Old Times, such spells were common, or so Zann had heard. But he would never use that type of magic either.
"I'm sorry," he said, shaking his head. "I don't believe in using magic to hurt people. I won't teach you to do it."
The man rolled his eyes. "Grow up, kid. The world is a nasty place. I'm just trying to protect myself. You'll do the same if you know what's good for you."
Was that a threat? Zann wasn't sure, but he didn't like the look in the man's eyes.
"I've made up my mind. I'm sorry. I'd better get back to camp now." He tried to step past the miner.
The man stopped him with a hand on his chest. "You're not going anywhere," he said. "Not until you give me what I want."
Zann stepped back. "No," he said as firmly as he could. "I won't do it."
The miner scowled. "Fine. Then I'm going back right now to wake up your bosses and tell them exactly what you've been doing."
"No!" Zann cried in alarm. "Please don't do that."
The man smirked. "Oh, are you afraid they'll punish you? Maybe you'd prefer I punish you myself, huh?"
Before Zann could figure out what he meant, the man ran at him with his fists raised.
"Hey!" Zann yelped, leaping out of the way just in time to avoid being punched.
"Hold still, kid," the miner growled, trying to grab him.
Zann darted away. He was shaking with fear. Nobody had ever attacked him physically before!
"Well, except for Zing," he thought, with a stab of worry for his dragon friend. "But that's just playing, at least most of the time."
The man was already coming at him again. Zann jumped out of the way, which also reminded him of Zing. Sometimes the easiest way to avoid the little dragon's attacks was just to jump out of the way.

"Zing hates when I do that though," he thought as he barely dodged another blow. "If I don't get out of here soon, this guy is likely to get even angrier if he can't catch me. And if he does manage to grab me . . ."
Not wanting to think about that, Zann rubbed his hands together to create enough friction to zap away.
As magic energy sparked from his hands, he was forced to leap aside to avoid another punch. That brought him close to the wormhole, which swirled open in response to the friction he was creating.
The miner stopped short, his eyes going wide. "What's that?"

Zann stopped to catch his breath, being careful to stay out of reach. "It's a wormhole," he said. "It leads into the vortex, which connects all the known worlds." He glanced around at the Terrican landscape. "And some unknown ones too."
The man stared into the swirling wormhole, seeming mesmerized. "Other worlds? What do you mean?"
Zann shrugged. "If you promise to stop attacking me, I promise to tell you all about it."

The man turned and sneered at him. "Oh, another promise from you? Is this one a lie too? Because it sounds like a tall tale to me. Magic is one thing. But there's definitely no such thing as a portal to another world!"

He charged toward Zann, fists raised. Zann didn't have time to completely dodge the attack this time. Instead he ducked, letting the man's fists pass over his head. Then he slammed his shoulder into his attacker's torso, hoping to push him away.
He did push him away—straight into the wormhole!
"Ahh!" The miner disappeared into the vortex.
"Oh no!" Zann rushed forward. But the wormhole was already swirling shut. It opened again when Zann came closer, and he stared into its glowing depths, feeling guilty. What had he done?
"That man was a jerk," he thought. "But he won't have any idea what to do in the vortex. He might not even survive!"
Before he could figure out what to do, there was a buzz of magic energy behind him. He turned. Perda was standing there.
"Zann!" she exclaimed.
"Perda!" He rushed toward her, and then stopped and stared into her eyes. Was it really her? "How . . . where?"

Perda laughed. "I found you by using a Uniting spell. It wasn't easy to create enough friction to get here with these things on." She held up her shackled wrists. Zann looked down and saw that her legs were shackled too. "But I did it!" she said proudly.
"A Uniting spell," Zann echoed. "That only works if the person wants to be found." He smiled at her. "And of course I wanted you to find me."

"I know. I wanted to find you too. A lot. That made it easier." As she smiled back, Zann thought she'd never looked prettier. Suddenly he wasn't sure what to do next. He wanted to hug her, but he wasn't sure she'd like that.
So instead he just stood there, gazing into her beautiful brown eyes.
"Why is Zann staring at me like that?" Perda thought.
She felt strange and uncertain. She wasn't used to feeling that way around Zann. He was her best friend. They'd known each other all their lives!
Suddenly the sound of voices echoed through the dark woods.
Zann looked worried. "Someone must be awake at camp."
"We should get out of here before we're caught," Perda said. "But it took me two zaps to get here from the village, and I don't have much magic energy left. You'll have to zap us both away."
She thought about Mellis, who had sacrificed her own freedom to allow Perda's escape. They had to get back there and save her!
Then she noticed a shimmer over Zann's shoulder. Her eyes widened in hopeful surprise. "Oh! Is that a wormhole?"
Zann glanced back at it. "Yes."
He looked guilty, though Perda couldn't imagine why.
"This is exactly what we needed!" she exclaimed. "Now we don't have to get past Zira's Shield spell to reach that other wormhole!"
The voices in the woods got louder. "I heard something over this way!" a man shouted.
Zann gulped. "We'd better get out of here."
Perda expected him to zap them away. Instead Zann ran deeper into the woods. Perda followed.
"They'll hear us!" she whispered. "Let's zap away!"
Zann shook his head. "I don't want to leave. Not yet."
Perda didn't know why he would say that. But she didn't dare to talk anymore. Their pursuers might hear them.
She and Zann pushed through underbrush and jumped over fallen logs. Zann helped Perda when her shackles got in the way. Finally they splashed through a small stream into a dark meadow.
"Look, a cave!" Perda whispered, pointing.
They crawled inside. "We could be trapped in here," Zann said.
