"If that happens, we'll have to zap away." Perda looked at Zann. "Why didn't you want to do that before?"
Zann had a strange expression on his face. "Something happened right before you got here," he said. "I'd arranged to meet this miner who wanted to learn dark magic."
Perda listened carefully as he told her the whole story.
"It's my fault that he got sucked into the vortex," Zann said when he finished. "Maybe I should go in and try to rescue him."
Perda could tell that Zann felt terrible about what had happened. He was the type of person who always wanted to do the right thing.
"It's not your fault," she assured him. "Besides, we have other problems to worry about."
Just then shouts came from the meadow. The men stomped past the cave without seeing the kids.
"Quick," Zann whispered. "Let's go back to the wormhole while they're distracted."
He quickly sneaked out of the cave. Perda glanced out at the miners. There were three or four of them.
"I hope Yarb is okay," one said. "He told me he didn't trust that red-haired kid."
Perda gulped. The man sounded worried—and angry.
"Wait up!" she whispered, shuffling after Zann.
Soon they were back in the clearing. Zann stared at the wormhole's shimmer.

"Listen, Zann," Perda said. "I know you're worried about that guy. But we need to go back to the village for Mellis and Zing." She quickly told him about their narrow escape from the angry plonk farmer.
Zann's eyes lit up when Perda mentioned Zing. "He saved you? I'm so glad he's okay!"

"Yes." Perda swallowed hard. "I'll tell you more about that in a second. First I have to tell you what happened after Mellis and I got back to the village. We started getting dragged along by a Compel spell! It had to be Zira. She's the only person in Terrica with that kind of power. She's learning so fast that it's scary! We have to go back to rescue Mellis."
Perda thought about the struggle with the goons, and the way Mellis had used her new magical abilities to distract the goons so that Perda could escape.
"She sacrificed herself to let me get away," Perda told Zann. "It was really brave. She's changed a lot since we first met her."
"Wow." Zann looked back over his shoulder. "Maybe we should use this wormhole to go back to Magica right now."

Perda was still thinking about what Mellis had done. "Did I do the right thing by zapping away and leaving her there?" she thought. "I could have stayed and tried harder to fight off those goons and the Compel spell."
Then she realized what Zann had just said. "Wait, what?" she exclaimed. "We can't leave without rescuing Mellis!"
"Can't we?" Zann glanced at the wormhole again. "If we go back to Magica, we can tell my parents and Boz and the other Magic Masters what's happening here. I'm sure they'll want to help."

"But we can't just leave Mellis!" Perda exclaimed. "Who knows how long it would take us to find our way back here? This world isn't in any of the books, remember?" Suddenly she realized what would change Zann's mind. "Besides, I didn't tell you what happened to Zing yet."
She described how the plonk farmer had captured the feisty dragon.
Zann gasped. "Oh, no!" With one last look at the wormhole, he nodded. "Okay, you're right. We can't leave yet. Let's zap back to the village."
Perda was relieved. "Okay. But I'm still tired from zapping here. You'll have to zap us both. Here, grab my arm."
She shuffled closer. Zann's hand encircled her arm, squeezing tightly. She looked up at him. He looked back at her. For some reason, his cheeks looked red.
But before Perda could wonder why, Zann rubbed his other hand against his side.
"Zap!" he said.
"Finally!" Zann thought as he landed in front of Vilkor's farmhouse.

It had taken him and Perda two days to get there from the mines. The first zap had drained most of his energy, and both of them had needed to rest before continuing. Perda had speculated that the magic energy from the well was still making its way to the farthest reaches of Terrica, including the mines. That meant energy was weaker out there.

"She really is the smartest person I know," Zann thought, glancing over at her. He was happy they were back together. He was sure the two of them could figure out a plan to rescue Mellis and Zing and escape back to Magica.
Because of her Shackles, Perda stumbled when they landed. Zann grabbed her arm to steady her.
"Thanks," she said. "I wish I could get these Shackles off!"
"We'll convince Zira to remove them," Zann said confidently. "Do you have enough energy for another zap?"
"Yes," Perda said. "But I'm not sure where Mellis and Zing are now. Should we go to Zira's house to look for them or to Vilkor's new mansion?"
A man who was hurrying by stopped. "Are you looking for Sir Vilkor and Zira?" he asked excitedly. "I just heard Vilkor is offering more magical gifts out by the well! I'm going there now."
The man hurried away.
"Let's go see what's going on," Zann said.

He and Perda zapped to the well. Dozens of people were gathered there. Zann noticed that the tree had grown even more since the last time he'd seen it. It was nearly bursting out of the wall around the well.
"Stay back, everyone!" Vilkor shouted.
He was standing near the wall facing the crowd.
"What in the worlds is he wearing?" Perda asked.

"It looks like he created another fancy outfit for himself." Zann stared at Vilkor's clothing, which consisted of an elaborate robe, fancy boots with pointy toes, and a golden crown. He noticed a necklace decorated with several shiny red scales. "Hey!" he exclaimed. "Those look like dragon scales!"
He rushed forward. Vilkor was rubbing one hand on his side while waving his other hand around dramatically. "A new basin in which to bathe your baby," he said. "Here it is!"
A small metal tub appeared. The crowd gasped as a young woman repeatedly thanked Vilkor.
"You are truly wise and generous, Sir Vilkor!" She grabbed the tub and ran off.
Zann marched up to Vilkor, with Perda hopping behind him. "Where did you get those dragon scales?" he asked. "Where's Zing?"
"Hey, wait your turn!" a man complained. "We all came to ask favors."
Perda rolled her eyes. "That's not why we're here. We need a moment with Sir Vilkor, so stay back!"
She snapped her fingers and created a Shield between herself and the crowd. Zann barely noticed the villagers' cries of surprise and annoyance. He was still focused on those red scales.

"Oh! You two are alive!" Vilkor actually sounded pleased to see Zann and Perda. "Glad to see it. Zira wouldn't tell me where she'd sent you." He frowned. "It's almost as if she thinks she's in charge of this whole operation."
"Okay, but where's my dragon?" Zann said. "If you hurt him . . ."

"Don't worry," Vilkor said. "The fiery little creature is fine. These scales came off when he was fighting to get out of that cage the plonk farmer put him in." He chuckled. "He almost succeeded, actually. He'd burned halfway through the side before Zira created a metal cage to replace the old one."
"But where is he now?" Perda asked.
"At Zira's mansion," Vilkor replied. "Nobody in Terrica has seen anything like him. It really impresses the villagers when he breathes fire!"
Zann was relieved to hear that Zing was safe. But he was dismayed that the little dragon was Zira's prisoner.
"Vilkor," Perda said. "Where's Mellis?"

Vilkor looked troubled. "She's with Zira too. Zira claims that the girl has especially strong magic powers." He rolled his eyes. "Which I doubt is true. Mellis has always been a perfectly ordinary girl in every way. But Zira wants her close so she can train her. She also wanted to punish her for injuring one of her men with that rock she conjured a few days ago."
"What?" Perda cried. "But she was only protecting herself—and me! Those goons attacked us!"

Vilkor shrugged. "The man ended up with a nasty bruise." He seemed to be already losing interest in the conversation. His gaze wandered toward the crowd behind Perda's Shield. "Now if you'll excuse me, my fans are waiting."
"No, we won't excuse you!" Perda glared at him. "Mellis is your only relative! How can you allow Zira to mistreat her?"

Zann could see that Vilkor wasn't really listening. The crowd was chanting his name, and he was watching the group with a smile. Zann tried to think of a way to get through to him so he might help them.
"Vilkor only really cares about himself," Zann thought. That gave him an idea.
"It's not right that Zira is making all the decisions," Zann blurted out. "The well is on your property. That means you should be in charge, right?"
Vilkor frowned, suddenly looking annoyed. "That's true, boy. What right does she have to order me around and try to run things? Perhaps I'd better speak to her about it immediately. Zap!"
He disappeared, prompting a disappointed sigh from the crowd.
Zann glanced at Perda. "I'm sure he just zapped to Zira's place. Let's follow him."
She nodded, waited for Zann to grab her arm, and then snapped her fingers. "Zap!"
"Wow!" Perda thought when she saw Zira's mansion. "Things have changed since I left!"
"Zira made her house even bigger," Zann said. "And look! There are fancy houses all around now."
The humble shacks of Zira's closest neighbors had been replaced by large houses.
"I wonder if other people are figuring out how to use magic," Perda said hopefully. "That would be a good thing for Terrica."
Vilkor was nearby, heading toward Zira's front door. When he heard Perda's comment, he laughed.
"Don't be silly," Vilkor said. "Only a few trusted and worthy people know the secret of . . ." He glanced around and lowered his voice. "Friction."
"I see." Perda frowned. "So you and Zira are still hoarding all the magic power."
Vilkor shrugged. "Why not? That's how the world works. Some people have power, and some don't." He went inside.
"Let's go in and see if Mellis and Zing are safe," Zann said.

The front door opened into an enormous reception room. Zira was seated in a throne-like chair at the center, with several goons standing guard beside her. People in fancy clothes were sitting on sofas or chatting with one another. Perda didn't see Mellis or Zing though.
Zira was talking with one of the goons, but she looked up when Vilkor strutted toward her. "Oh, you're back." She didn't sound particularly pleased.

"Yes, and we need to talk." Vilkor put his hands on his hips. "It has come to my attention that you might be trying to take over this whole operation. I've been suspicious ever since you shared our secret with that shifty Krub."

Zira smirked. "So you're worried about losing a little power, are you? You're afraid I'll kick you out of the inner circle? Oh, dear." She snapped her fingers to create a large fireball, which she flung lazily in Vilkor's direction.
He dodged it. "Hey! You could have burned me!"
"She created that fireball so easily," Zann whispered. "It reminds me of Morb. Nobody believed that a Void could have that much power."

Perda thought about what Zann had said. "Yes, Zira seems powerful and scary," she murmured. "Still, most of the magic she uses is flashy but fairly easy to counteract. For instance, I had no trouble zapping out of that Compel spell."
Zann nodded thoughtfully. "I see what you mean. That fireball looked impressive, but it didn't even come close to hitting Vilkor."

"Zira is quick and clever about learning magic. But maybe she's not quite as powerful as she's making herself seem." Perda stepped forward. "Hey, Zira!" she shouted. "You have no right to hold Mellis prisoner. We demand that you release her—along with the dragon—right away!"
Zira frowned when she saw Perda and Zann. "How did you—? Oh, never mind. I have no time to deal with bratty children right now."
She clapped her hands to create several large fireballs.
Perda didn't flinch as they came toward her and Zann. Instead, she snapped her fingers and created a glowing purple shield that easily repelled the missiles, causing them to bounce back toward Zira.
"Hey!" Zira ducked, falling out of her throne. The goons also dodged the fireballs, shouting with dismay. One of them didn't move quite fast enough and ended up with a singed shoulder.
"Get ready," Perda whispered to Zann. "She'll try to scare us, but just remember that we know more magic than she does."
Zann nodded, rubbing his hands together vigorously. "Join friction," he whispered back.
Perda held out her shackled hands, and Zann started rubbing them. Within seconds, magic energy was crackling around them.
"That wasn't funny," Zira snarled. "You'll be sorry you tried to humiliate me."
She rubbed her hands together. Angry red smoke appeared, billowing away from Zira. People coughed and fainted as it reached them.
Perda thought quickly. "Rain!" she said.

Sheets of water poured down from the ceiling, beating down the smoke until it disappeared. The people who were still conscious ran around in confusion or crawled under the furniture to protect themselves from the downpour.
Zira snapped her fingers to create an umbrella. Then she strode forward. "Don't be cowards, kids," she said. "Face me without your silly magical wall."
"Sure, why not?" Perda snapped her fingers, and the shield disappeared. So did the rain. "We're not afraid of you."
"You should be." Zira rubbed her hands. An enormous fireball appeared, almost as big as Zira herself.
As it flew toward her and Zann, Perda sighed loudly. "Don't you know how to do anything else?" she commented. "I mean, really—this is getting boring."
She used a Deflect spell to send the fireball spinning upward. Then she used a Levitation spell to lift Zira off her feet. The woman dangled in the air, her eyes wide with alarm.
"Put me down!" Zira shouted.
Perda obeyed. As soon as the woman's feet touched the floor, Zira clapped her hands. Right away a gorzog appeared.
"Whoa!" Zann cried. "I thought you couldn't create animals with magic!"
"You can't." Perda could see that the gorzog looked surprised and confused. "Zira just transported it here from somewhere else."
The gorzog regained its senses enough to snarl and leap toward Perda. But Perda was ready. "Cage," she thought. A sturdy cage formed around the creature in midair and then crashed to the floor.

Zira looked surprised. But she recovered quickly. "Ah, well done," she said smoothly. "You've proven yourselves and passed my test." She turned toward Vilkor. "It was wise of you to bring them here, my trusted friend."
Vilkor tilted his head. "Huh?"
Zira ignored him. She turned back to Zann and Perda. "Welcome to the inner circle, you two."
"Is Zira kidding?" Zann thought in disbelief. "Perda and I don't want to be part of her little power club. Especially since we were just about to show everyone what a fraud she is!"
He opened his mouth to say so. But Perda elbowed him.
"Thank you for your kind offer, Zira," she said. "Please allow us to take a moment and discuss whether we should accept."

"Of course." Zira sounded slightly displeased, though she continued to smile. "But first, as a demonstration of good faith, I'll remove your Shackles." She snapped her fingers, and the Shackles disappeared from Perda's wrists and legs.
"Thank you," Perda said, rubbing her wrists.
She headed outside, and Zann followed.
"Did you say that just so she'd Unshackle you?" Zann asked, a little confused by the way Perda was behaving. "Because we definitely don't want to be in the inner circle!"

"Of course we don't," Perda said, looking sly. "But I think we should pretend that we do. That way, maybe we can figure out what Zira's plans are for Terrica. Then we'll know whether it's safe to leave Mellis here. Plus, if Zira thinks we're on her side, she'll probably allow us to free Zing."
Zann thought about that. He wanted his dragon back, and he wanted to get back to Magica. He also wanted to make sure Mellis was safe. As usual, Perda had concocted a clever plan.

"I suppose you're right," he said. "Also, if we're in the inner circle, we might be able to get access to the original wormhole. Then we won't have to zap all the way to the other wormhole near the mines."
They went back inside. "Thank you, Zira," Perda said with a bow. "We accept your very generous offer to join your inner circle."
"Wonderful!" Zira said.
Vilkor looked less enthusiastic. "If you keep letting people in, soon everyone in Terrica will be part of the inner circle," he grumbled.
Perda ignored him. "May we say hello to Mellis now?" she asked politely.
Zann stepped forward. "We also want to see Zing." When all the adults looked confused, he added, "The dragon."
"Oh, yes, of course." Zira signaled to the goons. "Bring Mellis out at once and release the dragon."
"Are you sure?" One of the goons looked scared. "That ungrateful little beast almost burned my hand off when I fed him this morning!"
"You heard me," Zira snapped. "Go!"
The goons hurried off. Moments later Mellis stepped into the room. Zann and Perda rushed to greet her.
"You're here!" Mellis exclaimed. She looked pale but unharmed. "I didn't think I'd ever see you two again."
Perda hugged her. "I'm glad you're safe."

Zann could tell that Perda wanted to say more. But Zira, Vilkor, and several others were watching them, obviously listening to every word they said. Zann felt frustrated. How were they supposed to figure out what to do if they couldn't speak freely?

Meanwhile Perda touched a strand of Mellis' reddish-brown hair. "Your hair looks so pretty today," she said in a cheerful voice. "Oh! I figured out a new way to braid my hair yesterday. I'd love to show you! Yours would look even prettier that way!"
Zann blinked in surprise. "What is Perda talking about?" he thought. "She didn't braid her hair yesterday."

But Mellis was smiling. "You're so sweet, Perda! Your hair is so much prettier than mine! But I'd love to have you braid it. I could braid yours, too, so we would match!" She looked around. "We could sit right here and do it, and you can tell me all about the different hairstyles where you come from."
Vilkor laughed. "Ugh, please don't!" He waved his hands. "I can't stand to listen to that sort of silliness."
Zira looked less amused. "I agree. The adult members of the inner circle have serious business to discuss. You three are too young to appreciate it."
Zann opened his mouth to protest. But a warning look from Perda made him change his mind and shut his mouth.

"Perhaps you're right, Zira," Perda said with a giggle. "I'm so tired from doing all that magic that I can't think straight! I'd love to lie down and let Mellis braid my hair, so I don't have to think about all this grown-up stuff for a while."
"Begone then," Zira said, rolling her eyes. "You may retire to Mellis' chamber."
Mellis led Zann and Perda to a small room in one of the house's new towers.
Before they entered, Mellis looked around to make sure that no goons were close enough to hear them. "Perda, that was a good idea to trick Zira into letting us be alone."
Perda smiled. "Thanks. I'm glad you caught on quickly and helped convince her. Now tell us what's been going on here since we left."
Zann felt sheepish. So that was why Perda had been talking and acting so weird! She was trying to get the three of them some privacy.
"I should have known," he thought, shooting Perda an admiring look.

Whispering, Mellis told Zann and Perda that she'd been trapped in Zira's mansion ever since Perda had zapped away. This was the first time she'd been allowed to see anyone other than Zira and the goons guarding her door.
"I was relieved to see Uncle Vilkor out there just now," she said. "I was worried for his safety. I don't think Zira intends to share power with anyone, no matter what she says."
Zann nodded. Before he could say anything, he suddenly felt an intense, searing heat strike his entire body.
"Aaah!" he cried, spinning around.
Suddenly his terror and pain turned to joy. "Zing!"
Perda smiled as Zing shot another burst of flame at Zann. "Good old Zing," she thought.
Then her smile faded. She was troubled by what Mellis had just told them.
"I don't care much about what happens to Vilkor," she thought. "But Mellis cares about him, and I care about Mellis. Zann and I haven't known her that long, but she already feels like a true friend."

"Let's decide what to do," she said after Zing settled down, and Zann magically healed his burns. "Should we return to Magica, or stay and try to convince Zira to share the truth about magic with everyone?"
Zann shrugged. "I don't like the thought of Zira and Vilkor running things. But it's not our world. Maybe it's none of our business."
Perda felt more troubled than ever. Could Zann be right?
"If Mellis can convince her uncle and Zira to rule for the benefit of all, maybe it wouldn't be so bad," she said. "But still, leaving now doesn't seem right."
She glanced over to see what Mellis thought. But Mellis hardly seemed to be listening. She was gazing out the window.
"What's wrong?" Perda asked.
Mellis sighed. "I was just thinking about the pendant I lost."
Perda recalled hearing Mellis mention that she'd lost something. "What kind of pendant?" she asked.
"It was the only thing I still had that belonged to my mother," Mellis said sadly. "I noticed it was gone shortly after you two arrived. I must have broken the cord while digging the well."
"We could zap out there later and help you search," Zann said. "We should probably check on the wormhole anyway."
"We haven't decided yet if we're leaving right away," Perda reminded him.
"I know," Zann said. "But we don't even know if we can get to the wormhole by the well. If we can't, we'll have to zap all the way back out to the mines."
"The mines?" Mellis echoed. "What do you mean?"

While Zann told her about the wormhole he'd discovered near the mines, Perda paced the room and thought about what to do. She didn't trust Zira, or Vilkor, for that matter. How could they even think about leaving Mellis—and all of Terrica—in their greedy hands?

She was still pondering the same question a few hours later at a sumptuous feast in the banquet hall that overlooked Zira's courtyard garden. The purple berries on the bush outside seemed to glow as a moon rose in the darkening sky.
Zann pushed back his chair. "I'd better take Zing for a walk," he said to Zira. "He gets restless and starts setting things on fire if he's kept indoors for too long. May I be excused?"
"Of course," Zira said before returning her attention to her conversation with the woman beside her.
A few minutes later, Mellis excused herself as well, saying she wanted to prepare sleeping chambers for Perda and Zann. Perda forced herself to wait several more minutes before standing up.
"I'm exhausted," she said, faking a yawn. "I think I'll head straight to bed."
She hurried outside and found Zann and Mellis waiting. Zing was there too.
"Are you sure we should bring him?" she asked as the little dragon flew in a circle overhead. "He tends to attract attention."
"I'm not leaving him behind again," Zann said.
Perda shrugged. "Okay, you're right. We should stick together from now on."

They zapped to the well. The villagers were gone, but the area wasn't completely deserted. A pack of gorzogs was there, circling a large metal cage. A man cowered inside the cage, dodging as the gorzogs occasionally stuck a clawed paw in to try to grab him.
"It's Trof, the plonk farmer!" Perda cried.
Trof stared at the kids with terror in his eyes. There was a long scratch on his face and another on his arm. "Help me!" he cried.
Perda didn't like Trof. But she hated to see anyone suffer. She rubbed her hands together. "Get out of here!" she yelled as she sent several fireballs toward the gorzogs.
The creatures jumped in surprise and dodged the fireballs. But they didn't run away. Perda and Zann tried creating a loud horn sound next and then bright, flashing lights.
"Stop," Mellis cried, pointing. "All you're doing is attracting more! Gorzogs are practically fearless."
Perda glanced toward the horizon, where more gorzogs were creeping into view out of the darkness. "We'd better zap away," she said. "Maybe we can figure out how to zap this guy with us."
"No, wait," Zann said. "The gorzogs seemed to react to Zing's song before, remember? Zing! Try singing!"
The little dragon started whistling. At first nothing happened.
"A fire whistler's song doesn't usually work on otherworldly creatures," Perda reminded Zann.
"Wait," Mellis said. "Look!"
One of the gorzogs had stopped to stare up at Zing. Several others did the same. Their eyes were glassy. A couple of them drooled slightly as they swayed in time with the dragon's song.
"It's working!" Perda exclaimed. She and Zann rushed to the cage. As soon as Trof was free, he raced away without even thanking the kids.
"Let's get out of here," Zann said. "We'll come back later when the gorzogs are gone."
Perda nodded, but Mellis didn't respond. She appeared to be listening carefully to Zing's song. Then she opened her mouth—and started to sing! Her voice echoed the dragon's song almost perfectly!
The gorzogs heard it too. They swayed and turned to face her adoringly. After a moment Mellis stepped forward and patted one on its scruffy head!
"Wow!" Zann exclaimed.
Suddenly Zira zapped into view.
"Uh-oh!" Perda thought. "We're in trouble!"

"I can't believe Zira isn't mad at us," Zann thought a short while later as he helped himself to another serving of pudding. "She knows we zapped away without permission and freed the plonk farmer. And I'm pretty sure she saw Mellis using magic."
He tried not to worry about it. They were back in the banquet room, eating dessert. However, Vilkor and most of the other guests were gone.
"Where did you say my uncle went?" Mellis asked Zira, looking around at the empty chairs.
"He's busy with a few errands," Zira replied. "Don't worry—he'll return shortly."
One of the other remaining guests leaned over to ask her something, and Zira stopped paying attention to the kids again.
"I can't believe that plonk farmer turned us in," Perda whispered, leaning closer to Zann and Mellis.

Zann nodded. Zira had told them that Trof had zapped straight back to town to tell her he'd seen them by the well. Apparently he was hoping for a reward. Instead Zira locked him in the dungeon in her mansion.

"I was afraid she'd punish us too," Zann whispered. "But she's treating us like royalty!" He ate another spoonful of the delicious pudding and then slipped some to Zing, who was curled up under the table.
Perda looked uneasy. "I wonder what Zira is up to."

Vilkor hurried in. "I just spoke to the representative for the villagers, as you suggested, Zira." He puffed out his chest, sounding self-important. "The villagers are willing to do whatever we say in exchange for our magic gifts. They've promised not to question any decision we make."
"Excellent," Zira said. "You have truly won their respect through your strong leadership, my friend. Well done."

That made Vilkor look even more pleased with himself. Zann rolled his eyes. It was obvious that Zira was flattering Vilkor just so that he'd do what she wanted him to do. It was even more obvious that Vilkor was enjoying every moment of it.
"He really is pathetic and selfish," Zann thought. "He doesn't care what happens to anyone else as long as he feels good."
As soon as the kids finished their dessert, they excused themselves again.
"Now, no zapping off this time," Zira said with a wink. "It's getting late."
"Don't worry, we won't," Mellis said with a weak smile.
The three kids hurried into the hallway.
"Wow," Perda said. "I wonder why she's being so nice to us."
"Me too," Mellis said. "When she caught us out by the well, I was sure we'd end up in that dungeon."

"Who has a dungeon in their house, anyway?" Zann commented. He straightened a statue that Zing had just accidentally knocked over with his wing. "Then again, who locks someone in a cage and leaves him for the gorzogs?"
Perda shuddered. "That was horrible. I mean, Trof is a jerk. But even he doesn't deserve that."
"Zira probably hoped to make an example of him so the other villagers would be afraid of her," Mellis said. "Or maybe she was trying to scare them away from the well."
"I wonder if your uncle knows she did that," Zann said.
Mellis looked troubled. "He wouldn't go along with something so cruel. At least I hope he wouldn't."

"Maybe we should ask him." Zann had just spotted Vilkor emerging from the banquet room. "If he doesn't agree with the way Zira is acting, maybe we can convince him to tell everyone how to do magic for themselves. Then Zira won't have any power over the rest of Terrica, and Perda and I can go back to Magica knowing everything is okay here."
They caught up to Vilkor in the courtyard.
"Oh, I thought you children went to bed," he said.
"We couldn't sleep after what we saw by the well," Mellis said. With help from Zann and Perda, she went on to tell her uncle about Trof and the gorzogs.

When they finished, Vilkor looked slightly concerned. But then he shrugged. "Oh well, Trof probably deserved it. In any case, it's Zira's decision. I've agreed to leave her in charge of security, while I'm the brains of the operation."

Zann traded a look with his friends. "Vilkor isn't smart enough to be the brains of anything," he thought. "It's obvious that Zira is using him as a figurehead. She's the real brains of the operation—and the muscle too."

"Please, Uncle," Mellis pleaded. "You must see that Zira is up to no good! Leaving someone to be attacked by gorzogs isn't security. It's cruelty!" She touched her neck, as if reaching for the pendant that wasn't there anymore. "I wish my mother were still alive. She would be able to convince you."

Vilkor's expression softened. "Ah, yes, my kind-hearted sister," he murmured. Then he sighed. "Oh, fine. If you kids are truly concerned about this Trof situation, I'll go ask Zira about it right now."
They checked the banquet hall, but it was deserted except for a few servants cleaning up the dishes. They continued on to the reception room.
Zira was seated on her throne, talking to a few members of the inner circle.
"Go on," Mellis whispered, giving her uncle a push. "Ask her!"
"Very well." Vilkor straightened his clothes, smoothed back his hair, and then walked slowly toward Zira.
"Hello, Vilkor," she said. "I thought you went home."
"I did," he said. "Er, I mean I was about to. That is, I wanted to ask, uh . . ." He cleared his throat, looking uncomfortable.
Before he could go on, the front door slammed open. Krub strode in, red-faced and frowning.
"Aha! There you are!" He pointed straight at Zann. "Zira, take this boy prisoner immediately. He's a murderer!"
Zira and the other adults looked shocked. One woman took a step back from Zann, obviously a bit frightened.
"What happened, Krub?" one man asked.

Krub glared at Zann. "A well-liked miner disappeared around the same time Zann did. Everyone is saying that the strange red-haired kid must have killed him." Perda glanced at Zira. "This could be the excuse she's been waiting for to lock us up!" Perda thought. After seeing what Zira was willing to do to punish a lowly plonk farmer, Perda didn't want to see how creatively she might "punish" Zann—and maybe his friends too.
Perda caught Zira smirking. But the woman quickly arranged her face into a concerned expression.
"Oh, dear!" she exclaimed. "To think we've had a murderer in our midst! He certainly had us all fooled!"
"What? I didn't kill anyone!" Zann cried. He gulped. "At least . . . not on purpose!"
A gasp went up around the room, and Perda winced.
"Oh, Zann," she thought. "I know you feel guilty about that guy falling into the vortex. But it wasn't your fault!"

"Hold on." Mellis stepped out from behind Krub. Her voice sounded shaky but determined. "Uncle Vilkor, you can't let her lock someone up based only on what Krub is saying. How do you know he's telling the truth?"
Vilkor rubbed his chin thoughtfully. "Hmm, the girl has a point, Zira," he said, shooting a mean look at Krub. "We'd better investigate the matter."
"Fine," Zira said. "But while we do, it's best if we keep Zann confined for the safety of Terrica." She started rubbing her hands together.
Perda couldn't let Zann be taken prisoner again. She grabbed his arm. "Get Zing," she hissed at him.
She looked toward Mellis, but Krub stood between them.
"Oh, no," Perda thought. "There's no time to get to her before Zira uses whatever spell she's concocting to capture Zann."
She hated to leave Mellis behind again. But what other choice did she have?
"I'm sorry," she thought, doing her best to send a mental message. "I have to get Zann out of here right now."
Mellis didn't react, so Perda didn't know if the message had reached her. But she didn't have any more time to worry about it. Zann grabbed Zing by the tail.
Perda rubbed her free hand against her side. "Ready?" she whispered.
Zann nodded. Zira noticed what Perda was doing. She narrowed her eyes and raised her hands.
Mellis let out a loud scream. "No! You can't do this!" she shrieked loudly. "Please, don't!"
Zira, Vilkor, and the other adults turned to stare at her.
"This is our chance," Perda thought.
"Zap!" she cried.
She, Zann, and Zing landed in a rural area. A few lights glowed from nearby farmhouses, and a brighter glow came from the village on the horizon.
"Whew!" Zann said, releasing Zing. "That was close."
Perda glanced toward the village. "I can't believe I had to leave Mellis behind again," she said, feeling miserable. "She seemed really scared that we were leaving without her."
"Are you sure that's why she screamed?" Zann asked. "I thought she was trying to distract everyone so we could zap away."

Perda blinked. Could Zann be right? "Mellis is so much braver now than she was when we arrived," she said thoughtfully. "It does seem strange that she'd scream out in fear like that." She shrugged. "Still, I wish we hadn't had to leave her."
"Me too," Zann said. "But now that I'm a fugitive, we should probably keep moving." He whistled for Zing, and then grabbed Perda's hand. "Zap!"
Splash!
They landed in a cold stream in a dark, hilly area.
"Where are we?" Perda asked, looking around at the unfamiliar landscape.

Zann stepped out of the stream and magically dried his shoes and pants. "Sorry about that." He grinned sheepishly. "Maybe you should do the next zap. If we try, we might be able to reach the mines by morning."
"You want to go to the wormhole?" Perda said. "But we can't leave Mellis behind!"
"She told us she didn't want to leave Terrica," Zann said. "I doubt she's changed her mind. But we don't really have a choice now that everyone thinks I murdered that man." He looked sad.
Perda bit her lip. "What if Zira takes Mellis prisoner again?" she thought. "I doubt Vilkor would lift a finger to stop Zira. But Zann's right. He's in danger if we stay."
She sighed, staring at the rushing stream. "We're not safe here anymore," she said. "But promise me we'll tell your parents and Boz what happened here as soon as we get back to Magica, okay?"
"Absolutely!" Zann said. "I bet they can help us figure out how to help Mellis. Besides, my parents will definitely want to visit this world."
Perda slowly nodded. "Grab Zing again, and let's keep going."
They reached the wormhole just as the sun rose. In the distance they heard the sounds of miners getting ready to start the day's work.
"Let's not waste any time," Zann said. "I don't want anyone to see us."
Perda nodded and looked around. Terrica was a beautiful world now that it was filling up with magic. The trees were lush, and birds fluttered everywhere, filling the air with their songs.
"I'd like to come back here sometime," she said. "It will become even more beautiful as the magic spreads. Maybe your parents will let us join their expedition."
"Maybe," Zann said, reaching for her hand. "Come on, Zing, we're going home."
He whistled, and the dragon joined them. Perda created Mutual Shackles so they couldn't be accidentally separated in the vortex. Then she glanced at Zann.
"Ready to go?" she asked.
He nodded. "Let's do this."
Zann was tired after their rapid zapping to reach the mines. But he felt relieved to be back in the vortex.
"I know Perda didn't want to leave Mellis," he thought. "I didn't either. But my parents and Boz can help her better than we can."
"I wish we knew how to go straight back to Magica," he said. "We might need to stop and rest in the first safe world we find."
"Yes." Perda sounded distracted. "Hey, Zann, did you notice the vortex looks familiar?"
Zann laughed. "Of course it does! We've been through it lots of times."
"No, that's not what I mean," Perda said. "Remember how strange it was when we were on our way to Terrica? Now it looks just like it usually does."
Zann realized she was right. "I hadn't even noticed," he said. "I was just glad to be away from Zira and her goons! But you're right. Not that it matters though. We're on our way home."
He couldn't imagine how worried their families must be by now. Still, he knew they had to rest to regain their magic energy. Otherwise the vortex wouldn't be safe.
"Sort of like it wasn't safe for the miner I accidentally pushed in," Zann thought. Would he ever stop feeling guilty about that? He tried not to think about it as he grabbed a passing wormhole.
He pulled himself partway through so that he and Perda could see the world on the other side. It was barren and dark, with no sign of people and hardly any plants.
"This isn't Fardark again, is it?" Perda sounded uneasy.

"There's no lightning or monsters around, so probably not," Zann said. "But let's keep going just in case. We still have enough energy to find a better world to rest in. Or maybe we'll find Magica next."

"Maybe," Perda said as they let go of the wormhole and tumbled on through the vortex. "But right now I'd settle for any friendly, peaceful world. Especially if it's a familiar one like Pax or Rood or maybe Niffia!"
"Niffia?" Zann laughed. "You must be desperate if you want to find that stinky place!"
They grabbed another wormhole and looked out. But this world was overcast, with lightning flashing between the clouds.
Zann shuddered. "Okay, this world definitely looks like Fardark. At least, it's similar enough that I don't want to take a chance."
"I agree," Perda said. "It's a good thing the vortex is back to normal. It's not sapping our energy as fast as it did on the way to Terrica."
They tried a third wormhole. It showed a barren, rocky world with tall mountains. But the sky was bright and clear. Zann spotted a man wandering around in the distance.
"Look, there's a person!" he said. "Let's stop here. Maybe that guy can help us figure out how to find Magica."
"I don't recognize this world," Perda said. "It doesn't look much more pleasant than the last two, but I suppose it will have to do."
They pulled themselves out and onto the rocky ground. Perda undid their shackles, and they hurried toward the man. His back was to them, but he heard them coming and spun around.
His face looked terrified. It also looked familiar.
Zann gasped. "It's you!" he blurted out as he recognized the miner from Terrica.
The miner stared at him. "Yes, it's me, Yarb." Then he glanced around. "How did you get here? This place is dangerous!"
A large shadow passed overhead. Perda glanced up and gasped with fear. "Zann, I recognize that species from your parents' book. I think we're in Drac! It's the only world the species lives in."
"We have to get out of here," Zann told Yarb. "Dragons eat people in this world!"
"Dragons?" Yarb said. "Is that what they're called? They keep trying to attack me!"
Zann shackled their arms together while Perda grabbed Zing and shackled herself to Zann. Then they all sprinted back to the wormhole.
The dragon dived toward them. A burst of flame shot out, but they leaped into the wormhole before it reached them.
Soon they were tumbling through the vortex again.
"I can't believe we found you," Zann said to Yarb. "Perda, this is the guy I was telling you about—the miner I accidentally pushed into that wormhole."
"Wormhole?" Yarb said. "I don't understand."
"I'm really sorry," Zann said. "I didn't mean to do it."
He quickly explained what had happened and how the vortex worked.
"You don't need to apologize," Yarb said. "I was wrong to attack you. And I got what I deserved." He shuddered. "That world was terrifying!"
Feelings of relief swept over Zann. "I was so worried that I'd killed him," he thought. "And I'm glad he's not mad!"
"Let's find another world," Perda said. "We all need to rest."
Yarb looked amazed. "How many worlds are there?"
Zann gave a short laugh. "Lots!"
"Okay. There's another wormhole coming up." Perda reached out and grabbed the edge.
When they looked out, they saw a beach. In one direction lay a lush, dripping forest. In the other was the sea, its waves rolling over the sandy shore. A gentle rain fell.
"It looks pretty damp out there," Perda commented. "Maybe it's Mistafar."
Zann felt a flare of hope. If Perda's guess was right, their friend Ello's people would be able to help them return home.
They pulled themselves out and onto the beach. When Zann looked toward the sea, he noticed something bobbing along in the surf nearby. He squinted, trying to get a better look through the drizzle.
"Hey, look at that," he said. "Am I so tired that I'm seeing things? Or does that look like a gulper heading this way?"
"Uh-oh," Perda thought. "We're in Skellia!"
"That's definitely a gulper," she said. "And it's coming to eat the wormhole! Back into the vortex—hurry!"
She, Zann, Yarb, and Zing leaped for the wormhole. Perda was relieved when they were back in the vortex, even though she felt more exhausted than ever.
"Something strange is happening here," she said as they tumbled along.
"What do you mean?" Zann asked.

"I'm not sure yet," Perda said. "But it seems strange that we came out in two worlds we've visited before—Drac and Skellia—but they looked very different this time. The mountains were much taller than those we've seen before in Drac, for instance."
"That's not so strange," Zann said. "We probably came out in a different part of Drac, where there are taller mountains."

"Maybe," Perda said slowly. "But how do you explain what just happened? Gulpers are from Skellia, but there was land in that world we just left. Skellia is completely covered in water. That's why Wyssa had to rescue Ello's people."
"Maybe there are gulpers in other worlds besides Skellia," Zann said.

Perda thought about that. "That's possible," she said. "A lot of species are introduced from one world to another. Morb brought several horrible creatures to Magica, remember? And I read that there were no dragons in Magica originally. They were brought there during the Old Times, probably from Drac or one of the other worlds where they're native."
"I didn't know that." Zann looked impressed. "You really have been learning a lot about Magica's history!"
"What's Magica?" Yarb asked.
"It's our home world," Zann said. "It's filled with magic energy. That's why we already know how to use magic."

Perda was still trying to figure out why the vortex seemed different. "Nobody really knows exactly how the vortex works," she said. "Not even Wyssa, or the queen of Rood, or your parents. Could we be stuck in a different part of it?"
"What do you mean?" Zann asked. "Wait! Hold on, there's another wormhole."
He grabbed the edge. But when they looked through, they saw a frozen tundra with no signs of life. Zann let go and they tumbled on.

"Maybe the vortex has branches that wander off in different directions, like a river," Perda said. "Or maybe it's like the Wormwood tree, where every branch seems to twist and turn unexpectedly. If a wormhole leads into a different branch from the one we've traveled before, it would explain why we haven't found a familiar world yet. The place we thought was Drac could be another world with dragons, and obviously that couldn't have been Skellia we just visited."
"Maybe your theory is right." Zann sounded worried. "But whatever's going on with the vortex, we need to rest soon. Let's try another wormhole."
He grabbed the next one they passed. Perda pulled herself out to look, and a strong, unpleasant, but also familiar smell struck her.
"Ew!" Zann wrinkled his nose. But then he grinned. "Hey, there's no way this could be anywhere else but good old Niffia!"
Perda felt like laughing with relief. The people of Niffia had no noses, which was a good thing, since their world smelled absolutely awful. As she breathed in, the stench was overwhelming.
"Why are we stopping here?" Yarb asked. "It stinks!"
"Yes, it does," Perda told him. "But we know this world. Its residents are kind and welcoming."
She and Zann pulled themselves out through the wormhole. As soon as they unshackled, Yarb grabbed his nose.
"Yuck," he said. "When can we leave?"
Perda looked around, expecting to see a delegation of friendly Niffians coming to greet them. That was what had happened on their previous visits to Niffia.
But there was no sign of anyone. "Let's start walking," Zann suggested. "They might not have noticed we're here yet. Maybe we can find a town."
They set off, ignoring Yarb's complaints. But after walking for several minutes, they hadn't found any signs of civilization.

"Maybe your branch idea is right," Zann said. "But maybe this branch is letting us out in completely different parts of the worlds than usual. We could be as far from the Niffian towns we know as the Far Frontier is from Swamp Bottom back in Magica."
"Maybe." Perda was feeling uneasy again. On previous visits Niffia had been dotted with pretty villages and well-tended gardens. All she could see now were wild forests and meadows.
Zing, who was flying overhead, let out a chirp.
"Look!" Zann pointed. "Zing just spotted smoke."
Perda laughed with relief. "That must be a town, or at least a farm or something."

They hurried toward the thin plume of smoke. It was coming from a clearing in the forest. A few rough huts were huddled around a firepit. Several noseless people looked up in surprise when the visitors stepped into view. They were dressed in drab rags tied together with crude rope.

"Hello," Perda said. This didn't look anything like the civilized villages she'd visited before. But at least these people looked similar to the Niffians she'd met. "We're from Magica. We're trying to find our way back home. Can you help us?"
The Niffians stared at her. Some of them smiled while others looked confused.
One woman scratched her head. "Magica? Is that on the far side of the forest?"
Perda traded a worried look with Zann.
"Could you tell us how to reach a town?" Zann asked the Niffians. "We need to speak with your leaders."
"I am the leader." Another woman stepped forward. She smiled proudly as she glanced around at the huts. "And this is the largest settlement in all of Niffia!"
"This is weird," Zann thought. "How can this woman not know about the Niffian towns we've seen?"
"We're sorry to have bothered you," Perda said, her voice shaking slightly. "Come on, you guys. Let's go."
She rushed away. Zann and Zing followed.
"Wait up," Yarb called. "Don't leave me in this smelly place!"
When they reached a meadow, Zann stopped. "Why don't we stay here for a little while and rest?"
Perda shook her head. "Not here. Not until we figure out what's going on."
Zann barely had time to grab Zing before Perda zapped the whole group to the wormhole. Soon they were back in the vortex.
Zann wasn't sure why Perda looked so scared. But now he was starting to worry too. Nothing about the worlds they'd found made sense.
"There's a wormhole," Perda said, reaching out to grab it.
When Zann pulled himself up beside her, he saw a world with purple trees and green grass. "This is Wyssa's home world!" he exclaimed. "I'm sure of it!"
They pulled themselves out. "Who's Wyssa?" Yarb asked.
Zann barely heard him. "This world has very weak magic," he said, remembering their previous visit.
Perda nodded. "It should be enough for us to create food and refresh our energy though. Let's look for people."
On their previous visit, Wyssa had purposely landed in a deserted area. She had been shunned by her people and didn't want to see them. She hadn't even told the kids the name of this world.

"Wyssa is so powerful," Zann said as they walked, with Zing flying overhead. "Maybe someone here knows how to contact her. We could ask her to take Yarb home, check on Mellis, and point us toward Magica."
They reached a small settlement. Several people emerged to greet them.
"Welcome!" an older man said. "Are you visitors to Roxo?"
"Is that the name of this world?" Perda asked. "Thanks for the welcome. We're from Magica."
"Magica?" The man furrowed his brow. "Is that a settlement in Niffia?"
A woman laughed. "Of course not," she said. "They have noses! They must be from Illumos or perhaps Skellia."
"No, we're from Magica." Zann was surprised that nobody seemed to recognize the name. "Well, except for Yarb," he added. "He's from Terrica."
"Terrica," the man said. "Isn't that the world you discovered a few years ago, Tassa?"
A young woman stepped forward. Zann blinked. "Wow, you look like a younger, taller, friendlier version of Wyssa!" He immediately regretted saying that. What if these people were still mad at her?
But Tassa didn't look mad. She looked confused. "Who's Wyssa? Is she a friend of yours?"
"Sort of," Perda said. "She helped us a few times. We think she was born in this world."
The Roxons traded looks.
The older man shrugged. "I don't know anybody with that name."
Zann was surprised. He was certain that this was Wyssa's home world and that she was well-known.
"You've been to Terrica?" Yarb asked Tassa eagerly.
"Yes," Tassa replied. "But only a couple of times, since it doesn't have magic. I advised a woman I met there on some basic potions. I hope she was able to help her people by using them."
"Was her name Zira?" Perda asked.
Tassa nodded.
Perda gasped. "That's why Zira believed we came from another world, Zann! She already knew other worlds existed!"
"You're right," Zann said.
"This also explains how she knew how to make that purple healing potion she used on your arm," Perda said.
"Yes, I left her a supply of oogberry seeds I picked up in Niffia," Tassa said. "The berries make any magic stronger."
Perda smacked herself in the forehead. "I knew those berry bushes in her courtyard looked familiar! We saw Wyssa pick oogberries in Niffia, Zann, remember?"
Zann nodded. "If those berries make magic stronger, it's no wonder Zira got so good at magic so fast."

Perda looked grim. "I saw purple marks on some of her goons too," she said. "This explains why Zira has been letting Vilkor pretend to be leader. Those bushes are still growing. She's probably just waiting to gather enough oogberries to help her take total control over Terrica!"
Yarb looked confused. "What are you talking about? Who's taking over Terrica?"
"We'll explain in the vortex on the way back there," Perda said.
"What?" Zann was surprised. "I thought we were going home to Magica!"
"Now that we've guessed Zira's plan, we have to warn Mellis," Perda said. "Those berry bushes are growing fast. There's no time to waste!"
Zann imagined how nice it would be to reunite with his parents, Boz, and Darb. It would be even nicer to hand over all the problems in Terrica to the adults and let them take care of everything.
But he knew Perda was right. They had to help their friend.
Perda looked at Yarb. "We'll take you back with us," she told him. "Unless you'd rather stay here where it's safe."
"Yes, you are welcome to stay," the Roxon man said.
"Thanks, but I want to go home," Yarb said. "If Terrica is in danger, I want to help save it."
"Good," Perda said. "We'll tell you about friction on the way. Then you can share that knowledge with all your friends. The more people who know the truth, the less power Zira will have."
Tassa and the other Roxons looked slightly confused. But Tassa agreed to guide them back to Terrica.
"I'm the most skilled at navigating the vortex," she said.
Zann peered at her. "Are you sure you aren't related to someone named Wyssa?"
Tassa chuckled. "I'm sure. But I like the sound of your friend's name. Now let's get going."
"Too bad Tassa couldn't find the wormhole by the well," Perda thought. "But I suppose this is good enough."
The Roxon woman had just dropped them off at the wormhole by the mines. "I'll go show everyone how to use friction," Yarb said.
"Even your enemy?" Zann asked.
Yarb looked sheepish. "Yes, even him. Saving Terrica is more important than petty squabbles." He disappeared among the trees.
"Let's walk for a while," Zann said. "I'm too tired to zap right now."
They hiked through the woods as Zing flew overhead. Perda felt impatient. Now that she knew how sneaky Zira had been all along, she was more worried than ever about Mellis.
"Vilkor said Mellis had powerful magic," Perda said. "That's why Zira wanted to keep her close. Do you think it's true?"
Zann shrugged. "Maybe. Mellis did toss that pond water up to the sky pretty easily. Remember?"
"Yes," Perda said. "She was able to magically tame the gorzogs too. Maybe her magic is extra strong because she was in the well when the magic first poured out."
"That makes sense," Zann said. "Look! Doesn't that flowering vine remind you of songflowers from back home?"
Perda nodded. "This really is a beautiful world, isn't it? I hope we can help bring magic to everyone. If we do, Terrica will be a great place to live."
Suddenly a scream of terror shattered the peace of the wilderness. "Help, help!" a woman's voice cried.
Perda ran fast. "We're coming!" she shouted.
She burst into a small clearing with Zann at her heels. A woman was there, cowering in front of a looming, hideous creature.
"What is that thing?" Zann exclaimed. "It looks like an extra-large troll!"
"It's a rock tromper!" the woman cried. "I threw a stick at it to stop it from eating a cute little chupo, and now it's trying to eat me instead!"
Perda remembered that Mellis had mentioned the dangerous creatures. "Rub your hands together," she shouted. "Make a fireball, and throw it right at its face!"
"What?" The woman sounded confused. "How am I supposed to make a fireball?"
"You can use magic," Perda said. "Trust me and just try it!"
The woman rubbed her hands together. The rock tromper grunted and took a step closer.
"Now think about a fireball, and say the word," Perda instructed. "One should appear in your hand."
The woman blinked. "Uh, fireball?"
Nothing happened.
"Never mind!" Zann said. "Zing, see what you can do!"
The little dragon flew over the rock tromper's head, whistling his special song. The tromper paused and stared around dully.

"It not only looks like a troll, it acts like one too," Perda said, remembering that trolls back in Magica responded in a similar way to the dragon's song. "Quick! Let's get her out of there before the creature snaps out of it!"
She and Zann ran past the rock tromper and grabbed the woman by the arms.
"Zap!" Zann said.
Splash!
They landed in the shallow water at the edge of a pond. Zing flew into view and joined them.
"Good job, little buddy." Zann gave the dragon a scratch on his scaly head.
"Are you hurt?" Perda asked the woman.
"No." The woman seemed relieved. "But I would have been, if you hadn't showed up. Thank you!"
"You're welcome." Perda shook her head. "I don't know why you couldn't use magic to rescue yourself though."
She and Zann quickly told the woman, whose name was Vari, about magic and friction. They tried again to teach her how to create things. But she wasn't able to conjure so much as a cup of water.
Finally Zann sat back. "Maybe she's a Void, like Darb."

He sounded wistful, and Perda guessed that he was missing his friend. "I've never heard of any known world with Voids except Magica," she said thoughtfully. "If Vari is a Void, that means Terrica really is a brand-new, undiscovered world!"

They walked Vari to her village and stayed there for a while, eating and drinking and resting. They also showed the other villagers how to create friction. Everyone except Vari was able to start using magic almost immediately. That made Perda more certain than ever that Vari was a Void, and that they had discovered a world that even Zann's parents had never heard of.

When they felt rested enough, Perda and Zann zapped away with Zing. It took them two more zaps, but finally they landed in the village square. A large crowd was gathered there, but people were drifting away.
"What's going on?" Zann asked a couple of teenage boys.
"There was supposed to be a parade," the taller boy said. "But Sir Vilkor tricked everyone. He just wanted an audience for his speech."
"Yeah," his friend said. "He talked about how he brought magical prosperity to us and went on and on about a ton of other stuff. It was really boring."
"'I'm Sir Vilkor,'" the first boy mimicked Vilkor. "Blah blah blah!"
The friend laughed. "Anyway, now he wants to share magic with other parts of Terrica, or whatever."
Zann gulped. "It sounds like he's planning to take over this whole world."
The shorter boy was staring at Zing. "What's that thing? Does it bite?"
"Sometimes," Perda said. "What else did Vilkor say?"
The tall boy shrugged. "A lot. He only shut up, like, five minutes ago. Then he grabbed his niece by the arm and, like, disappeared into thin air."
"Yeah." The other boy laughed. "It was the coolest thing he did all day!"
Perda barely heard him. "We're too late!" she thought, dismayed. "Vilkor just set off to take over Terrica, and he took Mellis with him!"
"Oh no," Zann thought. "Maybe we should have kept trying to get home instead of coming back here."
"This is really bad news!" Perda exclaimed. The teenage boys had wandered off, but a man and woman walked by.
Perda tapped the man on the arm. "Excuse me. Did you see Vilkor and Mellis leave just now?"
"Mellis?" The man sounded distracted as he stared at Zing, who was puffing smoke at a beetle. "Do you mean that girl who was with King Vilkor?"
"Yes, that's her," the woman said. She smiled at the kids. "King Vilkor and Princess Mellis left a few moments ago."
"Did Mellis fight back when her uncle dragged her away with him?" Zann asked.
The man and woman traded a surprised look. "No, of course not," the woman said. "They're both eager to spread magical peace and prosperity throughout Terrica."
The pair walked away.

Zann thought back to how Mellis had screamed right before he and Perda zapped away earlier. "Do you think the man and woman are right?" he asked Perda. "Maybe Mellis guessed we were leaving Terrica and decided to join forces with Vilkor and the rest of the inner circle for real."
"No way." Perda sounded certain. "She probably wanted to get away from Zira, so she could talk some sense into Vilkor. We have to find her. Maybe we can try a Uniting spell."
Zann still felt troubled. "A Uniting spell only works if the person wants to be found. If Mellis is mad at us for leaving her behind, it won't work."
Perda rolled her eyes. "Don't be silly. Of course she isn't—hey, look! There's Anso!"
She rushed toward a boy who was standing nearby. Zann followed her, and she introduced the two of them.
"What's going on?" Perda asked Anso. "We heard Mellis left with Vilkor."
Anso looked around. "We shouldn't talk about this in public," he whispered. He led them to a hidden spot behind a large, flowering shrub.
"Okay, tell us what happened," Zann said.

"After you two left, Mellis convinced Zira and the others that she was on their side now, since you'd left her behind." Anso looked nervously over his shoulder. "They believed her, but she found me and told me the truth."
"What's the truth?" Perda asked.
"She overheard Zira, Vilkor, and Krub talking after you left," Anso said. "They were happy because they thought you two had escaped to your own world and would never come back."
"We did try to go home," Zann said. "We were planning to get help, though, and then come back."
Perda nodded. "We wanted to come back and help because we suspected that Zira was up to no good."
"You were right." Anso stopped talking and peeked out around the shrub. "Uh-oh, Krub is out there," he whispered. "Let's get out of here before he sees us."
He dashed out of their hiding place. Zann and Perda followed him away from the village green, with Zing flying alongside them.
Finally Anso darted into a narrow alley between two houses. Laundry flapped over the entryway, hiding the kids from the street.

"We should be okay here, at least for now," he said, breathing hard after the run. "Anyway, as I was saying, Mellis overheard Zira, Vilkor, and Krub plotting to take over all of Terrica by using their secret knowledge of friction. Zira is planning to use those purple berries in her courtyard to create a potion that will make her magic even stronger."
"I knew it!" Perda said. "We found out those berries came from another world."
"Really? Wow." Anso looked impressed. "But wait," he added, sounding worried. "That's not all."
Zann grabbed Zing, who was sniffing at the laundry. Then he looked back at Anso, concerned by the other boy's worried tone. "What happened?" he asked.
"Mellis knew that her uncle and the others were planning something bad," Anso said. "She wanted to stop them, so she started teaching people how to use friction."
Zann glanced at Perda, who appeared surprised too. "Mellis didn't want to do that earlier," Zann said.
Perda nodded. "She must have decided it's worth the risk now."
Anso looked miserable. "She was right to be afraid. Zira caught her showing some servants how to use magic to do their work. So Zira used magic to stop Mellis from talking to them."
"What do you mean?" Zann asked. "Did she zap her away from the servants or something?"

"No, she used some kind of spell to silence her," Anso said. "Mellis can't speak at all now! The only reason I know what happened is because she wrote it down and convinced a servant to bring it to me." He shook his head. "I don't know what she wants me to do about it though. I'm just one kid! How can anyone fight back against someone as powerful as Zira?"
"Hold on," Perda said. "Zira knows that Mellis was working against her. Why did she let her go off with Vilkor instead of punishing her? That doesn't seem like her style."
Zann shuddered, remembering how Zira had punished Trof by trapping him with some gorzogs.

Anso shrugged. "Zira and Krub were ready to dump Mellis in a deep dungeon somewhere. But Vilkor wanted to take her along, so they let him. They're still pretending he's in charge, even though pretty much everyone else knows it's really Zira who's running things."
"Zira probably wants to keep Vilkor happy until she grows more berries," Perda said grimly. "And Mellis can't speak, so Zira probably isn't worried about her."
Zann clenched his fists, suddenly glad that he and Perda hadn't found their way back to Magica after all. "We have to find Mellis and rescue her!"
"Zann's right," Perda thought. "We have to find Mellis!"
"Let's use a Uniting spell," she said.
"Okay," Zann said. "Now that we know she's still on our side, it should work."
Perda turned to Anso. "Stay here in the village, okay? Try to learn more about what's going on."
Anso agreed and hurried off.
"Let's join friction," Zann said. "Uniting spells take a lot of energy."
They rubbed their hands together. Perda pictured Mellis and murmured, "Unite!" She grabbed Zann's hand, and he grabbed Zing's wing as they were zapped away. They landed in an empty meadow.
"Did it work?" Zann asked. "I don't see anyone."
"It took me several zaps to unite with you earlier," Perda said. "Luckily Vilkor and Mellis didn't have much of a head start. I bet we'll catch up to them on the next zap."
But she was wrong. It took three more zaps before they finally spotted Vilkor. He was surrounded by a small group of goons and other servants.
"I wonder why they stopped here." Zann looked around at the wooded foothills where they'd landed. "There aren't any other people around."

Perda made sure that they were hidden behind some bushes. Then she sat down to catch her breath. "They probably stopped to rest," she said. "I'm glad. I don't think we could have zapped any more today."
"Where's Mellis?" Zann murmured.
Just then Vilkor shouted, "Mellis! Where are you?"
Mellis stepped into view from behind an extra-large goon. Perda was relieved to see that she looked okay.
Vilkor pointed to a flat bit of ground. "Create my sleeping quarters here," he said. "Make sure it's comfortable. I want to be well rested when we arrive at the mountain village tomorrow."

Mellis nodded and rubbed her hands together, quickly creating a large, luxurious tent with soft cushions inside. Next she created a table full of delicious-looking food and drink. Zing noticed the food and tried to fly toward it, but Zann held him back.
Perda watched Mellis create a comfortable lounge chair, which she magically placed next to the food table.
"Wow," Perda whispered. "No wonder they were able to zap so far today. Mellis has a lot of power!"
"I guess Zira was right," Zann said. "And I bet you were right when you said it's because Mellis was in the well when all that magic energy poured out."
Perda nodded, feeling worried. If Zira knew how strong Mellis really was, she probably wouldn't let her remain free for long. "We need to get Mellis alone and talk to her."

They didn't have a chance to do so for a while. While Vilkor lounged by the table, eating and drinking, he made Mellis work. He ordered her to make small, plain tents for the goons and servants. Then he told her to create an addition to his tent for herself.
"Don't make it too big though," he said. "You don't want to wear yourself out. And what does a mere girl need with a lot of space?"
Mellis nodded meekly. She snapped her fingers, and a smaller tent appeared, attached to Vilkor's large one.
Meanwhile the goons were digging a fire pit. As darkness fell, they lit a campfire.
Vilkor peered at it from his lounge chair. "Fetch more wood," he ordered. "We can't let the fire go out. I don't sleep well when it's chilly."
"Doesn't he realize he could snap his fingers and make more wood?" Zann whispered. "Or he could create a fire that doesn't require wood to burn."
Perda shrugged. "Vilkor still doesn't seem to understand how magic works. No wonder Zira can trick him so easily."
She noticed two servants, a man and a woman, hiking into the woods nearby. She and Zann ducked down farther so they wouldn't be seen, holding Zing still between them.
As the servants passed the kids' hiding place, one bent to grab a fallen branch. The second glanced back over her shoulder.

"This is ridiculous," the woman whispered. "Vilkor and Zira claim that magic involves secret spells and that only certain people can do it. But I heard a rumor back in town that magic can be done by anyone and that it's not difficult at all!"
"Really?" The male servant looked skeptical. "Who told you that?"
"My friend Finna," the woman replied. Then she looked worried. "It was right before she disappeared. You don't think Zira did something to her, do you?"

The man shrugged. "Who knows what Zira might do?" He lowered his voice even more. "But actually, my sister told me the same thing Finna told you. She heard it from a miner who'd just returned to the village. Do you think it could be true?"
The pair moved farther into the woods until Perda couldn't hear them anymore. "Wow," she whispered. "I guess the truth is spreading!"
Eventually Vilkor ate and drank so much that he fell asleep in the lounge chair, snoring loudly. The servants discussed whether to move him into the tent. Finally a goon shrugged.
"Doesn't look like rain," he said. "Let's just get some rest."

Everyone else crawled into their tents, including Mellis. Perda and Zann waited until they heard snores from all directions. Then they crawled cautiously past the sleeping Vilkor to Mellis' tent. Zing followed, sniffing in the direction of the mostly empty food table.
"Zing, stop!" Zann whispered. But the little dragon had just spotted Mellis sleeping inside the tent. He rushed in and breathed hot air in her face, flapping his wings in greeting.
Mellis sat up and rubbed her face. Her eyes widened when she saw Zing. She glanced at Perda and Zann, and her expression went dark. She pushed Zing away and shook her head angrily.
"Uh-oh," Zann thought. "Maybe I was right, and Mellis is angry that we abandoned her!"
But Perda was gesturing for Mellis to come with them. Without hesitation, Mellis tossed aside her bedding and crawled out of the tent. The kids all ran for the woods with Zing flying overhead.
Once they were out of sight of the camp, Mellis gestured wildly with her hands.
"Oops," Zann said. "I forgot she can't speak."

"Hold on," Perda told Mellis. "I'll see if I can undo the spell Zira put on you. I've been thinking about it, and I bet it's something called a Muting spell. I read about it recently. It was used a lot during the Old Times in Magica."

Zann was impressed. He hadn't even thought about how they were going to release Mellis from the spell. He helped Perda create friction, and then she touched Mellis' lips with her finger. It took a couple of tries, but finally Mellis let out a gasp.

"Oh, thank you!" she exclaimed softly. "But I didn't want you to come back here. I was hoping you were safe at home in Magica by now! I tried to help distract Zira and the others by screaming so you could get away."
"So Perda was right, as usual," Zann thought with a smile.

"Thank you," Perda said. "We did get away. But while we were in the vortex, we heard something you need to know." As they walked deeper into the woods, she quickly told Mellis about the oogberry bushes at Zira's house.

"Wow." Mellis looked worried. "Zira already has too much power. And my uncle doesn't seem to realize that she's only using him! He's happy to go along with whatever she suggests, since he loves the attention he gets as the so-called supreme ruler. But what will happen once Terrica is fully under her control, and she and Krub don't need him anymore? I'm afraid for him—and for Terrica."

Zann grabbed Zing to stop him from eating a spiky caterpillar. "I'm not that worried about Vilkor," he thought. "He's pretty annoying, and most of the problems are at least partly his fault. But it would be terrible if Terrica fell under the power of Zira and Krub!"
"We have to do something," he said as he hopped over a fallen tree trunk.
"I know." Mellis sighed. "But what can a few kids do against adults who will do anything to gain power?"
Zann grinned. "You might be surprised. We told you what happened back in Magica, right?"
Mellis nodded. "You mean when you guys defeated that guy Morb? I almost forgot about that." She smiled back at Zann. "Maybe there is hope after all! Especially with you two helping."
"We need a plan," Perda said. "Let's—hey, what was that?"
Zann had heard the same sound. Loud growling and grunting sounds were coming from somewhere in the dark woods.
Mellis' eyes widened with alarm. "Look!" she whispered, pointing through a break in the trees. "Rock trompers!"
Zann saw them now too. Several of the huge creatures were chasing after some smaller creatures. At first he couldn't see what they were. But when they moved closer, he recognized them.
"Chupos!" he exclaimed.
One of the rock trompers heard him. It looked at the kids, grunted at the others, and then charged toward them.
"They see us!" Mellis cried. "Run! We have to warn my uncle and the others!" She ran back toward camp.
"Do a Shield spell!" Perda called after her. "Just like we taught you, remember?"
Zann glanced back and saw that the rock trompers and the chupos were both chasing them now. "Uh-oh," he thought. "They're fast!"
"We'd better zap to camp!" he yelled, grabbing Zing. "Otherwise we'll never make it. Zap!"
He landed in the clearing. A split second later, the two girls appeared.
"Join friction!" Perda cried.
"It's okay—I've got it," Mellis said. She snapped her fingers, and a glowing purple shield appeared over the entire camp.
Vilkor awakened and sat up, looking dazed. "What's going on?" he grumbled. "I'm trying to sleep!"
"Let's get out of here before he sees us," Zann whispered.
Perda nodded. "We'll be in touch," she whispered to Mellis. Then she grabbed Zann and Zing. "Zap!"
They landed in the forest. Zann could still hear the rock trompers grunting. The chupos started howling. Zann guessed the creatures were frustrated because Mellis' shield had stopped them.
Perda was listening too. "Let's make our own shield," she said. "Hold on to Zing for a second so he stays put."
Zann grabbed the dragon. Perda quickly created a smaller blue bubble over the three of them.
"There," she said. "Now we can get some sleep. We'll need to be well rested so we can follow Vilkor wherever he goes tomorrow."
"Right." Zann released Zing and stretched out on the ground, gazing up at the stars that twinkled overhead. He sneaked a peek at Perda as she settled down beside him.
"The stars look so familiar, don't they?" she said. "Looking up, you can almost believe we're back home in Magica."
"Uh-huh." Zann wasn't sure what else to say.
Suddenly he couldn't stop thinking about Darb and Gliss holding hands. "What if I reached over and held Perda's hand right now?" he thought. "What would she think?"
Just then Zing crawled over him and settled down between him and Perda. Seconds later the little dragon was sound asleep, snoring out smoky breath into Zann's face.
"Good night, Zann," Perda whispered.
"Good night," Zann said. Then he turned over on his side, away from Zing, and did his best to forget about holding hands as he fell asleep.
"Finally!" Perda thought as she, Zann, and Zing landed from a zap and saw signs of civilization.
"This must be the village Vilkor mentioned yesterday," Zann said.
It was the day after they'd found Mellis. They'd spent the morning following Vilkor's group farther up into the mountains.
The village consisted of about a dozen rough huts built on a steep, craggy ridge. The only flat area contained a rough but strong-looking curved stone wall.
"I bet that's where the villagers hide from rock trompers and other scary stuff," Perda said.
"This whole place is kind of scary, isn't it?" Zann said.
Tufts of weedy grass and slimy-looking moss grew here and there on the rocky ground. The forest was dark and thick. Vines seemed to choke the twisted trees.
"Who would want to live here?" Zann asked.
"Those people, I guess." Perda watched as a crowd of people emerged from their huts to face Vilkor and his group.
"Who are you?" a man called, sounding suspicious. "What are you doing here? We don't like outsiders."
"You'll like me, I promise." Vilkor sounded confident. "I am your supreme ruler, and I've come to bless you with the wonders of my magic powers."
"Supreme ruler?" a woman said with a laugh. "Step back, or you'll meet the magic of our sharp spears!"
Several other villagers murmured in agreement and lifted their crude weapons.
Vilkor chuckled. "I was hoping we could do this the easy way. Oh well. Perhaps this will convince you."
He rubbed his hands together and then waved them dramatically over his head. "Behold my awesome power!"
Bursts of colorful light erupted all over the area. The villagers gasped in fear. Some ran behind the stone wall to hide.
Perda noticed that Mellis was snapping her fingers. Each time she did, a weapon flew out of a villager's hands and landed behind Vilkor's group.

"Mellis is doing more practical magic, as usual," she whispered to Zann. "Vilkor likes flashy spells, but he always makes Mellis do the harder work." She remembered with disgust how Vilkor had expected his niece to dig the well all by herself.
The villagers shouted in alarm. "Who are you, and what do you want?" a man cried.
"I told you. I am the ruler of all the land." Vilkor rubbed his hands together. He pointed at one of the huts, causing it to explode.
"My house!" a villager cried.
"What's he doing?" Perda cried. "He won't win them over by destroying their homes!"
Mellis seemed to be thinking the same thing. She grabbed her uncle's arm and shook her head. Then she snapped her fingers and magically repaired the hut. The villagers gasped and then cheered.
But Mellis wasn't finished. She pointed at the stone wall. Seconds later it was taller and stronger than before, with a sturdy roof and a solid wooden door.
The villagers gasped again. "The rock trompers will never reach us now!" a woman exclaimed. "Thank you, strangers!"
"You're welcome," Vilkor said, stepping in front of Mellis. "Now I'll tell you more about my amazing powers."
He levitated onto the roof, to more gasps from the crowd. Then he looked around.

"Hmm, nice view from up here," he said. "Very secure, too, with dense forest all around. This might be a good place to build a fortress for myself." He pointed to Mellis. "Join me, dear niece, while I tell these villagers how lucky they are that I've mastered the wonders of magic."
Mellis floated up to stand beside her uncle.
"Good," Zann whispered. "It will be easier for her to put our plan into action from up there. Especially since Vilkor thinks she's still muted."

Perda nodded. She'd woken up that morning with an idea for a plan, and she and Zann had sneaked into camp to tell Mellis about it before everyone else woke up. Once the villagers were gathered, Mellis was supposed to speak up and tell them the truth about friction.
"Do you think it will work?" Zann asked as Vilkor began to speak bombastically about his amazing powers. "Some Terricans seem to have trouble believing they can do magic themselves."

"That's true," Perda said. "But hearing those servants talking in the woods last night makes me think people are starting to believe it. Let's disguise ourselves and hide in the crowd. That way we can start showing people what to do once they hear what Mellis has to say."

"Good idea." Zann rubbed his hands together and used a Cloaking spell to make himself look more like the villagers. Perda did the same. They also used a Cloaking spell to make Zing resemble a large bird.

Meanwhile Vilkor was still speaking. "And with the mighty powers I now possess, I shall turn Terrica into a peaceful and prosperous land. If you follow me, I'll shower you with magical wonders beyond your wildest dreams."
"Are you the only one who can perform these magical wonders?" a man called out.
"Yes!" Vilkor cried. "Er, that is, my niece also possesses some ability, along with a couple of other assistants back in the village."
"Is he talking about Zira and Krub?" Zann whispered. "I wonder how they'd like being called his assistants!"
"Shh," Perda said. "I think Mellis is about to speak."
She held her breath, watching Mellis square her shoulders and step forward. Would their plan work?

Vilkor was still talking. "However, I've decided that a land made fertile and affluent through magic needs a better name than Terrica, so I'm officially renaming it. From here on, you may refer to me as the supreme ruler of the great land now known as . . ." He waved his hands, sending up puffs of smoke and glitter. "Magica!"
"Huh?" Zann thought in surprise. "We never told Vilkor anything about Magica. How did he come up with that name? Did Mellis tell him?"
Perda let out a gasp so loud that a man glanced over in surprise. "Oh, wow!" she blurted out. Then she grabbed Zann by the arm. "Come with me. We have to talk!"
Feeling confused, Zann allowed Perda to drag him away and into the woods. Zing hurried after them.
When Perda turned to face Zann, she looked pale and stunned.
"What is it?" he asked. "Are you okay?"
"Don't you get it?" she asked.
"Get what?" Zann scratched his head. "Are you talking about what Vilkor just said?"
