"Yes!" Perda said. "It explains everything—like why the stars and trees and other stuff seem so familiar. And why the rock trompers look similar to trolls. And why the worlds we visited the other day seemed so odd."

Zann tapped his chin, barely paying attention. "I wonder if Zira overheard us talking about Magica. She spied on us a lot to learn about magic, remember? Maybe she heard us mention the name of our world to Mellis."
Perda grabbed him by the shoulders, staring into his eyes. "This is our land. Terrica is Magica!"
Zann was a little distracted by Perda's pretty brown eyes. "Huh?" he said, trying to focus on what she was saying. "Yeah, I know, Vilkor decided to rename it. But how did he—"
"You're not listening to me!" Perda let go of Zann's shoulders and started pacing back and forth. "Don't you see what's happening yet? Even that riddle should have given us a clue. Remember?"
She stopped, cleared her throat, and quoted the verse from Zann's parents' lab:
"Bygone days lost to time's haze
Yet visible to careful gaze
Rooted in the depths of time
Touch and see—no need to climb."
Zann was impressed that Perda remembered the rhyme so perfectly. Then he blinked.
"Wait," he said slowly, finally catching on. "'Bygone days.' Do you mean . . ."
"Yes, Zann," Perda said. "When we fell into that strange wormhole at the base of the Wormwood tree, we didn't travel to another world. We traveled back in time!"
Zann gasped, hardly daring to believe it was true. But the more he thought about it, the more sense it made to him.
"The swamps near the mines," he blurted out. "I thought the birdcalls there sounded familiar!"
Perda nodded. "You must have been in the place that will be Swamp Bottom someday."
Just then there was a rustle in the bushes nearby. A chupo poked its snout out, sniffed at the kids, and then howled. Zing chirped in alarm, and then shot a stream of flames at the chupo.
"Good boy," Zann said to the dragon as the chupo disappeared.
"Let's get away from here," Perda said. "Someone might come to investigate that howl."
They headed deeper into the woods. It was dark beneath the canopy of twisted trees. Noisy insects buzzed in the air, and Zann could hear animals moving just out of sight.

"It's creepy in here," he said with a shudder. "Maybe this is Mount Mystery! That would explain why it's so scary." He searched his mind, trying to remember what he'd learned in history class. "Do you think this is the Old Times?"
"I doubt it." Perda looked thoughtful. "In the Old Times, there was a ton of dark magic, and everyone used all kinds of dangerous spells. No, I think this is the time before that."
"Before the Old Times? Wow." Zann tried to imagine it. Then he realized he didn't have to imagine it—he was living it!
"Right," Perda went on, sounding awed. "We're in the distant past, and that scrawny little tree near the well must be the Wormwood tree. We witnessed Mellis opening the Source of magic!"

Zann thought hard as he trudged through the forest with Zing flying overhead. "The wormhole by the tree," he said. "It brought us to a vortex through time, right? So then when we went through the other wormhole . . ."
"It took us into the regular vortex," Perda said, finishing his sentence. "And since we're in the distant past here, we're also in the distant past in all the other worlds we visited."
"So that really was Skellia that we visited," Zann said. "It just hasn't been covered in water yet."
"And the Niffians haven't yet built their beautiful towns," Perda said. "It's also why nobody in Wyssa's home world had heard of her. She won't be born until years and years from now!"
"Let's circle back toward the village," Zann said. "We have to tell Mellis about this."
They reached the clearing just in time to hear Mellis speaking.
"It's not difficult at all!" she said, her voice shaking a little. "If you just rub your hands together—"
"Silence!" Vilkor roared, striding over and grabbing her by the shoulder. He covered her mouth with his free hand and then shouted, "Zap!"
The two of them disappeared to cries of confusion from the villagers. Vilkor's servants and goons seemed alarmed.
"Hey, where'd they go?" a goon said.
The clearing erupted into chaos. Servants, goons, and villagers started running around, shouting in alarm.
"I bet Vilkor zapped them back to the village," Perda said to Zann. "Zira probably did that Muting spell on Mellis, and he doesn't know how to restore it."

Zann nodded, grabbing Zing and taking Perda's arm. "We have to get back there and save her!" he cried. He gulped, glancing up at the peak of what he now knew was Mount Mystery. "And then figure out what we're going to do about all this!"

Perda rubbed her hands together and thought about doing a Uniting spell. But her head was spinning with what she had just realized, and she couldn't focus on what she was trying to do. It was amazing to think that she and Zann were living through some of the Magica history she found so fascinating.

"Hardly anyone in Magica knows what the world was like this far in the past," she thought. "Now Zann and I will be able to tell them." She gulped, realizing something. "Well . . . if we can figure out how to get back to our own time, that is!"
"What's wrong?" Zann squeezed her arm impatiently. "Are you going to do the Uniting spell, or what?"
"Um, sorry," Perda said. "Please zap us back to the village, okay? I'm sure that's where they went, so we don't need to do the Uniting spell. I'll help create friction for the Zap."
"Okay," Zann said, looking slightly confused. He held on tightly to Perda's arm, and also to Zing. "Zap!"
Splash!

They landed in a clear, cold stream bubbling through a pretty meadow in the foothills of the mountains. Birds were chirping all around, and Perda couldn't help wondering how many species she would recognize from her own time.
"It's too bad Darb isn't with us," she said. "He would have recognized more of the plants and animals here. Maybe we would have figured things out faster."
"Maybe," Zann said. "But you figured it out anyway. I'm not sure I would have."

Perda smiled at him. "We can rest here for a few minutes," she said as they stepped out of the water and magically dried their shoes. "Now that Vilkor knows Mellis isn't on his side, he's probably doing the zapping himself. He's not as strong as she is, so he'll have to rest too."

She flopped onto the ground, still thinking about everything she'd just figured out. Mentioning Mellis made her think again about how powerful their new friend's magic was. She appeared to have nearly as much magical ability as an experienced Magic Master like Zann's grandfather, Boz.

"It all makes sense now," Perda said thoughtfully. "If that's really the Wormwood tree, and Mellis opened the Source of magic, then it's no wonder she's got super strong magic energy. She was completely surrounded by it when it first emerged in its purest form."

Zann looked interested. "So the energy was more concentrated, right?" he said. "I get it. That's probably why she fainted at first. It overwhelmed her since she wasn't used to magic at all. But maybe it's also why she's so good at magic now."
"Right." Perda glanced at Mount Mystery, now a dark peak in the distance. "It's weird to think about all the stuff we've seen here and compare it to our own time."
"Yeah, I was thinking about that while we zapped," Zann said. "The mine where Krub made me work is probably where the spellstone mines are in our time."

Perda nodded. They had visited those mines a couple of times on school trips. Spellstones were another relic of the Old Times. They didn't contain much power in modern times, but during the Old Times, they'd been important for different kinds of magic.
"Let's zap again," she said. "I don't want to let Vilkor get a head start. Are you rested enough?"
"Sure," Zann said with a smile. "Are you sure you don't want to zap us this time? We've already landed in the water once."
"It's okay—you do it." Perda still felt distracted by all the thoughts running through her head.

The next zap brought them to a flat area with only a few trees and shrubs. There was no water around, either, so their shoes stayed dry this time. However, Zann accidentally landed them in a prickly bush.

"I'm still trying to figure out which sites in this time correspond with landmarks in our own time," Perda said as she healed the scratches from the thorns. "If the area by the well eventually turns into Wormwood, that means First City will be created all across Mellis and Vilkor's farm."

"You're probably right," Zann agreed, flopping down on the grass to rest. He shooed away Zing, who was breathing smoke into his face. "But First City is so big, it probably stretches as far as their village too. I wonder where the palace will be? Maybe we can figure it out."
"Maybe." Perda shrugged. "We'd better not wait too long to zap again. If we get to the village before Vilkor does, maybe we can figure out a plan to rescue Mellis before they find Zira."
"Good idea," Zann said. "I'm not looking forward to seeing Zira again. Last time we saw her, she tried to take me prisoner!"
Perda realized he was right. "We'll have to be careful." She smiled. "Which means I'll do the zapping this time. Otherwise we might land right in her lap!"
Zann laughed sheepishly. "Okay. Come here, Zing. Let's go!"
Perda grabbed Zann's arm, and then waited for him to catch Zing. She created friction, took a deep breath, and focused on where she wanted to go.
"I'll aim for the farmhouse," she said. "Now that Vilkor has his fancy mansion in town, there probably won't be anyone at the farm." She took a deep breath. "Zap!"
When they landed, the first thing Perda saw was the farmhouse right beside them, which made her glad they'd landed where she'd wanted to land.
But the second thing she saw was . . .
"Gorzogs!" Zann shouted, yanking Perda aside just as one of the fearsome creatures leaped at her.

"What are those things doing here?" Zann thought as he stared at the gorzog that had just tried to attack Perda. It had crashed into the dirt when it missed its target. Now it rolled over, growling with frustration, and climbed back to its feet.
"Look out!" Perda shouted.

Zann spun around and saw another gorzog running toward them. He and Perda leaped aside, and the creature passed between them, crashing into the first one. Meanwhile Zann noticed a third gorzog peering out the farmhouse door.
"We have to get out of here!" he called to Perda. "Grab my hand!"

All three gorzogs charged, slime dripping from their curved teeth and ugly snouts. The one from the house jumped out and landed in between Zann and Perda, turning one way and then the other as if wondering whom to attack first. Zing whistled in fear while zipping around overhead. Zann realized there was no way he could get to Perda before the gorzogs got to both of them.
"Just zap!" she called, already rubbing her hands together. "Meet me in front of Zira's house!"
Zann nodded. As Perda zapped out of sight, he reached up and grabbed Zing, snapping his fingers with the other hand to create friction. "Zap!" he cried.
Splash!
Zann landed in a fancy stone fountain inside a large room. Zing muttered and spit out water and steam as Zann looked around.
"Uh-oh," he thought as he recognized the room. "I tried to zap in front of Zira's house like Perda said. But instead I zapped inside her house!"
The room was deserted, but Zann heard voices coming closer. He jumped out of the fountain, grabbed Zing, and hid behind a piece of furniture.
"Oops," he thought as he saw the wet footsteps he'd left behind. He quickly snapped his fingers and used magic to dry them.
A second later Vilkor and Mellis stepped into the room. "Uncle, please listen to me!" Mellis was saying. Zann realized that the pair must have zapped into the house at about the same time he had.

Vilkor's eyes swept the room, but he didn't spot Zann. "Where is Zira?" he snapped. "She won't be pleased to hear about your disloyalty, niece!" He glared at Mellis. "Why couldn't you just go along with our plans? We have a good thing going here—it's everything we've ever wanted!"
"No, it's everything you wanted!" Mellis said. "I don't care about power and glory. All I want is a peaceful land where everyone can use magic to create what they need."
Vilkor frowned. "But then I wouldn't have any more power than anyone else."
"Exactly," Mellis said. "What's wrong with that?"
Vilkor rolled his eyes. "You don't understand," he said. "You remind me more and more of your mother. She was always a do-gooder too. But I won't let you ruin this for me!"
Before Mellis could respond, Zira zapped into the room. Krub was with her, along with a pair of hideous gorzogs.
Vilkor gasped. "Look out! Gorzogs!"

Zira smirked, seeming to enjoy his fear. "That's right," she said, holding up one hand and examining her own purple-stained fingers. "I've discovered yet another useful application of my otherworld potions. I've figured out how to use their extra power to tame these fearsome beasts and bend them to my will."

Zann's eyes widened. "The oogberries!" he thought, glancing toward the nearest window. Through it, he caught a glimpse of the courtyard where the purple-berried bushes were growing. "Perda was right," he told himself grimly. "Zira wants to use the berries' power to make herself even more powerful."
Krub snickered. "Don't worry, Vilkor," he said mockingly. "The gorzogs won't hurt you as long as you obey your supreme ruler—Zira."
"What?" Vilkor frowned, seeming to forget about the gorzogs for a second. He took a step toward the other two. "Hold on one second. Have you forgotten that I'm the supreme ruler?"
Zira snapped her fingers. One of the gorzogs crept closer, its eyes locked on Vilkor.

Vilkor gulped. "Er, on the other hand, there's no need to be hasty." He took a step back. "When I said I was the supreme ruler, I meant we , of course. We're all in this together, a team. We're, um, partners, right?"

Zira looked disdainful. "Are you really that feeble-minded, Vilkor? I suppose you are. After all, you don't even realize when you're being spied on. Otherwise you never would have dared to call me . . . what was it? Your assistant ?"

Zann realized Zira must have seen what Vilkor had said to the mountain villagers. "But how?" he thought. "Did she discover spy flies? Or . . ." His gaze wandered back to the window. "I know! It's probably another otherworld trick she invented using those oogberries."

He forgot about that when Zira's nose twitched, and then she turned to stare toward his hiding place. "Ah, and it seems you're being spied on again right now," she said to Vilkor. "We both are. But not for long."

Raising one hand, she made a beckoning gesture with her purple-stained fingers. Zann couldn't help crying out as he felt himself being magically lifted into the air. He floated out of his hiding place toward Zira.
"It's you," she hissed when she recognized him. "This time I'll make sure you don't escape. Immobilize!"
Zann felt his limbs go numb. "Zing, quick!" he croaked out, seconds before the spell took away his ability to speak. "The berries!"

Luckily the little dragon understood. As Zann felt himself go motionless, Zing sprang into action, flying out the window and spitting fire. Zann's face was already immobilized, so he couldn't even smile as he saw the oogberry bushes burst into flames.
Perda didn't have time to focus on where she wanted to go when she zapped away from the gorzogs. When she landed, she found herself by the well.
"That's the Wormwood tree," she thought, staring at the tree growing behind the wall Zira had erected. "Even though nobody will call it that for years, I suppose."

For someone like her, who wanted to be a researcher, it was a dream come true to travel to ancient Magica. But with a shiver of anxiety, she wondered once again how she and Zann would ever travel back to their own time.
Perda noticed several gorzogs near the wall. She almost zapped away again but then saw at least two dozen people hanging around nearby.
"Why aren't the gorzogs attacking anyone?" she thought.
"Perda! Is that you?" a familiar voice called. It was Anso. He hurried over.
"What are you doing here?" Perda asked him.
"My father heard that the well's waters have special powers," Anso said. "He brought my mother to see if it might cure her illness."
"What's holding back the gorzogs?" Perda asked.
Anso shrugged. "Nobody knows. But they've been staying right by the wall. They growl when anyone goes too close."
"I bet Zira figured out how to control them," Perda said. "She probably ordered them to guard the well."
As she took a step closer, her foot hit something on the ground. It was a cracked pottery cup—the same one Zira had dropped days earlier. Perda wondered why it looked so familiar.
Then she gasped as she realized it looked exactly like that ancient, cracked cup at Zann's parents' lab!
"It's a relic," she whispered. "At least, it will be one someday."
"Where's Mellis?" Anso asked. "Is she safe?"
"I'm not sure," Perda said. "Zann and I are going to help her though. I just need to find him. But first, let's heal your mother."

Anso brought Perda to his parents. At first his mother looked nervous, but she agreed to let Perda try to heal her illness. Perda was nervous too. She was good at healing cuts and scrapes, but she'd never healed anything serious. She created friction and then touched the woman on the arm.
"Heal," she murmured.
Anso's mother immediately looked healthier. Anso and his father gasped.
"It worked!" Anso cried. "Thank you so much!"
"You're welcome," Perda said.
At that moment Zira zapped into view, surrounded by goons. Krub was there, too, holding onto Zann, who wasn't moving.

"Oh no," Perda thought. "It looks like Zira did an Immobilization spell on him!" In her own time, people were supposed to use that spell only in self-defense. She hid behind a flowering shrub so Zira wouldn't see her while she decided what to do. Anso came with her, looking confused.
Then Vilkor zapped into view, gripping Mellis' arm. "Zira!" he cried. "Please reconsider your decision, my old friend!"
"What decision?" Anso whispered.
"I don't know," Perda whispered back. "But we have to get Zann and Mellis away from Zira."
She noticed that neither of her friends was saying anything. She guessed that Zira had put a Muting spell on both of them.
Vilkor dragged Mellis closer to the others. "We make such a good team, Zira!" he exclaimed. "And you can trust me. I'll prove my loyalty however you like."

"Really?" Zira smirked, clearly enjoying his groveling. "Then perhaps I'll give you one more chance. You can prove your loyalty by tossing your niece to my gorzog guards." She glanced toward the beasts guarding the wall. "They're getting hungry."
Vilkor gasped. So did Perda.
"He won't do it," Anso said, sounding uncertain. "Will he?"
"Please, Zira!" Vilkor grabbed her sleeve, looking distraught. "Choose another test, I beg you. Mellis is my only family, and she's a good girl. Well, mostly, anyway!"
"I've made my decision." Zira shot a cold look at Mellis and then returned her gaze to Vilkor. "Now you must make yours."
Perda held her breath. Would Vilkor actually sacrifice Mellis just to get back into Zira's good graces?
She was shocked when Vilkor started shoving Mellis toward the gorzogs.
"Sorry, Mellis," he said. "This is your own fault, you know. You should have stuck to our plan." Then he glanced back at Zira. "They won't eat me , will they?" he asked nervously.
"We have to do something!" Anso whispered urgently.
Perda nodded. "Leave it to me."

She rubbed her hands together and stepped forward. Vilkor was still pushing Mellis in the direction of the gorzogs. The creatures watched, sticky saliva dripping from their snouts. The largest took a step toward Mellis.

Perda knew she had to act now. "Blast!" she shouted, sending a strong bolt of magic energy straight at Vilkor. She felt a touch of guilt, since Blast spells were supposed to be used only in self-defense. The magic energy hit Vilkor and sent him flying through the air.
But the gorzogs were still creeping toward Mellis. She backed away, looking anxious. Perda created friction, preparing to repel the creatures.

At that moment Zing flew into view, panting with exertion. Perda guessed that Zira and the others had left him behind in the village when they'd zapped out here. The little dragon must have been flying as fast as he could to reach Zann. He shot a burst of flame at Zira, who jumped away from Zann to avoid being burned.
"Zing!" Perda shouted. "Help Mellis!"
Zing spun toward the gorzogs, shooting more fire. They growled and spit at him, but he had learned their tricks and stayed just out of range.
Meanwhile Zira glared at Perda. "You!" she hissed. "You'll regret crossing me, little girl!"
Zann was relieved when Perda rushed over and removed his Immobilization spell. He wanted to thank her, but he couldn't because the Muting spell was still in place.
"We have to help Mellis," Perda said, ignoring Zira and her goons as they shouted for them to stop.
Zann nodded. He turned and ran toward Mellis with Perda at his side.

But when they got close to their friend, Zann realized she didn't need much help. Mellis had created a Shield spell, which was holding back the gorzogs. Zing flew overhead, occasionally sending out a blast of flame to singe the creatures' fur.
"Stop or you'll be sorry!" Zira shrieked.
Zann glanced back. Zira was gnashing her teeth and striding after them.
Mellis zapped herself out of her shield bubble and joined him and Perda. Zann gulped as Zira pointed at them.
"It was a mistake to defy me," she said. "Now I'm going to make an example of you in case anyone else is thinking of following in your footsteps."
She paused to glare at Vilkor and the gathered crowd. Krub smirked and stepped up behind Zira, cracking his knuckles. Zann wasn't afraid of a fight, but he knew that sometimes it was better to flee.
He grabbed the two girls. "Zap," he thought, doing his best to focus.
The three of them landed at the base of the tree beside the well. Zann sighed with relief. His zap had been perfectly accurate for once!
Perda looked confused. "Why did you zap us here?" she asked. "Oh. And I guess Zira's Shield spell isn't working anymore."
Zann's eyes widened. He hadn't even thought of that! He was relieved that the shield was gone.
Meanwhile Mellis pointed to her own mouth. "Oh, right," Perda said. "I almost forgot about the Muting spell."
She quickly removed the spell from both Mellis and Zann.
"Thanks," Zann said as soon as he could speak. "Listen, I have a plan. We have to go back through the time vortex."
"What?" Mellis cried.
But Perda immediately nodded. "Zann's right," she said to Mellis. "Zira is out to get you. The only way to keep you safe is to take you to our time, where she can't reach you."
Mellis hesitated. Zann felt anxious as he listened to the shouts from outside the wall. How long would it take Zira to find them?
"Hurry," he said. "Let's check the wormhole. If it works like the regular ones, there should be enough magic in the air to open it now."
They joined hands and stepped closer to the tree. But nothing happened.
"It was right here." Perda tapped the ground with her foot. "I know it was!"
Zann's heart sank. "Are we trapped here?"
Perda's shoulders slumped. But then she straightened up. "Wait. It didn't open the regular way back in our own time either. Remember, Zann? It opened when I grabbed that old metal leaf thing."
"Metal leaf?" Mellis blurted out. "My pendant is shaped like a leaf."
"Whoa, really?" Zann glanced at Perda. "Could it be the same leaf?"
"I bet it is!" Perda looked excited. "That must be the key that opens this wormhole! After all, it's something from 'bygone days,' just like in the riddle."
"But the pendant is back in our time," Zann said. "Does that mean we can't open the wormhole?"
Perda shook her head. "There must be another way."
Just then Zing flew over the wall, chirping irritably. "Get down here, little buddy!" Zann called.
But someone else had seen Zing fly over the wall. "They're in there!" Krub shouted. "Inside, by the well!"
"Should we zap away somewhere else?" Zann asked. "If we can get to the other wormhole, we could hide out in Wyssa's world."
"No, wait." Perda looked thoughtful. "We don't have that key anymore, but maybe a different key would work. Something that survived through time, like Mellis' pendant or like that cup!"
"What cup?" Zann asked.

Perda quickly reminded him and Mellis about the cracked cup lying on the ground outside. "I'm pretty sure it's the same one that becomes a relic in our time," she said. "I saw it in your parents' lab."
The three of them levitated to the top of the wall. Mellis pointed. "There it is!"
Zann saw the cup. He also saw Zira rushing forward.
"Stand back, everyone!" she cried.
Magic energy crackled from her fingertips as she raised her arms. Zann created friction for a Shield spell. Beside him, Perda did the same.
But Mellis acted faster. She raised both hands. "Away!" she cried, her voice amplified by a Swelling spell.
A huge wave of energy swept out from Mellis, knocking Zira and her entourage off their feet and halfway to the horizon!
"Wow!" Zann was amazed by Mellis' power.

"Hurry." Perda was still rubbing her hands together. "She'll be back soon. And the gorzogs are still out there, so we'll have to bring the cup to us. Let's use a simple Transportation spell. Be sure to focus. We might have only one chance before Zira returns."

Zann nodded, already rubbing his thumb against his other fingers. Transportation spells were basic magic, but that didn't mean they were easy. He thought back to the time he'd tried a Transportation spell in school and accidentally blew up the stuff he was supposed to transport.
"Come to me," he murmured.
The cup wiggled and then lifted off the ground. It floated toward the kids, finally landing in Zann's hand.
"Got it!" he cried.
He didn't bother to levitate down. Instead he released the spell and fell beside Zing with a grunt. Perda and Mellis did the same.
With the cup in his hand, Zann stepped toward the tree. The wormhole swirled open!
"I never thought I'd be so glad to see Wormwood again!" Perda thought as everyone stepped out of the wormhole.
"Who has the cup?" she asked.
Zann looked sheepish. "I guess I dropped it as we jumped into the vortex."
"My pendant!" Mellis cried, picking something up from the ground. Tears filled her eyes. "I thought I'd never see it again."
Darb and Gliss ran toward them. Zing chirped with joy and flew to meet Darb.
"Where did you guys go?" Gliss asked. "You disappeared for a second."
"A second?" Zann said. "Are you kidding? We were gone for weeks!"
Gliss laughed. "No way! We just saw you a moment ago."
"Hmm," Perda said. "The time vortex must have returned us to the same moment we left. So to everyone here, it's as if we weren't gone at all."
"The time vortex?" Darb glanced up from scratching Zing's head and noticed Mellis. "Oh, hello," he said politely.
Mellis didn't respond. She was staring around, her eyes wide with wonder. "Can this truly be Terrica?"
"No, it's Magica," Gliss said. "Did you just arrive through the wormhole?"
Zann nodded. Then he and Perda took turns telling their friends everything that had happened.
"Wow!" Gliss and Darb said together.
After that, the friends gave Mellis a tour of the city. They visited the palace, the zoo, and Zann's favorite park.
"This place . . . ," Mellis said. "It's amazing!"
At last they stopped in at Zann's parents' lab, where Boz, Asta, and Nax were waiting.
"We were about to send a message moth," Nax said. "It's almost time for dinner."
"Great," Zann said. "But first, we have something to tell you guys." He quickly told them about their adventures. His mom seemed especially interested in Mellis.
"Mellis is an unusual name," Asta said. "I was just reading about Queen Mellis, the first elected ruler of Magica."

She grabbed a dusty old book. "She lived a long time ago, before history was being recorded. Later, during the Old Times, her descendants wrote about her. They were trying to convince people to return to the peaceful, prosperous times that existed under her rule."
Boz nodded. "Her natural magic powers were stronger than anyone's before or since. She was able to defeat everyone who tried to harm Magica during her lifetime."
Gliss glanced at Mellis. "Is that you?"
Mellis didn't answer. Her face had gone pale.
"It must be her," Perda thought. "But she looks . . . scared."
Perda squeezed Mellis' hand. "Mellis is probably a common name in your time, right?"
"But what if it's not?" Mellis said. "What if it's my destiny to defeat Zira and help Terrica—I mean, Magica—to become peaceful?"
"Zira will be waiting to take you prisoner," Zann said.
Perda remembered how Mellis had swept Zira and her goons away with one word. "It's okay," she told Zann. "I think Mellis can handle it."

"I think I can too." Mellis' voice was quiet but assured. "You guys taught me so much, including how to be brave." She smiled at Perda and Zann. "Besides, I can't abandon the people I care about, like Anso and my other friends." She sighed. "And even my uncle."
She looked at the group. "Thank you for showing me what Magica will be someday. Now I'll know what I'm fighting for."
After dinner Perda and her friends zapped back to Wormwood with Mellis.
"We don't have the cup," Zann said. "I hope Mellis' pendant will work to open the wormhole instead."
"I've been thinking about that cup," Perda told him. "I think you dropped it because you had to. Otherwise, it would exist twice in our time."
Zann looked confused. "What do you mean?"
"I agree," Mellis said. "The cup exists here as an ancient relic in your parents' lab. Who knows what would happen if a newer version of the same cup suddenly existed here at the same time?"
Perda smiled at her. Mellis was so smart, thoughtful, and brave. After all their adventures together, she definitely felt like a true friend.
"I'll miss you," Perda told her.
Mellis hugged her. "I'll miss you too. All of you." She pulled out her pendant. "Thanks for everything." As the wormhole swirled open, she stepped in and disappeared.
The wormhole closed, but the pendant popped back out and landed on the ground!
Zann picked it up. "She dropped it!"
Perda shook her head. "She had to drop it. Another version of this pendant still exists in her time, even if she can't find it."
Perda wasn't sure she understood exactly how time travel worked. But she planned to think more about it.
"It's getting dark," Gliss said. She reached for Darb's hand. "Let's zap back to Zann's house and get ready to go home."
She zapped away. Darb had been playing with Zing, so the little dragon disappeared with them, leaving Perda and Zann alone.
"I guess we should go too." Zann looked wistful. "Happy birthday, Perda. I hope you guys can visit again soon."

"Me too." Perda squeezed the pendant in her hand. She knew that Zann would miss her most of all, just as she always missed him when they were apart. She thought about Gliss holding Darb's hand and suddenly had an idea.
"Sure, Zann and I are both perfectly capable of zapping on our own," she thought with a smile. "But that doesn't mean we can't zap together once in a while."
She grabbed his hand and squeezed it. His eyes went wide, and his cheeks turned pink.
Perda could feel her cheeks turn pink too. But she smiled and squeezed Zann's hand again.
"Zap!" she said happily.
"How much farther is it, Wugg?" Loro asked, stepping over a small tree trunk lying across the wooded trail. "I thought you said we wouldn't have to walk very far."
Wugg stopped and turned around. "The town is just ahead. And please call me Dad, not Wugg." He started walking again.
Dara nodded. "It's exciting to be in our new home, Loro, but we need to remember to try to fit in."

"I know, Mom ," Loro said. "I'm sorry." Despite the reminder from Wugg and Dara, he felt a shiver of excitement. They'd been planning this move for so long, it was amazing that the day had finally arrived.

They followed the trail a little farther and then emerged from the woods. To the left, a cliff dropped off sharply. To the right, a steep stone slope rose up, blending into the mountain towering above. In between was a rocky clearing. The ancient ruin of a stone wall lay just ahead, and beyond that was a tiny village. A group of houses were nestled into the sloped ground. Several shops and official buildings stood around a small town square in the flat area near the ruin. It was midmorning, and nobody was in view.
"It's quieter here than I expected," Wugg said.
"Yes." Dara looked around. "But that's okay. We'll be able to—oh, look! There's someone."
A man holding a broom had just come out of a house. "Hello there," he said when he spotted the newcomers. "Are you visiting Stone Wall?"
Dara smiled. "Actually, we're moving here."
"Really? Hardly anyone moves here," the man said with a chuckle. "Which part of Magica did you come from?"
Wugg waved his hand. "Oh, just a little town a couple of zaps from First City. You've probably never heard of it."
"Most people have never heard of Stone Wall either." The man chuckled again. "What made you decide to settle here?"
"We wanted to see someplace new," Wugg said.
"Yes," Dara added. "And we heard the views in Stone Wall are spectacular."

Loro climbed onto part of the ruined wall for a better look around. Stone Wall was about halfway up Mount Mystery, the tallest mountain in Magica. From atop the wall, he could see out over the densely forested foothills. Beyond lay a vast plain covered with fields, towns, and rivers.
"Any thoughts on where we should create our house?" Wugg asked the man.
He used his broom to point to an empty area nearby. "Nobody uses that spot over there. I'll go and let Mayor Ruxton know we have three new residents."
"Great. Thanks," Dara said.
They waved good-bye, and Loro followed Wugg and Dara over to the empty land.
"Let's join friction," Dara said. "That way our magic will be strong enough to build everything at once. I want to get settled right away."
The three of them stood in a circle and rubbed their hands together. Magic energy sparked around them.
Loro smiled. "Making magic feels great," he thought.
"Create!" Wugg said.
Instantly a house appeared. They went inside and looked around. The place was small but cozy with a few pieces of simple furniture.
"Nice," Loro said. "Now what? Should I help you make more stuff?"
"We can finish up here," Dara said. "You should go out and start making friends."
"Okay. See you later!" Loro went back outside.
The man with the broom had disappeared. Everything was quiet. The only sound was a bird singing nearby.
"I hope I can meet some kids here," Loro thought.
Suddenly a loud sound rang out. Hee-haw! Hee-haw!

Curious, Loro followed the sound. It was coming from the forest at the edge of town. He was surprised. He, Wugg, and Dara hadn't passed anyone on their way. Then he spotted a narrow, winding path that was narrower than the other trail. He followed it until he emerged into a clearing.
A girl around his age was there with a slightly younger boy whose hat was pulled down over his ears. A strange-looking creature was standing with them. It had a gray coat, four legs, and long ears.
"What's that thing?" Loro blurted out.
The two kids spun around, surprised.
"Hi! Who are you?" the girl asked.
"I'm Loro. My family just moved here."
The girl smiled. "Wow, I can't remember the last time a kid moved to Stone Wall. Actually, I'm not sure it's ever happened! I'm Zella. This is my brother, Raff."
"Nice to meet you, Loro," the boy said.
Zella gestured at the gray animal. "Oh, and this is Muncher. He's our donkey."
Muncher let out his loud sound again and glared at Loro.
"He doesn't look very friendly," Loro said uneasily.
Zella laughed and patted the donkey. "Oh, don't worry about him. He's not used to new people, that's all. Where did you move from?"
"Will you two show me around Stone Wall?" Loro asked quickly. "My parents and I just arrived. I haven't seen anything yet."
Zella shrugged. "There's not much to see. But sure, we'll give you the grand tour." She looked at her brother. "Should we zap back to town?"
"No, let's walk there," Raff said. "We can show Loro more of the forest on the way."
"Uh-oh," Loro thought, wriggling his toes. "I've got to do more walking. These shoes feel so tight, and my feet are already sore."
But he forced himself to smile at the two kids. "My parents will be happy to hear I'm already making friends," he thought. "So far everything is going according to our plans!"
Zella was excited about the new kid in town. Nothing interesting ever happened in boring Stone Wall.
"Follow me, Loro," she said eagerly. "We'll show you our house first."
She headed along a forest trail. The new boy walked beside her, with Raff and Muncher behind them.
"Do you two spend a lot of time in the forest?" Loro asked, stopping to watch a rock rat scurry past. "There must be lots of interesting animal species in here."
"There are." Raff tugged his hat lower on his head. "I like to look for animals in the forest."
"He's like Darb that way," Zella said. "You know, Zann's best friend?"
"Zann and Darb? The kids who saved Magica from that evil guy?" Loro sounded interested. "Do you know them?"
"I wish!" Zella's eyes lit up. "Zann, Darb, Perda, and Gliss are my heroes!"
They stepped out of the forest. Muncher started eating the sparse weeds growing between some rocks.

Zella noticed Loro watching the donkey. "That's how he got his name—he likes to munch on everything he sees! Anyway . . ." She looked toward the left. "This is a nice view, but I wish we could see First City from here. It's too far away, though."
Raff smiled. "My sister is obsessed with First City because Zann lives there."
"His friends live in Swamp Bottom," Zella said. "That's even farther away."
Next Zella and Raff showed Loro their house. Then they led him to the town square.
Raff pointed to a low, squat building. "That's our school. There's just one classroom, since there are only 14 kids in Stone Wall."
Zella smiled at Loro. "Fifteen, now that you're here."
As they kept walking, Zella pointed out the mayor's house, the theater, and the restaurant.
A very old man was sitting on a bench. He narrowed his eyes and jerked his head at Loro.
"Who's that?"
Zella introduced Loro to the old man, whose name was Panno. "Loro just moved here."
"Interesting." Panno got up and hobbled away.
Loro winced. "Panno seems friendly," he joked.
"Panno is usually nicer than that," Zella said, surprised by the man's rudeness. "He must be in a bad mood."
"Panno moved to Magica from another world," Raff said. "Our mom says his people have the gift of seeing what's in people's hearts."
Zella shrugged. "I don't believe it. Nobody can do that." She was tired of talking about Stone Wall. "So, Loro, you didn't tell us earlier . . . Where did you move from? Is it close to First City?"
Loro shook his head. "I've never been to First City."
Zella often dreamed of visiting Magica's capital. "I bet it's way more interesting than Stone Wall. I want to visit the palace and the zoo. Maybe I'd even get to meet Zann!"
Raff laughed. "That's the part you'd like best."
Zella laughed too. She didn't mind when her brother teased her about being a fan of the kid heroes. "I wish I had a zap accelerator so I could go there."
"What's that?" Loro asked.
"Zann's parents invented it," Raff said. "It's a magical device that lets you travel long distances on a single zap."

"Maybe someday everybody will have one," Zella said. "Right now there are only a few. Zann's friends from Swamp Bottom have one. The others are being tested by Voids, to see if it helps them get around."
Voids were Magicians who didn't have any natural magic. There were none in Stone Wall, so Zella had never met one.
"Darb is a Void," Zella said. "He's really cool. He knows more about animals than just about anyone."
"Well, you sure know a lot about those kids!" Loro said, grinning. "Let's go back into the forest. I'd love to explore some more."
"We'll show you our favorite spot," Raff said.
Zella knew exactly where her brother meant. They led their new friend past the clearing where they'd met him and kept walking. Soon the trees thinned out again.
"Wow," Loro said when they emerged from the forest.
They were near the edge of another cliff, a rocky outcropping that extended over the valley. Immediately below was the silvery expanse of Infinity Lake.
"Be careful!" Zella said as Loro stepped closer to the edge.
He turned around to look at her. "What's wrong? Are you afraid of that lake?"
"Zella is afraid of heights," Raff said.

Zella flushed. "But some people are scared of Infinity Lake. Anything that touches its waters is lost forever—even magic can't help them find it." She changed the subject, pointing upward. "There's an even better view if you look up."
Far overhead, Mount Mystery stretched toward the sky. Near the top a fortress loomed out of the craggy rock.
"That's old King Zanta's fortress," Zella said. "Morb lived there when he was trying to take over Magica."
Raff nodded. "It was a pretty terrible place even before that. King Zanta ruled during the Old Times. Back then dark magic was everywhere."
"Yes, I know." Loro peered up toward the fortress thoughtfully. "Zanta was the most powerful ruler Magica ever had."
"I suppose so." Zella frowned. "But he sounds horrible. We learned in school that he used otherworld magic to control people."
"That's where Morb got the idea for his evil contraptions," Raff said.
Just then they heard a loud hee-haw. Zella realized Muncher had wandered off.
"Muncher sounds scared!" Raff rushed toward the sound.
Zella followed with Loro, and soon they burst into another clearing.
"Oh no!" Zella cried. The donkey was struggling to escape from the swirling center of a wormhole!
"Whoa!" Raff gasped. "Hold on, Muncher!"
He leaped forward and tried to grab one of the donkey's back legs. The wormhole pulsed with magic energy, trying to suck Muncher into its depths.
"I've never seen a live wormhole before," Raff thought. "It's scarier than I expected!"

There were no wormholes in Stone Wall. But everyone in Magica could recognize the swirling portals that led into the vortex. Children were warned not to go near them, since wormholes' energy could be unpredictable.
Just then the wormhole sparked. Muncher disappeared a little farther into it.
"Help!" Raff cried.
Zella and Loro jumped forward. Together the three of them pulled the donkey free. As soon as they moved away, the wormhole swirled shut.
They collapsed a safe distance away. From here, the wormhole looked like nothing but a faint shimmer in the air.
But something else caught Raff's eye at the end of the clearing. "Whoa, I never noticed that before!" he thought.
Before he could point it out, Zella sprang up. "Maybe we should go back and test that wormhole."
Loro looked alarmed. "What do you mean, Zella?"
She grinned. "We could use it to get to First City. Or maybe somewhere even more exciting."

"No way!" Raff knew that the vortex connected all the wormholes in all the worlds. It could be used to travel long distances quickly—but only if travelers knew what they were doing. If not, the vortex could be deadly.
Zella was already moving close to the wormhole. Raff leaped up and pulled her back.

"Zella, we don't know anything about navigating the vortex. Mom and Dad said there used to be a wormhole an hour's walk from here. More than one villager disappeared through it, never to be seen again."
Zella yanked out of Raff's grip, and the wormhole swirled open. "Those were just stories to scare us into being good."
"Maybe," Raff said. "But even Zann didn't jump into the first wormhole he saw, right?"
"It's too dangerous, Zella," Loro said, giving a nervous laugh. "We just became friends. I'd hate to have you disappear so soon!"
Zella still looked tempted.
Luckily Raff had a way to distract her. "Look over there." He pointed to the end of the clearing. "Is that a cave?"
The other two turned to look.
"I don't see anything," Zella said. "Where?" She moved closer to it.
"Stay back!" Loro snapped. "If it's a cave, there could be something dangerous inside!"
"I doubt it." Raff led the way across the clearing. "There aren't many dangerous animals around here."
"I see it now," Zella said. "I can't believe we never noticed it before."
"We don't usually come this way," Raff said. "If Muncher hadn't found that wormhole, we might never have seen the cave either."
Loro hung back, looking anxious. "Maybe we should leave it alone. I'd love to see more of Stone Wall."
"We can do that later." Zella pushed tall grass away from the cave opening. Then she snapped her fingers to create friction. "Light!"
A glow appeared at her fingertips. She used it to look inside the dark cave. Raff peered over her shoulder.
"We shouldn't go in there!" Loro said again. "Some creature could be living in there."
Raff and Zella ignored him.
"Let's try a Life Force Locator spell," Raff said.
Zella looked confused. "What's that?"

Raff hesitated. Trying new magic always made him nervous. He usually let his sister or someone else do it. But he'd just read a book about Life Force Locator spells. So he rubbed his hands together. "Locate!"
A translucent map floated into view. It showed the cave and a tunnel leading off the back. The tunnel branched out into numerous other tunnels and rooms.
"Whoa," Raff said. "This cave is pretty big." A few bright dots flashed on the map. When Raff squinted at them, they showed the Magica creatures that were in the cave.
"There are only a few rock rats and bugs," Raff said. "I also see a bunch of buzz worms."

Loro still looked hesitant. But he followed as the siblings and Muncher stepped into the cave. The first chamber was large, with a smooth floor and a high ceiling. A few crude, faded drawings decorated the walls.
Zella peered at them. "I bet trolls drew these. They must have lived here once."
"Trolls?" Loro bit his lip.
"Don't worry," Raff said. "All the trolls were run out of this part of Mount Mystery a long time ago."
Zella nodded. "They came back while Morb was around. But even then, we never saw any."
The map had faded away, but Raff could still picture it. "That's weird. The map showed a tunnel leading out of this chamber, but I don't see one."
"Maybe it collapsed," Loro said, looking around. "This whole place might be unstable."
"Or maybe Raff's spell didn't work right." Zella rolled her eyes. "My brother often reads about magic, but he doesn't actually practice it that much."

Raff barely heard his sister. He ran his hands over the solid stone wall, thinking about a book he'd read recently. In it, an adventurer had discovered an underground city full of passageways hidden by spells.
"Maybe the tunnels are hidden," he thought.
"What are you doing, Raff?" Loro said, edging toward the mouth of the cave. "It's really cold in here. Come on. Let's go back outside."
"In a second." Raff rubbed his hands together, trying to remember a spell they'd learned in school. Then it came to him. "Reveal!"
The air shimmered, and a tunnel appeared!
"Cool!" Zella said, surprised by her brother's Reveal spell.

As she'd told Loro, Raff was rarely interested in practicing spells, even though he was a Red like Zann and Gliss. All Reds were supposed to have strong magic, but her brother was the only one in town. He didn't like to stand out, so he always wore a hat to cover his red hair.
"Let's see what's inside this tunnel." Zella started to enter it. "It must be something interesting. Otherwise nobody would have bothered to hide it with a spell."
All three kids created lights to help them see better. Muncher followed them at first. Then the tunnel grew too narrow, and he backed out.
"See you soon, Muncher," Raff said.

After a short distance, the tunnel opened into a chamber even larger than the first one. A stone slab stood at the center like a table. An ancient metal cup sat on it, coated in dust. On the wall hung a rusty sword, along with the tattered remains of a tapestry.
"Hey!" Zella pointed to another dusty old item. "That's a crown." She picked it up. "Because of those drawings, I thought this was an old troll cave. But this stuff didn't belong to trolls."

Raff nodded. "I think I know what this place is!" He sounded excited. "Don't you remember our local history classes, Zella? Experts think old King Zanta had a secret lair where he hid from his enemies."
Zella gasped. "This cave might be King Zanta's secret hideaway!"
"Really?" Loro sounded dubious. "We're pretty far down the mountain, aren't we?"
"Yes, we're on the boring part of Mount Mystery," Zella said. "But you saw that map of the cave. There are lots of tunnels back here. Maybe one of them goes all the way up to Zanta's fortress!"
She could hardly believe they'd discovered something so interesting. This ordinary day was turning into the kind of adventure Zann and his friends might have.
"Let's keep exploring," Raff said.

Several tunnels led off from the chamber. The first one they tried led to a dead end. The next opened into a narrow room with more drawings on the walls. These drawings looked more like symbols and words than art, but they were so old and faded, Zella couldn't make out many details.

The kids continued to explore. The tunnels had plenty of twists and turns, and there were lots of other rooms. Some were large like the first two, and some were smaller. Once they almost stumbled into a deep, dark hole.
Raff peered down into it. "I wonder if this was a trap or a hiding place."
"Let's see how deep it is." Zella snapped her fingers to create an extra ball of light. The first one she created was too dim, so she rubbed her hands together and tried again. "Light!"
This ball was brighter. She dropped it into the hole. It landed on a hard stone floor, showing the hole to be about four times deeper than she was tall.
Raff grimaced. "Maybe this hole used to be covered with straw or something. That way victims wouldn't see it and would fall right in."
"Yeah," Zella said. "That's pretty creepy."
As they explored, the kids encountered most of the insects and other creatures the map had shown them. Zella was surprised there weren't more animals living in the cave.

"This would be a perfect den for some of the smaller species of wild dragons," she said as they peered into another small room. "I wonder if there used to be a Shield spell at the entrance or something."
"Morb used Zanta's fortress," Loro said. "Maybe he used this cave too."
"I don't think so." Raff lit up the footsteps they'd left in the thick layer of dust on the floor. "It seems like we're the first ones to enter this cave in a long time."
"We've seen some cool stuff," Loro said uneasily. "But let's go, okay? I should get home before my parents start to worry."

Zella didn't want to go, but she didn't want Loro to get in trouble. She nodded. "We can go now, but let's come back tomorrow morning." Then she had an even better idea. "I'm going to send a message to Zann about this place. His parents might want to check it out!"
Raff smiled. "And maybe they'll bring the whole gang to Stone Wall so you can meet them?"
Zella grinned, snapping her fingers to summon a message moth. "Stranger things have happened!"
Zann was walking through First City with Perda when a message moth landed on his finger. He saw the sender's name and smiled ruefully. It was from a girl who lived in a tiny town on Mount Mystery.
Perda looked at the moth. "Is that from our fan Zella?"
"Yes," Zann said. "Maybe she's writing again to tell us how cool we are. It's kind of embarrassing to be famous, isn't it?"
Perda shrugged. "I think it's nice. We get to meet lots of interesting people."
"True." Zann nodded, feeling glad that Perda had decided to use the zap accelerator to visit that day. Darb and Gliss were busy and couldn't come, but he was always happy to hang out with Perda.
He scanned the words inscribed on the moth's wings. "Zella and some other kids found a cave. They think old King Zanta used to hide out there."
"Really?" Perda said. "That's cool—if it's true. Maybe we should tell your parents."
Zann smiled. Perda loved any chance to visit the lab where his parents worked. "Sure, why not." He grabbed her hand. "Zap!"
The next morning Wugg and Dara packed two small bags.
"Are you sure you'll be okay staying here in Stone Wall without us?" Wugg asked.
"Yes." Loro smiled. "Bring me a gift from First City, okay? Maybe one of those zap accelerators I was telling you about."
Dara chuckled. "We'll be sure to look for one. They sound very useful."
"Right," Wugg added with a wink. "Your new friends are already teaching you interesting things, aren't they? Good luck, and we'll see you in a few days!"

They zapped away. It was very early, and the village was quiet. Loro thought about trying to zap to the cave on his own. But he was still very new to this area. He didn't want to accidentally land in the wrong spot. So he set off across the village on foot.
Panno was sitting on the same bench where the kids had encountered him the previous day. Loro noticed Panno staring at him with an odd expression.
"Good morning," Loro said politely.
Panno grunted a greeting, but his expression remained strange, almost threatening.
"I get the sense that Panno thinks I don't belong here," Loro thought. He hurried on, feeling uncomfortable. "I hope he doesn't know that I—"
"Hey, Loro!" Zella's voice interrupted Loro's thoughts. She and Raff were sitting in the yard outside their house. They were eating breakfast at a little table beneath a tree.
"Are you on your way to the cave?" Raff asked. "You seem even more eager to get there than Zella is!"
Zella laughed. "Yeah, especially since you couldn't wait to get out of there yesterday!"
Loro smiled sheepishly. "I got excited about exploring the cave while I was telling my parents about it. Besides, I wanted to get away before they gave me a bunch of chores around our new house."
"We're almost finished eating," Raff said. "We can head out to the cave in a few minutes."
Loro had hoped to look around the cave by himself first. But he figured it wasn't a big deal. It was important to make friends here.
"Where's Muncher?" he asked as the siblings gulped down the rest of their puckerberry pancakes.
"Our dad loaned him to a neighbor for the day." Raff pointed to a fence nearby. Muncher was on the other side of it. The donkey's nose was buried in a patch of brightly colored flowers.
"As you can see, the neighbor has a bunch of sprinkle thistles growing in her yard," Raff said. "That's why she asked to borrow him—she wants Muncher to eat them all up."
"Sprinkle thistles?" Loro said. "What are they?"

"I thought they grew all over Magica but maybe not," Raff said. "They're a type of thistle that scatters its seeds everywhere. It's easier for Muncher to eat them than to use magic to get rid of them."
Soon the three kids arrived back at the clearing. Zella looked over at the wormhole.
"I wonder if Zann got my message moth," she said. "I still wish I could just pop over to First City and talk to him."
Raff rolled his eyes. "If you went through that wormhole, Zella, you'd probably end up in Fardark or some other terrible world."
Zella stuck out her tongue at her brother.
"I've heard about Fardark," Loro said. "It's a world filled with horrible, dangerous creatures, right?"
"Yes," Raff said. "Zann's parents went there a few times. I read about it in one of their books."
Loro cocked his head. "Wait, Raff. I thought Zella was the Zann fan, not you!" He laughed.
Zella laughed too. "That's true, but Raff has read every book in the village, including my copies of Zann's parents' books. But never mind that. Let's go into the cave!"

At the mouth of the cave, Zella and Raff snapped their fingers to create a light. Loro created one too, and then followed them inside. The first chamber looked the same as before. So did the one with the stone table. The kids started following some tunnels they hadn't explored the previous day.
One tunnel was so narrow that they had to squeeze through sideways. Another dropped steeply down, almost like a slide. The kids had to go down on their rear ends.

"This reminds me of one of Zann's adventures," Zella said when they reached the bottom. "Remember? He talked about it in that interview we saw on his Directory page. They slid down a ramp that was hidden under a statue in a park. The tunnel at the bottom led all the way to the palace!"
Loro was barely listening to Zella as she went on about Zann again. He'd just spotted something leaning against the cave wall. It was a long staff with a dusty jewel on the end.
"Oh wow!" he thought, his heart pounding with excitement. "I know what that is!"
Raff and Zella had spotted it too.
"That looks interesting," Raff said.
Zella rushed toward it. "Maybe it belonged to old King Zanta!"
"Careful!" Loro blurted out. "I think you're right, Zella. That looks like the Sovereign's Staff. It's a very powerful ancient relic!"
Zella's eyes widened with awe. "A relic, like the Mouth of the Undead or the Mask of Zanta or the Dragontamer's Charm? Like the relics Zann and Perda and the others saw in the Cave of the Unknown?"

Loro nodded. "Yes. I've heard that the Sovereign's Staff is one of the most powerful relics ever. If you touch it, it's likely to send you halfway to First City—or something even more dangerous might happen."
Raff moved closer to the Sovereign's Staff for a better look. He was trying to remember everything he'd read about the notorious relic.

"Maybe this staff is the real thing, or maybe it's not," he said thoughtfully. "It was lost so long ago that nobody knows exactly what it looks like. I mean, it would be exciting to discover an important relic, but most experts think the Sovereign's Staff was taken to another world, maybe Fardark or . . ." He paused. "Narakan."
Based on what Raff had read, Fardark was scary, but Narakan was worse. It was the terrifying world where the Beast of the Otherworld was from.
"Whatever it is, it's giving off a lot of chaotic magic energy." Loro backed away. "Can you feel it?"
"Yes," Raff said. "We should leave it alone. Come on, let's get out of this room."

He and Loro took a few steps away. But Zella stayed where she was, staring at the staff. "Nobody knows what happened to the Sovereign's Staff. We should tell someone about this. Even if it's not that relic, it could be a different one, just as important."

Raff wasn't surprised that Zella was excited about their discovery. She was always looking for adventures. "You're not Zann or Perda, and we're not in the Cave of the Unknown," he teased her. "This thing is probably nothing."
"Yeah, it's probably nothing," Loro said quickly.

Zella shrugged. "Well, I'm going to contact Zann again. His parents will want to make sure it's not dangerous." Her eyes lit up. "Maybe I can send him a video message! Perda figured out how to do that, remember?"
"Like I said, you're not Perda," Raff said. "Do you even know how?"
"I think so," Zella said. "Perda wants everyone to be able to use new forms of magic. I saw her talking about video messages on a Newsblink a few weeks ago."

Every night after dinner, Zella and their parents watched the latest Newsblink. It was a magical video showing interesting stories and images from all over Magica. Sometimes Raff watched too. But usually he went to his room to read.
They hurried back outside, and Zella summoned a spy fly. She rubbed her free hand against her leg. Then she touched the spy fly and set it on a branch.
"Spy on us," Zella said. She looked at the others. "Okay, now we just talk to them. Let's try it."
Loro looked interested. "You should do the talking, Zella."
"Okay." She took a deep breath and looked at the spy fly. "Hi, Zann. It's Zella again. I hope you got my message yesterday."
She went on to tell Zann about the jeweled staff they'd found inside the cave. Then she sent the spy fly off to find him.
"There," she said. "I hope it works."
Raff nodded. He couldn't make up his mind about their discovery. "It's probably not the Sovereign's Staff," he thought. "But what if it is? Loro's right. It could be very dangerous."
"We shouldn't leave that staff unguarded," Loro said. "What if someone else stumbles across it? They might think it's valuable and take it."
"Nobody ever comes out here," Zella said.
"Still, we should tell the mayor about it," Raff said. "She can put a Shield spell on the cave to keep people out."
"Why don't you two go and find her," Loro said. "I'll stay here and guard the cave entrance."
"Are you sure?" Raff said. "I could stay with you."

Loro shook his head. "I'll be fine. It's not dangerous if I stay out here, right?" He grinned. "Besides, you should be there when your sister tells the adults. I mean, I only just met her, and I already know she's always looking for adventure. What if nobody believes her?"
Zella smiled ruefully. "The mayor still teases me about that funny-looking rock. I thought it was from another world and made a big fuss. Come on, Raff. Let's go!"

Leaving Loro in the clearing, Raff and Zella zapped back to the village. Mayor Ruxton was watering her shrubs. She looked skeptical when Zella told her about the staff. Then Raff described the power he'd felt emanating from it.
"Hmm, that's odd. I'd better get some people to take a look," she said. "Just in case."
Soon a small group, including Raff's parents, the mayor, and some other adults, was walking back to the cave. Old Panno heard what they were talking about and limped along at the back of the group.
When they reached the cave, Loro rushed to meet them. "I heard noises from inside while you were gone! There was a weird wave of magic energy too."
"Are you all right?" Raff's mother asked Loro, and he nodded.
Mayor Ruxton performed a Testing spell. "I don't sense any stray energy right now. I think it's safe to go in." She pointed at the three kids. "Please show me where you saw this mysterious staff."

Raff, Zella, and Loro led the adults into the cave. The adults gasped in surprise over the crown and the other items in the large room. Then they reached the room at the end of the steep tunnel. This time it was the kids who gasped in shock.
"Oh, no," Zella said. "It was right over there!"
Raff stared at the spot where the staff had leaned. He could see its faint outline in the dust, but the staff itself was gone.
The mayor frowned. "Are you sure this is the right chamber, kids?" she asked.
Raff gulped. "Yes, we're sure. Whatever that thing was, it's gone!"
"Do you think it's actually the Sovereign's Staff?" Perda asked.
Zann and Perda were walking through the campus of First City University. They were on their way to watch an invisible airball game.
Zann thought about the spy fly message he'd just received from Zella. "I doubt it. Zella's village is probably just as boring as Swamp Bottom."
"Yeah," Perda said. "Zella and her friends were pretty excited about finding that cave. Every stick and stone probably looks like a relic to them."
Zann remembered being an overexcited small-town kid himself. Back in Swamp Bottom, he'd dreamed of adventure—just like Zella.
"I guess we can mention it to my parents later. I don't want to miss that airball game," he said. "By the way, Zella said she got the idea to send a video fly from you."

He smiled at Perda, feeling proud of her. She was really clever with magic. She'd figured out how to transform an ordinary spy fly into a video message carrier. She was always coming up with good ideas like that.
"Why are you staring at me like that?" Perda poked him in the arm.
Zann jumped, feeling slightly flustered. "Sorry. I was just—hey, look, a message moth."
The moth fluttered over and landed on his hand.
Perda leaned closer. "Is it from Zella?"
"Yes." Zann read the message, and his eyes widened. "She says the staff disappeared!"
"Huh?" Perda said in surprise.

Zann scanned the message again. "Zella and her brother went to tell some adults what they'd found. Their friend stood guard outside the cave entrance the whole time they were gone. But when they went back in, the staff was gone."
"That's strange," Perda said. "Maybe they got confused and went down the wrong tunnel."

"Maybe," Zann said. "But now I'm thinking we should tell my parents and Boz about this right away, just in case. They were more interested in Zella's cave than I thought they'd be." He touched his red hair. "They've been studying the Mask of Zanta recently. A few researchers want to try to piece that relic back together, but others think it's too dangerous."
"Are you thinking about how you're related to old King Zanta?" Perda asked.
That was another thing Perda was good at—guessing what Zann was thinking.
He nodded. "It's weird being related to someone like that."

"I bet. Zanta was super evil. Even worse than Morb." Perda glanced across the campus. At the far end, an enormous clear cube floated above the ground. It was half filled with water. In the middle was a small island where a tall, thin man was pacing between a cot and a table. Morb noticed the kids staring and glowered at them.

But Zann didn't feel scared of Morb. He even felt a little sorry for him, stuck in that clear prison. Then he remembered how many times Morb had tried to take over or destroy Magica. Suddenly he didn't feel sorry for him at all!
"Let's go to the lab," Zann said, grabbing Perda's hand. "Zap!"
Splash! They landed in a puddle of bright pink rain near the entrance to his parents' lab.
"Drat," Zann muttered, magically drying his shoes.
Perda was already hurrying into the lab. When Zann followed her, the only person there was an intern whose name he couldn't remember.
"Your parents and the others got called to the palace," the intern said. "I'm not sure why."
"Thanks." Zann looked at Perda. "I wonder what's going on. Mom and Dad didn't say anything about a meeting at the palace today."
"There's one way to find out." Perda grabbed his hand. "Zap!"
They landed in front of the palace doors.
"Oh, hello, kids." The guard looked worried. "Is Queen Venna expecting you? It's, uh, a little busy here today."
"We heard my parents are here," Zann said. "We have important information to tell them."
"Oh, I see." The guard waved them in. "I think everyone is in the throne room."
Zann and Perda hurried inside.
"See? Sometimes it's nice being famous," Perda whispered with a smile.
Zann tried to smile back. But he was feeling nervous now. What was going on?
When they reached the throne room, it was deserted.
"Now what?" Perda said.
"Let's find Yog," Zann suggested. "If something important is happening, he'll tell us."
They rushed to the office where the young man worked. When they arrived, he was just coming out.
"We heard my parents were called here. Is something wrong?" Zann said.
Yog hesitated. "I'm not supposed to tell anyone. But I'll take you to your parents."

The kids followed Yog through the palace to the safe room. That was where the most powerful and dangerous relics were kept. It had only one entrance, which was protected by powerful Shield spells. Two burly guards stood outside the door all the time.
Zann's parents, Nax and Asta, were outside the room, along with Zann’s grandfather, Boz. Queen Venna and several other important people were there too.
"What's going on?" Zann asked his parents.
His mother looked grim. "It's the Mask of Zanta."
Zann's father nodded. "It was in the safe room this morning when we stopped by to do some experiments. But when another researcher went in just now to check something, it was gone!"
Zann gasped. "Gone? How?"
"We don't know," Queen Venna said. "The guards were here all day. The only people they let in were a couple of researchers and the cleaning person."
Zann and Perda exchanged another look. Then Zann took a deep breath. "Speaking of Zanta and disappearing relics. We have something to tell you . . ."
